affected_groups.group: Hotels in municipalities where a Chapter 351 hotel occupancy tax applies
affected_groups.explanation: Would be excluded from the county tax authorized by this bill.

affected_groups.group: The municipality that is the largest municipality in a county described by Tax Code Section 352.002(a)(14)
affected_groups.explanation: Section 351.1035 applied to that municipality and governed the hotel occupancy tax revenue it collected: at least 50 percent had to be allocated to the purposes in Section 351.101(a)(3), and no more than 15 percent each could be used for the purposes in Sections 351.101(a)(4) and (5). The bill repeals the section for revenue collected on or after the Act’s effective date.

major_effects.label: County hotel occupancy tax authority
major_effects.explanation: Permits the qualifying county’s commissioners court to impose a hotel occupancy tax, excluding hotels where a municipal Chapter 351 tax applies.

major_effects.label: Repeal of municipal hotel-tax revenue allocation requirements
major_effects.explanation: The repealed provision applied to the largest municipality in a county described by Section 352.002(a)(14), requiring at least 50 percent of its hotel occupancy tax revenue to go to Section 351.101(a)(3) purposes and capping use for Sections 351.101(a)(4) and (5) purposes at 15 percent each. The repeal applies to revenue collected on or after the Act’s effective date.

HB162.summary: The bill would create a nine-member Texas Redistricting Commission and give it sole responsibility for drawing districts for the U.S. House, Texas House, and Texas Senate. It establishes member selection and eligibility rules, provides for state funding and staff, and sets plan standards, reporting, and court-review procedures. The bill takes effect only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise, it has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a commission to draw congressional and state legislative election districts and establishes procedures for adopting and challenging its plans.
Establishes a state commission, its membership and procedures, and assigns duties to state bodies.
Requires legislative appropriations for commission member compensation, expenses, and staff.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The commission draws districts for Texas legislative seats and the state's representation in the U.S. House.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for and members of the Texas Redistricting Commission
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants are subject to eligibility and political-activity criteria; appointed members serve terms and have restrictions on certain activities.

affected_groups.group: Members of the Texas Legislature and legislative political parties
affected_groups.explanation: Legislators belonging to the largest and second-largest parties in each chamber appoint eight commission members.

affected_groups.group: People affected by congressional and state legislative district boundaries
affected_groups.explanation: The commission's plans determine district boundaries, and an aggrieved person may challenge an adopted plan.

major_effects.label: Creates a redistricting commission
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a nine-member commission with sole responsibility for creating congressional and state legislative districts.

major_effects.label: Sets membership and conduct rules
major_effects.explanation: Defines applicant eligibility and bars specified officeholding, campaign, employment, and lobbying activities for applicants or members, subject to the stated time periods.

major_effects.label: Provides funding and staff support
major_effects.explanation: Requires sufficient appropriations for commission compensation, expenses, and staff, and assigns technical and clerical support to the Texas Legislative Council.

major_effects.label: Sets plan rules and court review
major_effects.explanation: Sets district composition standards and plan-adoption procedures; the Texas Supreme Court must adopt a plan if the commission misses its deadline, and plans may be challenged in court.

major_effects.label: Requires plan reports and public access
major_effects.explanation: Each adopted plan must include specified district, map, financial, and supporting information, and the Secretary of State must make the report available to the public.

agencies.name: Texas Redistricting Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill creates the commission and assigns it responsibility for drawing and adopting redistricting plans.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: Receives commission applications and reports, keeps commission records after operations are suspended, and makes plan reports available to the public.

agencies.name: Texas Legislative Council
agencies.explanation: Must provide technical staff and clerical services for preparation of redistricting plans; no matching registry ID is supplied.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Texas Supreme Court may appoint a presiding officer if required, must adopt a plan if the commission misses the deadline, and hears challenges to adopted plans.

HB163.summary: The bill would require pharmacy benefit managers to communicate with prescribing health care providers and their staff through a secure digital communication system. It would prohibit them from requiring fax communications.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how pharmacy benefit managers communicate with prescribing providers and their staff.
Imposes communication-method requirements on pharmacy benefit managers.
Requires a digital communication method that protects confidential health care information through encryption or authentication.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds a generally applicable requirement to the Texas Insurance Code.

affected_groups.group: Pharmacy benefit managers
affected_groups.explanation: Must use secure digital communication and may not require fax communication with prescribing providers and their staff.

affected_groups.group: Prescribing health care providers and their staff
affected_groups.explanation: Would communicate with pharmacy benefit managers through a secure digital system and could not be required to use fax.

major_effects.label: Secure digital communication required
major_effects.explanation: Requires pharmacy benefit managers to use a communication method that protects confidential health care information through encryption or user authentication.

major_effects.label: Fax cannot be required
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits pharmacy benefit managers from requiring fax communication with prescribing providers and their staff.

HB164.summary: HB 164 would repeal Education Code Subchapter J, ending the statutory education savings account program. It would also remove the Comptroller’s program-related registry access and repeal the ESA provider-employee criminal-history provision in Government Code § 411.109(b-1), and remove the Comptroller from Health and Safety Code Chapter 810’s applicability list. Amended § 411.109(c) would still authorize the Comptroller to obtain criminal-history information about persons described by Subsections (a) and (b), while retaining a reference to repealed Subsection (b-1); the effect of that reference is unclear.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill repeals an Education Code program and changes related education-registry access.
The repealed program is an education savings account program.
Repealing the program affects a statutory program under which money is distributed.
The bill changes which state agency is subject to Health and Safety Code Chapter 810.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes governing a statewide education program.

affected_groups.group: Children and families participating in or seeking to use the education savings account program
affected_groups.explanation: Repeal of the program would affect its participants and prospective users.

affected_groups.group: Education service providers and vendors of educational products
affected_groups.explanation: The bill removes their program-related provider-approval registry access and repeals a provision concerning criminal-history information for provider employees.

major_effects.label: Repeal of education savings account program
major_effects.explanation: Repeals Education Code Subchapter J, removing the statutory basis for the education savings account program.

major_effects.label: Changes to program-related agency access and screening provisions
major_effects.explanation: Removes the Comptroller’s access to the education registry for ESA provider preapproval and repeals Subsection (b-1), concerning criminal-history information about certain ESA provider or vendor employees. Amended Subsection (c) still authorizes criminal-history access for persons described by Subsections (a) and (b), while retaining a reference to repealed Subsection (b-1); the effect of that reference is unclear.

major_effects.label: Removes the Comptroller from Chapter 810 applicability
major_effects.explanation: Amends the list of state agencies to which Health and Safety Code Chapter 810 applies by deleting the Comptroller.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill removes the Comptroller’s ESA-related registry access and repeals Subsection (b-1), which concerns criminal-history information about certain ESA provider or vendor employees. Amended Subsection (c) continues to authorize the Comptroller to obtain criminal-history information about persons described by Subsections (a) and (b), and still refers to (b-1); the effect of that reference after repeal is unclear.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the recipients to whom this agency must provide equivalent registry access, but the supplied text does not identify the agency by name.

HB165.summary: The bill changes the comptroller’s authority to establish or authorize electronic payment systems using currency backed by gold and silver bullion held in a depository into a requirement. The systems would enable depositors and vendors to make and receive payments using that currency.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill makes establishment or authorization of the specified payment systems a mandatory duty of the comptroller.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill assigns the duty to the state comptroller without limiting it to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Depositors and vendors
affected_groups.explanation: The systems would enable these users to make and receive payments using the specified currency.

major_effects.label: Mandatory transactional-currency systems
major_effects.explanation: Changes the comptroller’s discretion to establish or authorize the systems into a requirement.

HB166.summary: HB 166 would exempt certain alternative-fueling facilities from the rule that grant awards must first go to applicants agreeing to make facilities available to the public at contract-designated times. The exemption applies only to facilities owned or operated by specified transit authorities, located in a county with more than one million people, and located in a nonattainment area or affected county; it applies to grant rounds beginning on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes grant-award conditions for alternative-fueling facilities.
Changes which facilities may receive grant awards without first satisfying the public-access priority condition.

locations.name: Counties with a population of more than one million that are in a nonattainment area or are affected counties
locations.explanation: Facilities qualify for the exception only when located in a county meeting the population threshold and in a nonattainment area or affected county.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for grants for alternative-fueling facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes the public-access condition's role in grant award prioritization for qualifying facilities.

affected_groups.group: Transit authorities governed by Transportation Code Chapter 451 or 452
affected_groups.explanation: Facilities owned or operated by these authorities may qualify for the exception if they also meet the location conditions.

major_effects.label: Exception to grant-award public-access priority
major_effects.explanation: The commission's restriction on awarding grants before public-access applicants have been awarded one would not apply to facilities meeting all three ownership and location conditions.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: Health and Safety Code Chapter 393 defines “Commission” as the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality. The proposed amendment changes the commission’s grant-award restriction and adds a facility exception.

HB167.summary: The bill would repeal sales and use tax exemptions for qualifying data centers and large data center projects, including the exemption for gas and electricity used directly in data processing. Projects certified before the effective date could keep their existing exemption until its applicable term expires, subject to existing limits, but pending certification applications would be treated as denied. It also makes conforming changes to provisions governing the application of state exemptions to local taxes.

policy_tags.explanation: Repeals specified sales and use tax exemptions and changes related provisions governing local-tax treatment.
The repealed exemptions specifically applied to qualifying data centers and large data center projects.
The bill removes the sales and use tax exemption for gas and electricity used directly by qualifying data centers in processing, storing, and distributing data.
The bill changes provisions concerning exemptions from taxes imposed by municipalities and taxes authorized under related local-tax chapters.

locations.name: Texas (statewide)
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide Tax Code provisions governing taxes in this state; it identifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Data centers and large data center projects
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying projects would lose the exemptions, except previously certified projects may retain them through the applicable exemption period, subject to any limitation provided by the applicable section; pending applications would be denied.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes provisions governing the application of exemptions to taxes imposed by municipalities.

major_effects.label: Repeal of data-center tax exemptions
major_effects.explanation: Removes the specified data-center exemption from the gas-and-electricity tax provisions and repeals the listed data-center tax provisions.

major_effects.label: Transition for certifications
major_effects.explanation: Previously certified projects may retain their exemption through its applicable expiration, subject to existing limits; applications pending on the effective date are deemed denied and cannot be approved.

major_effects.label: Conforming local-tax provisions
major_effects.explanation: Removes references to the repealed data-center exemption provisions from rules applying state exemptions to local taxes.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill addresses the Comptroller's certification role: pending certification applications are denied, while previously certified projects may continue their exemptions under the stated transition rule.

HB168.summary: HB 168 would add providing health care services for fertility as a reason a state or county employee may use time from the applicable family leave pool, but only after exhausting eligible compensatory, discretionary, sick, and vacation leave. It expands eligibility in existing pools; it does not create a new pool.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands employee eligibility to use time from an existing family leave pool.
The bill changes eligibility under county family leave pool programs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to state and county family leave pool programs across Texas.

affected_groups.group: State employees who have exhausted eligible leave
affected_groups.explanation: They could use their employing agency's family leave pool for the added fertility-care circumstance.

affected_groups.group: County employees who have exhausted eligible leave
affected_groups.explanation: They could use their county's family leave pool for the added fertility-care circumstance.

major_effects.label: Family leave pool eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Adds providing health care services for fertility as a qualifying reason for state and county employees to use pool time, subject to exhausting eligible leave.

agencies.name: state agency that employs the employee
agencies.explanation: The bill refers to the family leave pool of the employing state agency. The statutory definition identifies categories of state agencies, not specific agencies by name: executive-branch agencies created by constitution or statute, institutions of higher education, legislative agencies (excluding either house and its members), and specified courts or state judicial agencies.

HB169.summary: HB 169 would require political subdivisions to register for E-Verify and use it to verify all new employees; an employee responsible for verification would be subject to immediate termination for failing to comply. It would also bar a political subdivision from awarding a goods-or-services contract unless the contractor and any subcontractor register and participate in E-Verify, require their continued participation during the contract term, and require termination in specified noncompliance cases. Verification would not be required during any year the federal government has not funded E-Verify; these contract rules would apply only to contracts entered into on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Imposes E-Verify duties on political subdivisions and changes the conditions under which they may award and continue contracts.
Requires employment verification through the federal E-Verify program, identified in the bill as a program for employment authorization verification.
Makes contractor and subcontractor E-Verify participation a condition of receiving and retaining covered political-subdivision contracts.
Changes hiring-related verification requirements for political subdivisions and employees of contractors and subcontractors.

locations.name: Statewide political subdivisions
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to the defined types of political subdivisions, not to a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions, including counties, municipalities, school districts, junior college districts, and other special districts
affected_groups.explanation: Must register for E-Verify and verify information for all new employees; they also administer the contract requirements.

affected_groups.group: Contractors and subcontractors seeking or performing political-subdivision contracts
affected_groups.explanation: Must register and participate in E-Verify during covered contracts, subject to the federal-funding exception.

affected_groups.group: Political-subdivision employees responsible for verifying new hires
affected_groups.explanation: Are subject to immediate termination if they fail to comply with the verification requirement.

major_effects.label: E-Verify for political-subdivision hiring
major_effects.explanation: Political subdivisions must register and participate to verify information for all new employees.

major_effects.label: E-Verify as a contract condition
major_effects.explanation: For contracts entered into on or after the Act's effective date, contractors and subcontractors must participate for the subdivision to award the contract, and participation must continue during the contract. Verification is not required in a year when the federal government has not funded the program.

major_effects.label: Termination for noncompliance
major_effects.explanation: The subdivision must terminate a contract in specified contractor or subcontractor noncompliance cases, except where the federal-funding provision makes verification unnecessary; a responsible subdivision employee is subject to immediate termination for failing to comply with the hiring-verification duty.

HB170.summary: HB 170 would broaden the professionals whose written statements may be requested to verify a voluntarily reported condition or disability that may impede communication with a peace officer. It would require the vehicle-registration department to send the person’s registration information to the Department of Public Safety and identify whether the person has a speech or language impairment, a hearing impairment or deafness, or autism spectrum disorder.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes requirements tied to vehicle registration applications and registration information.
The bill requires sharing registration information with DPS along with specified indicators about a person’s health or disability.
The information-sharing change is intended to notify peace officers about conditions that may impede effective communication.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to vehicle registration applications and information under Texas law, rather than to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Vehicle registrants who voluntarily indicate a communication-impeding health condition or disability
affected_groups.explanation: Their registration information and specified condition indicators would be sent to DPS.

affected_groups.group: Health care and other listed professionals providing verification statements
affected_groups.explanation: The bill adds several professional types whose written statements may be requested to verify a condition or disability.

major_effects.label: Registration information and condition indicators sent to DPS
major_effects.explanation: The department must send registration information for each person who voluntarily indicates a communication-impeding condition and tell DPS whether the person has one of the specified conditions.

major_effects.label: Expanded verification options
major_effects.explanation: The department may request a written verification statement from a broader range of professionals, as appropriate for the person’s condition or disability.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The department has direct duties concerning verification and transmitting registration information, but the bill text does not name it or supply a definition establishing its canonical identity.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: DPS is the named recipient of vehicle registration information and the specified condition indicators.

HB171.summary: The bill directs the Texas Transportation Commission to designate Farm-to-Market Road 1021 in Dimmit, Maverick, and Webb Counties as part of the state highway system. This is a proposed change; it does not itself specify additional funding or road improvements.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the highway-system designation of a specified road.

locations.name: Dimmit, Maverick, and Webb Counties
locations.explanation: The specified road is located in these counties.

affected_groups.group: Users of Farm-to-Market Road 1021
affected_groups.explanation: The road's designation in the state highway system is directly relevant to people who use it.

major_effects.label: State highway-system designation
major_effects.explanation: Directs the Commission to designate the specified farm-to-market road as part of the state highway system.

agencies.name: Texas Transportation Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the designation duty to the Texas Transportation Commission. Transportation Code Section 201.001 separately defines the Commission as the Texas Transportation Commission and the Department as the Texas Department of Transportation; therefore, the Commission should not be mapped to the Department’s registry entry.

HB172.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, the bill would require each school district to provide tampons and sanitary napkins free of charge in every restroom designated for female students at each campus. Districts could accept donations of clean and safe products for this purpose.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a required school-campus provision of menstrual products for students.
Imposes a new duty on local school districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to each school district and each campus in the district.

affected_groups.group: Female students in public school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Would have free menstrual products available in restrooms designated for female students at each campus.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Would be required to provide the products and could accept qualifying donations.

major_effects.label: Free menstrual products at school
major_effects.explanation: Requires districts to make tampons and sanitary napkins available without charge in each restroom designated for female students at every campus.

HB173.summary: The bill would prohibit intentionally or knowingly transferring a semiautomatic rifle capable of accepting a detachable magazine and with a caliber greater than .22 to a person younger than 21, subject to exceptions for peace officers, certain current or former military members, and specified temporary loans. Such a transfer offense would be a state jail felony; the bill also narrows which transfers to children younger than 18 fall under the existing child-transfer provision.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill restricts transfers of specified semiautomatic rifles to people younger than 21, with listed exceptions.
The bill makes a violation of the new transfer restriction a state jail felony.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law without limiting the changes to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: People younger than 21 who may receive a qualifying semiautomatic rifle
affected_groups.explanation: Transfers to this group are prohibited unless an exception applies.

affected_groups.group: People who transfer qualifying semiautomatic rifles
affected_groups.explanation: A person who knowingly or intentionally makes a prohibited transfer may commit a state jail felony.

affected_groups.group: Peace officers and certain current or honorably discharged members of the United States armed forces
affected_groups.explanation: Transfers of qualifying rifles to these recipients are excepted from the new restriction.

major_effects.label: Restriction on transfers to people under 21
major_effects.explanation: Creates an offense for intentionally or knowingly transferring a qualifying semiautomatic rifle to a person younger than 21, except for the stated recipient and temporary-loan exceptions.

major_effects.label: State jail felony
major_effects.explanation: Classifies an offense under the new under-21 transfer provision as a state jail felony.

major_effects.label: Revised child-transfer provision
major_effects.explanation: Limits the under-18 provision to transfers of a club, location-restricted knife, or firearm other than a rifle covered by the new under-21 provision; the new provision separately covers those qualifying rifles.

HB174.summary: The bill would prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, and add military-veteran status, in public accommodations, employment, and specified housing and real-estate transactions; the public-accommodation rule excludes private clubs and establishments not open to the public. It would establish a Texas Workforce Commission complaint and alternative-dispute-resolution process, create civil-action routes and remedies, and allow commission-requested Attorney General actions with civil penalties for pattern-or-practice violations; existing veteran-preference programs are preserved.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds protected bases to nondiscrimination rules for public accommodations, employment, and housing.
Expands protections against discrimination in employment and related employment practices.
Expands fair-housing protections and changes a related Property Code offense.
Restricts discriminatory conduct by businesses and other entities offering goods, services, or facilities to the public.
Expands the nondiscrimination purposes of optional local commissions and limits when the state commission may refer certain complaints to a municipality.
Adds protected bases to an existing offense involving intentional intimidation or interference by force or threat of force in specified housing-related contexts.
Assigns the Texas Workforce Commission complaint, investigation, alternative-dispute-resolution, and enforcement responsibilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The public-accommodation prohibition applies to covered places throughout Texas.

affected_groups.group: People seeking equal treatment in public accommodations, employment, and housing, including people covered by the added sexual-orientation, gender-identity, and military-veteran protections
affected_groups.explanation: They gain protections against specified discriminatory practices, subject to the bill's exceptions and procedures.

affected_groups.group: Employers, employment agencies, labor organizations, and other covered employment entities
affected_groups.explanation: Their employment, referral, membership, and related practices become subject to additional nondiscrimination requirements.

affected_groups.group: Public-accommodation operators and housing or real-estate providers
affected_groups.explanation: Covered entities face expanded restrictions on discriminatory access, transactions, services, and related practices.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities and local commissions
affected_groups.explanation: Local commissions' stated nondiscrimination purposes are expanded, and municipalities' local protections affect referrals of certain complaints.

major_effects.label: Public-accommodation nondiscrimination
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits specified denials, discriminatory communications, and segregation in public accommodations on the listed protected bases. It does not cover private clubs or establishments not in fact open to the public.

major_effects.label: Employment nondiscrimination
major_effects.explanation: Adds sexual orientation, gender identity, and military-veteran status to several Labor Code employment protections. The changes preserve state and federal veteran-preference programs, including a related test-score preference exception.

major_effects.label: Housing and real-estate protections
major_effects.explanation: Adds sexual orientation, gender identity, and military-veteran status to specified fair-housing restrictions on dwelling sales and rentals, notices, inspections, and related real-estate practices.

major_effects.label: TWC complaint and dispute-resolution process
major_effects.explanation: Creates a commission office for alternative dispute resolution and assigns the commission complaint investigation and related administrative responsibilities.

major_effects.label: Civil enforcement and remedies
major_effects.explanation: Allows commission civil actions after the specified findings and unsuccessful conciliation, complainant civil actions, and commission-requested Attorney General actions for pattern-or-practice or public-importance cases. A civil penalty is authorized for a pattern-or-practice violation; complainants may also seek court-ordered relief and damages subject to the bill's limits.

major_effects.label: Limits on municipal complaint referrals
major_effects.explanation: The commission may not refer a housing-discrimination complaint to the municipality where the alleged discrimination occurred when it alleges one of the specified new bases and the municipality lacks a law prohibiting that alleged discrimination.

major_effects.label: Expanded housing-related intimidation offense
major_effects.explanation: Expands the protected bases covered by an existing offense, which still requires intentional intimidation or interference by force or threat of force in the specified housing-related circumstances.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the commission as the Texas Workforce Commission and assigns it complaint administration, investigation, alternative dispute resolution, and enforcement roles.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The commission may request that the Attorney General bring a district-court action in specified pattern-or-practice or public-importance cases, and the court may grant relief including a civil penalty for a pattern-or-practice violation.

HB175.summary: The bill would require a single common course numbering system for covered higher-education courses and require institutions to use those numbers in course listings and transfer guidelines. A student’s completed course in the system could transfer to another institution offering the same-numbered course and must be substituted for that institution’s course; specified course types are exempt. The system is to be approved by June 1, 2028, with full institutional compliance for covered courses offered in 2032–2033 or later and annual certifications beginning that academic year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes course numbering, transfer, and course-listing requirements for institutions of higher education.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The numbering and transfer requirements apply among institutions of higher education in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Students transferring completed courses between institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: Students completing a covered, numbered course may transfer it to another institution offering a course with the same number, where it must be substituted for the receiving institution’s course.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: Institutions must use applicable common numbers in course listings and transfer guidelines and certify course-identification information.

major_effects.label: Single common course numbering system
major_effects.explanation: Requires the board to approve one system for covered courses and institutions to use applicable numbers in transfer guidelines and course listings. The bill exempts specified course types.

major_effects.label: Transfer and substitution of covered courses
major_effects.explanation: A completed course included in the system may transfer to an institution offering the same-numbered course and must be substituted for the receiving institution’s course.

major_effects.label: Institutional certification and compliance review
major_effects.explanation: Institutions must annually certify course-numbering information and publish a transfer-guidelines web address; the board may recommend corrective action and identify noncompliant institutions in its next appropriations request.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the board duties to develop a transferability policy, approve the single numbering system, and review institutional compliance. The bill does not identify the board by a canonical name in the supplied text.

HB176.summary: The bill would add a rule for civil actions seeking damages for injury, death, or loss caused by a motor vehicle collision: a claimant who wins against a defendant unlawfully present in the United States at the time of the collision must receive three times the actual damages. It would apply only to causes of action accruing on or after its effective date; earlier-accruing causes would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: The enhanced civil damages rule depends on whether the defendant was unlawfully present in the United States at the time of the collision.

affected_groups.group: Claimants seeking damages for injury, death, or loss caused by a motor vehicle collision
affected_groups.explanation: Successful claimants may receive treble actual damages when the defendant meets the bill's unlawful-presence condition.

affected_groups.group: Defendants unlawfully present in the United States at the time of a motor vehicle collision
affected_groups.explanation: Defendants meeting this condition face a mandatory treble-damages award if the claimant successfully asserts a covered claim against them.

major_effects.label: Treble civil damages
major_effects.explanation: Requires an award of three times actual damages to a successful claimant in a covered motor-vehicle-collision action when the defendant was unlawfully present in the United States at the time of the collision.

agencies.name: a court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly directs the court adjudicating a qualifying civil action to award treble actual damages, but does not identify which courts or establish that the referenced court is a Texas state body.

HB177.summary: The bill would limit pretrial jail detention for defendants charged with a Class B misdemeanor or higher when the detention period, accounting for the maximum sentence credit they could earn in county jail, would exceed the offense’s maximum confinement term. The limit would not apply to defendants undergoing competency evaluation or subject to a Chapter 46B commitment order, and it would apply only to people arrested on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the limit on how long certain accused defendants may be detained in jail pending trial.
The detention limit affects county jail operations and the counties in which the offenses occurred.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas criminal procedure and applies to qualifying arrests statewide.

affected_groups.group: Defendants charged with a Class B misdemeanor or higher
affected_groups.explanation: Their cumulative pretrial detention may not exceed the offense’s maximum confinement term when accounting for the maximum sentence credit they would be entitled to earn for conduct while confined in the county jail. The article does not apply during competency evaluation or when the defendant is subject to a Chapter 46B commitment order.

affected_groups.group: County governments and county jail operators
affected_groups.explanation: The bill limits detention in county jails for covered defendants.

major_effects.label: Limit on pretrial detention
major_effects.explanation: Bars continued jail detention when the cumulative period, accounting for maximum sentence credit the defendant could earn, would exceed the maximum confinement term for the charged offense; this article does not apply to a defendant being evaluated for competency or subject to an order of commitment issued under Chapter 46B.

HB178.summary: The bill would raise the Foundation School Program basic allotment formula from $6,160 to $7,500. Beginning with the 2028–2029 school year, the allotment would also increase annually based on the inflation rate determined by the comptroller.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the Foundation School Program basic allotment for school districts.
Raises the state-program allotment amount districts are entitled to receive and indexes it to inflation.
Changes funding for local school districts through their basic allotments.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The allotment formula applies to school districts under the statewide Foundation School Program.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts receive the increased basic allotment and annual inflation adjustment.

major_effects.label: Increase in the basic allotment
major_effects.explanation: Raises the base amount in the allotment formula from $6,160 to $7,500.

major_effects.label: Annual inflation adjustment
major_effects.explanation: Starting with the 2028–2029 school year, increases the basic allotment annually by the amount calculated using the inflation rate determined by the comptroller.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The inflation adjustment uses a rate determined by the comptroller, giving the office a direct role in the new allotment calculation.

HB179.summary: The bill would give state employees up to 20 hours of paid leave per fiscal year for prenatal care and require state agencies to provide lactating employees needed time off without a deduction in salary or accrued leave, through the third anniversary of childbirth or reproductive loss. It would also require covered employers with at least five employees to provide eligible employees time off after specified reproductive losses; the leave would be unpaid unless the employee uses accrued paid leave. The bill would protect employee confidentiality, prohibit retaliation, make violations an unlawful employment practice, and direct the Texas Workforce Commission to offer an optional certification form.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates leave entitlements for state employees and qualifying employees of covered employers, with related employer duties and protections.
Prohibits retaliation for exercising the new leave right and makes violations an unlawful employment practice.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply across state government and to employers covered by the Texas Labor Code; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: State employees receiving prenatal care
affected_groups.explanation: Employees in the executive, judicial, or legislative branch would receive up to 20 hours of paid prenatal-care leave per state fiscal year.

affected_groups.group: Lactating employees of state agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive needed time off to express breast milk without losing salary or accrued leave, until the specified third anniversary.

affected_groups.group: Employees who meet the reproductive-loss leave eligibility criteria
affected_groups.explanation: Employees of covered employers who meet the service and prospective-parent criteria would be eligible for leave after specified reproductive losses.

affected_groups.group: Employers with five or more employees
affected_groups.explanation: Covered employers, including public employers but excluding federal agencies, would have new leave, notice, confidentiality, and nonretaliation duties.

major_effects.label: Paid prenatal-care leave
major_effects.explanation: State employees in the executive, judicial, or legislative branch would be entitled to paid leave for prenatal care, capped at 20 hours per state fiscal year.

major_effects.label: Time off for lactating state-agency employees
major_effects.explanation: Agencies would provide sufficient time off to express breast milk without a salary or accrued-leave deduction, through the third anniversary of childbirth or reproductive loss.

major_effects.label: Leave following reproductive loss
major_effects.explanation: Eligible employees of covered employers would receive five days off within the three-month period after a specified loss. The leave is unpaid unless the employee elects to use accrued paid leave, and multiple losses are subject to a 20-workday limit in a 12-month period.

major_effects.label: Employer safeguards and anti-retaliation duties
major_effects.explanation: Employers would have to maintain confidentiality of the fact that an employee requested or took time off and related records, except to the extent disclosure is requested or consented to in writing by the employee. Employers would also have to notify employees of the leave right and refrain from retaliation; violations would be unlawful employment practices. Employees cannot be required to disclose the cause of a loss or provide related documentation.

major_effects.label: Optional certification form
major_effects.explanation: The Texas Workforce Commission would create and make available a form employees may use for certification; employees would not be required to use it.

agencies.name: state agencies
agencies.explanation: Government Code § 661.001(4) defines “state agency” to include a constitutionally or statutorily created executive-branch board, commission, department, or other agency; an institution of higher education defined by Education Code § 61.003; a legislative agency, excluding either house and individual legislators; and the supreme court, Court of Criminal Appeals, a court of appeals, or a state judicial agency. The bill requires each state agency to provide the specified time off to its agency||||

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: Must create and make available an optional employee certification form.

HB181.summary: HB 181 would set mandatory terms for county contracts to confine prisoners in out-of-state correctional facilities, including Commission-established standards, release in the sending county, inspections, and limits on transferring prisoners with specified violence or escape histories unless the Commission grants a waiver. Contracts would also have to ensure appropriate care for prisoners identified through specified continuity-of-care searches unless waived, and would require Commission approval before execution; an unapproved contract would be void. The bill would require incident notifications, county investigations and reports, and permit counties to terminate contracts on 90 days' notice, including when directed by the Commission.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes standards and transfer conditions for county prisoners confined in out-of-state correctional facilities.
It imposes contracting, inspection, investigation, and reporting duties on counties.

locations.name: Out-of-state correctional facilities
locations.explanation: The bill applies to covered contracts for confinement in correctional facilities located in another state.

affected_groups.group: County governments
affected_groups.explanation: Counties entering covered contracts must submit them for approval and take on inspection, investigation, and reporting duties.

affected_groups.group: County prisoners transferred to out-of-state facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Their transfer eligibility, care, and release location would be subject to new contract conditions; matched prisoners must receive appropriate care unless the commission grants a specific waiver.

affected_groups.group: Receiving entities and out-of-state correctional facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Covered facilities and receiving entities would be subject to standards and incident-notification terms in the contract.

major_effects.label: Commission contract oversight
major_effects.explanation: Counties must submit covered contracts for Commission review and approval before entering them; a contract not approved is void, and the Commission must adopt implementing rules.

major_effects.label: Limits on prisoner transfers
major_effects.explanation: Prisoners with specified records of violence or escape are ineligible for transfer unless the Commission grants a specific waiver.

major_effects.label: Care for identified prisoners
major_effects.explanation: Contracts must provide appropriate care for prisoners identified as an exact or probable match through the specified continuity-of-care search, unless the Commission grants a specific waiver.

major_effects.label: Facility inspections and incident reporting
major_effects.explanation: Sending entities must inspect receiving facilities and provide reports; receiving entities must notify sending entities of major incidents, and counties must investigate and report specified incidents to the Commission.

major_effects.label: Contract conditions and termination
major_effects.explanation: Contracts must provide for release within the sending county, and the sending county may terminate a contract with 90 days' notice, including when directed by the Commission.

agencies.name: Commission on Jail Standards
agencies.explanation: The Commission must review and approve covered contracts and adopt rules to implement the new requirements. Its name is stated in the bill, but the supplied canonical registry does not include a matching entry.

HB182.summary: HB 182 would redefine “closing” for certain private activity bonds as delivery in exchange for required payment, rather than issuance and delivery. For a qualified residential rental project bond, a partial payment of at least 10% for incremental funding would also count as a closing; delivery would still not count when spending the bond proceeds is conditioned on obtaining credit enhancement.

policy_tags.explanation: The revised closing definition specifically covers incremental funding of qualified residential rental project bonds.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Texas Government Code with statewide application.

affected_groups.group: Issuers of private activity bonds for qualified residential rental projects
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes when delivery of these bonds constitutes a closing, including for qualifying incremental funding.

major_effects.label: Revised bond-closing definition
major_effects.explanation: Defines closing by delivery in exchange for required payment and includes qualifying partial payments of at least 10% for incremental funding of a qualified residential rental project bond; the existing credit-enhancement exclusion remains.

HB183.summary: HB 183 would let a court, on the state’s attorney’s motion, reduce an eligible incarcerated person’s sentence—including below the statutory minimum or to time served—based on rehabilitation, risk, or changed circumstances; specified Article 42A.054 offenses are excluded, and sentences may not be increased. It would add victim notice and objection-related protections for commutation proceedings and delete the express Family Code §71.004 cross-reference from an existing victim continuance provision. The Act would have effect only if voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment authorizing judicial commutations; otherwise, it has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a judicial process for reducing certain prison sentences and changes procedural rights for victims in criminal cases.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The new criminal procedure applies across Texas, with a motion filed in a district court in the county of conviction.

affected_groups.group: Inmates serving terms of imprisonment for offenses not excluded by Article 42A.054
affected_groups.explanation: A state attorney may seek a sentence reduction for an eligible inmate under the new chapter.

affected_groups.group: Victims, guardians of victims, and close relatives of deceased victims
affected_groups.explanation: They receive new commutation-related information rights; a victim who opposes a motion may have the objection conveyed to the court. The bill also amends a continuance-related victim provision.

affected_groups.group: Attorneys representing the state
affected_groups.explanation: They may file commutation motions and must inform the court of a victim's objections when notified of them.

major_effects.label: Judicial commutation authority
major_effects.explanation: On a state attorney’s motion, a court may reduce an eligible inmate’s sentence, including below the statutory minimum or to time served; specified Article 42A.054 offenses are excluded, and a sentence may not be increased.

major_effects.label: Victim rights in commutation and continuance proceedings
major_effects.explanation: Victims gain rights to notice of commutation motions, hearings, and orders, and a prosecutor must relay a victim's opposition to the court. The bill also deletes the express Family Code definition cross-reference in an existing continuance-related victim provision; whether that changes the reach of the “family violence” condition is uncertain.

agencies.name: District court
agencies.explanation: The bill gives a district court authority to decide commutation motions. The bill uses a generic court designation and does not identify a specific canonical judicial body.

agencies.name: Presiding judge of the administrative judicial region
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the presiding judge a role in assigning the commutation motion to a district court; it does not identify a specific canonical judicial body.

HB184.summary: The bill would bar the Public Utility Commission of Texas from approving construction of a 765-kilovolt transmission line until it first studies line performance, estimated ratepayer costs, cost overruns, and supply-chain and workforce limitations. The commission would then have to submit the study results to an independent third party, with an exclusion for certain parties that conducted similar studies; the section would expire September 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the commission's process for approving construction of 765-kilovolt electric transmission lines.

locations.name: Permian Basin
locations.explanation: The specified Permian Basin Reliability Plan project is expressly included, although the approval condition also applies to other 765-kilovolt lines.

locations.name: ERCOT power region
locations.explanation: The bill references a transmission plan submitted for this region; the provision is not limited to projects there.

affected_groups.group: Proponents of 765-kilovolt transmission lines
affected_groups.explanation: Their construction proposals would be subject to a study requirement before commission approval.

affected_groups.group: Residential electric customers and other ratepayers
affected_groups.explanation: The required study must consider estimated costs to ratepayers, with particular emphasis on residential customers; the bill does not itself change rates.

major_effects.label: Study required before line approval
major_effects.explanation: The commission may not approve construction of a 765-kilovolt transmission line unless it first conducts the specified study.

major_effects.label: Study and independent review
major_effects.explanation: The commission must examine line performance, costs, cost overruns, and supply-chain and workforce constraints, then submit the results to an eligible independent third party for review.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The commission must conduct the study before approving a covered line and submit its results for independent review, subject to the restriction against submitting them to certain third parties that conducted similar studies after January 1, 2020.

HB185.summary: The bill would prohibit courts from requiring a party or child to participate in a service or intervention related to family violence or child abuse or neglect unless it is evidence-based and generally accepted proof supports its effectiveness, therapeutic value, and physical and psychological safety. It would also allow a counselor’s relevant training to include child abuse or neglect, require evidence-based judicial instruction on evaluating these services, and direct the Supreme Court of Texas and Texas Court of Criminal Appeals to adopt necessary training rules.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes standards for court-required services and interventions addressing family violence and child abuse or neglect.
Changes judicial instruction requirements and directs two Texas courts to adopt rules for the required training.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to covered suits pending in a trial court on the effective date or filed afterward.

affected_groups.group: Parties and children in suits affecting the parent-child relationship
affected_groups.explanation: Courts may require participation in a covered service or intervention only if the bill's applicable conditions are met, including that the service or intervention is evidence-based.

affected_groups.group: Mental health professionals providing court-ordered counseling
affected_groups.explanation: Their relevant training for counseling may include training in child abuse or neglect when the court finds it relevant to the counseling needed.

affected_groups.group: Texas judges and judicial officers receiving the required instruction
affected_groups.explanation: The bill adds evidence-based instruction and methods for assessing covered services and interventions.

major_effects.label: Limits court-ordered services and interventions
major_effects.explanation: A court may not require a party or child to participate in a covered service or intervention unless it is evidence-based and generally accepted proof supports its effectiveness, therapeutic value, and physical and psychological safety.

major_effects.label: Adds relevant child-abuse training to counseling qualifications
major_effects.explanation: For counseling ordered in cases involving conflict over conservatorship or possession or access, the professional's training may address child abuse or neglect if the court determines that training is relevant to the counseling needed.

major_effects.label: Requires evidence-based judicial instruction and implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The instruction must be evidence-based and cover methods for evaluating the validity and safety of covered services; the Supreme Court of Texas and Texas Court of Criminal Appeals must adopt rules necessary to provide their respective required training.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Supreme Court of Texas must adopt rules for the training required under Section 22.011, Government Code; the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals must do so for the training under Section 22.110.

HB186.summary: HB 186 would bar deferred adjudication for improper relationship between educator and student and set a 10-year minimum term of imprisonment; if community supervision is granted, the court must require at least 10 years of imprisonment in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice. It would make a conviction or adjudication for the offense reportable for sex-offender registration and prevent parole or mandatory supervision before 10 actual years have been served, with mandatory supervision still subject to other eligibility requirements. These changes would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes deferred-adjudication eligibility, imprisonment terms, release eligibility, and sex-offender registration for this offense.
The bill adds the offense to the list of reportable convictions or adjudications for sex-offender registration.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas criminal laws and makes the changes applicable to qualifying offenses committed on or after the effective date.

affected_groups.group: People charged with or convicted of improper relationship between educator and student
affected_groups.explanation: They would face restricted deferred-adjudication eligibility and increased imprisonment requirements; conviction or adjudication would also trigger reportable-conviction status.

affected_groups.group: Inmates serving a sentence for the offense
affected_groups.explanation: They would not be eligible for parole or mandatory supervision before serving at least 10 actual calendar years, subject to the separate mandatory-supervision eligibility condition.

major_effects.label: Minimum imprisonment term
major_effects.explanation: The offense would carry a 10-year minimum term of imprisonment. If community supervision is granted, the court must require at least 10 years of imprisonment in TDCJ.

major_effects.label: Deferred adjudication
major_effects.explanation: A defendant charged with the offense would be added to the categories for which a judge may not grant deferred adjudication.

major_effects.label: Sex-offender registration
major_effects.explanation: A conviction or adjudication for the offense would be included among reportable convictions or adjudications.

major_effects.label: Parole and mandatory supervision
major_effects.explanation: Parole release is barred until 10 actual calendar years have been served, without good-conduct-time credit. Mandatory supervision is barred unless the inmate has served at least 10 actual calendar years without good-conduct-time credit; other eligibility requirements also apply.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: A court granting community supervision must require the defendant to serve at least 10 years of imprisonment in TDCJ.

agencies.name: Court granting community supervision
agencies.explanation: The bill directs a court granting community supervision for the offense to require a term of imprisonment. The bill does not name a specific court.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: Adding the offense to the reportable-conviction list affects the sex-offender registration system; DPS's operational role is not specified in the bill.

HB187.summary: HB187 would require the comptroller to establish and administer a grant program providing economic-development assistance to qualified small municipalities. A municipality qualifies if it has 10,000 or fewer residents and lost at least 15 percent of its total revenue in the preceding municipal fiscal year because private-sector contracts were reduced or terminated; grants may support economic-development programs or job-creating projects, and municipalities may not apply before January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a grant program for qualifying municipalities and limits their use of grant funds.
Authorizes grants using money appropriated to the comptroller or other available funds.
Provides municipal grants for economic-development programs and projects to create or promote jobs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The program is established to support small municipalities throughout Texas.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities with 10,000 or fewer residents that meet the revenue-loss criterion
affected_groups.explanation: These municipalities may apply for grants, subject to the program's eligibility requirements and application restriction.

major_effects.label: Municipal revenue recovery grant program
major_effects.explanation: Requires the comptroller to establish and administer a program offering economic-development assistance to qualifying municipalities.

major_effects.label: Grants for economic development
major_effects.explanation: Allows grants from appropriated or other available money, with separate amounts for programs and qualifying job-creating projects.

major_effects.label: Qualified municipality criteria and application start
major_effects.explanation: Defines eligible municipalities by population and revenue loss linked to reduced or terminated private-sector contracts; applications are barred before January 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: Program rules and grant oversight
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules for applications, deadlines, monitoring grant disbursements, and returning funds used for unauthorized purposes.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The comptroller is assigned to establish and administer the grant program, award grants, and adopt implementing rules.

HB188.summary: HB 188 would prohibit, with criminal negligence, selling or providing a hookah for retail use to someone under 21, or supplying one to someone who intends to deliver it to an under-21 individual; the bill provides a proof-of-age defense and a limited military-identification exception for certain sales. The offense would be a Class C misdemeanor, and retailers would have to check identification for customers younger than 30 and adequately train and supervise employees to prevent violations.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates sales and customer-identification requirements for hookah retailers and requires retailer owners to train and supervise staff.
Creates a criminal offense and assigns it a misdemeanor classification.
Restricts hookah distribution to people under 21, including certain supplies intended for delivery to them.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds a chapter to the Texas Health and Safety Code, establishing generally applicable state law.

affected_groups.group: Individuals younger than 21
affected_groups.explanation: The bill restricts hookah sales and provision for use involving under-21 individuals, with a limited exception for certain 18-or-older purchasers presenting military identification in the retail-use circumstance.

affected_groups.group: Hookah retailers and their employees and agents
affected_groups.explanation: A person may not sell, give, or provide a hookah to someone younger than 30 unless that person presents apparently valid proof of identification. Retailer owners must adequately supervise and train employees and agents to prevent a violation. If an offense under the section occurs in connection with a sale by an employee or agent of a retailer that sells hookahs at retail or provides hookahs for customer use on-site, that employee or agent is criminally responsible and subject to prosecution.

major_effects.label: New criminal offense for specified hookah distribution to under-21 individuals
major_effects.explanation: A person acting with criminal negligence commits an offense for specified sales or provision to an under-21 individual, or for supplying a hookah to someone intending to deliver it to an under-21 individual. The offense is a Class C misdemeanor; the bill includes a proof-of-age defense and a limited military-identification exception for subsection (a)(1).

major_effects.label: Identification checks and retailer staff training
major_effects.explanation: A retailer may not sell, give, or provide a hookah for retail use to an individual younger than 30 unless the individual presents apparently valid identification; the retailer's owner must adequately train and supervise employees and agents to prevent violations.

HB189.summary: For covered applications filed on or after January 1, 2028, the bill would require groundwater-supplied subdivision plats, subject to the existing exception, to include a certification that complies with TCEQ rules on its form and content and on credible evidence of groundwater availability. Municipal authorities and county commissioners courts would have to disapprove applications that do not meet the section’s requirements. A commissioners court in a priority groundwater management area may adopt water-availability requirements where platting is required if it determines they are necessary to prevent current or projected county water use from exceeding the safe sustainable yield, notwithstanding Section 232.001(h), Local Government Code.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes groundwater-availability certification rules and county authority to impose water-availability requirements under a safe-sustainable-yield condition.
It assigns plat-disapproval duties to municipal authorities and commissioners courts and addresses county water-availability requirements.
The bill changes requirements for subdivision plats, which govern subdivision of land.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The plat requirements apply generally under the cited Local Government Code provisions, with no locality limitation stated.

locations.name: Priority groundwater management areas
locations.explanation: The additional county water-availability authority applies to a county in a priority groundwater management area.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for groundwater-supplied subdivision plats, except as provided by Subsection (a-1)
affected_groups.explanation: Their applications must include a groundwater-availability certification complying with TCEQ rules, subject to the existing exception.

affected_groups.group: Municipal authorities and county commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: They must disapprove noncompliant plat applications; qualifying county commissioners courts may also adopt water-availability requirements.

affected_groups.group: Licensed engineers and geoscientists preparing groundwater certifications
affected_groups.explanation: The required statement must be prepared by a licensed engineer or geoscientist and comply with TCEQ rules.

major_effects.label: Groundwater certification requirements for plats
major_effects.explanation: Covered groundwater-supplied subdivision applications must include a certification meeting TCEQ rules, subject to the existing statutory exception.

major_effects.label: TCEQ groundwater-certification rules
major_effects.explanation: TCEQ must establish certification form and content and define credible evidence of groundwater availability.

major_effects.label: Required disapproval of noncompliant plats
major_effects.explanation: Municipal authorities and county commissioners courts must disapprove applications that fail to comply with the applicable section.

major_effects.label: County water-availability requirements in priority groundwater management areas
major_effects.explanation: A county commissioners court may adopt requirements in an area where platting is required if it determines they are necessary to prevent current or projected county water use from exceeding safe sustainable yield; the provision applies notwithstanding Section 232.001(h), Local Government Code.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill directs TCEQ to adopt rules governing certification form and content and credible evidence of groundwater availability.

HB190.summary: The bill would make certain vehicle burglaries state jail felonies, including offenses involving firearm-related conduct or multiple vehicles connected by the same transaction or course of conduct. The changes would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands the circumstances in which burglary of a vehicle is punishable as a state jail felony.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a Texas Penal Code provision applicable statewide.

affected_groups.group: People who commit burglary of a vehicle in the specified circumstances
affected_groups.explanation: They may face state jail felony punishment when the offense involves a rail car, firearm possession or theft, use of a stolen vehicle, or multiple vehicles connected by the same transaction or course of conduct.

major_effects.label: Expanded state-jail-felony circumstances for vehicle burglary
major_effects.explanation: Adds state jail felony grounds involving a rail car, possessing or stealing a firearm during the offense, using a stolen vehicle to facilitate it, or committing the offense with respect to two or more vehicles linked by the same transaction or course of conduct.

HB191.summary: HB191 would shift appointment of Public Utilities Commission commissioners from the governor with Senate consent to a committee, shorten their staggered terms from six years to five, and extend the post-service restriction on registered lobbying before the commission from one year to three. It also creates a three-member committee to select eligible commission members and designate the commission chair and vice chair; the appointment provision calls the appointing body the “Public Utilities Commission Appointment Committee,” while the new section names the created body the “Public Utilities Commission Selection Committee.”

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the appointment and terms of commissioners of the Public Utilities Commission.
The bill changes commissioner appointment and terms, creates a selection committee, and extends a post-service lobbying restriction.
Members of the newly created committee are entitled to reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses incurred in official duties.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The committee's membership is limited to residents of the state, and the bill governs the statewide commission.

affected_groups.group: Public Utilities Commission commissioners and prospective commissioners
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes the appointment process and shortens commissioner terms.

affected_groups.group: Former Public Utilities Commission commissioners
affected_groups.explanation: They would face a longer restriction on registered lobbying activities before the commission after leaving office.

affected_groups.group: Members of the selection committee
affected_groups.explanation: A person may be appointed as a selection committee member only if the person is a resident of this state; members receive no compensation for serving but are entitled to reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses incurred in performing official duties.

major_effects.label: Commissioner appointing authority
major_effects.explanation: The bill replaces appointment by the governor with Senate advice and consent with appointment by a committee. The amended appointment provision and the new committee section use different names for the committee.

major_effects.label: Commissioner terms shortened
major_effects.explanation: Commissioners would serve staggered five-year rather than six-year terms.

major_effects.label: Commission selection committee
major_effects.explanation: A three-member committee appointed by the governor, lieutenant governor, and House speaker is created to select eligible commission members and designate the commission chair and vice chair.

major_effects.label: Committee expense reimbursement
major_effects.explanation: Committee members are not compensated for service but are entitled to reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses incurred in official duties.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the appointment process for Public Utility Commission commissioners by assigning appointments to a Public Utilities Commission Appointment Committee, and changes the restriction on former commissioners’ registered lobbying activities before the commission.

agencies.name: Public Utilities Commission Selection Committee
agencies.explanation: The bill creates this committee and assigns it commissioner-selection and leadership-designation duties. Its relationship to the differently named appointing body in Section 12.051 is unclear.

HB192.summary: The bill would authorize commissioners courts in counties meeting one of four population or geographic criteria to regulate roadside and parking-lot vending, vendor structures, and solicitation of money. The authority would apply only in the county’s unincorporated area and only when the activity occurs on a public highway or road, its right-of-way, or in a parking lot.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes which counties’ commissioners courts may regulate specified activities by order.
The bill authorizes county regulation of vendors’ sales and structures, as well as solicitation of money, in specified locations.
The county regulatory authority is expressly granted to promote public safety.

locations.name: Unincorporated areas of counties meeting the bill's population or geographic criteria
locations.explanation: The regulatory authority is limited to qualifying counties and their unincorporated areas.

locations.name: Interstate Highway 69 and Sam Houston National Forest
locations.explanation: The bill uses a county’s containing a portion of either geographic feature as part of two county-eligibility criteria.

affected_groups.group: Commissioners courts of qualifying counties
affected_groups.explanation: These county governing bodies would gain authority to regulate the specified activities by order.

affected_groups.group: Roadside and parking-lot vendors
affected_groups.explanation: Vendors of food or merchandise, including live-animal vendors, could be subject to county regulation of sales and structures in the specified areas.

affected_groups.group: People soliciting money in the specified areas
affected_groups.explanation: Their solicitation activity could be regulated by qualifying counties.

major_effects.label: County authority to regulate vendors and solicitors
major_effects.explanation: Qualifying counties may regulate sales, vendor structures, and solicitation by order, subject to the bill’s geographic and activity limits.

HB193.summary: HB 193 would require educational entities and private schools, during investigations of specified alleged misconduct against a student, to provide a parent or guardian an advocate and updates, offer safety and supportive measures, and take steps to minimize trauma. It would also expand parent notifications about services and the alleged employee’s work status, and allow a related absence to be excused through the investigation or the end of the school year in which the incident occurred, whichever is later; the changes apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes student supports, school notifications, and excused-absence rules related to alleged school misconduct.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to covered educational entities and private schools under Texas law, rather than a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Students alleging they experienced specified misconduct
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive investigation-time support options and could have a related absence excused for the specified period.

affected_groups.group: Parents and guardians of affected students
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive an advocate or liaison, investigation updates, and additional notices about services and the alleged person's work status.

affected_groups.group: Educational entities and private schools
affected_groups.explanation: They would have new investigation-time support, safety, trauma-minimization, and notification duties.

major_effects.label: Investigation-time student supports
major_effects.explanation: Covered entities and private schools would provide a designated advocate or liaison, make appropriate safety and supportive measures available—including specified at-home or protective on-campus arrangements—and pursue measures to minimize trauma. The advocate must meet a listed qualification or serve in a position designated by commissioner rule.

major_effects.label: Additional parent notifications
major_effects.explanation: Policies must notify parents or guardians that specified services are available and disclose whether the alleged person was placed on leave or moved away from direct student contact, including whether that status later ended.

major_effects.label: Excused absence for a related incident
major_effects.explanation: A school district must excuse an absence relating to the alleged incident during the investigation or the school year in which it occurred, whichever ends later.

agencies.name: commissioner
