agencies.explanation: The bill allows an advocate or liaison to be in a position designated by commissioner rule, implicating an education-related rulemaking role; the supplied text does not identify the commissioner or establish the agency identity.

HB194.summary: The bill requires the Texas Water Development Board to study water resources in counties within Regional Water Planning Area M, including groundwater conditions, projected production, funding mechanisms, and existing water programs. The Board must submit its findings to legislative committees with primary jurisdiction over water development by September 1, 2028, and make the report available to the public.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires a regional study of water resources, groundwater conditions, and water management.
The bill assigns the Texas Water Development Board a new study and reporting duty.

locations.name: Counties located in Regional Water Planning Area M
locations.explanation: The study applies to counties within the regional planning area designated by the Texas Water Development Board.

affected_groups.group: State policymakers and agency leadership
affected_groups.explanation: The study is intended to support their water-resource management, resource-allocation, and contracting decisions.

affected_groups.group: Members of the public seeking water-resource information
affected_groups.explanation: The Board must make the study report available to the public.

major_effects.label: Regional water-resource study
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Board to assess water resources in Regional Water Planning Area M counties, including groundwater conditions, projected production, funding mechanisms, and existing state-funded programs.

major_effects.label: Legislative and public report
major_effects.explanation: Requires submission of study findings to the specified legislative committees and public availability of the report.

agencies.name: Texas Water Development Board
agencies.explanation: The Act defines “board” as the Texas Water Development Board and assigns it the study and report duties.

HB195.summary: The bill requires the commission to implement express-lane eligibility processes for CHIP and Medicaid, using findings from designated public-assistance agencies and applicant data; these processes cover CHIP reenrollment and Medicaid recertification. It requires automatic enrollment of people found eligible through the express-lane processes and revises related income-verification and child Medicaid recertification procedures. If an agency determines a federal waiver or authorization is necessary for a provision, it must request it and may delay implementing that provision until it is granted.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility determination and enrollment procedures for the child health plan and medical assistance programs.
Creates an express-lane option for medical assistance eligibility and recertification and requires automatic enrollment for people found eligible through it.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes concern Texas state public-assistance and health-coverage programs, without identifying a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Children applying for or reenrolling in CHIP
affected_groups.explanation: Children found eligible through express-lane determinations must be automatically enrolled; the option also covers eligibility for reenrollment.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid applicants and beneficiaries subject to recertification
affected_groups.explanation: The express-lane process may be used to determine medical-assistance eligibility, including recertification, and people found eligible through it must be automatically enrolled.

major_effects.label: Express-lane eligibility determinations
major_effects.explanation: The commission must implement express-lane options and use applicant data from other public-assistance programs to assess CHIP and medical-assistance eligibility; the provisions also cover CHIP reenrollment and Medicaid recertification.

major_effects.label: Automatic enrollment
major_effects.explanation: A child or person determined eligible under the applicable express-lane section must be automatically enrolled in CHIP or medical assistance, respectively.

major_effects.label: Verification and recertification procedures
major_effects.explanation: The bill permits express-lane verification, provides an income-verification exception when reported household income exceeds the CHIP income limit, and adds an express-lane-related exception to telephone or mail recertification reviews for children receiving medical assistance.

major_effects.label: Conditional federal waiver process
major_effects.explanation: If a state agency determines before implementation that a federal waiver or authorization is necessary for a provision, it must request it and may delay implementing that provision until granted.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the commission express-lane implementation, eligibility assessment, and automatic-enrollment duties. The supplied text does not state the commission's full identity, so no canonical registry ID is assigned.

HB196.summary: HB 196 would require research facilities to offer eligible retired research dogs and cats for adoption through an animal rehoming organization or shelter, or to an individual through an arrangement with the facility. The requirement would not apply when the facility’s attending veterinarian determines an animal is unsuitable for rehoming, including because of a substantial medical condition that prevents successful integration into an adoptive home; the bill also provides specified civil-liability immunity for qualifying transfers.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill imposes adoption-offer and transfer-agreement requirements on covered research facilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes a generally applicable Texas statutory requirement for covered research facilities, rather than limiting it to a named place or defined area.

affected_groups.group: Research facilities using dogs or cats for experiments
affected_groups.explanation: Covered facilities must offer eligible retired animals for adoption and meet the bill’s transfer conditions.

affected_groups.group: Animal rehoming organizations and animal shelters
affected_groups.explanation: These organizations may receive retired animals through the adoption pathway, subject to a written agreement with the facility.

affected_groups.group: Individuals adopting retired research animals
affected_groups.explanation: A facility may offer a retired animal to an individual through an arrangement between them.

major_effects.label: Adoption offer for eligible retired animals
major_effects.explanation: Facilities must offer eligible retired dogs and cats through a rehoming organization or shelter, or by an arrangement with an individual; animals deemed unsuitable for rehoming are excluded.

major_effects.label: Transfer conditions and facility guidelines
major_effects.explanation: A research facility may not offer a retired animal to an animal rehoming organization or shelter unless it has entered into a written agreement addressing the transfer. Facilities may establish guidelines for determining whether an animal may be transferred and must post any adopted guidelines online.

major_effects.label: Limited civil-liability immunity
major_effects.explanation: A facility acting in good faith and complying with the chapter and its rules receives immunity for claims based on specified transfers or adoptions.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The HHSC executive commissioner is authorized, but not required, to adopt rules to implement the chapter.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the executive commissioner as the HHSC executive commissioner and authorizes that official to adopt implementing rules.

HB197.summary: The bill would allow a municipality, by ordinance, to establish rent control for people age 75 or older. It also specifies that the existing continuation or discontinuation procedure applies to rent control established under subsection (a), not expressly to the new authority in subsection (a-1).

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes municipal authority to regulate rents for a specified group of renters.
The bill grants municipalities authority to establish rent control by ordinance.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies to municipalities as a general category and does not name a particular place.

affected_groups.group: People age 75 or older who rent housing
affected_groups.explanation: Municipalities could establish rent control for this age group.

affected_groups.group: Municipal governing bodies
affected_groups.explanation: The bill grants them authority to establish rent control by ordinance.

affected_groups.group: Owners of rental housing
affected_groups.explanation: They may be affected if a municipality exercises the new authority.

major_effects.label: Municipal rent-control authority
major_effects.explanation: A municipality could establish rent control by ordinance for people age 75 or older.

major_effects.label: Scope of continuation procedure
major_effects.explanation: The bill specifies that subsection (b)'s continuation or discontinuation procedure covers rent control established under subsection (a).

HB198.summary: HB 198 would require each state agency to report grants it anticipates awarding in the next state fiscal year and update that report at least quarterly. The Comptroller would compile the submissions into a PDF organized by grant purpose, send it to legislative leaders and members, and update it quarterly; the Comptroller could adopt submission rules. For the initial cycle, agencies’ reports are due July 20, 2027, if the bill receives the vote for immediate effect; the Comptroller’s report is due September 20, 2027, either way, and without that vote the Comptroller may rely only on information then known.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a state-agency grant reporting process and requires the Comptroller to compile and update a report for the Legislature.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The reporting process applies to state agencies and the Comptroller, rather than to a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: State agencies that anticipate awarding grants
affected_groups.explanation: They must report anticipated grants and submit periodic updates.

affected_groups.group: Texas legislators
affected_groups.explanation: The Comptroller’s compiled report is submitted to legislative leaders and other members of the Legislature.

major_effects.label: Grant reporting and consolidated legislative report
major_effects.explanation: Agencies report grants they anticipate awarding in the next fiscal year and update their submissions; the Comptroller compiles the reports and updates the consolidated PDF at least quarterly.

major_effects.label: Optional implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: The Comptroller may adopt rules, including rules on the form and manner for agency reports and updates.

agencies.name: state agency
agencies.explanation: State agencies, as a statutory class, must submit reports on anticipated grants and update them. The bill refers to the definition in Government Code Section 403.013, which is not included in the supplied definitions.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The Comptroller must compile and submit the combined report and may adopt rules governing submissions.

HB199.summary: HB 199 would require the Legislative Budget Board to account for revenue made available for budget certification under a reenactment of Section 403.095, as well as under the current section. For each state fiscal biennium, the Board would incorporate measures to reduce reliance on that revenue into its budget recommendations and include an adopted plan for further reductions over the three bienniums following adoption.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the Legislative Budget Board's duties in preparing biennial budget recommendations and an associated reduction plan.
The required recommendations and plan concern state budgeting and the state's reliance on dedicated revenue for budget certification.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The bill concerns this state's revenue and state-government budgeting.

affected_groups.group: State budget officials and decision-makers
affected_groups.explanation: They would use the Board's budget recommendations and adopted plan addressing state reliance on available dedicated revenue.

major_effects.label: Biennial budget recommendations and reduction plan
major_effects.explanation: The Board must incorporate measures to reduce reliance on available dedicated revenue in each biennial budget recommendation and include an adopted plan for further reductions over the next three bienniums.

agencies.name: Legislative Budget Board
agencies.explanation: The bill identifies the Legislative Budget Board and assigns the board revised budget-planning duties. No canonical registry entry is available.

HB201.summary: The bill would allow a seven-member independent school district board eligible for an allotment under Education Code Section 48.101(b) to reduce its membership to five by resolution, if it certifies that it was unable to fill all trustee seats in the two preceding trustee elections. The change would take effect with the next regular trustee election, would not shorten the term of any trustee in office when the resolution is adopted, and would require a transition in trustee numbers; when the transition is complete, trustees would be elected as provided by Section 11.059.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the permitted size and election transition of certain independent school district boards of trustees.
Grants qualifying independent school district boards authority to change their membership size.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision applies to qualifying independent school districts under the statewide Education Code, without limiting eligibility to a named place.

affected_groups.group: Independent school districts eligible for an allotment under Education Code Section 48.101(b)
affected_groups.explanation: A qualifying district with a seven-member board could use the new authority if it meets the election-seat condition.

affected_groups.group: Trustees of qualifying independent school districts
affected_groups.explanation: The board-size change would take effect at a future regular election and would not shorten the term of a trustee already in office when the resolution is adopted.

major_effects.label: Option to reduce board membership
major_effects.explanation: A qualifying seven-member board could adopt a resolution reducing its membership to five if it could not fill all trustee seats in the two preceding elections.

major_effects.label: Certification prerequisite
major_effects.explanation: The board must certify its inability to fill all seats in the two preceding trustee elections to the commissioner before using the new authority.

major_effects.label: Election transition and current terms
major_effects.explanation: The reduction would begin with the next regular trustee election, preserve terms already in office when the resolution is adopted, and require a transition to elections under Section 11.059.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill requires the district board to certify election information to the commissioner, but the bill text does not identify the commissioner or establish the recipient's canonical agency identity.

HB202.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, the bill would require a student who engages in specified assault or harassment against a school district employee to be removed from class and placed in a disciplinary alternative education program for at least 30 days. The requirement is subject to Section 37.009(a), Education Code.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes public-school student discipline by requiring alternative-program placement for specified conduct against school district employees.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change amends the Texas Education Code and applies to school districts statewide.

affected_groups.group: Public school students who engage in the specified conduct
affected_groups.explanation: They would be subject to removal from class and at least 30 days in a disciplinary alternative education program.

affected_groups.group: School district employees
affected_groups.explanation: Subject to the requirements of Section 37.009(a), the disciplinary requirement applies when a student engages in the specified assault or harassment against a school district employee.

major_effects.label: Mandatory alternative-program placement
major_effects.explanation: Requires class removal and placement in a disciplinary alternative education program for at least 30 days for the specified conduct, subject to Section 37.009(a), Education Code.

HB203.summary: The bill would make personal information collected during jury selection about a person who reports for jury duty confidential and generally prohibit its disclosure by the court, parties, their attorneys, and court personnel. A court could authorize disclosure only on a good-cause application by a party or a person acting in the actual discharge of news-media duties; the change would apply only to people reporting for jury duty on or after the effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates confidentiality protections for personal information collected during jury selection.
Changes the disclosure duties of courts and court personnel regarding jury-selection information.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a statewide provision of the Texas Government Code concerning jury selection.

affected_groups.group: People who report for jury duty
affected_groups.explanation: Their personal information collected during jury selection would be confidential, subject to the limited disclosure procedure.

affected_groups.group: Parties and attorneys in proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: They would be barred from disclosing covered information and parties could apply for authorized disclosure on a showing of good cause.

affected_groups.group: News media
affected_groups.explanation: A person acting in the actual discharge of news-media duties could apply to the court for disclosure on a showing of good cause.

major_effects.label: Confidentiality of jury-selection information
major_effects.explanation: Makes covered personal information confidential and generally bars disclosure by courts, parties, attorneys, and court personnel.

major_effects.label: Limited court authorization for disclosure
major_effects.explanation: Allows a court to authorize disclosure only after a party or a person acting in the actual discharge of news-media duties submits an application showing good cause.

agencies.name: the court
agencies.explanation: The provision directly restricts disclosure by the court and gives it limited authority to authorize disclosure. The bill uses the generic term “court” and does not identify a particular state body.

HB204.summary: HB 204 would expand the Texas Information and Referral Network’s disaster capabilities, messaging, referral and data-sharing functions, and require around-the-clock call centers. It would also require consent for specified screening and volunteered demographic information, biennial public reporting, accreditation for certain contracted area information centers, and usability improvements to any network website developed under the applicable section.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes a health and human-services referral network, including screening for nonmedical drivers of health and care coordination with health care systems and managed care organizations.
Expands the network’s disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and emergency-management coordination functions.
Adds electronic messaging, data-sharing and searchable-data functions, alongside consent requirements and privacy protections for client information.
Changes the operation and coordination of a statewide network and requires the commission to report on its operations and improvements.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill concerns the statewide network and its integration into state plans.

affected_groups.group: Clients and households served by the network
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive expanded messaging, referrals, screening, and service navigation; specified screening and volunteered demographic information are consent-dependent.

affected_groups.group: Area information centers contracting to provide network operations
affected_groups.explanation: Those centers must obtain accreditation from a nationally recognized accreditation organization.

affected_groups.group: Health care systems and managed care organizations
affected_groups.explanation: They may partner with the commission and area information centers to share data for care coordination and to address nonmedical needs.

major_effects.label: Expanded network capabilities
major_effects.explanation: Adds requirements for disaster readiness, electronic messaging, closed-loop referrals, resource-data exchange, and continuous call-center operations.

major_effects.label: Consent-based data and screening
major_effects.explanation: Requires aggregated, de-identified demographic information with specified details only when volunteered after an opportunity for informed and explicit consent; screening also requires informed and explicit consent.

major_effects.label: Biennial public report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to report on network operations, service gaps, recommendations, and coordination efforts, and to publish the report on its and the network’s websites.

major_effects.label: Accreditation for contracted area information centers
major_effects.explanation: Requires accreditation only for an area information center that contracts with the commission to provide network operations.

major_effects.label: Network website usability
major_effects.explanation: If a website is developed under the section, it must be user-friendly and support easy searching and navigation.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission network coordination and reporting responsibilities. The supplied text does not establish which commission the term identifies.

agencies.name: Texas Division of Emergency Management
agencies.explanation: The commission must coordinate with the division to integrate the network into state emergency plans; the bill does not assign the division a separate duty in this clause.

agencies.name: Homeland Security Council
agencies.explanation: The commission must coordinate with the Council on integrating the network into state plans. The supplied text does not establish the Council’s precise legal identity.

HB205.summary: HB 205 would authorize counties, alone or jointly, to establish family violence court programs for specified participants and to charge a reasonable, ability-to-pay-based fee of up to $1,000 for program purposes. A participant who completes a program could receive a dismissal and expunction only through the specified process and conditions; eligible participants may separately petition for nondisclosure no earlier than two years after completion. The bill would also expand the statutory specialty-court definition used for grant funding and advisory recommendations to cover programs established under Subtitle K, Title 2.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a family violence specialty court program and changes routes to dismissal, expunction, and nondisclosure of criminal records for qualifying participants.
Authorizes county commissioners courts to establish individual or regional programs and permits those programs to collect participant fees.
Expands the statutory specialty-court category used for evaluating grant applications and making funding recommendations; the bill does not itself appropriate funds.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill authorizes programs for counties statewide, including regional programs formed by participating counties.

affected_groups.group: People arrested and charged with covered family-violence misdemeanors, and people convicted of or placed on deferred adjudication for such offenses
affected_groups.explanation: These are the populations for whom a county may establish a program.

affected_groups.group: Family violence court program participants
affected_groups.explanation: Participants may be charged a program reimbursement fee and qualifying completers may pursue record relief.

affected_groups.group: Alleged victims of program participants
affected_groups.explanation: The program's essential characteristics include consideration of their health and safety.

affected_groups.group: County governments
affected_groups.explanation: County commissioners courts may establish and fund individual or regional programs through participant reimbursement fees.

major_effects.label: County and regional family violence court programs
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes a county to establish a program, or two or more counties to establish one jointly, for the specified participants.

major_effects.label: Program reimbursement fees
major_effects.explanation: Programs may charge a reasonable fee capped at $1,000; it must reflect ability to pay and be used only for program purposes.

major_effects.label: Expunction after program completion
major_effects.explanation: Adds successful completion of a family violence court program as an expunction basis, but a person is eligible under this paragraph only if they have not previously received an expunction under it. Other statutory requirements apply.

major_effects.label: Nondisclosure of criminal-history information
major_effects.explanation: Creates a petition route for qualifying program completers to obtain an order barring public disclosure of information related to the program offense; petitions may be filed only on or after the second anniversary of completion.

major_effects.label: Specialty-court grant and advisory scope
major_effects.explanation: Replaces an enumerated list with a definition covering specialty court programs established under Subtitle K, Title 2, broadening the programs covered by grant review and advisory recommendations.

agencies.name: Specialty Courts Advisory Council
agencies.explanation: Its grant-review and best-practice recommendation work applies to the expanded statutory category of specialty courts.

agencies.name: Office of Court Administration of the Texas Judicial System
agencies.explanation: The office is expressly identified as a recipient of best-practice recommendations, whose specialty-court scope is expanded.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Council
agencies.explanation: The Council is expressly identified as a recipient of best-practice recommendations, whose specialty-court scope is expanded.

agencies.name: Criminal justice division
agencies.explanation: The division receives grant-funding recommendations for specialty courts, and the statutory specialty-court category is expanded.

HB206.summary: HB 206 would require the department to operate and market an instant-ticket lottery game to benefit animal-welfare programs in Texas. The portion of the lottery account balance attributable to the game, after reserves for prizes and operating costs, would be transferred to the animal friendly account; the bill separately directs the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation to establish the game and begin selling tickets by March 2, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Directs the portion of lottery-account funds attributable to the new game to the animal friendly account, after required reserves.
Creates an operating and marketing requirement for a new state lottery game.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The game is intended to benefit animal-welfare programs in the state; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: Animal-welfare programs in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: The game is created to benefit these programs, and its attributable funds are directed to the animal friendly account.

affected_groups.group: Lottery ticket purchasers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill provides for an instant-ticket game to be offered for sale and requires its tickets to disclose the animal-welfare purpose.

affected_groups.group: Lottery sales agents
affected_groups.explanation: The department must encourage sales agents who sell instant-ticket or similar lottery games to sell tickets to this game.

major_effects.label: Animal-welfare lottery game
major_effects.explanation: Requires operation, sale, and marketing of a new instant-ticket game for animal-welfare programs; separately assigns TDLR a deadline to establish the game and start sales.

major_effects.label: Game proceeds directed to animal friendly account
major_effects.explanation: Directs the portion of the balance attributable to the game to the animal friendly account after reserves for prizes, costs, and other specified obligations; it does not dedicate gross ticket sales before those amounts.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns this entity responsibility for operating, marketing, and administering the new game, but the supplied text does not establish the entity's identity.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly directs the department to establish the game and begin selling tickets by the stated deadline.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the department to make recommendations about marketing and advertising the game.

HB207.summary: HB 207 would remove the separate 1.08 and 1.035 multipliers and unused-increment component from voter-approval tax-rate calculations, while revising related formulas for taxing units that add or end an additional sales tax. An adopted tax rate above the voter-approval rate would require voter approval for any taxing unit; water-district elections would also be required when the proposed rate raises taxes on the average homestead above the preceding year's amount. The bill would define “developed district” for the existing water-district budget-appendix requirement using a 95-percent projected-build-out threshold.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how taxing units calculate voter-approval tax rates and when adopted property-tax rates require voter approval.
Requires an election for voters to decide whether to approve a taxing unit's adopted rate when it exceeds the voter-approval rate, and changes the water-district election threshold.
Alters property-tax rules affecting local taxing units and water districts, including their boards and district budget requirements.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions amend generally applicable Texas tax laws and apply to ad valorem taxes of taxing units.

affected_groups.group: Local taxing units and their governing bodies
affected_groups.explanation: Their voter-approval tax-rate calculations and approval process would change.

affected_groups.group: Registered voters in taxing units
affected_groups.explanation: Voters would decide whether to approve an adopted tax rate that exceeds the unit's voter-approval rate.

affected_groups.group: Water districts and their taxpayers
affected_groups.explanation: Water-district elections would be triggered by an increase in average-homestead taxes above the preceding year's amount.

affected_groups.group: Developed water districts
affected_groups.explanation: The bill defines which districts are covered by the existing requirement to append specified financial and engineering records to the annual budget.

major_effects.label: Voter-approval tax-rate calculations
major_effects.explanation: Removes the separate 1.08 and 1.035 multipliers and unused-increment component from the general formulas, and revises related formulas for years when additional sales taxes are imposed or discontinued.

major_effects.label: Voter approval of rates above the voter-approval rate
major_effects.explanation: Requires registered voters to decide whether to approve an adopted rate above the voter-approval rate for any taxing unit.

major_effects.label: Water-district tax-rate election threshold
major_effects.explanation: Requires an election when the district's combined rate would impose more tax on the average residence homestead than in the preceding year; if voters reject the rate, the district's rate is the voter-approval rate.

major_effects.label: Definition used for water-district budget appendices
major_effects.explanation: Defines “developed district” in this section by financing, completion, bond issuance, and service capacity for at least 95 percent of projected build-out, determining which districts are covered by the existing appendix requirement.

HB208.summary: For covered non-Medicaid health benefit plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028, HB 208 would require issuers to pay providers the full plan amount for emergency care and make the issuer solely responsible for collecting the enrollee’s cost-sharing; enrollees could request collection in installments during the plan year. It would also limit enrollees’ financial responsibility for emergency care, restrict issuer practices, require more detailed emergency-care cost information in explanations of benefits, and make violations subject to Insurance Code Chapter 541 enforcement.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes emergency-care cost-sharing and payment rules for covered health benefit plans.
Imposes payment, collection, and other conduct requirements on health benefit plan issuers.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill regulates covered plans and providers under Texas law, including providers authorized to practice in this state.

affected_groups.group: Enrollees in covered health benefit plans, excluding Medicaid enrollees
affected_groups.explanation: Enrollees receive the emergency-care cost-sharing protections and may request installment collection during the plan year; the chapter expressly excludes Medicaid.

affected_groups.group: Health care providers furnishing covered emergency care
affected_groups.explanation: Providers would receive the full amount payable under the plan, including the enrollee’s cost-sharing amount, from the issuer.

affected_groups.group: Issuers of covered health benefit plans
affected_groups.explanation: Issuers would assume responsibility for collecting emergency-care cost-sharing and face new restrictions on their payment and premium practices.

major_effects.label: Emergency-care payment and collection
major_effects.explanation: The issuer must pay the full plan amount to the provider and is solely responsible for collecting the enrollee’s cost-sharing; on request, collection must be spread in issuer-determined increments during the plan year.

major_effects.label: Issuer restrictions and enrollee liability
major_effects.explanation: Issuers may not withhold the enrollee’s cost-sharing from provider payment, demand extra emergency-care discounts, cancel coverage for failure to collect that cost-sharing, or pass compliance expenses through by raising premiums or reducing provider payments. Enrollees’ emergency-care liability remains capped by applicable plan cost-sharing and is not based on additional amounts determined under Chapter 1467.

major_effects.label: Emergency-care cost disclosures
major_effects.explanation: For emergency care subject to Section 1271.155 or Section 1301.0053 or 1301.155, explanations of benefits must state the total payable to the provider, any amount the provider may bill the enrollee or insured, the cost-sharing owed to the issuer, and an itemization of that cost-sharing.

major_effects.label: Insurance-code enforcement
major_effects.explanation: A violation of the new chapter is treated as an unfair method of competition or an unfair or deceptive act or practice and is subject to Chapter 541 enforcement.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the commissioner to adopt rules implementing the new chapter. The supplied text does not verify the commissioner’s canonical agency identity.

HB209.summary: If enacted, the bill would require the Health and Human Services Commission to operate a statewide co-navigation services program for individuals who are deaf-blind, providing services through co-navigators and reimbursing them at rates based on training and skill. The commission must begin operating the program by September 1, 2028; the bill's stated effective date is September 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a statewide program and assigns its operation and oversight to the commission.
Requires reimbursement of co-navigators and funding and technical assistance for training, while directing the commission to develop additional funding sources.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The program is expressly required to operate statewide.

affected_groups.group: Individuals who are deaf-blind
affected_groups.explanation: They are the intended recipients of the co-navigation services, and the bill also provides for training to help them use the program.

affected_groups.group: Co-navigators
affected_groups.explanation: Co-navigators would provide services under the program, receive reimbursement, and be subject to program compliance monitoring.

major_effects.label: Statewide co-navigation program
major_effects.explanation: Requires HHSC to operate a program providing co-navigation services through co-navigators to individuals who are deaf-blind.

major_effects.label: Reimbursement and training support
major_effects.explanation: Requires co-navigator reimbursement and funding and technical assistance for training; HHSC must also develop additional funding sources to reduce reliance on state sources.

major_effects.label: Rates and program standards
major_effects.explanation: Requires the executive commissioner to set tiered reimbursement rates based on co-navigators' training and skills, and permits rules concerning efficient program operation and adequate training.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the commission as HHSC and assigns it responsibility for operating and overseeing the program.

HB210.summary: HB 210 would require a school district’s board of trustees to resume management when the academic-performance basis for state-imposed alternative management continues for two consecutive years. After the board resumes management, the commissioner could not impose new academic-performance-based alternative management until after five consecutive school years under the board; management contracts would also have to provide for automatic termination in the specified circumstances.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes state intervention and management rules for low-performing campuses and school districts.
Changes when a school district’s locally governed board of trustees resumes management of a campus or district.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes Education Code rules applying to campuses and school districts across Texas.

affected_groups.group: School district boards of trustees
affected_groups.explanation: Boards must resume management in the specified circumstances and receive a period before academic-performance-based alternative management may be imposed again.

affected_groups.group: Conservators, boards of managers, and other alternative managers
affected_groups.explanation: Their management may end when the statutory two-consecutive-year condition is met, and contracts must provide for automatic termination in the specified circumstances.

major_effects.label: Return to district management and pause on renewed academic intervention
major_effects.explanation: If the academic-performance basis for the intervention continues for two consecutive years under alternative management, the district board resumes management. The commissioner may not impose another academic-performance-based alternative manager until after the fifth consecutive school year under the board.

major_effects.label: Automatic termination provision in management contracts
major_effects.explanation: Contracts must provide for automatic termination under the circumstances in Section 39A.008. This contract requirement applies to contracts entered into, amended, or renewed on or after September 1, 2027; the Act otherwise applies beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

major_effects.label: Change to a commissioner appointment pathway
major_effects.explanation: The bill removes the reference in Section 39A.209(c) to removal under subsection (b) and repeals subsection (b). The effect of removing that pathway cannot be determined without the former subsection’s text.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns intervention and removal duties to the commissioner under the Education Code; impact on the Texas Education Agency is inferred because the agency is not named in the bill.

HB211.summary: The bill would make the six-month period for a municipality or county to authorize a public improvement district begin on the date the establishment hearing finally adjourns. For specified districts, it would revise consent rules for adding hotel property, allow inclusion without notice or a hearing when the owner or qualified representative consents, and permit assessment rolls for a narrower class of hotel districts to report only each hotel's annual assessment rate. The inclusion and assessment-roll changes would apply only to requests or levies made on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes municipal and county authority and procedures for public improvement districts, including property inclusion and assessment-roll requirements.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide Local Government Code provisions governing municipal and county public improvement districts.

affected_groups.group: Municipal and county governing bodies
affected_groups.explanation: Their authority and procedures for authorizing or modifying public improvement districts would change; the hotel-property inclusion provisions apply to municipalities.

affected_groups.group: Hotel property owners and qualified petitioners representing property
affected_groups.explanation: Newly constructed hotel property may be added to a public improvement district under this section only if the record owner or a qualified petitioner representing the property consents to its inclusion.

affected_groups.group: Appraisal districts in which property subject to assessment under the district is located
affected_groups.explanation: They receive public improvement district assessment rolls, whose required contents would be limited for a specified class of hotel districts.

major_effects.label: Changes the district-authorization window
major_effects.explanation: The six-month period for authorizing an improvement district would begin on the date the establishment hearing finally adjourns, rather than after that date.

major_effects.label: Revises consent rules for hotel-property inclusion
major_effects.explanation: For a district described by Section 372.0035, qualified petitioners representing property may count with record owners toward the consent requirements. The revised test requires consenters to own or represent more than 60 percent of appraised value and to meet either the specified owner-and-petitioner count or area test.

major_effects.label: Allows consent-based inclusion without notice or a hearing
major_effects.explanation: For inclusion under this section, the municipality may proceed without the specified establishment notice or hearing if the record owner or qualified representative of the property consents.

major_effects.label: Limits assessment-roll contents for specified hotel districts
major_effects.explanation: For districts described by Section 372.0035(a-1), the assessment roll may state only the annual assessment rate levied on each hotel.

HB212.summary: For social-media access on or after January 1, 2028, HB 212 would, to the extent federal law permits, prohibit people under 16 from using social media platforms and require platforms to verify age before accepting account holders. It would limit how platforms handle information used for age verification, require ways for parents or guardians to request deletion of a minor’s account, and make knowing violations actionable as deceptive trade practices.

policy_tags.explanation: Sets age-verification, account, and deletion requirements for social media platforms and makes knowing violations actionable under the Deceptive Trade Practices–Consumer Protection Act.
Regulates age verification and the use, retention, transmission, and deletion of personal information by platforms.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds requirements to Texas law and defines an account holder as a state resident.

affected_groups.group: Individuals younger than 16
affected_groups.explanation: Would be prohibited from using social media platforms, subject to the federal-law qualification.

affected_groups.group: Social media platforms
affected_groups.explanation: Would have to verify age, restrict under-16 users, and follow requirements for verification data and account deletion.

affected_groups.group: Parents and guardians of minors under 16
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive a means to request account deletion, with verification requirements that vary depending on whether the platform is regulated under Chapter 509.

major_effects.label: Under-16 access and account limits
major_effects.explanation: To the extent federal law permits, people under 16 may not use a social media platform, and platforms may not accept them as account holders.

major_effects.label: Age verification and verification-data limits
major_effects.explanation: Platforms must verify age before accepting account holders and restrict handling of information obtained for that verification, including immediate deletion when verification is complete.

major_effects.label: Parent-requested account deletion
major_effects.explanation: Platforms must provide an eligible parent or guardian a verifiable deletion-request process; after a request, the account must be deleted within 10 days, with limits on further collection and use of the minor’s identifying information.

major_effects.label: Deceptive-trade-practice actionability
major_effects.explanation: Knowing violations of the specified requirements are treated as deceptive trade practices and are actionable under Chapter 17.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill makes violations actionable under Business & Commerce Code Chapter 17, which may implicate the Attorney General’s consumer-protection enforcement role; the bill does not name the office.

HB213.summary: The bill would generally bar an institution of higher education from withdrawing or revoking an athletic scholarship because a student athlete has an injury, illness, or disability that prevents participation in intercollegiate athletics. An exception would allow withdrawal or revocation if the condition resulted from a violation of the institution’s student code of conduct; the protection would apply to awards initially made for the 2027–2028 academic year or later.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes protections for athletic scholarships awarded by institutions of higher education and directs the coordinating board to implement them.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The scholarship protections apply to covered awards at institutions of higher education under the Texas Education Code, without limiting them to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Student athletes receiving athletic scholarships, grants, or similar aid
affected_groups.explanation: Their covered financial assistance would generally be protected from withdrawal or revocation based on an injury, illness, or disability that prevents athletic participation, subject to the conduct-code exception.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: Institutions would be subject to the restriction on withdrawing or revoking covered athletic scholarships and to the stated exception.

major_effects.label: Protection against injury-based scholarship revocation
major_effects.explanation: Generally bars withdrawal or revocation when an injury, illness, or disability prevents athletic participation, including when temporary or permanent; allows it if the condition resulted from violating the institution’s student code of conduct.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Directs the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to adopt rules as necessary to implement and enforce the protection.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly assigns the Board responsibility to adopt rules to implement and enforce the scholarship protection.

HB214.summary: HB 214 would authorize the Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas to award grants for research on whether endometriosis leads to or increases cancer incidence, and on endometriosis’s causes, biological markers, and treatment efficacy. It would also make grants for that research an allowable use of the institute’s fund; it does not require that grants be awarded.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands eligible medical and cancer research to include specified endometriosis research.
Broadens the research grants that may be supported by the institute’s fund.

locations.name: Statewide in Texas
locations.explanation: The eligible cancer research and research facilities are specified as being in this state.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of learning and advanced medical research facilities and collaborations seeking research grants
affected_groups.explanation: These entities may seek grants for the newly specified endometriosis research.

major_effects.label: Expanded grant authority
major_effects.explanation: The institute may award grants for research on endometriosis and its possible relationship to cancer.

major_effects.label: Expanded allowable fund use
major_effects.explanation: The institute’s fund may support grants for the specified endometriosis research.

agencies.name: Cancer Prevention and Research Institute of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill directly expands the institute’s grant authority to cover specified endometriosis research. The provided canonical registry does not list this named institute.

HB215.summary: The bill would require a preauthorization determination to be made by a physician in the same specialty as the physician or health care provider proposing or recommending the service. This requirement would apply only to preauthorization requests made on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the physician specialty standard for preauthorization determinations involving health care services.
Imposes a new requirement on the process for determining preauthorization requests under the Insurance Code.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Insurance Code without limiting the requirement to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Physicians and health care providers proposing or recommending services
affected_groups.explanation: Their specialty determines which physician may make the related preauthorization determination.

affected_groups.group: Entities handling preauthorization determinations
affected_groups.explanation: They must ensure a determination is made by a physician of the required specialty.

major_effects.label: Same-specialty preauthorization determinations
major_effects.explanation: Requires a physician of the same specialty as the physician or health care provider proposing or recommending the service to make the preauthorization determination; applies only to requests made on or after January 1, 2028.

HB216.summary: For an area subject to a state of disaster declaration, the bill activates an optional disaster identification system; individuals may choose to participate. Participants must use illuminated displays to identify household members and domesticated animals, and use continuous or flashing light to signal whether an individual needs medical assistance; disaster relief personnel may patrol at night to locate activated displays.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a disaster-response identification and signaling system to help relief personnel locate people and animals and identify medical-assistance needs.
Adds activation of the system to the effects of a disaster declaration and permits the state emergency management plan to address its use.

locations.name: Area subject to a state of disaster declaration
locations.explanation: The system activates only in the area covered by a state of disaster declaration.

affected_groups.group: Individuals and households in an area subject to a state of disaster declaration that elect to participate
affected_groups.explanation: Participants must display lights on household members, with multicolored displays differentiating some household members by age or disability.

affected_groups.group: Domesticated animals in participating households
affected_groups.explanation: Participants must affix a display to each domesticated animal in their household; multicolored displays use yellow for animals.

affected_groups.group: Disaster relief personnel
affected_groups.explanation: Personnel responding to the affected area may use nighttime air or ground patrols to locate people and animals with activated displays.

major_effects.label: Optional disaster identification system
major_effects.explanation: A disaster declaration activates the system in the affected area, where people may opt in; the emergency management plan may include provisions for using it.

major_effects.label: Participant display and signaling protocol
major_effects.explanation: Participants must affix displays to household members and domesticated animals. Monochromatic displays are white; multicolored displays use specified colors, and continuous versus flashing light distinguishes whether an individual needs medical assistance.

major_effects.label: Nighttime locating patrols
major_effects.explanation: Permits disaster relief personnel to patrol the designated disaster area by air or ground at night to locate people or animals with activated displays.

agencies.name: Texas Division of Emergency Management
agencies.explanation: Chapter 418 defines “Division” as the Texas Division of Emergency Management. The bill assigns the division responsibility for preparing and maintaining the state emergency management plan and adds optional provisions for use of the disaster identification system.

HB217.summary: The bill makes the failure-to-report offense a state jail felony, rather than a Class A misdemeanor, if it is shown at trial that the actor intended to conceal abuse or neglect, or that the unreported conduct involved specified sexual offenses or sexual exploitation of a child. The change applies only to offenses committed on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill increases the criminal classification for specified failures to report child abuse or neglect.

locations.name: Texas (statewide)
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Family Code and states no narrower geographic limit.

affected_groups.group: People who commit the failure-to-report offense
affected_groups.explanation: They may face a state jail felony classification when the specified circumstances are shown at trial.

affected_groups.group: Children whose abuse or sexual exploitation is not reported
affected_groups.explanation: The increased penalty applies when the unreported conduct includes specified offenses or sexual exploitation involving a child.

major_effects.label: State jail felony for specified failures to report
major_effects.explanation: Raises the offense from a Class A misdemeanor to a state jail felony if trial evidence shows intent to conceal abuse or neglect, or that the unreported conduct falls within the specified sexual-offense or child-exploitation categories.

HB218.summary: HB 218 would create a process for family or household members, certain guardians, and peace officers to seek extreme risk protective orders when a person with serious mental illness and firearm access poses an immediate danger. Courts could issue temporary firearm restrictions and, after a hearing and a clear-and-convincing-evidence finding, orders generally lasting one year that require firearm relinquishment and may require a mental-health examination or recommended outpatient services. The bill would also require related court, law-enforcement, and Department of Public Safety actions, and create offenses for knowingly false requests to an officer and firearm violations of an order.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates court orders restricting firearm access when a person is found to pose an immediate and present danger.
Establishes a court process for protective orders and creates criminal offenses for specified conduct related to applications and orders.
Allows an order to require an examination to determine serious mental illness and, if recommended after examination, outpatient mental-health services.
Requires law-enforcement agencies holding firearms under an order to provide notices, check possession eligibility, and handle possible return or sale of firearms.
Makes specified medical or mental-health information confidential in court records and requires identifying information about order subjects to be sent for federal background-check-system inclusion.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and creates a protective-order process applicable across the state.

affected_groups.group: People who are subject to an extreme risk protective order
affected_groups.explanation: A person subject to the order is prohibited from purchasing, owning, possessing, or controlling a firearm for the order’s duration. If applicable, the person must receive outpatient mental health services if recommended after the specified examination.

affected_groups.group: Family and household members, certain guardians, and peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: May apply for an order or, for a peace officer, be asked to file an application.

affected_groups.group: Courts and law-enforcement agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Courts would process applications and orders; law-enforcement officers may take custody of firearms, and an agency’s related duties apply to a firearm subject to disposition under the article.

affected_groups.group: Local mental-health authorities and qualified mental-health experts
affected_groups.explanation: May conduct examinations used in the order process and may recommend outpatient mental-health services.

major_effects.label: Extreme risk protective-order process
major_effects.explanation: Creates an application and hearing process, permits temporary ex parte orders, and requires a final order when the court makes the specified clear-and-convincing-evidence finding.

major_effects.label: Firearm restrictions and handling
major_effects.explanation: Orders prohibit firearm possession or control and require relinquishment; law enforcement must follow specified return and disposition procedures, and an unclaimed firearm may not be destroyed or forfeited to the state.

major_effects.label: Handgun-license eligibility and suspension
major_effects.explanation: A person currently restricted under a protective order, including an extreme risk order, is ineligible for a handgun license; a license held by a person subject to an extreme risk order is suspended for the order's duration.

major_effects.label: Order information and background-check reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires court clerks to send order and license information to DPS, and DPS to provide received information to the FBI for inclusion in the national background-check system.

major_effects.label: Mental-health examinations and services
major_effects.explanation: A temporary order may require an examination; a final order may require outpatient mental-health services if recommended after the examination.

major_effects.label: New criminal offenses
major_effects.explanation: Creates a Class B misdemeanor for knowingly making a false statement to an officer about a request for an order and a Class A misdemeanor for firearm conduct violating an order after notice and before rescission or expiration.

agencies.name: Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: Receives protective-order information, records handgun-license suspensions, reports them to local law enforcement, and must establish a procedure for sending information to the FBI.

agencies.name: District, juvenile, statutory county, and constitutional county courts
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns these courts duties to receive applications, decide whether to issue orders, and handle confidential information; it identifies court classes rather than a single named court.

HB219.summary: The bill would increase the gross annual salary of full-time state-agency employees, including employees of institutions of higher education, by $5,000 for each fiscal year in the biennium beginning September 1, 2027. Part-time employees would receive a proportional increase; legislators and certain state-agency governing-body members who receive no full-time salary are excluded.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill would increase salary costs for covered state-agency employees.
The bill changes compensation for state-agency employees.
The salary increases expressly cover employees of institutions of higher education.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision covers state-agency employees across the state rather than a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Full-time state-agency employees, including higher education institution employees
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive a $5,000 gross annual salary increase for each fiscal year of the specified biennium.

affected_groups.group: Part-time state-agency employees, including higher education institution employees
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive an increase proportional to their hours compared with a full-time employee.

affected_groups.group: Legislators and certain state-agency governing-body members
affected_groups.explanation: Excluded if they may receive a per diem or expense reimbursement but not a salary for full-time employment.

major_effects.label: Salary increases for covered state employees
major_effects.explanation: Subject to Section 2, would provide a $5,000 gross annual salary increase to full-time employees, with a proportional increase for part-time employees, during each fiscal year of the biennium beginning September 1, 2027; specified legislators and governing-body members are excluded.

HB220.summary: The bill authorizes the Railroad Commission of Texas to impose administrative penalties on propane distribution system retailers for violations of Chapter 141 or rules adopted under it, including failure to meet the financial-surety requirement. Penalties may be up to $1,000 per violation, with each day potentially counted separately and a $10,000 cap for a related series; they may be assessed only after the retailer has an opportunity for a hearing, and apply only to violations occurring on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes enforcement of requirements governing propane distribution systems.
The bill establishes administrative penalties for regulated distribution system retailers that violate the chapter or its rules.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies generally to distribution system retailers violating Chapter 141 or rules adopted under it, within the scope of the Railroad Commission of Texas.

affected_groups.group: Propane distribution system retailers
affected_groups.explanation: Retailers become subject to administrative penalties for violations of Chapter 141 or rules adopted under it, including noncompliance with the financial-surety requirement.

major_effects.label: Administrative penalties
major_effects.explanation: The commission may penalize chapter or rule violations, with a per-violation ceiling of $1,000 and a $10,000 maximum for a related series; continuing or recurring days may count separately.

major_effects.label: Penalty assessment procedure
major_effects.explanation: A penalty requires an opportunity for a hearing; if a hearing is held, the commission must make findings and issue a written decision.

agencies.name: Railroad Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill names the Railroad Commission of Texas and authorizes the commission to assess penalties and issue related orders.

HB221.summary: The bill lets a county that adopts a fire code contract with a municipality or emergency services district in the county to administer and enforce it. It also allows a qualifying emergency services district to agree to enforce all or part of the county’s fire code authority, and requires the county fire marshal to delegate administration and enforcement under a contract.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how counties, municipalities, and emergency services districts may contract and delegate county fire-code enforcement.
The bill changes administration and enforcement of county fire codes.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes county fire-code administration under the statewide Local Government Code.

affected_groups.group: Texas counties that adopt a fire code
affected_groups.explanation: Their commissioners courts may contract for fire-code administration and enforcement, and their fire marshals must delegate those functions under a qualifying contract.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities located in a county that adopts a fire code
affected_groups.explanation: They may contract with the county to administer and enforce its fire code.

affected_groups.group: Emergency services districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts may contract with a county for fire-code administration and enforcement; a district that has adopted a fire code may also agree to take on all or part of the county's enforcement authority.

major_effects.label: Local contracting and delegation of fire-code enforcement
major_effects.explanation: A county that adopts a fire code may contract with an in-county municipality or emergency services district; a qualifying district may separately agree to enforce all or part of the county's authority. Under a contract entered under Section 233.061, the county fire marshal must delegate administration and enforcement.

HB222.summary: The bill changes the priority list of people who may make an anatomical gift for a decedent, removing hospital administrators and the catch-all category of people authorized to dispose of the decedent’s body. The changes apply only to anatomical gifts made on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes who may authorize anatomical gifts for transplantation, therapy, research, or education.

locations.name: Statewide (Texas)
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing anatomical gifts.

affected_groups.group: People in the statutory priority classes who may make an anatomical gift for a decedent
affected_groups.explanation: The bill revises the classes of people authorized to make a gift, including by removing two categories from the list.

affected_groups.group: Hospital administrators and other people authorized to dispose of a decedent’s body
affected_groups.explanation: The bill removes these categories from the list of people who may make an anatomical gift.

major_effects.label: Revises who may authorize an anatomical gift
major_effects.explanation: Removes hospital administrators and the catch-all category of people authorized to dispose of the decedent’s body from the priority list. The amendments apply only to gifts made on or after the effective date.

HB223.summary: HB 223 would raise from 12 to 14 the age limit for several Family Code provisions governing admissibility of a child’s abuse or family-violence statements and use of recorded or closed-circuit testimony. Existing safeguards and conditions remain, including reliability findings for one hearsay rule and court discretion over closed-circuit testimony. The changes apply to pending or later-filed parent-child suits as specified, but the expanded protective-order rule applies only to hearings begun on or after the Act’s effective date.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to covered proceedings under the Texas Family Code statewide.

affected_groups.group: Children alleged to have been abused or subjected to family violence
affected_groups.explanation: Children through age 14 would fall within the age limit for the specified evidence provisions.

affected_groups.group: Parties to parent-child suits and protective-order proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: The provisions govern evidence in these proceedings and provide parties with specified opportunities concerning recorded statements.

major_effects.label: Expanded age range for child-evidence provisions
major_effects.explanation: Raises the age limit from 12 to 14 for the specified hearsay, prerecorded-statement, and testimony provisions; the provisions’ other admissibility conditions remain.

HB224.summary: The bill would recognize a person as honorably discharged if the person’s military record shows a discharge or separation based on sexual orientation and a previous characterization of service indicates the person otherwise would have received a more favorable discharge. A person so recognized would be entitled to state-law benefits, rights, privileges, and immunities for honorably discharged veterans, and state agencies or officers would have to accept specified copies of the person’s DD Form 214.

policy_tags.explanation: Extends honorably discharged veteran status and its associated state-law protections to qualifying people separated from service on the basis of sexual orientation.
Expands eligibility for the state-law benefits provided to honorably discharged veterans.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill establishes recognition and entitlements under Texas law.

affected_groups.group: People whose military records show separation from active service based on sexual orientation
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying people may be recognized as honorably discharged if their prior characterization of service indicates they would otherwise have received a more favorable discharge.

affected_groups.group: State agencies and officers
affected_groups.explanation: They must accept specified copies of a qualifying person's DD Form 214 for purposes of the subchapter.

major_effects.label: Honorably discharged veteran recognition
major_effects.explanation: Creates a state-law basis for treating a person as honorably discharged when the record shows a sexual-orientation-based discharge or separation and a prior service characterization supports a more favorable discharge.

major_effects.label: State-law veteran entitlements
major_effects.explanation: People recognized under the bill become entitled to the benefits, rights, privileges, and immunities state law provides to honorably discharged veterans.

major_effects.label: Acceptance of DD Form 214 copies
major_effects.explanation: For purposes of the subchapter, state agencies and officers must accept a copy identified as “Service 2 Copy” or “Member 4 Copy.”

agencies.name: an agency or officer of this state
agencies.explanation: The bill directly requires this general category of state entities or officials to accept specified DD Form 214 copies; it does not name a particular agency.

HB225.summary: For offenses committed on or after the Act's effective date, the bill generally bars warrantless arrests for offenses punishable only by fine, subject to exceptions including lack of appropriate identification, specified probable-cause grounds, and exclusions for certain assault and alcohol offenses. It requires law enforcement agencies to adopt citation policies and generally requires citations or notices to appear instead of taking people to a magistrate for fine-only misdemeanors, with specified exceptions.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes warrantless arrest limits and citation procedures for fine-only misdemeanors.
The arrest exceptions include probable cause to believe release would create an immediate danger or allow a continued breach of the peace.
The policy requirement applies to law enforcement agencies of political subdivisions and requires consultation with local governing bodies and commissioners courts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The policy-adoption requirement applies to each law enforcement agency in Texas.

affected_groups.group: People suspected of or charged with fine-only misdemeanors
affected_groups.explanation: They are affected by the limits on warrantless arrest and the citation procedures.

affected_groups.group: Law enforcement agencies and peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: Law enforcement agencies must adopt written citation policies for fine-only misdemeanors, including procedures for verifying identity and issuing citations. For fine-only offenses covered by the arrest restriction, officers generally may not arrest without a warrant unless the person fails to present appropriate identification or the officer has the specified probable cause; listed offenses are excluded.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions, including municipalities and counties
affected_groups.explanation: Their law enforcement agencies may be covered, and their governing bodies or commissioners courts are among the policy consultees.

major_effects.label: Limits warrantless arrests
major_effects.explanation: Generally prohibits warrantless arrest for offenses punishable only by fine, unless identification is not presented or probable cause supports specified safety, public-peace, or court-appearance concerns; certain assault and alcohol offenses are excluded from the prohibition.

major_effects.label: Requires agency citation policies
major_effects.explanation: Each covered law enforcement agency must adopt a written citation policy, developed in consultation with specified justice-system officials, local governing bodies, and residents in its jurisdiction.

major_effects.label: Requires citations or notices for covered offenses
major_effects.explanation: Officers generally must issue citations instead of taking people to a magistrate for fine-only misdemeanors, and must issue a notice to appear for covered traffic misdemeanors when the officer is not authorized to arrest; specified exceptions remain.

agencies.name: law enforcement agency
agencies.explanation: The bill defines a covered class of state or political-subdivision agencies that employ peace officers conducting arrests, and directly requires each covered agency to adopt a written citation policy. The bill does not identify specific agencies by name.

HB226.summary: For rates filed on or after January 1, 2028, HB 226 would require prior approval before an insurer may use a residential property or personal automobile rate that changes by more than five percent from its previously filed rate; the previous rate would remain in effect while approval is pending. The commissioner would review those rates under specified premium standards and deadlines, with the review period paused while requested information is outstanding and a possible good-cause extension, and the department would track and analyze reasons for disapprovals.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a prior-approval process and standards for certain residential property and personal automobile insurance rates.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The rate provisions concern insurance risks written in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Insurers writing residential property or personal automobile insurance
affected_groups.explanation: These insurers would need prior commissioner approval to use covered rate changes exceeding five percent.

affected_groups.group: Residential property and personal automobile policyholders
affected_groups.explanation: The prior rate would remain in effect while a covered rate change awaits approval.

major_effects.label: Prior approval for larger rate changes
major_effects.explanation: A rate increase or decrease of more than five percent requires prior commissioner approval, and the previously filed rate remains in effect pending the new rate's effective date.

major_effects.label: Review standards and deadlines
major_effects.explanation: The commissioner must decide within the prescribed review period using specified premium standards; a rate not disapproved within the required period is considered approved.

major_effects.label: Analysis of rate disapprovals
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to track and routinely analyze factors contributing to rate disapprovals.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the department a duty to track, compile, and routinely analyze factors contributing to rate disapprovals. The text does not identify the department by its canonical name.

HB227.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, school district superintendents would electronically report campus-organized data on student restraints and complaints under Section 37.145, plus citations and arrests on school property resulting from a district employee’s request for law-enforcement intervention. Open-enrollment charter schools would become subject to the reporting requirement, and the agency would compile and publish the data subject to student-privacy limits; the data would not constitute prima facie evidence of racial profiling. Districts with an agreement for regular campus police presence would have to designate in the agreement which entity collects the data.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates student-incident reporting requirements for school districts and makes open-enrollment charter schools subject to the reporting requirement.
Imposes reporting and data-collection allocation duties on school districts, including districts' agreements with local law enforcement agencies.
Requires incident data reporting while restricting disclosure of personally identifiable student information and protecting officer identity.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The reporting requirements apply to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools statewide.

affected_groups.group: Students involved in reported restraints, complaints, citations, or arrests
