affected_groups.explanation: Their incidents and specified demographic and other characteristics would be included in the reports, subject to privacy restrictions.

affected_groups.group: Students in demographic and other identified groups
affected_groups.explanation: Reports include applicable information and campus comparisons for groups including students receiving special education services, emergent bilingual students, students in state conservatorship, and homeless students.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: District superintendents must submit reports, and open-enrollment charter schools become subject to the reporting requirement.

affected_groups.group: Local law enforcement agencies and school resource officers involved in district arrangements
affected_groups.explanation: For a district agreement providing regular campus police presence, the agreement must assign responsibility for collecting the specified data.

major_effects.label: Campus-based incident reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires district superintendents to submit incident-based data on restraints and Section 37.145 complaints, as well as citations and arrests on school property resulting from a district employee's request for specified law-enforcement intervention. Charter schools are also made subject to the reporting requirement.

major_effects.label: Compilation and public availability with confidentiality limits
major_effects.explanation: Directs the agency to compile and make the data public, with district disaggregation only to the extent possible while protecting student confidentiality; reports may not include personally identifiable student information.

major_effects.label: Assignment of data collection in campus-police agreements
major_effects.explanation: A district entering an agreement with a local law enforcement agency for regular campus police presence must designate which entity will collect the data.

major_effects.label: Limits on use and disclosure of reported information
major_effects.explanation: The report cannot identify the peace officer who issued a citation, that identity is confidential, and the collected data does not constitute prima facie evidence of racial profiling.

agencies.name: the agency
agencies.explanation: The bill directs the agency to collect, compile, and publish the reports. The source does not identify the agency by a canonical name; the commissioner is also assigned rulemaking.

HB228.summary: HB 228 would bar a covered state employee from cumulative employment exceeding 24 years, require the employing agency’s governing body to terminate an employee who becomes ineligible, and count only service after January 1, 2028; elected officials and qualifying faculty are excluded. For employment relationships under contracts entered into before the effective date, the bill would apply only to renewals on or after that date. It would take effect January 1, 2028, only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise, it would have no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the maximum cumulative employment duration for covered state employees.
Sets a service-duration limit and termination duty for employees of defined state agencies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply across the defined state agencies of Texas, including executive-branch and legislative bodies and agencies.

affected_groups.group: Covered state employees
affected_groups.explanation: Employees may not exceed 24 cumulative years of service counted after January 1, 2028; elected officials and qualifying faculty are excluded.

affected_groups.group: Governing bodies of employing state agencies
affected_groups.explanation: They must terminate the employment of a person who becomes ineligible under the limit.

affected_groups.group: Employees under pre-effective-date contracts
affected_groups.explanation: The bill applies to these employment relationships only when the contract is renewed on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Cumulative employment limit
major_effects.explanation: Bars covered state employees from exceeding 24 cumulative years of employment, counting only service after January 1, 2028, and requires termination once an employee becomes ineligible.

agencies.name: state agency
agencies.explanation: The bill defines this broad category to include specified executive-branch agencies and legislative bodies and agencies; an employing agency’s governing body must terminate an employee who exceeds the limit. The bill does not identify a particular agency with a canonical registry identity.

HB229.summary: The bill would bar a municipality or county from entering a contract with a private entity to develop or operate a qualifying project unless a majority of voters voting in an election for that purpose approve it. The requirement would apply only to contracts entered into on or after the Act’s effective date; earlier contracts would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill limits when municipalities and counties may enter qualifying-project contracts.
It makes voter approval at an election a condition for these contracts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision applies generally to municipalities and counties and specifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities and counties
affected_groups.explanation: For a contract with a private entity to develop or operate a qualifying project, a municipality or county may not enter it unless a majority of voters voting at an election held for that purpose approves it.

affected_groups.group: Municipal and county voters
affected_groups.explanation: Municipal or county voters voting at an election held for that purpose decide whether to approve such covered contracts; the contract may be entered only if a majority approves it.

affected_groups.group: Private entities seeking qualifying-project contracts
affected_groups.explanation: A private entity's contract with a municipality or county to develop or operate a qualifying project may be entered only if a majority of voters voting at an election held for that purpose approves it.

major_effects.label: Voter approval for qualifying-project contracts
major_effects.explanation: A municipality or county could enter a covered contract only after approval by a majority of voters voting in an election held for that purpose.

HB230.summary: HB 230 would let a certified person who employs at least one apprentice in a qualified apprenticeship for at least seven months in a calendar year claim a $2,500-per-apprentice sales and use tax refund, subject to Subsections (d) and (e), limited to taxes paid and ordinarily capped at one apprentice. The cap could rise to six if at least half of the apprentices employed are from specified groups; the Texas Workforce Commission executive director would certify no more than 100 persons, and refunds would apply only to apprentices first employed on or after January 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a sales and use tax refund for eligible persons employing apprentices.
The refund incentivizes qualifying apprenticeship employment and training.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The refund concerns taxes paid under the Texas Tax Code, with no narrower geographic limit on eligibility.

locations.name: Areas of Texas not designated as metropolitan statistical areas
locations.explanation: The selection rules must give preference to applicants offering apprenticeships in these areas.

affected_groups.group: Persons employing apprentices in qualified apprenticeship positions
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible, certified employers may seek refunds subject to the bill's employment, apprentice-count, and tax-paid limits.

affected_groups.group: Apprentices who are foster children transitioning to independent living, military veterans, military spouses, or women
affected_groups.explanation: These groups can count toward the condition for an employer to claim refunds for as many as six apprentices.

major_effects.label: Apprentice-employer tax refunds
major_effects.explanation: Creates a refund of $2,500 per qualifying apprentice, subject to the apprentice-count limit and capped at the person's sales and use taxes paid for the calendar year.

major_effects.label: Employer certification
major_effects.explanation: Establishes certification as a prerequisite to applying for a refund and limits the executive director to certifying 100 persons at a time.

major_effects.label: Merit-based certification selection
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules establishing merit-based selection criteria, including preferences for nonmetropolitan apprenticeship locations and training in emerging or developing fields.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the executive director as the executive director of the Texas Workforce Commission and assigns that official certification, application, and rulemaking duties.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill directs the comptroller to receive refund applications and any required supporting information.

HB231.summary: The bill would require blood banks to comply with physician orders for autologous or direct blood donations, and licensed hospitals that facilitate donations to allow such donations for individuals undergoing a medical procedure. Blood banks could charge a reasonable fee limited to administrative costs, and direct donations would remain subject to the federal and state requirements applicable to anonymous donations.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes blood donation requirements for blood banks and certain hospitals.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and its requirements apply statewide.

affected_groups.group: Individuals undergoing medical procedures who seek autologous or direct blood donations
affected_groups.explanation: Hospitals covered by the bill would have to allow physician-ordered donations for these individuals.

affected_groups.group: Blood banks
affected_groups.explanation: Blood banks would have to comply with physician orders and could charge a limited administrative fee.

affected_groups.group: Hospitals licensed under Chapter 241 that facilitate blood donations
affected_groups.explanation: These hospitals would have to allow physician-ordered autologous or direct donations for patients undergoing procedures.

major_effects.label: Required accommodation of physician-ordered donations
major_effects.explanation: Blood banks must comply with physician orders, and covered hospitals must allow donations for individuals undergoing a procedure; direct donations remain subject to requirements applicable to anonymous donations.

major_effects.label: Administrative cost fee
major_effects.explanation: A blood bank may charge a reasonable fee only to cover its administrative cost of facilitating the ordered donation.

HB232.summary: The bill changes the conditions for required in vitro fertilization coverage under group health benefit plans: it removes the requirement that fertilization use the patient's spouse's sperm and changes the infertility-history condition from five years for the patient and spouse to at least three years for the patient or spouse. Other conditions remain, including prior unsuccessful less costly covered treatment and use of a facility meeting American Society for Reproductive Medicine standards; the changes apply to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes conditions for required coverage of in vitro fertilization procedures under group health benefit plans.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The coverage-condition changes apply to qualifying health benefit plans under the amended Texas law, rather than to a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: Patients and spouses seeking in vitro fertilization
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes whose infertility history may satisfy a coverage condition and shortens the required duration.

affected_groups.group: Group health benefit plans and their issuers
affected_groups.explanation: The revised coverage conditions apply to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after the specified date.

major_effects.label: Revises conditions for required IVF coverage
major_effects.explanation: Removes the spouse-sperm restriction and permits the patient's or spouse's infertility history of at least three years to satisfy the history condition; the other stated coverage conditions remain.

HB233.summary: The bill would add a short title, the “Terrin Solbrig Act,” to Chapter 125, Acts of the 88th Legislature. The supplied text makes no other substantive change.

major_effects.label: Short title
major_effects.explanation: Adds a short title for the existing Act without changing its substantive provisions in the supplied text.

HB234.summary: HB 234 would provide a January 2028 cost-of-living adjustment of 2% to 8% for qualifying annuitants whose benefits are based on employee-class service, subject to specified eligibility dates and living-status rules. It would also provide eligible annuitants a one-time January 2028 payment of $2,500 to $10,000, with eligibility subject to specified service-class and retirement or payment-date limits. Neither benefit could be paid unless the Employees Retirement System of Texas trustees find that the Legislature appropriated sufficient money to provide it without increasing the system’s unfunded actuarial liabilities; the appropriation must be in addition to the state’s otherwise-required contributions to the system.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes retirement benefits for qualifying annuitants based on service credited in the employee class.
Provides for increased retirement-benefit payments, contingent on sufficient legislative appropriations; the bill does not itself appropriate the money.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes concern benefits administered by the statewide Employees Retirement System of Texas.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying Employees Retirement System of Texas employee-class annuitants and beneficiaries
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible retirees, beneficiaries, disability annuitants, death-benefit annuitants, and alternate payees may receive the adjustment or supplemental payment, subject to the bill’s eligibility limits.

major_effects.label: Cost-of-living adjustment
major_effects.explanation: Creates a January 2028 adjustment for eligible employee-class benefits, with rates of 2% to 8% determined by the relevant retirement, death, or alternate-payee election date; specified cutoff and living-status requirements apply.

major_effects.label: One-time supplemental payment
major_effects.explanation: Provides eligible annuitants a payment in January 2028, ranging from $2,500 to $10,000 according to the relevant retirement, death, or alternate-payee election date.

major_effects.label: Benefits conditioned on sufficient appropriations
major_effects.explanation: Neither benefit may be paid unless the trustees find that the Legislature appropriated sufficient additional money to provide it without increasing unfunded actuarial liabilities; the bill itself does not make an appropriation.

agencies.name: Employees Retirement System of Texas
agencies.explanation: The system is assigned the one-time payment, while its board of trustees administers the adjustment and determines eligibility and amounts, subject to the funding condition.

HB235.summary: The bill directs the Texas Interagency Council for the Homeless to study housing needs and homelessness risks for youth transitioning from foster care or the juvenile justice system, including specified dual-status and disproportionately represented youth, and to evaluate relevant state agency programs and practices. By November 1, 2028, the council must submit a report with legislative recommendations to the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs and the legislature; the Act expires December 31, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires a study focused on housing needs and homelessness risks among youth transitioning from foster care or the juvenile justice system.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The study addresses homelessness risks for youth in this state.

affected_groups.group: Youth transitioning from foster care or the juvenile justice system to independent living
affected_groups.explanation: Their housing needs and homelessness risks are the subject of the required study.

affected_groups.group: Youth previously classified as dual-status children and youth from disproportionately represented populations
affected_groups.explanation: The council must assess the unique housing needs of these youth.

major_effects.label: Housing needs study
major_effects.explanation: Requires a study of housing needs and homelessness risks for youth leaving foster care or the juvenile justice system, including an assessment of relevant agency programs and practices.

major_effects.label: Study report and recommendations
major_effects.explanation: Requires the council to submit study results and legislative recommendations to the department and legislature.

agencies.name: Texas Interagency Council for the Homeless
agencies.explanation: The council is assigned the study and the duty to prepare and submit its report.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
agencies.explanation: The department is a required recipient of the council's report.

HB236.summary: The bill would designate February 4 as Muslim Heritage Day in Texas, recognizing Muslim Americans’ historic, cultural, and social contributions. Appropriate ceremonies and activities could be held to observe the day.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The designation recognizes contributions to this state.

affected_groups.group: Muslim Americans
affected_groups.explanation: Their contributions are recognized by the designated observance.

major_effects.label: Designates Muslim Heritage Day
major_effects.explanation: Designates February 4 as Muslim Heritage Day; appropriate ceremonies and activities may be held.

HB237.summary: The bill directs the commission to create optional Texas Rising Star certifications that can enhance providers’ ratings, including a certification for providers who include children with disabilities alongside typically developing peers. It also establishes annual grants for providers receiving or maintaining a certification, subject to application, and directs the Texas Workforce Commission to adopt implementing rules.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes certifications in the Texas Rising Star child-care quality program, including one focused on inclusion of children with disabilities.
Establishes a grant program providing additional funding to qualifying child-care providers.

locations.name: Texas (statewide)
locations.explanation: The bill changes the Texas Rising Star Program and its provider certifications and grants.

affected_groups.group: Child-care providers participating in the Texas Rising Star Program
affected_groups.explanation: Providers may obtain optional certifications that enhance their program rating and may receive grants while they receive or maintain a certification.

affected_groups.group: Children with disabilities
affected_groups.explanation: Their inclusion with typically developing peers is the subject of a required provider certification; the bill does not create an individual entitlement for children.

major_effects.label: Optional provider certifications
major_effects.explanation: Creates optional certifications that can enhance a provider’s Texas Rising Star rating, including one addressing inclusion of children with disabilities.

major_effects.label: Certification-linked provider grants
major_effects.explanation: Creates grants for providers who receive or maintain an optional certification; grant amounts must consider the ages of children served and provider enrollment capacity.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules to administer the new section and directs the Texas Workforce Commission to adopt rules necessary for implementation.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission responsibility for creating certifications, administering grants, and adopting rules, but the supplied text does not establish the commission’s identity.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly directs the Texas Workforce Commission to adopt rules necessary to implement the new section.

HB238.summary: HB 238 would require three-fifths voter approval for school-district bonds under Education Code Section 45.001 and taxes described there, while requiring majority approval for taxes under Section 45.002 except as provided by that section. It also applies the election-calling procedure to both types of election; the changes take effect January 1, 2028, only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment, and otherwise the Act has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes voter-approval requirements for school-district bond elections.
Changes the approval threshold and applies the election-calling procedure to both specified election types.
Raises the voter-approval threshold for taxes described by Section 45.001 while retaining majority approval for Section 45.002 taxes.
Affects school-district election costs and the local governing bodies that call the elections.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to school-district elections across the state.

affected_groups.group: Qualified voters in school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Their approval threshold for Section 45.001 bonds and related taxes would increase.

affected_groups.group: School districts and their governing boards
affected_groups.explanation: Districts bear the election expense, and their governing boards call the specified elections.

affected_groups.group: School-district taxpayers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes the approval threshold for levying taxes described by Section 45.001; Section 45.002 taxes retain a majority threshold.

major_effects.label: Higher voter-approval threshold
major_effects.explanation: Requires three-fifths approval for bonds under Section 45.001 and taxes described by that section. The amended requirement applies only to elections ordered on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Majority threshold for Section 45.002 taxes, subject to exceptions in the section
major_effects.explanation: Requires majority voter approval to levy taxes described by Section 45.002, except as provided by the section.

major_effects.label: Election-calling procedure applies to both election types
major_effects.explanation: Requires each election under either subsection to be called by a governing-board resolution or commissioners-court order.

HB239.summary: HB 239 would automatically apply municipal firefighter and police civil service requirements to municipalities with at least 25,000 residents and a paid fire or police department, without an adoption election. It would require sheriff's departments in counties with at least 250,000 residents to adopt civil service; newly covered municipalities and counties would have to implement the applicable system. Qualifying municipal employees with more than six months of service would receive the specified civil service status, and employees whose primary duties are municipal emergency medical services would be treated as firefighters under the chapter.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes civil service requirements and implementation duties for qualifying municipal and county governments.
Changes civil service status and examination requirements for certain municipal firefighters and police officers.
Changes civil service coverage for municipal fire and police departments and county sheriff's departments.

locations.name: Municipalities with at least 25,000 residents and a paid fire or police department
locations.explanation: These municipalities become subject to the amended municipal civil service chapter.

locations.name: Counties with at least 250,000 residents
locations.explanation: Sheriff's departments in these counties must adopt a civil service system.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Must implement the municipal civil service system when the chapter becomes applicable.

affected_groups.group: Municipal firefighters and police officers, including certain emergency medical services employees
affected_groups.explanation: Some incumbent employees receive civil service status without a competitive examination, and employees primarily providing municipal emergency medical services are treated as firefighters under the chapter.

affected_groups.group: Sheriff's departments and county governments in counties with at least 250,000 residents
affected_groups.explanation: The sheriff's department must adopt a civil service system, which the county must implement when applicable.

major_effects.label: Municipal civil service coverage
major_effects.explanation: Sets a 25,000-person threshold for municipalities with a paid fire or police department and makes the chapter applicable without an adoption election.

major_effects.label: Status of certain municipal employees
major_effects.explanation: Employees with more than six months of service who are entitled to civil service classification receive civil service status and need not take a competitive examination to remain in their current positions. Certain employees primarily providing municipal emergency medical services are treated as firefighters under the chapter.

major_effects.label: Required county sheriff civil service systems
major_effects.explanation: Requires sheriff's departments in counties with populations of at least 250,000 to adopt a civil service system.

major_effects.label: Municipal civil service bodies
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a civil service commission and a director's office in each municipality subject to the chapter.

HB240.summary: For qualifying water or sewer system acquisitions with applications filed on or after the Act’s effective date, HB 240 would let the acquiring utility charge the system’s rates in force on the application date or ask its regulator to approve rates in force for another system in the utility’s tariff. While the acquisition is pending, the utility could not initiate a new rate proceeding, and the regulator could not require one to establish initial rates for the alternate-rate request. The section would not apply to rates charged under Water Code Section 13.046.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes rate-setting rules for utilities providing water or sewer service after acquiring a system.
Changes the initial rates that may be charged for water or sewer service after a system acquisition.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a Water Code rule for qualifying system acquisitions and contains no geographic limitation to a particular area.

affected_groups.group: Utilities applying to purchase or acquire water or sewer systems
affected_groups.explanation: They receive the specified initial-rate options and are barred from initiating a new rate proceeding while the acquisition is pending.

affected_groups.group: Customers of acquired water or sewer systems
affected_groups.explanation: The rates initially charged to them may remain at the acquired system’s rates or, with regulatory authorization, use rates from another system.

affected_groups.group: Regulatory authorities with original jurisdiction over water or sewer rates
affected_groups.explanation: They may not require a new rate proceeding for the utility’s specified request to use another system’s rates.

major_effects.label: Initial-rate options after acquisition
major_effects.explanation: A utility may charge the acquired system’s rates in force when the application is filed or request authorization to use rates then in force for another system in its tariff. This section excludes rates charged under Water Code Section 13.046.

major_effects.label: Limits on new rate proceedings during acquisition
major_effects.explanation: During the purchase or acquisition, the utility may not initiate a new rate proceeding; the regulatory authority also may not require one to establish initial rates for the specified alternate-rate request.

agencies.name: Regulatory authority with original jurisdiction over the rates
agencies.explanation: The bill directly limits the regulatory authority’s ability to require a new rate proceeding for an alternate-rate request. The bill text does not identify which specific state body, if any, holds that authority in a given case.

HB241.summary: HB 241 would authorize county and district attorneys, in addition to the attorney general, to enforce human-trafficking awareness and prevention requirements for commercial lodging establishments. Local prosecutors could issue the required opportunity-to-cure notice and sue for civil penalties or injunctive relief; penalties they recover would be payable to the county where the violation occurred.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands enforcement of legal requirements applicable to commercial lodging establishment operators.
Gives county and district attorneys enforcement authority and directs locally recovered civil penalties to the relevant county.
Changes enforcement of human-trafficking awareness and prevention requirements in commercial lodging establishments.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The enforcement provisions apply to covered commercial lodging establishments and violations in counties across Texas, without naming a particular county.

affected_groups.group: Operators of commercial lodging establishments
affected_groups.explanation: May receive cure notices and face civil penalty or injunctive actions from additional enforcing officials.

affected_groups.group: County attorneys and district attorneys
affected_groups.explanation: Would gain authority to issue notices and bring enforcement actions under the chapter.

affected_groups.group: Counties
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive civil penalties recovered by a county or district attorney for violations occurring in the county.

major_effects.label: Local enforcement authority
major_effects.explanation: Adds county and district attorneys as officials who may provide cure notices and bring actions to recover civil penalties or obtain injunctive relief.

major_effects.label: Local allocation of recovered penalties
major_effects.explanation: Civil penalties recovered by county or district attorneys are payable to the county where the violation occurred.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The Attorney General remains an authorized enforcer under the amended provisions, which also revise the action and recovery provisions applying to enforcement actions.

HB242.summary: HB 242 would expand a Family Code protection so individuals, religious organizations and related organizations, clergy, and certain employees could refuse to solemnize a marriage or provide related services when doing so would violate a sincerely held religious belief. It would bar civil causes of action based on such a refusal and bar the state or a political subdivision from taking action to penalize or withhold specified benefits from protected individuals or organizations.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands protections for religious-belief-based refusals to provide marriage-related services and limits legal recourse for such refusals.
Restricts political subdivisions from penalizing protected individuals or organizations or withholding benefits from them based on a covered refusal.
Limits state and local government actions, including withholding governmental contracts, grants, or licenses, in response to a covered refusal.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The restrictions apply to actions by the state and its political subdivisions across Texas.

affected_groups.group: Individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs
affected_groups.explanation: Would extend the refusal protection to individuals when providing covered marriage-related services would violate their sincerely held religious belief.

affected_groups.group: Religious organizations, related organizations, clergy, ministers, and certain employees
affected_groups.explanation: These providers are included in the protection from being required to solemnize marriages or provide related services when the statutory belief condition is met.

affected_groups.group: People seeking marriage-related services
affected_groups.explanation: Covered providers may refuse marriage-related services when the statutory religious-belief condition is met.

major_effects.label: Expanded religious-belief-based refusal protection
major_effects.explanation: Would protect individuals as well as specified religious organizations, related organizations, clergy, ministers, and employees from being required to solemnize a marriage or provide related services when doing so would violate the applicable sincerely held religious belief.

major_effects.label: Limits on legal and governmental action
major_effects.explanation: Would make a covered refusal unavailable as the basis for a civil cause of action and bar state or political-subdivision actions to penalize or withhold benefits or privileges from protected individuals or organizations.

HB243.summary: The bill would restrict when day-care centers, group day-care homes, and registered family homes may deny care to a child with a disability: after meeting with the child and family, the center or home must determine under the Americans with Disabilities Act that accommodating the child would pose an undue burden. It would provide for certified childhood-intervention providers to access client children for services under an individualized family service plan while the child is integrated in an educational or instructional area.

HB244.summary: HB 244 would require the child health plan to cover FDA-approved prescription contraceptive drugs, supplies, or devices, subject to Subsection (i). The plan may not cover abortifacients or other drugs or devices that terminate a pregnancy. For an enrolled child under 18, coverage for primary and preventive reproductive health care is permitted only if the provider receives written consent from a person authorized under the specified Family Code provisions.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes covered reproductive health benefits under the child health plan and conditions coverage for minors on written consent.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends benefits under the Texas child health plan rather than targeting a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Children enrolled in the child health plan
affected_groups.explanation: Enrollees gain access to covered contraceptives, subject to the bill's limits; coverage for enrollees under 18 is permitted only with the specified written consent.

affected_groups.group: Parents, guardians, managing conservators, and other persons authorized to consent
affected_groups.explanation: These people may provide written consent for contraceptive coverage for an enrolled child under 18, as authorized by the bill's terms.

affected_groups.group: Prescribing and dispensing health care providers
affected_groups.explanation: Providers must receive the required written consent before the plan may cover contraceptives for an enrolled child under 18 for the stated purpose.

major_effects.label: Child health plan contraceptive coverage
major_effects.explanation: Requires coverage of FDA-approved prescription contraceptives, but bars coverage of abortifacients and other drugs or devices that terminate pregnancy. For enrollees under 18, the plan may cover contraceptives for primary and preventive reproductive care only with the specified written consent.

major_effects.label: Conditional federal waiver process
major_effects.explanation: If an affected state agency determines a federal waiver or authorization is necessary before implementation, it must request it and may delay implementation of that provision until it is granted.

agencies.name: executive commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill amends the executive commissioner's duty to ensure primary and preventive benefits exclude reproductive services, making that duty subject to the new contraceptive coverage provision. The bill does not identify the commissioner's agency.

agencies.name: agency affected by the provision
agencies.explanation: If it determines a federal waiver or authorization is necessary before implementation, the affected agency must request it and may delay implementation until it is granted; the bill does not identify that agency.

HB245.summary: HB 245 would let the Texas Transportation Commission authorize the City of Roma to issue oversize- or overweight-vehicle permits for cargo on specified Starr County roads. That authorization could occur only after the applicable U.S. 83 Strategic Highway Network designation ends, or overweight vehicles are authorized on the network or applicable U.S. 83 segment. Roma could charge up to $200 per trip, except that it may adjust the maximum fee each September 1 to reflect the preceding year’s CPI-U percentage change. Fees are restricted to roadway and administrative costs and distributed between the city and state.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a permit process and movement rules for oversize or overweight vehicles on specified roads.
Gives the City of Roma authority to issue permits and collect and use permit fees.
Directs the state's share of permit fee revenue to the state highway fund and limits permitted uses of collected fees.
Sets movement speed limits, excludes specified hazardous-material vehicles from permits, and makes a speed-limit violation a moving violation.

locations.name: Starr County specified roadways
locations.explanation: The permit process is limited to specified roadway segments in Starr County.

locations.name: City of Roma
locations.explanation: Roma is the local government that may be authorized to issue the permits and collect fees.

affected_groups.group: City of Roma
affected_groups.explanation: May receive permit-issuing authority, collect fees, and use permitted revenues for road and administrative costs.

affected_groups.group: Carriers and operators of oversize or overweight cargo vehicles
affected_groups.explanation: May use the permit process on the specified roads, subject to route, weight, timing, and speed restrictions.

affected_groups.group: Operators of certain overweight hazardous-materials tank vehicles
affected_groups.explanation: Cannot receive permits under this subchapter when their vehicles meet the specified axle and placarded-material conditions.

major_effects.label: Conditional local permit authority
major_effects.explanation: The commission may authorize Roma to issue permits on listed roads, but only after one of the federal-network or overweight-operation conditions is met.

major_effects.label: Permit fees and roadway revenue
major_effects.explanation: Roma may charge a per-trip fee; revenue is limited to roadway operation and maintenance and city administration capped at 15 percent, with the balance shared by lane-mile calculations and the state's portion deposited in the highway fund.

major_effects.label: Permit reporting
major_effects.explanation: Roma must report permits issued under the subchapter to TxDOT.

major_effects.label: Pavement management plan
major_effects.explanation: Requires TxDOT to create a pavement management plan for the specified roadways.

major_effects.label: Vehicle and movement limits
major_effects.explanation: Permits are subject to vehicle and route conditions, including a 125,000-pound gross-weight ceiling and an exclusion for specified hazardous-materials tank vehicles.

major_effects.label: Speed-limit enforcement
major_effects.explanation: Permitted movement cannot exceed the posted limit or 55 mph, whichever is lower; violations are moving violations, and DPS may enforce the subchapter.

agencies.name: Texas Transportation Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly identifies the commission and authorizes it to permit Roma to issue permits, potentially require a surety bond, and adopt implementing rules.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: Receives permit reports, must create a pavement management plan, and is the payee for any required surety bond.

agencies.name: Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: Is expressly given authority to enforce the new subchapter.

agencies.name: comptroller
agencies.explanation: Receives the state's share of permit fees for deposit to the state highway fund; the bill uses only the generic title.

HB246.summary: The bill would require employers, except as provided by Labor Code Section 62.057, to pay employees at least the greater of $17 an hour or the federal minimum wage. It would also repeal Labor Code Section 62.151; the supplied text does not explain what that section currently provides.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the statutory minimum wage employers must pay employees.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Labor Code wage requirements, with statewide reach.

affected_groups.group: Employees covered by the minimum-wage requirement
affected_groups.explanation: Their statutory wage floor would be set at the greater of $17 an hour or the federal minimum wage, subject to the stated exception.

affected_groups.group: Employers covered by the minimum-wage requirement
affected_groups.explanation: They would be subject to the revised minimum-wage floor, subject to the stated exception.

major_effects.label: Minimum-wage floor
major_effects.explanation: Would require payment of at least the greater of $17 an hour or the federal minimum wage, except as provided by Labor Code Section 62.057.

HB247.summary: For benefits paid beginning January 1, 2028, the bill directs the Teacher Retirement System of Texas board of trustees to set inflation adjustments for service retirement, disability retirement, and death benefits using specified CPI-W increases. The board may not pay an increase for a calendar year unless it finds that the system is actuarially sound and has money available to pay increased benefits that year. If the system is actuarially sound but available money is insufficient for the full adjustment, the board must calculate and apply the largest adjustment possible while maintaining actuarial soundness. The bill also requires a biennial study of inflation’s effects on annuitants and a report to the legislature, with recommendations when appropriate.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes inflation adjustments to benefits paid through the state retirement system, subject to actuarial-soundness and available-funds limits.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply to benefits paid by the Teacher Retirement System of Texas, rather than to a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: Teacher Retirement System annuitants receiving service retirement, disability retirement, or death benefits
affected_groups.explanation: Their benefits may receive inflation adjustments, subject to the system’s actuarial soundness and available funds.

affected_groups.group: Teacher Retirement System board of trustees
affected_groups.explanation: The board sets adjustment rates, determines whether payment conditions are met, and defines actuarial soundness by rule.

major_effects.label: Inflation-linked benefit adjustments
major_effects.explanation: The board sets an adjustment rate based on specified CPI-W increases and applies it to covered benefits; increases are payable only if the system is actuarially sound and has funds, with a reduced rate when necessary to maintain soundness.

major_effects.label: Definition of actuarial soundness
major_effects.explanation: The board must define “actuarially sound” by rule for purposes of these adjustments.

major_effects.label: Biennial inflation study and legislative report
major_effects.explanation: The system must study inflation’s effects on annuitants and report its findings to the legislature, including potential legislative recommendations when appropriate.

agencies.name: Teacher Retirement System of Texas
agencies.explanation: The system must conduct the annuitant inflation study and report to the legislature; its board of trustees sets benefit adjustment rates and adopts a rule defining actuarial soundness.

HB248.summary: The bill would require social media platforms to attach and retain provenance data for photos, videos, and audio created using the platforms’ generative-AI tools, and to provide users an easy way to access that data. For posted files, the duties apply only when the platform can discern provenance data showing generative-AI creation or modification; a platform may avoid compliance under either section only by providing the attorney general clear and convincing documentation that it lacks the technology and is actively working to obtain it. For posted files, platforms need not independently verify user- or third-party-provided provenance, and inaccurate-data liability protection applies only if the platform meets the bill’s stated conditions.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires provenance metadata identifying generative-AI creation or modification and makes that data accessible to users.
Imposes data attachment, retention, and access requirements on social media platforms.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds generally applicable requirements to Texas law for covered social media platforms.

affected_groups.group: Social media platforms
affected_groups.explanation: Platforms must attach and retain provenance data and provide user access, subject to the bill’s specified conditions and exception.

affected_groups.group: Users of social media platforms, including people posting AI-generated media
affected_groups.explanation: Users may access provenance data, and posted media may have provenance data attached when the platform can discern it and it indicates generative-AI use.

major_effects.label: Provenance data requirements
major_effects.explanation: Requires covered AI-generated media created with platform tools, and qualifying AI-generated or modified media posted to a platform, to have provenance data attached and retained in an industry-adopted format that identifies the AI tool and its provider.

major_effects.label: User access and compliance limits
major_effects.explanation: Platforms must provide an easy access method. Posted-content duties do not require independent verification of user- or third-party-provided provenance, and the bill limits liability for inaccurate data only when its specified conditions are met.

major_effects.label: Conditional lack-of-capacity exception
major_effects.explanation: A platform is excused from compliance under the applicable section only if it provides the attorney general clear and convincing documentation that it lacks the technological capacity and is actively taking steps to obtain it.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The attorney general is the recipient of documentation that can qualify a platform for the lack-of-technological-capacity exception; the bill does not otherwise assign the office an enforcement duty.

HB249.summary: The bill would allow a county bail bond board in a county with fewer than 1.3 million people that contains a municipality of at least 750,000 people to meet at least six times each year, in specified alternating months, rather than monthly. It would extend the existing license-continuation protection to boards under this new schedule: if a renewal application is tabled or not acted on, the current license remains effective until the board’s next meeting; this applies to applications filed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the required meeting schedule for county bail bond boards in qualifying counties.
Extends the period a bail bond license remains effective when a covered board has not acted on a renewal application.

locations.name: Counties with fewer than 1.3 million people that contain a municipality with at least 750,000 people
locations.explanation: The alternative meeting schedule applies to boards in counties meeting both population criteria.

affected_groups.group: County bail bond boards in counties meeting the population criteria
affected_groups.explanation: These boards would have a six-meetings-per-year minimum in the specified months and may meet at other times when called by the presiding officer.

affected_groups.group: Bail bond license holders seeking renewal before a covered board
affected_groups.explanation: Their current license would continue until the board’s next meeting if the renewal application is tabled or the board does not approve or deny it.

major_effects.label: Alternative board meeting schedule
major_effects.explanation: Boards in counties meeting both population criteria would be required to meet at least six times each year in January, March, May, July, September, and November, with additional meetings possible when called by the presiding officer.

major_effects.label: License continuation pending board action
major_effects.explanation: For boards covered by subsection (c) or (d), a current license remains effective until the next board meeting when a renewal application is tabled or the board does not act. The amended provision applies only to renewal applications filed on or after the Act’s effective date.

HB250.summary: The bill would require covered health benefit plans, including the state Medicaid program and other specified plan types, to cover a treating-physician-approved hair prosthesis for an enrollee undergoing or previously treated for breast cancer, with a benefit of at least $100 and no additional premium. Consistent annual cost sharing may apply, and repair or replacement is covered unless necessitated by the enrollee’s misuse or loss; the rules would apply only to plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028, and an affected state agency that determines a federal waiver or authorization is necessary must request it and may delay implementation until it is granted.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a required health benefit for hair prostheses associated with breast cancer treatment.
Expressly extends the new coverage requirement to the state Medicaid program, including Medicaid managed care.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision applies to group health benefit coverage provided to Texas residents, including when the policy is issued outside the state.

affected_groups.group: Enrollees undergoing or previously treated for breast cancer
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive coverage for a hair prosthesis that their treating physician considers appropriate in connection with treatment side effects.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plan providers and sponsors
affected_groups.explanation: Covered plans must provide the specified hair-prosthesis benefit without charging an additional premium.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid enrollees
affected_groups.explanation: The new coverage requirement expressly applies to the state Medicaid program, including Medicaid managed care.

major_effects.label: Required hair-prosthesis coverage
major_effects.explanation: Covered plans must cover a physician-approved hair prosthesis for an enrollee undergoing or previously treated for breast cancer. The benefit must be at least $100, with no additional premium; otherwise consistent annual deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance may apply.

major_effects.label: Repair and replacement coverage
major_effects.explanation: Repair or replacement must be covered unless it is necessitated by the enrollee’s misuse or loss.

major_effects.label: Conditional federal waiver process
major_effects.explanation: If an affected state agency determines before implementation that a federal waiver or authorization is necessary, it must request it and may delay implementation until it is granted.

agencies.name: agency affected by the provision
agencies.explanation: If a state agency determines that a federal waiver or authorization is necessary before implementing a provision, the affected agency must request it. The bill does not identify which agency, if any, will make that determination.

HB251.summary: HB 251 would require reimbursement under the medical assistance program for multisystemic therapy services classified by HCPCS and require a separate provider type for those providers’ enrollment and reimbursement. If an agency determines a federal waiver or authorization is necessary to implement a provision, it must request it and may delay implementation of that provision until it is granted.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes reimbursement and provider enrollment requirements under the medical assistance program.
The reimbursement requirement concerns multisystemic therapy services provided by health care providers.
Requiring medical assistance reimbursement may increase program expenditures for covered services.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes reimbursement under the Texas medical assistance program without limiting the change to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Medical assistance recipients receiving multisystemic therapy
affected_groups.explanation: Their providers would receive reimbursement for qualifying multisystemic therapy services under the program.

affected_groups.group: Health care providers furnishing multisystemic therapy
affected_groups.explanation: Providers furnishing the specified services would be eligible for reimbursement and have a separate provider type for enrollment and reimbursement.

major_effects.label: Medical assistance reimbursement
major_effects.explanation: Requires reimbursement for multisystemic therapy services classified by HCPCS when provided to a medical assistance recipient.

major_effects.label: Separate provider type
major_effects.explanation: Requires a separate provider type for multisystemic therapy providers for enrollment and reimbursement.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission a reimbursement duty and directs the executive commissioner to establish a separate provider type. The bill does not identify the commission by its full agency name.

HB252.summary: HB 252 would require manufacturers of electronics-enabled agricultural implements sold or leased in Texas to make parts, tools, software, and documentation available to owners and independent repair providers on fair and reasonable terms, and to enable non-damaging part replacement using commonly available or manufacturer-provided tools. Violations would be actionable as deceptive trade practices, but the bill preserves limits involving trade secrets and illegal safety or emissions modifications, and conflicting agreements entered before the Act’s effective date would prevail.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill regulates repair and maintenance access for implements used in agricultural operations.
The bill imposes parts, tool, software, and documentation access requirements on manufacturers and makes violations actionable as deceptive trade practices.
The bill regulates access to digital equipment, embedded software, firmware, and diagnostic tools for repair.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The chapter applies to covered implements sold or leased in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Owners and lessees of electronics-enabled agricultural implements
affected_groups.explanation: They would gain access to repair-related parts, tools, software, and documentation, subject to the bill’s terms and limitations.

affected_groups.group: Independent repair providers
affected_groups.explanation: They would be eligible to obtain covered repair resources from manufacturers on fair and reasonable terms.

affected_groups.group: Original equipment manufacturers of covered agricultural implements
affected_groups.explanation: They would have new access and part-replacement obligations and could face deceptive-trade-practice actions for violations.

major_effects.label: Repair-resource access
major_effects.explanation: Manufacturers must provide covered parts, tools, software, updates, and documentation on fair and reasonable terms, including resources for electronic security functions. Trade secrets need not be divulged except as necessary to provide required resources, and the chapter does not permit specified illegal or safety- or emissions-related modifications.

major_effects.label: Non-damaging part replacement
major_effects.explanation: Manufacturers must ensure required parts can be replaced without damage using a commonly available tool or a tool the manufacturer makes available on fair and reasonable terms.

major_effects.label: Deceptive-trade-practice actionability
major_effects.explanation: A violation is designated a deceptive trade practice and is actionable under the existing Business & Commerce Code subchapter.

major_effects.label: Pre-effective-date agreements
major_effects.explanation: If a provision of an agreement entered into before the Act’s effective date conflicts with the new chapter, the agreement provision prevails to the extent of the conflict.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill makes violations deceptive trade practices actionable under Business & Commerce Code Chapter 17, which may implicate the Attorney General’s enforcement authority; the bill does not name the office.

HB253.summary: HB 253 would require the commission to appoint a law enforcement agency other than the local agency operating a county jail to investigate a death of someone in the jail’s custody, regardless of where the death occurs. This expressly includes prisoners temporarily outside the jail for medical treatment, transport, a court appearance, or another purpose; the appointed agency conducts the investigation except as otherwise provided by existing Government Code Section 511.021(b).

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which law enforcement agency investigates deaths of people in county jail custody, including deaths occurring outside the jail.
Expands the circumstances in which an independent law enforcement investigation of a county jail prisoner’s death is required.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change applies to deaths of people in the custody of a county jail, without limiting coverage to a particular county or place of death.

affected_groups.group: People in the custody of a county jail
affected_groups.explanation: Their deaths would require appointment of an investigating agency regardless of where they occur, including while the person is temporarily outside the jail.

affected_groups.group: Law enforcement agencies appointed to investigate
affected_groups.explanation: An appointed agency other than the local law enforcement agency operating the jail would conduct the investigation, subject to the existing Subsection (b) qualification.

affected_groups.group: Local law enforcement agencies operating county jails
affected_groups.explanation: The agency operating the jail is excluded from appointment to investigate the death.

major_effects.label: Broader independent-investigation coverage
major_effects.explanation: Requires appointment of an investigating law enforcement agency for a death in county jail custody regardless of where the death occurs, including when the prisoner is temporarily outside the jail. The appointed agency conducts the investigation except as otherwise provided by Subsection (b).

agencies.name: Commission on Jail Standards
agencies.explanation: Section 511.001 defines “Commission” as the Commission on Jail Standards. Section 511.021(a), as amended by the bill, assigns the commission the duty to appoint a law enforcement agency to investigate a qualifying death.

HB254.summary: For criminal proceedings that commence on or after its effective date, the bill would allow certain video recordings of oral statements by a child under 18 or a person with a disability to be admitted despite the hearsay rule. The recording must meet specified existing requirements, be made during the offense’s initial investigation at a children’s advocacy center by a certified forensic interviewer, and be found reliable by the trial court in a hearing outside the jury’s presence.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the hearsay admissibility rule for recordings used in certain criminal prosecutions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The rule applies to covered criminal proceedings under the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure, without a geographic limitation in the bill.

affected_groups.group: Children under 18 and people with disabilities who make recorded oral statements
affected_groups.explanation: Their qualifying recorded statements could be admitted under the bill’s conditional hearsay exception.

affected_groups.group: People accused in covered prosecutions
affected_groups.explanation: The rule changes whether qualifying recorded statements may be admitted as evidence in the prosecution.

major_effects.label: Conditional hearsay admissibility
major_effects.explanation: Creates a route for admitting qualifying recordings despite the hearsay rule, subject to existing requirements, specified recording and interviewer conditions, and a trial-court reliability finding.

agencies.name: trial court
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the trial court a reliability determination, but does not identify a particular court or canonical judicial-body name.

HB255.summary: The bill would replace annual inspections with semiannual inspections for covered elevators, escalators, and related equipment; a semiannual inspection means two inspections in a 12-month period and may include an acceptance inspection. Owners would have to arrange the inspections unless the equipment is removed from service under commission rules.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill increases inspection frequency for equipment whose condition can pose safety risks to passengers and workers.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing covered equipment without limiting the requirements to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Owners of covered equipment
affected_groups.explanation: Owners would need to arrange semiannual inspections unless the equipment is removed from service in accordance with commission rules.

affected_groups.group: Registered elevator inspectors
affected_groups.explanation: Inspectors would conduct the more frequent inspections required for covered equipment, unless the equipment has been removed from service in accordance with commission rules.

affected_groups.group: Elevator and escalator passengers and workers
affected_groups.explanation: They are the populations whose safety the inspection requirements address.

major_effects.label: Semiannual inspection rules
major_effects.explanation: The commission would be required to provide by rule for semiannual inspection and certification of covered equipment.

major_effects.label: Owner inspection requirement
major_effects.explanation: Owners would have to arrange inspections twice in a 12-month period, unless equipment is removed from service under commission rules; an acceptance inspection may count within that period.

agencies.name: Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: Section 754.011(12) defines “Commission” as the Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation. The bill’s repeal of Section 754.011(4) removes the separate definition of “Annual inspection” and does not affect that identification.

HB256.summary: The bill would authorize a municipality to confiscate a sign placed without municipal authorization on the right-of-way of a road or highway it maintains. This authority would not apply to right-of-way in the state highway system.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds municipal authority to confiscate unauthorized signs on roads and highways maintained by the municipality.
The authority concerns signs placed on road and highway rights-of-way, with an exception for the state highway system.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes municipal authority applicable to municipalities statewide, subject to the state-highway-system exception.

affected_groups.group: Texas municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Municipalities would gain authority to confiscate unauthorized signs on the rights-of-way of roads and highways they maintain.

affected_groups.group: People placing signs on municipal road or highway rights-of-way
affected_groups.explanation: People who place signs without municipal authorization could have those signs confiscated.

major_effects.label: Municipal confiscation authority
major_effects.explanation: Municipalities could confiscate signs placed without authorization on rights-of-way they maintain; this section does not cover rights-of-way in the state highway system.

HB257.summary: Beginning in 2028 and every two years afterward, the bill would require an independent external efficiency audit of Operation Lone Star and other border security programs, examining resource use, effectiveness, potential savings, and related contracts and grants. The Comptroller would select the auditor and ensure the audit meets the bill’s requirements, while the Legislative Budget Board would set its scope; reports and recommendations would be sent to specified officials and legislative committees and published by the Governor and Comptroller. The department would pay audit costs using existing resources.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates recurring independent oversight of the implementation and administration of state border security programs and assigns audit and reporting responsibilities.
Requires the department to pay audit costs from existing resources and directs review of program resource use, contracts, and grants.
Adds audit oversight of Operation Lone Star and other border security programs, including their effectiveness in securing the border.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes an audit requirement for state border security programs and refers to the state's border security goals; it does not identify a particular border locality.

affected_groups.group: State agencies subject to evaluation or receiving or spending money under the covered programs
affected_groups.explanation: The audit must be independent of these agencies, and their use of program resources may be reviewed.

affected_groups.group: Independent external auditors
affected_groups.explanation: An external auditor must be selected to conduct each required audit and must be independent and not subject to direction from the department.

major_effects.label: Recurring efficiency audits
major_effects.explanation: Requires an independent external audit beginning in 2028 and every second year afterward, covering implementation, administration, resource use, effectiveness, and related contracts and grants.

major_effects.label: Audit selection and scope
major_effects.explanation: Assigns the Comptroller responsibility for selecting the auditor and ensuring compliance with the audit requirements, and the Legislative Budget Board responsibility for setting the audit scope.

major_effects.label: Audit reports and publication
major_effects.explanation: Requires the external auditor to submit a report and recommendations in the audit year; the Governor and Comptroller must publish the report, recommendations, and full audit.

major_effects.label: Audit costs from existing resources
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to cover the costs of each required audit using existing resources.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: Must select and contract with the external auditor, ensure the audit follows the bill's requirements, and publish the report, recommendations, and full audit.

agencies.name: Legislative Budget Board
agencies.explanation: Must establish the audit scope and determine areas of investigation.

agencies.name: Governor
agencies.explanation: Receives the audit report and recommendations and must publish them and the full audit on the Governor's website.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: Government Code Chapter 411 defines “Department” as the Department of Public Safety of the State of Texas. Section 411.952 requires the department to pay audit costs using existing resources and bars it from directing the external auditor.

agencies.name: Texas Military Department
agencies.explanation: May not direct the external auditor.

agencies.name: state auditor
agencies.explanation: Is named as a recipient of the audit report and recommendations; the bill uses this title without further identifying the office.

HB258.summary: The bill would require the Texas Medical Board, working with the Department of State Health Services, to establish and publish evidence-based endometriosis screening and diagnosis guidelines by September 1, 2028, and update them at least every five years. The board would report on the guidelines and endometriosis screening and diagnosis timelines every five years, with the reporting requirement expiring September 1, 2040. Physicians whose practice includes reproductive health would be encouraged, but not required, to take related continuing medical education; the board would set rules for course content and approval.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates statewide endometriosis screening and diagnosis guidelines and addresses related physician continuing medical education.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes medical guidelines and continuing education provisions under Texas law without limiting them to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Physicians whose practice includes reproductive health
affected_groups.explanation: They would be encouraged to include endometriosis screening and diagnosis in their continuing medical education; the bill does not make that course-taking mandatory.

affected_groups.group: People with endometriosis
affected_groups.explanation: The guidelines concern screening and diagnosis, and the board's reports would include statistics on patients' screening and diagnostic timelines.

major_effects.label: Endometriosis guidelines
major_effects.explanation: Requires evidence-based screening and diagnosis guidelines to be developed and posted publicly, with updates at least every five years.

major_effects.label: Continuing education course rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the board to set continuing medical education course content and approval requirements based on the guidelines.

major_effects.label: Periodic reports
major_effects.explanation: Requires reports every five years on the guidelines and patient screening and diagnostic timelines; the reporting provision expires September 1, 2040.

major_effects.label: Encouraged physician education
major_effects.explanation: Encourages, but does not require, physicians whose practice includes reproductive health to include related continuing medical education.

agencies.name: Texas Medical Board
agencies.explanation: The bill identifies the board as the Texas Medical Board and assigns it guideline development and publication, reporting, and rulemaking duties.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The board must collaborate with this department on the guidelines, and the bill names the department in the deadline provision.

HB259.summary: The bill would require an open-enrollment charter school's governing body to make the school's annual financial statement available under public-information law and keep it posted on the school's website. It would exempt school districts and open-enrollment charter schools from the newspaper-publication requirements in Local Government Code Section 140.006, while retaining publication rules for entities that remain covered by that section.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a financial-statement posting duty for open-enrollment charter schools and exempts school districts from the specified publication requirements.
Amends financial-statement publication requirements for district governing bodies under the Local Government Code.
Changes how covered public bodies make annual financial statements available to the public.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply to the specified school and district entities statewide.

affected_groups.group: Open-enrollment charter schools and their governing bodies
affected_groups.explanation: Their governing bodies would ensure financial statements are publicly accessible and continuously posted online.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: School districts would be excluded from the newspaper-publication requirements of Local Government Code Section 140.006.

affected_groups.group: Governing bodies of other districts covered by Section 140.006
affected_groups.explanation: Entities that remain covered must submit their financial statements for publication, except as provided by Subsection (e).

major_effects.label: Charter-school financial statement posting
major_effects.explanation: Requires an open-enrollment charter school's governing body to ensure its annual financial statement is available under Chapter 552 and continuously posted on the school's website.

major_effects.label: School-related newspaper-publication exemptions
major_effects.explanation: Exempts school districts and open-enrollment charter schools from Section 140.006; the section retains its two-month publication deadline for entities still covered.

HB260.summary: If voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment establishing the commission, HB 260 would set operating, disclosure, and reporting rules for the independent redistricting commission and make it a fallback for statewide judicial reapportionment if the Judicial Districts Board fails to act. It also updates county precinct-boundary procedures; without voter approval of the amendment, the bill has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill provides for a commission to develop legislative and congressional districts and specifies standards and disclosures for redistricting plans.
It establishes statutory duties, rules, records, and operating procedures for the independent redistricting commission.
The legislature must appropriate sufficient money for commission members' compensation and the expenses of the commission and its staff.
The bill updates the county precinct-boundary rule for redistricting under Article XVIII and requires reporting estimated county costs for necessary changes.

locations.name: Statewide Texas
locations.explanation: The commission's redistricting and potential judicial reapportionment apply statewide.

locations.name: Texas counties with election precinct boundaries requiring changes
locations.explanation: The bill addresses county precinct-boundary changes needed to conform to commission-adopted districts.

affected_groups.group: People living in areas covered by state legislative, congressional, or judicial districts
affected_groups.explanation: Their district boundaries may be set or changed through the redistricting and reapportionment processes addressed by the bill.

affected_groups.group: County governments and commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Counties may incur costs for necessary precinct-boundary changes, which commissioners courts must order when needed to give effect to a plan under Article XVIII.

affected_groups.group: Independent redistricting commission members and staff
affected_groups.explanation: The bill specifies member oath requirements and provides for compensation, expenses, and staff services.

major_effects.label: Commission duties and redistricting standards
major_effects.explanation: Creates statutory procedures for the commission, including rulemaking and limits on considering incumbency, candidate residence, and political performance or voting data, subject to stated federal-law and constitutional exceptions.

major_effects.label: Commission funding
major_effects.explanation: Requires sufficient legislative appropriations for commission members' compensation and commission and staff expenses; unspent commission appropriations revert to the general revenue fund.

major_effects.label: Plan reporting, public access, and records
major_effects.explanation: Requires plan reports to include population and deviation information, criteria and maps, and estimated county precinct-change costs; commission plans and related materials must be made available to the public.

major_effects.label: Fallback for statewide judicial reapportionment
major_effects.explanation: If the Judicial Districts Board fails to complete statewide reapportionment by its deadline, the commission must take over and complete the reapportionment within 90 days after that deadline.

major_effects.label: County precinct-boundary procedures
major_effects.explanation: Updates the Election Code rule to apply when precinct-boundary changes are needed for a redistricting plan under Article XVIII; the commission must estimate the related county costs.

major_effects.label: Challenges to final redistricting plans
major_effects.explanation: Allows a person aggrieved by a final commission plan to petition the supreme court to challenge it.

agencies.name: independent redistricting commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the commission as the body established under Article XVIII of the Texas Constitution and assigns it operating, rulemaking, disclosure, and redistricting duties. No matching canonical registry entry is available.

agencies.name: Texas Legislative Council
agencies.explanation: It must provide technical staff and clerical services at the commission's request; the canonical registry has no matching entry.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The Secretary of State receives adopted plans and must preserve commission records.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Texas Supreme Court receives petitions from persons aggrieved by a final redistricting plan challenging that plan.

HB261.summary: The bill would create a Class B misdemeanor for wearing an identity-concealing mask or other head covering in a public place, including a public school. It provides a defense to prosecution for specified uses, including occupational safety and protecting health or preventing illness.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a misdemeanor offense and specifies a defense to prosecution.

locations.name: Statewide public places, including public schools
locations.explanation: The proposed offense applies to public places statewide and expressly includes public schools; it identifies no narrower locality.
