affected_groups.group: People wearing identity-concealing masks or other head coverings in public places
affected_groups.explanation: Their conduct would be subject to the new offense, subject to the specified defenses.

major_effects.label: New misdemeanor offense
major_effects.explanation: Wearing a mask or other head covering in a public place would be a Class B misdemeanor, with a defense to prosecution for the specified uses, including safety, artistic, emergency, and health-related purposes.

HB262.summary: HB 262 would expand the definition of stationary commercial surface disposal facilities to cover certain facilities disposing of drill cuttings, drilling mud, or other solid or semi-solid oil. For these facilities, the commission could not approve a permit application unless the applicant demonstrated the necessity for an additional facility in the commission-established primary market area where the facility would be located. Applicants would have to submit specified location, well-count, and feasibility information, and pay a nonrefundable $100,000 application fee; the fee would not apply to renewal or modification of a permit already in effect before September 1, 2027. The bill would also require financial security for these facilities and apply associated permit procedures to the expanded category.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes permit application requirements, financial security requirements, and fees for commercial oil and gas waste disposal facilities.
The bill changes permitting and financial assurance requirements for facilities that dispose of oil and gas waste.
The bill imposes an application fee and directs proceeds from financial security required under this section to the oil and gas regulation and cleanup fund.

locations.name: Commission-established primary market area and 30-mile radius around the proposed facility site
locations.explanation: The necessity showing concerns the commission-established primary market area, and the application must provide facility and well information within a 30-mile radius of the proposed site.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for stationary commercial surface disposal facility permits
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants must demonstrate necessity, provide specified supporting information, and pay the application fee, subject to the stated renewal and modification exception.

affected_groups.group: Operators and permittees of stationary commercial surface disposal facilities
affected_groups.explanation: They would be required to maintain financial security conditioned on operating and closing the facility in accordance with applicable law, rules, and permit terms.

major_effects.label: Necessity condition for permits
major_effects.explanation: The commission may not approve a permit application unless the applicant demonstrates the necessity of an additional facility in the commission-established primary market area.

major_effects.label: Information required with applications
major_effects.explanation: Applicants must provide a map and list of permitted facilities and a prior-year well count within 30 miles of the proposed site, as well as other relevant economic, environmental, and feasibility information.

major_effects.label: Application fee and financial-security proceeds
major_effects.explanation: The bill imposes a nonrefundable $100,000 fee with each covered permit application, except for renewal or modification of a permit in effect before September 1, 2027. Subject to the refund provisions of Section 91.1091, proceeds from required financial security go to the oil and gas regulation and cleanup fund.

major_effects.label: Financial security requirement
major_effects.explanation: Applicants for or persons operating under a permit for a stationary commercial surface disposal facility must maintain a performance bond or other financial security covering operation and closure.

major_effects.label: Expanded facility coverage
major_effects.explanation: The definition expressly includes certain stationary facilities that provide surface disposal of drill cuttings, drilling mud, or other solid or semi-solid oil, bringing that defined category within the associated notice and permit provisions.

agencies.name: Railroad Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill identifies the Railroad Commission of Texas as the regulator and assigns it permitting-related responsibilities, including evaluating necessity demonstrations and receiving application fees and supporting information.

HB263.summary: The bill bars the board from awarding money under Chapter 58A or making a grant or distribution under Section 61.0594 for a graduate medical education program provided by a teaching hospital in partnership with a medical school located outside Texas. It restricts eligibility for these state funding streams; it does not prohibit the partnerships themselves.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility for funding graduate medical education programs.
The funding restriction directly concerns graduate medical education at teaching hospitals.
Restricts which programs may receive state funding through two statutory funding mechanisms.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The funding restrictions apply generally to the cited state funding mechanisms.

locations.name: Outside this state
locations.explanation: The restriction applies when the partner medical school is located outside Texas.

affected_groups.group: Teaching hospitals partnering with medical schools located outside Texas
affected_groups.explanation: Their graduate medical education programs are ineligible for the specified state funding.

affected_groups.group: Graduate medical education programs
affected_groups.explanation: Programs provided or to be provided through the specified partnerships cannot receive the covered funding.

major_effects.label: Restricts funding eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Makes graduate medical education programs involving a teaching hospital and an out-of-state medical school ineligible for awards under Chapter 58A and grants or distributions under Section 61.0594.

agencies.name: the board
agencies.explanation: The bill directly prohibits this body from awarding specified money or making specified grants or distributions. The bill uses only the generic term “the board,” so its canonical identity is not established by the supplied sources.

HB264.summary: The bill would require a health benefit plan that covers prescription contraceptive devices to also cover evidence-based anxiety and pain management related to device insertion or removal. The requirement would apply only to plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required health benefit coverage for anxiety and pain management associated with contraceptive-device procedures.
Imposes a coverage obligation on health benefit plans that cover prescription contraceptive devices.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Insurance Code requirements for health benefit plans without limiting the coverage requirement to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: People receiving insertion or removal of prescription contraceptive devices
affected_groups.explanation: They could receive coverage for evidence-based anxiety and pain management when their plan covers the device.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plans that cover prescription contraceptive devices
affected_groups.explanation: These plans would be required to cover the specified anxiety and pain management, subject to the bill's applicability date.

major_effects.label: Required coverage for procedure-related anxiety and pain management
major_effects.explanation: Plans that cover prescription contraceptive devices would also have to cover evidence-based anxiety and pain management related to insertion or removal; the requirement applies only to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

HB265.summary: Subject to the chapter’s exemptions, HB265 would create a licensing and safety framework for operators providing compensated swim instruction to groups of three or more children under age seven, with exceptions for instruction provided by licensed youth camps, regulated child-care facilities, and political subdivisions. It would require training, criminal-history checks, and serious-incident reporting, authorize fees and administrative penalties, and restrict disclosure and retention of criminal-history information.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates occupational licensing, operating standards, and administrative enforcement for covered swim instruction operators.
Requires minimum safety standards and training for operators and their staff serving young children.
Sets confidentiality, disclosure, and destruction rules for criminal-history information obtained by swim instruction operators.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds requirements to Texas law for covered swim instruction operators; it does not limit them to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Covered child swim instruction operators
affected_groups.explanation: Operators providing instruction to groups of at least three students are covered, except for the specified youth camps, child-care facilities, and political subdivisions.

affected_groups.group: Children under age seven receiving swim instruction
affected_groups.explanation: These children are the students covered by the chapter's safety requirements and serious-incident protections.

affected_groups.group: Swim-instruction managers, instructors, and other employees who interact with students
affected_groups.explanation: Managers and instructors would face certification requirements, while employees and prospective student-facing hires would be subject to training or criminal-history requirements.

major_effects.label: Operator licensing
major_effects.explanation: A person may not operate as a swim instruction operator without a license issued under the chapter.

major_effects.label: Safety and operating standards
major_effects.explanation: Directs the commission to set operating, licensing, training, and minimum safety standards, including instructor-to-student ratios and emergency equipment requirements.

major_effects.label: Incident reporting and inspection-report access
major_effects.explanation: Requires operators to report serious incidents to the department and provide recent department inspection reports to the public on request.

major_effects.label: Criminal-history screening
major_effects.explanation: Requires checks for license applicants and controlling persons, and bars hiring certain student-facing workers convicted of specified offenses involving minors.

major_effects.label: Administrative enforcement
major_effects.explanation: Makes violations subject to administrative penalties and other enforcement action, with the administrative penalty capped at $500 per day per violation.

major_effects.label: Criminal-history information safeguards
major_effects.explanation: Limits release of criminal-history information obtained by an operator, except to the person who is the subject of the information, and requires its destruction after use for the authorized purpose.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The department would administer and enforce the new chapter, issue licenses, conduct specified applicant and controlling-person criminal-history checks, and receive serious-incident reports.

agencies.name: Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The commission would adopt implementing and safety rules and set fees. The available registry does not separately identify this named commission.

HB266.summary: The bill would prohibit applying biosolids—including Class A, Class AB, and Class B materials—to agricultural land used for plant or food production, grazing, or raising livestock. It would limit the related land-application permitting framework to non-agricultural uses and cause TCEQ authorizations that allow agricultural-land application to expire when the Act takes effect, while leaving other parts of a combined authorization in effect if they do not authorize that application. It would also remove crops grown and the suggested agronomic application rate from the listed minimum contents of quarterly reports.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill prohibits biosolids application on land used for specified agricultural purposes.
The bill changes restrictions and authorization rules for applying sewage-treatment biosolids to land.

locations.name: Agricultural land as defined by the bill
locations.explanation: The prohibition applies to land used for plant or food production, animal grazing, or raising livestock.

affected_groups.group: People and businesses applying biosolids
affected_groups.explanation: They may not apply biosolids to agricultural land under the bill.

affected_groups.group: Holders of TCEQ authorizations for agricultural-land biosolids application
affected_groups.explanation: Authorizations allowing that application would expire when the Act takes effect; other authorization terms remain only if they do not allow the prohibited application.

affected_groups.group: Agricultural land users, including growers, grazing operators, and livestock raisers
affected_groups.explanation: Their land is within the bill's defined agricultural-land category and would be subject to the application prohibition.

major_effects.label: Prohibits application on agricultural land
major_effects.explanation: A person may not apply biosolids to agricultural land or incorporate them into its soil; the defined term includes Class A, Class AB, and Class B materials.

major_effects.label: Expires authorizations for agricultural application
major_effects.explanation: TCEQ permits, registrations, and other authorizations allowing agricultural-land application would expire when the Act takes effect; other parts of a combined authorization remain effective only to the extent they do not allow that application.

major_effects.label: Changes the land-application permit framework to cover non-agricultural purposes
major_effects.explanation: The amended definition covers land application units used for non-agricultural purposes, including treatment and disposal and maintaining public parks, golf courses, and athletic fields.

major_effects.label: Removes two items from the listed minimum quarterly report contents
major_effects.explanation: The bill removes crops grown at the site and the suggested agronomic application rate from the enumerated report contents. This does not preclude the commission from requiring other monitoring or reporting.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill causes TCEQ-issued authorizations allowing biosolids application to agricultural land to expire, while preserving other portions of combined authorizations that do not allow that application.

HB267.summary: The bill directs the commissioner to develop training resources for school administrators about bilingual education and dual language immersion programs. It also requires agency rules for monitoring bilingual and special language programs, including district engagement and technical assistance, and allows those rules to require additional program information in districts’ PEIMS reports.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds administrator training resources and monitoring and reporting provisions for public school language programs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply generally to school districts subject to the state bilingual or special language program requirements.

affected_groups.group: School administrators
affected_groups.explanation: They are the intended audience for the new training resources.

affected_groups.group: School districts offering bilingual education or special language programs
affected_groups.explanation: They are subject to the added reporting provisions and agency engagement or technical assistance.

affected_groups.group: Emergent bilingual students
affected_groups.explanation: The monitoring rules must focus on meeting their needs and closing learning gaps, and the agency's district engagement is directed toward improving their outcomes.

major_effects.label: Administrator training resources
major_effects.explanation: The commissioner must develop and make available training materials and other resources about bilingual education and dual language immersion programs.

major_effects.label: Program monitoring and district support
major_effects.explanation: Agency rules must provide for program review and direct engagement with districts, including identifying program deficiencies and providing technical assistance.

major_effects.label: Additional PEIMS program information
major_effects.explanation: Required district reports must include any other information the agency requires under the new monitoring provision; agency rules may require additional program information through PEIMS.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the agency rulemaking and monitoring duties and permits it to require additional PEIMS information. The bill does not identify the agency by canonical name; the commissioner is separately directed to develop training resources.

HB268.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, the bill would require public school districts to include expanded digital citizenship instruction in their curricula and require sixth-grade students to complete it in social studies. The instruction would cover evaluating information, including content created or modified by generative AI, online safety and ethics, respectful discourse, and cyberbullying prevention and response.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required public school curriculum and specifies digital citizenship instruction for sixth-grade students.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The curriculum requirement applies to each school district.

affected_groups.group: Public school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would need to incorporate digital citizenship instruction into their curricula.

affected_groups.group: Sixth-grade students
affected_groups.explanation: Students enrolled in grade six would be required to complete digital citizenship instruction as part of social studies.

major_effects.label: Digital citizenship curriculum rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt rules requiring each district to incorporate digital citizenship instruction.

major_effects.label: Sixth-grade instruction requirement
major_effects.explanation: Requires sixth-grade students to complete the instruction in social studies, with expanded content addressing media literacy, online conduct, and cyberbullying.

agencies.name: State Board of Education
agencies.explanation: The bill directs the State Board of Education to adopt a rule requiring school districts to include digital citizenship instruction.

HB269.summary: The bill would direct the board, coordinating with the Texas Education Agency and Texas Workforce Commission through the Tri-Agency Workforce Initiative, to study how industry-recognized credentials can support postsecondary success and labor-market outcomes. It would also require a pilot involving at least one two-year and one four-year institution to reduce regulatory burdens and encourage credential pathways across institutions.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill creates a study and pilot focused on credential pathways and degree and certificate programs at institutions of higher education.
The study evaluates credential pathways in relation to industry demand, labor-market outcomes, and workforce needs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The study concerns credential and labor-market outcomes in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: At least one two-year and one four-year institution would participate in the pilot, which aims to support credential pathways and partnerships.

affected_groups.group: Students pursuing postsecondary credentials, including high school students seeking program credit
affected_groups.explanation: The proposed framework is intended to support students earning credentials within degree programs and enable high school students to earn credit toward those programs.

major_effects.label: Credential feasibility study and model framework
major_effects.explanation: The board must assess credential availability, pathways, transferability, and labor-market outcomes, and include a model framework for incorporating credentials into degree and certificate programs.

major_effects.label: Institutional pilot project
major_effects.explanation: The board must administer a pilot with at least one two-year and one four-year institution to reduce regulatory burdens and encourage institutional partnerships. Its aims include exploring how student aid may apply to credential costs; it does not itself change aid rules.

major_effects.label: Study and pilot reports
major_effects.explanation: The board, coordinating with the agency and commission, must submit preliminary and final reports with findings and recommendations to state executive and legislative recipients.

agencies.name: the board
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the board duties to conduct the study, establish and administer the pilot, and submit reports. Its exact identity is not established by the supplied sources.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly defines “agency” as the Texas Education Agency and requires it to coordinate on the study and related work.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly defines “commission” as the Texas Workforce Commission and requires it to coordinate on the study and related work.

HB270.summary: The bill would define high-speed rail as intercity passenger rail reasonably expected to reach at least 110 miles per hour and require the department to enter a comprehensive development agreement with a private entity to construct, maintain, and operate a route from Dallas through Waco and Austin to San Antonio along the I-35 corridor. It would repeal Transportation Code Section 199.003, which—except as required by federal or other state law—bars legislative appropriations and state agencies’ acceptance or use of state money for specified costs of privately operated high-speed rail and requires semiannual expense reports. Repeal removes those statutory restrictions and reporting requirement, but does not displace other applicable law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires a private-entity agreement to construct, maintain, and operate intercity high-speed rail on a specified route.

The bill repeals Section 199.003, which restricts appropriations and state-agency use of state money for specified costs of privately operated high-speed rail, subject to federal- and other-state-law exceptions. Removing that section’s restriction concerns state spending.

locations.name: Dallas
locations.explanation: The required rail route connects Dallas with the other named cities.

locations.name: Waco
locations.explanation: Waco is included on the required rail route.

locations.name: Austin
locations.explanation: Austin is included on the required rail route.

locations.name: San Antonio
locations.explanation: San Antonio is included on the required rail route.

locations.name: Interstate Highway 35 corridor
locations.explanation: The bill places the required rail route along this corridor.

affected_groups.group: Private high-speed rail entities
affected_groups.explanation: A private entity would be party to the required agreement to construct, maintain, and operate the route.

affected_groups.group: Intercity rail passengers
affected_groups.explanation: The proposed route would provide the defined intercity passenger rail service.

major_effects.label: Required high-speed rail development agreement
major_effects.explanation: The department would be required to enter an agreement with a private entity for construction, maintenance, and operation of high-speed rail on the specified corridor.

major_effects.label: Repeal of limits on state money for privately operated high-speed rail
major_effects.explanation: Section 199.003 bars legislative appropriations and state agencies’ acceptance or use of state money for specified costs of privately operated high-speed rail, except as required by federal or other state law. Its repeal removes those statutory limits and the section’s semiannual expense-reporting requirement; other applicable law remains in force.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: Section 91.001 defines “Department” as the Texas Department of Transportation, and the bill directs the department to enter into the comprehensive development agreement.

HB271.summary: The bill would prohibit a person from knowingly owning or operating a virtual currency kiosk in Texas, or knowingly allowing one to be installed or operated on property the person owns, leases, or controls. A violation would be a Class A misdemeanor.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill would prohibit specified ownership, operation, and permission of virtual currency kiosks.
The bill creates an offense and classifies it as a Class A misdemeanor.

locations.name: Statewide, Texas
locations.explanation: The prohibition applies to kiosks and property located in this state.

affected_groups.group: Virtual currency kiosk owners and operators
affected_groups.explanation: Knowingly owning or operating a kiosk in Texas would be prohibited.

affected_groups.group: People who own, lease, or control property in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: They could not knowingly allow another person to install or operate a kiosk on that property.

major_effects.label: Prohibition on virtual currency kiosks
major_effects.explanation: Would prohibit knowingly owning or operating a kiosk in Texas and knowingly allowing one to be installed or operated on property owned, leased, or controlled by the person.

major_effects.label: Class A misdemeanor
major_effects.explanation: A violation of the new prohibition would be a Class A misdemeanor.

HB272.summary: HB 272 would add a judge of a United States immigration court to the definition of “federal judge” in the Government Code provisions concerning handgun-carry license issuance. The expanded definition would apply only to applications submitted on or after the Act takes effect, September 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands the federal-judge category in state handgun-carry license provisions to include immigration-court judges.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing handgun-carry license applications.

affected_groups.group: Judges of United States immigration courts
affected_groups.explanation: They would be included in the defined category of federal judges for the relevant handgun-carry license provisions.

major_effects.label: Expands the covered federal-judge category
major_effects.explanation: Adds immigration-court judges to the definition used in the handgun-carry license provisions; the change applies only to applications submitted on or after the Act's effective date.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: The bill amends the definition of “federal judge” in § 411.201, which governs judicial officers’ handgun-license applications. Section 411.001 defines “department” as the Department of Public Safety, and § 411.201 assigns the department the application and license-issuance functions; DPS is therefore directly affected.

HB273.summary: The bill would require the executive commissioner of the Health and Human Services Commission to regulate health care providers’ use of artificial intelligence and adopt rules for responsible use. Those rules must require providers using AI in care, when sending a message to the provider’s patients, to use an automated messaging system that discloses the AI use and provides contact information for a provider available to answer questions or concerns.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates requirements for health care providers’ use of AI in delivering health care services.
Establishes state regulation of artificial intelligence use by health care providers.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The regulation applies to health care providers in this state.

affected_groups.group: Health care providers using artificial intelligence
affected_groups.explanation: They would be subject to rules on responsible AI use and automated patient messages.

affected_groups.group: Patients of health care providers using artificial intelligence
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive messages disclosing AI use and giving contact information for a provider available to address questions or concerns.

major_effects.label: Regulation of provider AI use
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules addressing responsible AI use in providing care and analyzing or understanding health care information.

major_effects.label: Patient messages about AI use
major_effects.explanation: Rules must require an automated message when a provider using AI in care sends a message to patients; it must disclose AI use and provide contact information for a provider available to respond.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is assigned the rulemaking and regulatory duties under the bill.

HB274.summary: The bill allows a child under 16 to read or mark a ballot at the direction of the child's parent while accompanying the parent to a voting station; doing so is not treated as assisting a voter under Subchapter B. It also requires the Secretary of State to develop and publish voter education materials for parents, and county election administrators in counties covered by Section 31.125 to make those materials available on county websites.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes ballot-related rules for children accompanying parents and establishes voter education material duties.
Requires county election administrators in counties covered by Section 31.125 to make the materials available on county websites.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The ballot rule and Secretary of State materials duty concern Texas elections statewide; the county website duty is limited to counties to which Section 31.125 applies.

affected_groups.group: Parents voting with children under 16
affected_groups.explanation: Parents may direct an accompanying child under 16 to read or mark the ballot and are the intended audience for the voter education materials.

affected_groups.group: Children under 16 accompanying a parent to a voting station
affected_groups.explanation: These children may read or mark the ballot at the parent's direction.

affected_groups.group: County election administrators in counties covered by Section 31.125
affected_groups.explanation: They must make the Secretary of State's voter education materials available on the county website.

major_effects.label: Child participation in voting
major_effects.explanation: Allows a child under 16 accompanying a parent to read or mark the ballot at the parent's direction; that activity does not constitute assisting a voter for purposes of Subchapter B.

major_effects.label: Voter education materials
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Secretary of State to develop and publish parent-focused materials and covered county election administrators to make them available on county websites.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the Secretary of State responsibility for developing the voter education materials and making them available on the agency's website.

HB275.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, a student enrolled in a school district would qualify if the parent determines the student was subjected at that district to a specified sex-offense or sexual-grooming conduct and submits an affidavit. The parent could request a transfer to another campus or school district, or receive an annual state payment for private-school tuition and fees, capped at the lesser of the district’s Chapter 48 amount or the private school’s tuition and fees. The selected private school must meet the stated accreditation requirement, and the bill would bar applying state educational-program laws or rules that were not in effect on January 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates student eligibility for a transfer or state-funded private-school tuition and fees.
Allows a parent to choose a different public-school campus or district, or private-school attendance with funding.
Requires an annual payment from the state for eligible private-school tuition and fees, subject to a cap and funding-source restrictions.
Requires a school district board of trustees to transfer an eligible student on a parent's request.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The eligibility and transfer provisions apply to eligible students enrolled in school districts, without a geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: Students enrolled in school districts who meet the bill's parent-determined eligibility criteria
affected_groups.explanation: They may become eligible for a public-school transfer or private-school funding.

affected_groups.group: Parents of eligible students
affected_groups.explanation: Parents make the eligibility determination, submit an affidavit, and choose the transfer or private-school funding option.

affected_groups.group: School districts and their boards of trustees
affected_groups.explanation: The student's district board must transfer the student when the parent requests it.

affected_groups.group: Accredited private schools selected by parents
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive tuition and fee payments for eligible students and are covered by the bill's limit on later state educational-program requirements.

major_effects.label: Parent-determined eligibility
major_effects.explanation: A student enrolled in a district may qualify based on the parent's determination of specified conduct at that district and submission of an affidavit; eligibility ends at the stated graduation or public-school eligibility limit.

major_effects.label: Public-school transfer option
major_effects.explanation: On the eligible student's parent's request, the district board must transfer the student to another campus or school district of the parent's choice.

major_effects.label: State private-school tuition and fee payment
major_effects.explanation: The annual payment is capped at the lesser of the district's Chapter 48 amount or private-school tuition and fees; it is limited to tuition and fees at a qualifying accredited school and may not use federal money or available school fund appropriations.

major_effects.label: Limit on later state educational-program requirements
major_effects.explanation: A selected private school may not be required under this provision to comply with state laws or rules governing its educational program that were not in effect on January 1, 2027.

agencies.name: the commissioner / the agency
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the commissioner rulemaking and requires the parent to submit an affidavit to the agency, but does not identify either state body by its official name.

HB276.summary: The bill expands consumer delivery permits to cover manufacturer sales and authorizes direct-to-consumer malt-beverage shipments by Texas brewers and brewpubs and by licensed out-of-state breweries, including delivery to dry areas, subject to carrier, recipient-age, labeling, and other limits. It creates an out-of-state brewery direct shipper's license with recordkeeping and tax duties, and makes unlicensed out-of-state shipping to Texas consumers subject to escalating criminal penalties.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill creates a license and operating conditions for out-of-state breweries and expands eligible alcohol businesses' direct-shipping and consumer-delivery activities.
Out-of-state licensees must pay state excise and sales and use taxes on covered sales.
The bill creates an offense with escalating criminal classifications for unlicensed out-of-state shipping to Texas consumers.

locations.name: Statewide Texas
locations.explanation: The provisions authorize qualifying shipments and deliveries to ultimate consumers in Texas.

locations.name: Dry areas
locations.explanation: The bill expressly allows certain direct shipments to consumers in dry areas.

affected_groups.group: Texas brewers and brewpub license holders
affected_groups.explanation: They may ship malt beverages directly to ultimate consumers under the bill's conditions.

affected_groups.group: Out-of-state breweries
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying breweries may obtain a new license to sell and ship malt beverages to Texas consumers and become subject to its requirements.

affected_groups.group: Texas consumers purchasing shipped malt beverages
affected_groups.explanation: Consumers gain access to direct shipments, with delivery limited by age-verification and other recipient conditions.

major_effects.label: Expanded direct shipping and consumer delivery
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes direct-to-consumer malt-beverage shipments by Texas brewers, brewpubs, and licensed out-of-state breweries, including to dry areas; also extends consumer-delivery arrangements to manufacturer sales.

major_effects.label: Out-of-state brewery direct shipper's license
major_effects.explanation: Creates a license category for eligible out-of-state breweries to ship malt beverages to Texas consumers, subject to licensing and operational limits.

major_effects.label: Sales records and reports
major_effects.explanation: Requires license holders to keep sales and delivery records and authorizes commission rules requiring periodic reports.

major_effects.label: State taxes on out-of-state licensee sales
major_effects.explanation: Treats covered sales as Texas sales and requires license holders to pay state excise and sales and use taxes; purchasers are not charged the personal-import administrative fee.

major_effects.label: Penalty for unlicensed out-of-state shipping
major_effects.explanation: Creates escalating criminal penalties for a person who sells and ships alcohol from outside Texas to a Texas consumer without the specified license.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission rulemaking and report-related duties, but the supplied bill text does not verify the commission's canonical identity.

HB277.summary: HB 277 would require a written parole instruction in jury-assessed felony penalty phases for defendants who were under 18 when they offended, and set covered inmates’ parole eligibility at the earlier of 20 years of actual calendar time or the date otherwise allowed by law. It would require parole panels to assess youthful offenders’ growth and maturity under a board policy intended to provide a meaningful opportunity for release, including treating age as a mitigating factor and considering a comprehensive adolescent mental-health evaluation. The parole provisions exclude specified offenses and generally apply to qualifying inmates in TDCJ custody on or after the effective date regardless of when the offense occurred, with a separate exception for certain pre-effective-date Section 22.02 offenses determined to have been part of a mass shooting.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes criminal-trial jury instructions, parole eligibility, and the standards used in parole review for specified people who offended before age 18.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The changes concern statewide criminal proceedings and parole for people in TDCJ custody, with no narrower geographic area specified.

affected_groups.group: Defendants who were younger than 18 when they committed a felony, whose case is not for one of the specified excluded offenses, and whose punishment is assessed by a jury
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive the specified parole instruction in the penalty phase, except for the offenses excluded by the bill.

affected_groups.group: Inmates serving sentences for felony offenses committed before age 18
affected_groups.explanation: Covered inmates are those serving sentences for felony offenses committed before age 18, excluding inmates serving sentences for offenses under Penal Code Section 19.03(a)(1) or (7).

affected_groups.group: People with knowledge of a covered inmate before the offense or of the inmate’s subsequent growth and maturity
affected_groups.explanation: The board’s policy must permit these people to submit statements for parole-panel consideration.

major_effects.label: Parole eligibility for covered youthful offenders
major_effects.explanation: For covered inmates serving felony sentences for offenses committed before age 18, eligibility would begin at the earlier of 20 years of actual calendar time served without good-conduct-time credit or the date otherwise applicable under Section 508.145. The provision does not apply to inmates serving sentences for offenses under Penal Code Section 19.03(a)(1) or (7).

major_effects.label: Written jury parole instruction
major_effects.explanation: When a jury assesses punishment in a covered felony case involving a defendant who was under 18 at the time of the offense, the court must provide the written instruction; specified offenses are excluded. The instruction says eligibility does not guarantee release and jurors must not consider how parole law may apply to the particular defendant.

major_effects.label: Youth-focused parole review standards
major_effects.explanation: Parole panels must consider juveniles’ greater capacity for change when reviewing an inmate for release on parole. For inmates to whom this section applies, the board must adopt a policy treating age at the time of the offense as a mitigating factor and providing for consideration of a qualified adolescent mental-health evaluation.

major_effects.label: Applicability to inmates already in custody
major_effects.explanation: The new parole provisions generally apply to qualifying inmates confined in TDCJ-operated or contracted facilities on or after the effective date, regardless of when the offense occurred. They do not apply to an inmate confined for a pre-effective-date Section 22.02 offense if the applicable parole authority determines it was part of a mass shooting.

agencies.name: Board of Pardons and Paroles
agencies.explanation: Government Code Chapter 508.001 defines “Board” as the Board of Pardons and Paroles, and the bill directly directs the board to adopt parole-review policy.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: The department’s pardons and paroles division is assigned to determine whether a specified pre-effective-date offense was committed as part of a mass shooting, affecting application of the new parole provisions.

HB278.summary: The bill changes when a municipal budget officer must file a proposed budget with the municipal clerk: the filing must occur before the 21st day before the municipality levies taxes, instead of before the 30th day. Although the bill’s caption refers to public notice, the operative change does not amend a public-notice requirement.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes a municipal budget officer’s filing deadline in the municipal budget process.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change applies to municipalities under the statewide municipal budget statute.

affected_groups.group: Municipal budget officers
affected_groups.explanation: Their deadline to file the proposed budget with the municipal clerk changes.

affected_groups.group: Municipal governing bodies
affected_groups.explanation: The filing deadline is measured relative to the date the municipality’s governing body makes its tax levy.

major_effects.label: Changes proposed-budget filing deadline
major_effects.explanation: Moves the deadline from before the 30th day to before the 21st day before the municipal tax levy.

HB279.summary: HB 279 would broaden criminal-history nondisclosure pathways for qualifying defendants, including by extending a route to specialty-court completers and creating routes for people with multiple eligible convictions and people who were under 25 when a qualifying offense was committed. It also revises petition waiting periods and lets courts include certain offenses from the same transaction; eligibility remains subject to offense exclusions, sentence-completion requirements and, where specified, notice, a hearing and a best-interest-of-justice finding.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes eligibility and procedures for orders restricting public disclosure of criminal-history information.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill revises Texas statutory procedures for nondisclosure orders rather than limiting them to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: People with qualifying misdemeanor or state jail felony convictions or deferred-adjudication outcomes
affected_groups.explanation: The bill revises waiting periods and creates or expands nondisclosure routes for specified offense categories, subject to exclusions and other requirements.

affected_groups.group: People with more than one eligible misdemeanor or state jail felony conviction
affected_groups.explanation: A new route allows qualifying people to petition after completing all sentences and meeting the applicable waiting period and other conditions.

affected_groups.group: People who were younger than 25 when a qualifying offense was committed
affected_groups.explanation: A new route permits eligible people to petition after completing the sentence and waiting the applicable period, even if they have a prior conviction or deferred-adjudication outcome for another offense, subject to Section 411.074.

affected_groups.group: People who successfully complete specialty court programs
affected_groups.explanation: The bill extends the relevant nondisclosure procedure beyond veterans treatment court programs to specialty court programs within the stated statutory scope.

major_effects.label: Expanded nondisclosure pathways
major_effects.explanation: The bill extends the specialty-court procedure and adds pathways for multiple eligible convictions and qualifying offenses committed before age 25, subject to statutory exclusions and conditions.

major_effects.label: Revised petition waiting periods
major_effects.explanation: The bill changes when eligible people may petition, with different timelines based on offense category and, for multiple convictions, the most serious offense and sentence history.

major_effects.label: Public disclosure restricted by nondisclosure orders
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying petitions, a court may issue an order prohibiting public disclosure of the criminal-history information covered by the order, after the required process and findings.

major_effects.label: Certain related offenses may be included
major_effects.explanation: For the specified procedures, an order may include an offense arising from the same transaction if it meets the stated eligibility condition or has not resulted in a conviction or dismissal and discharge and is no longer pending.

agencies.name: criminal justice agencies
agencies.explanation: Orders under the expanded and new pathways prohibit these agencies from disclosing covered criminal-history information to the public. The bill does not identify which specific agencies are included.

HB280.summary: The bill would prohibit covered retailers from using customer information or other unique customer qualities to set a customer-specific price higher than the price expected without the model. It preserves specified market-based, promotional, negotiated, randomized-test, and regulated-pricing uses, and requires records for models that are not prohibited. The new chapter applies only to models in use on or after September 1, 2028; earlier-use models are not governed for determining whether a violation occurred.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a prohibition on certain pricing practices by covered retailers and makes violations actionable as deceptive trade practices.
Restricts covered pricing models that use personal identifying information or unique customer qualities to raise an individual customer's price.

locations.name: Statewide (Texas)
locations.explanation: The chapter applies to qualifying retailers conducting business in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Retailers conducting business in Texas, including qualifying online retailers
affected_groups.explanation: Covered retailers would be subject to the pricing restrictions and record-retention duty; online retailers are covered only if they meet the annual revenue threshold.

affected_groups.group: Retail customers
affected_groups.explanation: The prohibition protects customers from specified individualized price increases based on their information or unique qualities.

major_effects.label: Limits individualized pricing increases
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits using customer information or unique qualities to produce a customer-specific price above what would be expected without the model. The bill preserves specified market-based pricing and other listed uses.

major_effects.label: Requires retention of pricing-model records
major_effects.explanation: A person using a model not prohibited by the bill must retain records about the model, including information about its algorithms, inputs, and price-determining factors, for at least two years.

major_effects.label: Makes violations actionable as deceptive trade practices
major_effects.explanation: Violations are actionable under the deceptive-trade-practices subchapter, and each day of prohibited use is a separate violation.

major_effects.label: Limits the chapter's application to models in use on or after September 1, 2028
major_effects.explanation: Models in use before that date are not governed by the new chapter for determining whether a violation occurred.

HB281.summary: HB 281 would expand Human Resources Code regulation to include defined residential treatment centers and require onsite education for children with intense or intense-plus service levels, subject to the exception in Subsection (e) and TEA-approved deviations. It would establish related education funding and reporting, add center licensing and location restrictions, and create a Class A misdemeanor for specified intentional deception.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes educational services, enrollment arrangements, funding, and reporting for students residing in residential treatment centers.
Provides Chapter 48 funding for qualifying onsite programs and allocates a proportional amount of center reimbursement to the education agency for distribution.
Creates allotments for qualifying school districts that enroll students residing in residential treatment centers.
Expands residential treatment center regulation and adds licensing, ownership-record, and facility-location requirements.
Creates a Class A misdemeanor for specified knowing conduct done with intent to deceive.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill establishes statewide requirements for covered residential treatment centers.

locations.name: Attendance zones of school districts with 15,000 or more enrolled students
locations.explanation: Certain centers serving children with intense or intense-plus service levels may be licensed, renewed, or expanded only in these zones.

affected_groups.group: Children with intense or intense-plus service levels residing in residential treatment centers
affected_groups.explanation: Their onsite education, school enrollment, and educational progress reporting are addressed.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: They may enter enrollment agreements, and qualifying districts are entitled to proportional education allotments.

affected_groups.group: Residential treatment center owners, operators, and associated third parties
affected_groups.explanation: They are subject to ownership disclosures, licensing restrictions, and related center requirements.

major_effects.label: Expanded regulatory coverage
major_effects.explanation: Extends the subchapter’s applicability to residential treatment centers as defined by the Family Code, in addition to the stated general-residential-operation criteria.

major_effects.label: Education service and enrollment requirements
major_effects.explanation: Requires onsite education for covered children, except as provided by Subsection (e); a center may not deviate unless TEA reviews and approves the deviation and documents it in the educational records of each child subject to it.

major_effects.label: Education funding arrangements
major_effects.explanation: Provides Chapter 48 funding for onsite center programs and proportional reimbursement allocations for districts and charter schools under center agreements.

major_effects.label: Education progress reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires quarterly reporting on academic progress and attendance for specified onsite-program students, alongside reporting of educational outcomes.

major_effects.label: Licensing records and searchable database
major_effects.explanation: Requires commission records about owners and license status and a public searchable database listing centers, responsible owners or managers, and locations.

major_effects.label: Facility and operator licensing limits
major_effects.explanation: Restricts certain center licenses and expansions to qualifying school attendance zones and limits specified operator licensing or site reuse after specified events, subject to stated exceptions.

major_effects.label: Class A misdemeanor
major_effects.explanation: Makes specified knowing concealment or licensing applications violations criminal when done with intent to deceive.

major_effects.label: Education Code applicability exception
major_effects.explanation: Excludes a residential treatment center operating the specified educational program from Section 29.012.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: Receives quarterly reports on academic progress and attendance. A residential treatment center may deviate from the onsite-education requirement only if the Texas Education Agency reviews and approves the deviation and documents it in each affected child’s educational records.

agencies.name: Department of Family and Protective Services
agencies.explanation: The bill names this department as the source of funding under Section 42.2541(f), which assigns the department a proportional reimbursement allocation duty. The canonical registry has no matching entry.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission database, licensing, and monitoring duties, but the supplied text does not identify the specific state body meant by “the commission.”

HB282.summary: HB 282 would require a metropolitan planning organization policy board to include a voting Texas House member appointed by the Speaker, unless no eligible representative is willing to serve. The member’s term would run concurrently with the representative’s term, for no more than two years, and the board would have to amend its bylaws to implement the change.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes membership and voting on metropolitan planning organization policy boards, which are transportation planning bodies.
The bill changes the composition and operation of metropolitan planning organization policy boards.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to metropolitan planning organization policy boards under Texas law, without limiting it to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Metropolitan planning organizations and their policy boards
affected_groups.explanation: Their boards would add a legislative voting member when an eligible representative is willing to serve and would amend their bylaws to implement the change.

affected_groups.group: Texas House members representing districts within or partly within an MPO
affected_groups.explanation: An eligible and willing representative may be appointed to serve as a voting policy board member.

major_effects.label: Adds a legislative voting member to MPO policy boards when an eligible representative is willing to serve
major_effects.explanation: The Speaker would appoint an eligible House member as a full voting member who counts toward a quorum, except when no eligible representative is willing to serve; the board must update its bylaws to implement the requirement.

HB283.summary: The bill would create an exception to the concealed-handgun prohibition at a polling place for a person licensed to carry who is performing election-judge duties. It covers election judges and early voting clerks or deputy early voting clerks serving as election judges at early voting polling places; it does not create a general polling-place carry exception.

policy_tags.explanation: The exception applies to people performing specified election-judge duties, including at early voting polling places.
The bill changes when a concealed handgun may be carried at a polling place by creating a limited exception to the prohibition.
It changes the application of a Penal Code prohibition for the specified people and circumstances.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends state law concerning polling places and election judges without limiting the change to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Licensed handgun carriers serving as election judges
affected_groups.explanation: They may carry a concealed handgun while performing their election-judge duties under the specified exception.

affected_groups.group: Licensed handgun carriers serving as early voting clerks or deputy early voting clerks
affected_groups.explanation: They are covered only when serving as an election judge at an early voting polling place.

major_effects.label: Limited polling-place carry exception
major_effects.explanation: A licensed person is exempt from the specified prohibition while carrying a concealed handgun in the performance of election-judge duties; the exception is limited to the listed roles and circumstances.

HB284.summary: Except as provided by Subsection (c), creates a sales and use tax exemption for the sale, use, lease, or installation of a qualifying distributed energy system, defined as one that primarily generates electricity consumed solely by a nearby structure or facility. The exemption excludes costs for unrelated construction, repairs, and maintenance; claimants must provide eligibility records on request, and the Comptroller must adopt implementing rules, including reporting requirements.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for qualifying distributed energy systems.
The tax exemption applies to systems that generate electricity for nearby structures or facilities.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas state tax law and establishes an exemption under that law; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: People and businesses purchasing, using, leasing, or installing qualifying distributed energy systems
affected_groups.explanation: These parties may claim the exemption for qualifying system transactions or installations, subject to the bill's eligibility limits.

major_effects.label: Distributed energy system tax exemption
major_effects.explanation: Exempts qualifying systems from taxes imposed under the chapter, but not costs for unrelated construction, repairs, or maintenance.

major_effects.label: Eligibility records and reporting
major_effects.explanation: Claimants must make records sufficient to show eligibility available on request; the Comptroller's rules must also prescribe reporting requirements.

major_effects.label: Exemption implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Comptroller to adopt rules for administering the exemption, including rules on eligibility.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: Must adopt rules to implement and administer the exemption, including eligibility and reporting rules.

HB285.summary: The bill would bar the governor from suspending laws or rules governing residential child-care facility licensing and reinstate any such provisions already suspended under the disaster law. It would require specified providers of 24-hour care to unaccompanied children under federal contracts to be licensed or certified, except qualifying tax-exempt religious institutions; violations would be state jail felonies. The Health and Human Services Commission would establish a licensing issuance or renewal process for facilities affected by a governor's order.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a licensing or certification requirement for a defined class of residential child-care providers.
The new licensing requirement specifically covers care under federal immigration or refugee resettlement contracts for unaccompanied children.
Makes violation of the new licensing requirement a state jail felony.
Limits the governor's disaster-related suspension authority for residential child-care facility licensing and requires HHSC to establish a licensing process for affected facilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes Texas statutory licensing and disaster-suspension rules without limiting them to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Providers of 24-hour care to unaccompanied children under ICE or Office of Refugee Resettlement contracts
affected_groups.explanation: These providers would be required to obtain a residential child-care facility license or certification, except that the section does not apply to a qualifying tax-exempt religious institution.

affected_groups.group: Children receiving covered care
affected_groups.explanation: The licensing requirement applies to facilities caring for children who are not accompanied by or in the physical custody of a parent, guardian, or other adult family member, except that the section does not apply to a qualifying tax-exempt religious institution.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying tax-exempt religious institutions
affected_groups.explanation: Religious institutions meeting the specified federal tax-exemption and organizational criteria are excluded from the new requirement.

major_effects.label: Limits emergency suspension of child-care licensing rules
major_effects.explanation: The governor could not suspend laws or rules relating to residential child-care facility licensing; relevant provisions suspended under the existing disaster law would be reinstated.

major_effects.label: Requires licensing or certification for specified providers
major_effects.explanation: Providers furnishing 24-hour care under the named federal contracts to children without a parent, guardian, or other adult family member present must be licensed or certified, except qualifying tax-exempt religious institutions.

major_effects.label: Creates a state jail felony
major_effects.explanation: A person who violates the new requirement commits a state jail felony.

major_effects.label: Requires a licensing process for facilities affected by governor's orders
major_effects.explanation: HHSC must establish a process to issue or renew licenses for facilities whose licenses were affected by an order under the disaster statute.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: Must establish a process for issuing or renewing licenses for residential child-care facilities affected by a governor's order.

HB286.summary: HB 286 would require the Department of State Health Services and the Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee to study maternal mortality and morbidity among Black women in Texas, examine specified contributing factors, and develop recommendations. They would submit a written report by September 1, 2028; the Act would expire December 31, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires a study and recommendations concerning maternal health outcomes, disparities, and related health factors.
Assigns state bodies a joint study, recommendation-development, and reporting duty.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The required study concerns maternal health outcomes among Black women in this state.

affected_groups.group: Black women in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: They are the primary population whose maternal mortality and morbidity the study evaluates and whose disparities the recommendations address.

affected_groups.group: Health care providers
affected_groups.explanation: The study assesses provider implicit bias and may recommend provider training; it does not require providers to undergo training.

major_effects.label: Joint maternal health study and recommendations
major_effects.explanation: The committee and department must study specified aspects of maternal mortality and morbidity among Black women and develop recommendations to address disparities.

major_effects.label: Written report to state officials and legislative committees
major_effects.explanation: The two bodies must submit a report summarizing the study and recommendations by September 1, 2028; it may be consolidated with the existing biennial report.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the department as the Department of State Health Services and assigns it joint responsibility for the study, recommendations, and report.

agencies.name: Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee
agencies.explanation: The bill names the committee and assigns it joint responsibility for the study, recommendations, and report; no canonical registry identity is supplied.

HB287.summary: The bill expands who may participate in transition planning, represent a student in special-education due-process hearings, and exercise certain adult students’ educational rights, including agents under powers of attorney and educational representatives. It creates a limited process for a parent or specified alternate to be recognized as an educational representative for an adult special-education student after a professional certifies that the student cannot provide informed consent about the educational program; student safeguards include the ability to rescind and a rule that the certification is not a general finding of incompetence. School districts would have new information and representative-recognition duties, and the commissioner must post model forms and adopt implementing rules.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes special-education decision-making, representation, transition planning participation, and school-district procedures.
Imposes new information, notice, and educational-representative recognition duties on school districts.
Adds safeguards against treating hospitalization or a disability diagnosis alone as inability to consent, and limits the use of the certification as evidence of general incapacity.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions concern students enrolled in school districts generally, rather than a specified geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Students with disabilities who are 18 or older or whose disabilities of minority have been removed
affected_groups.explanation: Their educational decision-making rights, representation options, and transition-planning participation are affected.

affected_groups.group: Parents, agents, supporters, and educational representatives
affected_groups.explanation: Specified adults may participate in transition planning, represent students in due-process hearings, or exercise educational rights when applicable.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts must provide information and notices and follow procedures for recognizing an educational representative.

affected_groups.group: Qualified licensed professionals
affected_groups.explanation: Certain independent licensed professionals may certify whether a student can provide informed consent regarding the educational program.

major_effects.label: Educational representation and rights
major_effects.explanation: Allows specified parents, agents, supporters, and educational representatives to participate in covered proceedings or exercise rights accorded to parents for eligible students.

major_effects.label: Educational representative process
major_effects.explanation: Creates a limited recognition process for a parent or specified alternate to serve for an eligible adult student after a qualifying professional certification.

major_effects.label: Student safeguards
major_effects.explanation: Requires consideration of communication supports and alternatives to guardianship, bars reliance solely on hospitalization or diagnosis, and preserves the student's ability to rescind the representative's appointment.

major_effects.label: School-district procedures
major_effects.explanation: Requires districts to provide specified resources and notices and to recognize an educational representative after receiving the required notice and certification.

major_effects.label: Model forms and implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commissioner to post model certification forms and adopt rules implementing the new process, including privacy compliance.

agencies.name: the agency
agencies.explanation: The bill bars the agency from regulating educational-representative selection and removes its jurisdiction over adult-student capacity issues. The source does not identify the agency by canonical name.

agencies.name: the commissioner
agencies.explanation: The commissioner must develop and post model certification forms and adopt implementing rules. The source does not specify the commissioner's canonical title or identify the agency headed by that commissioner.

HB288.summary: HB 288 would expand Education Code §25.0344: on a parent’s request, a school district must transfer a student if the parent is a peace officer, servicemember, or judge or justice of a court in Texas. The parent selects the campus or, if a §25.035 agreement allows, the other school district; the district is not required to provide transportation. The bill also repeals Education Code §25.0345 and applies beginning with the 2027–28 school year, but the supplied text does not show what the repealed section provides.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility for a required transfer of public school students.
Allows the eligible student's parent to select the receiving campus or, subject to an agreement, school district.
School district boards or their designees receive an expanded mandatory transfer duty.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill changes the statewide school-district transfer framework; eligible judges or justices must serve a court in this state.

affected_groups.group: Students whose parent is a peace officer, servicemember, or judge or justice of a court in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: These students become eligible for the required transfer on a parent's request.

affected_groups.group: Parents and persons standing in parental relation to eligible students
affected_groups.explanation: They may request the transfer and select the receiving campus or eligible district.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: District boards or their designees must transfer eligible students upon request, subject to the stated terms.

major_effects.label: Expand eligibility for required student transfers
major_effects.explanation: Adds servicemembers and judges or justices to the eligible parents, alongside peace officers. The parent selects the campus or, under a §25.035 agreement, another district; the district is not required to provide transportation.

major_effects.label: Repeal of Education Code §25.0345
major_effects.explanation: The bill repeals this section, but its contents are not supplied, so the substantive effect of the repeal is unclear.

HB289.summary: HB 289 would direct the Texas Historical Commission to select locations and install a memorial plaque in each impacted Texas House district for victims of the 2025 Hill Country flood, coordinating with relevant local governments, state leaders, and property owners. Each plaque would have to include the flood dates; it could also include victims’ names and ages or other details the commission considers relevant, with content developed in collaboration with victims’ families and communities.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill assigns the Texas Historical Commission a new plaque-selection and installation responsibility.

locations.name: Each impacted Texas House district
locations.explanation: The bill requires a plaque in each district impacted by the flood but does not identify the districts.

affected_groups.group: Families and communities of victims
affected_groups.explanation: They would collaborate with the commission on plaque content.

affected_groups.group: Relevant local governments and property owners
affected_groups.explanation: They would be included in coordination on selecting plaque locations; the bill does not assign them installation duties.

major_effects.label: Memorial plaque installation
major_effects.explanation: Directs the commission to select locations and install plaques in impacted districts. Plaques must include the flood dates and may include victims’ names, ages, and other details the commission considers relevant.

agencies.name: Texas Historical Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines “Commission” as the Texas Historical Commission and assigns it the plaque-selection, installation, and content-development duties.

HB290.summary: HB 290 would require corn masa flour and wet corn masa products to meet specified folic-acid levels, with exceptions for cottage-food operations and their suppliers and for food-service establishments using corn masa. It would require product labeling, authorize rules, and impose administrative penalties for violations. Compliance with the chapter and its rules would not be required until January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Sets required folic-acid levels in specified food products, a substantive nutrition and public-health standard.
Regulates product composition and labeling for specified products manufactured, distributed, or sold in Texas, and provides for penalties.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The product requirements apply to specified products manufactured, sold, or otherwise handled in this state.

affected_groups.group: Manufacturers, distributors, and sellers of corn masa flour and wet corn masa products
affected_groups.explanation: They are subject to the composition requirements for covered products. A person may distribute, sell, or offer the products for sale in Texas only if they include the required notice, including the product’s folic acid content on the nutrition label.

affected_groups.group: Cottage food production operations and their suppliers
affected_groups.explanation: The chapter expressly excludes covered cottage-food operations and suppliers from its application.

affected_groups.group: Food service establishments
affected_groups.explanation: The chapter does not apply to food-service establishments that use corn masa as an ingredient in manufacturing a food product.

major_effects.label: Folic-acid content requirements
major_effects.explanation: Requires specified folic-acid levels in covered corn masa flour and wet corn masa products, subject to the chapter's exclusions.

major_effects.label: Product labeling
major_effects.explanation: Requires covered products offered for sale to state their folic-acid content on the nutrition label and identify that they contain corn masa.

major_effects.label: Administrative penalties
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to assess an administrative penalty for violations; the stated fine range is $1,000 to $25,000 per violation, and a continuing violation may count separately each day.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes the executive commissioner to adopt rules necessary to implement the chapter.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department responsibility for assessing administrative penalties, but the supplied text does not identify which state agency the term denotes.

agencies.name: executive commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the executive commissioner to adopt implementing rules, but the supplied text does not identify the state agency associated with that title.

HB291.summary: HB 291 would direct the Texas Indigent Defense Commission to establish, revise, and publish a maximum caseload for criminal defense attorneys based on their total workload, including criminal and family appointments and other work; the limit could use formulas rather than a single fixed number. County appointment procedures and indigent-defense program plans would have to comply, and the Commission would adopt compliance rules and impose a remedy only for a county whose prior-year Commission grant funds exceeded 50% of its indigent-defense expenditures. The changes would apply only to cases with an indictment or information filed on or after November 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill sets a maximum caseload standard for attorneys representing criminal defendants.
County appointment procedures and indigent-defense programs must comply with the caseload limit, with remedies required for noncompliance in specified counties.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The compliance rules apply to counties throughout Texas, subject to a separate funding threshold for required remedies.

affected_groups.group: Criminal defense attorneys
affected_groups.explanation: Their total caseload, including appointments and other work, would be considered in setting the maximum.

affected_groups.group: Indigent criminal defendants
affected_groups.explanation: The caseload standard is intended to allow attorneys time and effort for effective and diligent representation.

affected_groups.group: Texas counties administering indigent-defense services
affected_groups.explanation: County appointment procedures and program plans must observe the caseload limit; required remedies are limited to counties meeting the specified grant-funding threshold.

major_effects.label: Commission caseload standard
major_effects.explanation: The Commission must establish and revise a maximum caseload based on an attorney's total workload; the limit need not be a single fixed number and may use formulas.

major_effects.label: County compliance and remedies
major_effects.explanation: The Commission must adopt rules to promote compliance statewide and impose a remedy for noncompliance only in counties whose prior-year Commission grants exceeded 50% of their indigent-defense expenditures.

major_effects.label: Appointment and program-plan limits
