major_effects.explanation: County appointment procedures and indigent-defense program plans must ensure appointments do not exceed the established maximum caseload.

agencies.name: Texas Indigent Defense Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the Commission responsibility for establishing and revising the caseload limit, publishing it, adopting compliance rules, and imposing remedies in specified cases. The bill identifies the Commission as the Texas Indigent Defense Commission.

HB292.summary: HB 292 would create a commission to recommend improvements to public school assessment and accountability systems and report statutory recommendations to the governor and legislature by December 31, 2029. It would bar A–F ratings for districts and campuses after the 2027–2028 school year; existing sanctions could continue but not be increased or supplemented, and could still be reduced or suspended if standards are met. For multiyear sanction measures, 2027–2028 would be excluded without breaking a series continuing from 2026–2027, and later student assessment and academic evaluation would be allowed only to the extent required by federal law.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a commission on public school assessment and accountability and changes rating and sanction rules for school districts and campuses.
Provides that commission administrative and operating expenses are to be funded by legislative appropriation to the agency.
Establishes a state commission, assigns it duties, and provides for its membership, administrative support, and public meetings.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The commission's remit concerns the public school statewide assessment and accountability systems.

affected_groups.group: Public school students, including students receiving compensatory education and other special populations
affected_groups.explanation: The commission must consider whether assessments disproportionately affect these students and recommend possible policy responses.

affected_groups.group: Independent school districts and district campuses
affected_groups.explanation: They would no longer receive A–F ratings after the 2027–2028 school year, and existing sanctions could not be increased or supplemented.

major_effects.label: Create assessment and accountability commission
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a 19-member commission to develop recommendations on assessment and accountability issues, including fairness, student impacts, costs, and privacy protocols.

major_effects.label: Deliver recommendations report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to report statutory recommendations to the governor and legislature by December 31, 2029.

major_effects.label: End post-2027–2028 A–F ratings and limit sanctions
major_effects.explanation: Bars A–F ratings after the 2027–2028 school year; existing sanctions may continue but cannot be increased and additional sanctions cannot be imposed. The commissioner may still reduce or suspend an existing sanction when performance standards are met.

major_effects.label: Exclude 2027–2028 from multiyear sanction measures
major_effects.explanation: The 2027–2028 school year cannot be counted for sanctions based on multiyear performance measures, but this does not interrupt a series continuing from 2026–2027.

major_effects.label: Limit post-year assessment and evaluation
major_effects.explanation: After the 2027–2028 school year, student assessment and academic-performance evaluation are permitted only to the extent required by federal law.

major_effects.label: Fund commission operations by appropriation
major_effects.explanation: Provides for commission administrative and operating expenses through legislative appropriation to the agency.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Assessment and Accountability
agencies.explanation: The bill would establish the commission and assign it recommendation and reporting duties; it has no matching registry entry.

agencies.name: State Board of Education
agencies.explanation: The board chair designates a board member to serve on the commission.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The board is assigned to assist the agency as necessary in providing requested data and analysis to the commission.

agencies.name: the agency
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns this source-named agency administrative support, data and analysis duties, and the recipient role for commission appropriations; its identity is not established in the supplied text.

HB293.summary: The bill would prohibit the department or commission from agreeing to use state park property to construct, operate, or maintain border security infrastructure or related improvements, unless an act of the legislature expressly authorizes the agreement. The referenced definition includes a wall, barrier, fence, road, trench, apparatus, or other improvement designed or adapted to surveil or impede the movement of people or objects crossing the Texas-Mexico border. Section 11.38 applies only to real property in a county bordering the United Mexican States.

policy_tags.explanation: Restricts agreements allowing specified infrastructure and improvements on state park property.
The restriction specifically concerns infrastructure defined as border security infrastructure.
Limits the department's and commission's authority to enter specified agreements.

locations.name: Statewide state park property
locations.explanation: The restriction covers state park property generally, rather than a named park or locality.

affected_groups.group: State park administrators and decision-makers
affected_groups.explanation: The department and commission would be unable to enter the specified agreements unless authorized by an act of the legislature.

affected_groups.group: Entities seeking to construct, operate, or maintain border security infrastructure on state park property
affected_groups.explanation: Their ability to obtain an agreement for that use of state park property would be restricted unless expressly authorized by an act of the legislature.

major_effects.label: Restricts agreements using state park property
major_effects.explanation: The department or commission could not enter covered agreements unless an act of the legislature expressly authorizes them.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill directly prohibits this statutory actor from entering covered agreements; its formal identity is not established by the supplied definitions.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directly prohibits this statutory actor from entering covered agreements; its formal identity is not established by the supplied definitions.

HB294.summary: HB 294 would require the governor to seek federal authorization and, if authorization is received, allow the governor to negotiate an agreement with a state in Mexico to create a temporary guest worker program, subject to that authorization and Section 752.103. The agreement would set worker and employer requirements, including a local-worker availability certification and a condition that hiring not adversely affect similarly employed Texas workers’ wages or working conditions.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a state program, contingent on federal authorization, for Mexican temporary guest workers using U.S. nonimmigrant visas.
Addresses recruitment for jobs identified as needing skilled or unskilled migrant labor and sets conditions concerning available local workers and effects on similarly employed workers.
Participating businesses would have to certify that qualifying workers are not sufficiently available where the work will be performed.
Assigns the governor a duty to seek federal authorization and grants authority to negotiate a program agreement if authorization is received.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The program is for businesses and workers in this state.

locations.name: A state in Mexico selected for the program
locations.explanation: The agreement would be with a Mexican state, with the particular state selected for the program.

affected_groups.group: Texas businesses seeking temporary guest workers
affected_groups.explanation: Businesses could obtain workers through the program but would have to meet its hiring conditions.

affected_groups.group: Mexican temporary guest workers
affected_groups.explanation: Workers participating in the program would need to meet federal visa eligibility and other program requirements.

affected_groups.group: Workers in Texas similarly employed
affected_groups.explanation: The agreement must require that guest-worker employment not adversely affect their wages or working conditions.

major_effects.label: Conditional guest worker program
major_effects.explanation: Would allow the governor to negotiate an agreement with a Mexican state to create a temporary guest worker program only after federal authorization is received, and subject to that authorization and Section 752.103.

major_effects.label: Program and hiring conditions
major_effects.explanation: The agreement must require businesses to certify that qualified local workers are insufficient and must guard against adverse effects on similarly employed workers’ wages and working conditions; participating workers must meet specified requirements.

major_effects.label: Notice of failure to return
major_effects.explanation: If a guest worker fails to return to Mexico before the visa expires, the agreement must require the Mexican state to notify the hiring business, governor, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

agencies.name: governor
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the governor the duty to seek federal authorization and permits the governor to negotiate an agreement if authorization is received. The source names the governor but does not identify an agency-office name.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The program uses the Commission's identification of jobs most in need of migrant labor, though this bill does not expressly assign it a new identification duty.

HB295.summary: HB 295 would extend Chapter 167A beyond pelvic examinations to other sensitive health care services and require practitioners to give patients rights information, offer a medical chaperone, provide one if requested, and obtain informed consent before a potentially sensitive service. It would require covered facilities to ensure practitioners complete chaperone training, assign a commission to develop or adopt the curriculum, require the Health and Human Services Commission’s executive commissioner to adopt rules, and extend disciplinary action—including administrative penalties—to facilities that violate the chapter. The changes would apply only to services performed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes patient-consent and chaperone requirements and training requirements for sensitive health care services.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill concerns health care facilities authorized to provide care in Texas and applies prospectively to covered services under state law.

affected_groups.group: Patients receiving potentially sensitive health care services and their legally authorized representatives
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive rights information and have protections concerning participation in care decisions, chaperones, and informed consent.

affected_groups.group: Health care practitioners who perform sensitive health care services
affected_groups.explanation: A practitioner may not perform a potentially sensitive health care service unless the practitioner meets the applicable requirements, including providing the patient or legally authorized representative notice of the patient's rights. At a facility that provides sensitive health care services, each practitioner who performs those services must complete at least one medical chaperone training course.

affected_groups.group: Health care facilities providing sensitive health care services
affected_groups.explanation: They would have to require practitioner training and could face disciplinary action for violations of the chapter.

major_effects.label: Notice, chaperone option, and informed consent
major_effects.explanation: Before performing a potentially sensitive service, a practitioner would have to provide notice of patient rights, offer a chaperone and provide one if requested, and obtain informed consent.

major_effects.label: Medical-chaperone training
major_effects.explanation: Facilities providing sensitive services would have to require training for practitioners who perform those services, using a curriculum developed or adopted by the commission.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner of the Health and Human Services Commission would be required to adopt rules for the new provisions.

major_effects.label: Expanded disciplinary reach
major_effects.explanation: The bill extends disciplinary action, including administrative penalties, to health care facilities that violate Chapter 167A.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is required to adopt rules implementing the new provisions.

agencies.name: commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission a duty to develop or adopt the medical-chaperone training curriculum, but does not identify the commission by its full name.

HB296.summary: The bill would create the Texas Promise Grant Program, administered by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board, to provide eligible students at public two-year institutions with grants for tuition and mandatory fees and a $1,000 bonus upon completing an associate degree or certificate. Awards could begin only for an academic year for which money is appropriated, and not before the 2028–2029 academic year.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a student grant and completion-incentive program for eligible students at public two-year institutions.
Provides for grants and completion bonuses, with awards beginning only in an academic year for which money is appropriated and not before 2028–2029.
Requires each school district to notify students, school personnel, and parents or guardians about the program and its eligibility requirements.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The program applies to state residents and calls for program information to be distributed to each school district.

affected_groups.group: Eligible students attending public two-year institutions
affected_groups.explanation: Students meeting residency, recent high-school completion, enrollment, and other eligibility conditions may receive grants and a completion bonus, subject to ongoing requirements.

affected_groups.group: Public junior colleges, public technical institutes, and public state colleges
affected_groups.explanation: These institutions are eligible institutions under the program, and their student financial aid officers are consulted in developing program rules.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Each district must notify high school students, relevant school personnel, and students' parents or guardians about the program.

major_effects.label: Texas Promise Grant Program
major_effects.explanation: Creates a program to help eligible students pay tuition and mandatory fees at public two-year institutions and encourage completion of an associate degree or certificate.

major_effects.label: Student grants and completion bonuses
major_effects.explanation: Provides tuition-related grants and a $1,000 completion bonus. Awards may begin only for an academic year with an appropriation and not before 2028–2029.

major_effects.label: Grant eligibility and continuation requirements
major_effects.explanation: Sets initial and continuing eligibility conditions, including enrollment and academic progress, with rules required to allow certain hardship-based exceptions.

major_effects.label: Program administration and rules
major_effects.explanation: Assigns the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board program administration, rulemaking, and grant-award responsibilities.

major_effects.label: School-district program notification
major_effects.explanation: Requires school districts to notify high school students and specified school-community members about the program and eligibility requirements.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The bill identifies the coordinating board as the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board and assigns it administration, rulemaking, and grant-award duties.

HB297.summary: The bill would exempt sales of specified tools, work gear, and industry books or codebooks from Texas sales and use taxes during the Friday-through-Monday period around the first Monday in September, subject to item-specific price limits. Beginning in 2029, those limits would be adjusted every five years based on the consumer price index.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a limited-period sales and use tax exemption for specified qualified items, with price limits that are periodically adjusted.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The exemption applies to taxes imposed under Chapter 151 of the Texas Tax Code, without a geographic limitation in the bill.

affected_groups.group: Purchasers of qualifying tools and work-related items
affected_groups.explanation: Purchasers may receive the exemption during the specified period when the item meets the applicable price limit.

major_effects.label: Limited-period sales tax exemption
major_effects.explanation: Exempts listed tools, safety gear, work boots, and industry books or codebooks during the specified September period when their sales prices are below the applicable threshold. The thresholds are adjusted every five years beginning in 2029 based on CPI.

HB298.summary: The bill would allow a civil service commission, if authorized by commissioners court order and by commission rule, to offer deputy sheriffs covered by the applicable civil service system an independent hearing examiner appeal for specified demotions, suspensions of three days or more, and terminations. A deputy choosing that route generally waives district court appeal, subject to limited grounds for review; a commissioners court may repeal its authorization, but pending appeals would remain governed by the subchapter.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the options and responsibilities of county commissioners courts and civil service commissions administering covered deputy sheriff systems.
Changes the process deputy sheriffs may use to appeal specified employment discipline.
Establishes a procedure for administering certain local civil service appeals and assigning hearing authority.

locations.name: Statewide, where a civil service system under Chapter 158 covers deputy sheriffs
locations.explanation: The subchapter is available to qualifying systems across the state, subject to local authorization and commission rules.

locations.name: County in which the sheriff's department is located
locations.explanation: The bill specifies this county as the venue for an allowed district court appeal.

affected_groups.group: Deputy sheriffs covered by a Chapter 158 civil service system
affected_groups.explanation: May be offered the independent examiner appeal route for specified employment actions and must request that route.

affected_groups.group: Sheriffs and county commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Commissioners courts may authorize or repeal the alternative appeal process; sheriffs participate in examiner selection and appeal proceedings.

affected_groups.group: Civil service commissions administering covered systems
affected_groups.explanation: May establish the examiner appeal option by rule when authorized and have duties in the examiner selection process.

major_effects.label: Optional independent examiner appeal route
major_effects.explanation: When authorized by commissioners court order and commission rule, deputy sheriffs may appeal specified demotions, suspensions of at least three days, and terminations to an independent hearing examiner rather than the commission.

major_effects.label: Final decision and limited court review
major_effects.explanation: An examiner's decision is final and binding; choosing the examiner route waives district court appeal except for the specified jurisdictional or unlawful-means grounds.

major_effects.label: Appeal cost allocation
major_effects.explanation: The losing party is liable for the examiner's fees and expenses, and each party pays the costs of witnesses it calls.

HB299.summary: The bill changes which counties are covered by the law governing grants for public improvement projects in unincorporated communities. It adds counties on an international border that partly contain a national park of less than 100,000 acres, and changes the existing population limit from 3,000 or fewer to fewer than 3,000.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which counties are covered by a grant program law for public improvement projects serving unincorporated communities.
Changes the county coverage of a grant program, potentially changing which jurisdictions may benefit; it does not itself appropriate funds.

locations.name: Texas counties meeting the statutory criteria
locations.explanation: The bill applies the chapter to counties meeting either the revised existing criteria or the added international-border and national-park criteria.

affected_groups.group: Counties meeting the statutory criteria
affected_groups.explanation: The chapter's coverage is narrowed for the existing population-based category and extended to a new category of qualifying counties.

affected_groups.group: Unincorporated communities in covered counties
affected_groups.explanation: These communities are the stated beneficiaries of the public improvement grant program governed by the chapter.

major_effects.label: Changes counties covered by the grant program law
major_effects.explanation: Adds coverage for counties on an international border that partly contain a national park under 100,000 acres, while requiring the existing population-based category to have fewer than 3,000 residents.

HB301.summary: For workers’ compensation claims based on injuries occurring on or after September 1, 2027, HB 301 would let a custodial officer, detention officer, emergency medical technician, firefighter, or peace officer request another examination to define the compensable injury, even if an examination was already performed. It would require carriers to provide specific reasons and evidence in certain refusal notices, and waive a carrier’s right to contest the extent of injury if it does not contest within 60 days after receiving the specified report. If a carrier denied medical benefits and an administrative law judge determines the injury is compensable, the carrier would reimburse all medical expenses related to the specific injury claimed.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes workers’ compensation claim, examination, dispute, and reimbursement processes for specified workers.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to qualifying workers’ compensation claims under Texas law, subject to the injury-date limitation.

affected_groups.group: Injured custodial officers, detention officers, emergency medical technicians, firefighters, and peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: These workers receive the additional examination option and are covered by the new claim-contest and medical-expense provisions.

affected_groups.group: Workers’ compensation insurance carriers
affected_groups.explanation: Carriers face the new contest deadline, notice-content requirements, and conditional medical-expense reimbursement duty.

affected_groups.group: Treating doctors and affected health care providers
affected_groups.explanation: Treating doctors must send the specified examination report to the carrier and division; affected health care providers may file an extent-of-injury dispute in the circumstances stated.

major_effects.label: Additional examination and related treatment review
major_effects.explanation: A listed worker may request an examination to define the compensable injury even if one was previously performed. The existing preauthorization and treatment-review provisions are expressly extended to examinations under this new subsection.

major_effects.label: Medical reports and refusal notices
major_effects.explanation: Treating doctors must send the report to both the carrier and the division. For the specified workers, carrier refusal notices must state the specific dispute reasons and describe the evidence reviewed.

major_effects.label: Deadline to contest extent of injury
major_effects.explanation: For the specified workers, a carrier waives its right to contest the extent of injury specifically claimed or reasonably reflected in available medical records if it does not contest by the 60th day after receiving the report.

major_effects.label: Medical-expense reimbursement after a compensability decision
major_effects.explanation: A carrier that denied medical benefits must reimburse the specified worker’s medical expenses related to the claimed injury if the administrative law judge’s decision determines that the injury is compensable.

agencies.name: division
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the division examination-authorization duties for the specified workers and requires it to receive medical reports. The supplied text does not give the division’s full agency name.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The commissioner may adopt rules concerning examination requests and reports. The supplied text does not identify the commissioner’s agency affiliation.

HB302.summary: HB 302 would make applications for new uranium-mining area permits, major amendments, and renewals subject to the public notice requirements and opportunity for a contested-case hearing provided under Section 27.018, with notice to specified surface and mineral-right owners. It separates production-area authorizations from that area-permit notice process and allows staff-only review when technical and restoration requirements are met; it also revises groundwater-restoration value methods and permits commission-approved alternatives. The changes apply only to applications submitted on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes permitting procedures and groundwater-restoration value requirements for uranium mining.
The bill changes the permitting and authorization process applicable to uranium mining operations.

locations.name: Area-permit tract, adjacent tracts, and groundwater conservation district territory in the county
locations.explanation: The notice provisions identify the permitted tract and adjacent tracts, and include mineral-right owners under groundwater conservation district territory in the county.

affected_groups.group: Surface and mineral-right owners near proposed or existing uranium-mining permitted areas
affected_groups.explanation: They are recipients of application-receipt notices for area permits.

affected_groups.group: Uranium mining permit applicants and holders
affected_groups.explanation: Their area-permit applications and production-area authorizations are subject to revised procedures and restoration-value requirements.

major_effects.label: Area-permit notice and hearing process
major_effects.explanation: New area permits, major amendments, and renewals are subject to public notice and an opportunity for a contested-case hearing. The commission must also notify specified surface and mineral-right owners.

major_effects.label: Production-area authorization review
major_effects.explanation: Production-area authorizations are separated from the area-permit notice process and may receive staff-only administrative review when technical and restoration requirements are met. If an above-range restoration value is proposed, the permit-table value must be used or a major amendment to the table must be obtained; that major amendment is subject to an opportunity for a contested-case hearing.

major_effects.label: Groundwater-restoration table values
major_effects.explanation: The bill specifies sources for initial permit-table values and allows other values acceptable to the commission or proposed by an applicant and approved by the commission.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The Act assigns notice and permit-related procedures to the commission administering these applications; it identifies the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality as the recipient of the applications covered by the changes.

HB303.summary: The bill would allow counties with populations over 90,000 but under 300,000 to regulate roadside and parking-lot vendors and solicitors if they are adjacent to a county with more than 4 million residents. The authority would remain limited to the other specified qualifying counties and to activities in unincorporated areas on public highways or roads, their rights-of-way, or in parking lots.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands which counties may exercise regulatory authority over specified vendors and solicitation.
The county regulatory authority concerns roadside and parking-lot activities and is expressly for promoting public safety.

locations.name: Unincorporated areas of qualifying counties
locations.explanation: The authority is limited to qualifying counties and applies only in their unincorporated areas at the specified public roads, rights-of-way, and parking lots.

affected_groups.group: Commissioners courts of qualifying counties
affected_groups.explanation: These county governing bodies would gain authority to regulate specified roadside and parking-lot activities by order.

affected_groups.group: Food and merchandise vendors, including live-animal vendors, and people soliciting money
affected_groups.explanation: Their sales, vendor structures, or solicitation may be subject to county regulation in the specified locations.

major_effects.label: Expanded county authority over roadside and parking-lot activity
major_effects.explanation: Adds counties with populations over 90,000 but under 300,000 to the specified population categories eligible for this authority when adjacent to a county with more than 4 million residents. Regulation remains limited to the specified activities in unincorporated areas.

HB304.summary: The bill would make any qualified voter eligible to vote early by mail, while retaining a personal-delivery registration requirement for voters certified in the address confidentiality program. It revises related mail-ballot application and processing rules, repeals certain offenses concerning solicitation and distribution of mail-ballot applications, and applies only to elections ordered on or after September 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility and procedures for early voting by mail and related ballot processing.
Repeals specified Election Code provisions identified in the bill as offenses concerning solicitation and distribution of mail-ballot applications.
Changes the standards early voting clerks use to process mail-ballot applications and provide ballots, affecting local election administration.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes Texas Election Code rules for qualified voters and election administration statewide.

affected_groups.group: Qualified voters seeking to vote early by mail
affected_groups.explanation: The bill generally makes qualified voters eligible to vote early by mail, subject to applicable application requirements.

affected_groups.group: Voters certified in the address confidentiality program
affected_groups.explanation: These voters remain subject to a personal-delivery voter-registration application requirement to qualify for early voting by mail.

affected_groups.group: Certain voters confined in jail
affected_groups.explanation: The bill specifies which applicants confined in jail at the time of application are covered by the mail-ballot provisions for jailed applicants.

affected_groups.group: Early voting clerks and local election administrators
affected_groups.explanation: They must process mail-ballot applications and provide ballots under the revised application-compliance standard.

major_effects.label: Broader eligibility for early voting by mail
major_effects.explanation: Any qualified voter may vote early by mail, while voters certified in the address confidentiality program remain subject to a personal-delivery voter-registration application requirement.

major_effects.label: Revised mail-ballot application and processing rules
major_effects.explanation: Applications and ballot mailing rules are adjusted to reflect the applicant's circumstances; jailed applicants are covered only under the specified confinement conditions, and clerks provide ballots when applications meet applicable requirements.

major_effects.label: Repeal of certain mail-ballot application offenses
major_effects.explanation: The bill repeals specified Election Code provisions identified as criminal offenses concerning solicitation and distribution of mail-ballot applications.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The amended address-confidentiality provision remains subject to the secretary of state's expressly stated authority to adopt implementing rules; the bill does not impose a new mandatory rulemaking duty.

HB305.summary: The bill designates English as Texas’s official language and provides that a state agency is not required to provide written materials or website information in another language. Agencies may provide non-English translations or explanations only if they are unofficial and nonbinding, cost the state nothing, and explain how to obtain or view the official version. The bill also repeals Government Code Section 2054.116.

policy_tags.explanation: Sets rules for state agencies' provision of written materials and website information in languages other than English.
Changes the rules governing access to official state information for people who use languages other than English.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill designates the official language of the state and applies its agency rules statewide.

affected_groups.group: People seeking state documents, materials, or website information in languages other than English
affected_groups.explanation: They may not be able to rely on agencies to provide non-English information; any agency-provided translation or explanation must be unofficial and nonbinding and satisfy stated conditions.

affected_groups.group: State agencies as defined by the bill
affected_groups.explanation: The defined agencies are subject to the new rules for official-language materials and any optional non-English translations or explanations.

major_effects.label: Official-language designation
major_effects.explanation: Designates English as the official language of Texas.

major_effects.label: Rules for non-English agency information
major_effects.explanation: Agencies are not required to provide written materials or website information in another language. Optional translations or explanations must be unofficial and nonbinding, cost the state nothing, and state how to obtain or view the official content.

major_effects.label: Repeal of Government Code Section 2054.116
major_effects.explanation: Repeals the section, but the supplied bill text does not state what that existing provision requires.

agencies.name: state agency
agencies.explanation: The bill directly governs the bill-defined class of state agencies; it does not name an individual agency that can be matched to a registry entry.

HB306.summary: The bill expands the period in which family violence, abuse, sexual abuse, or related protective orders may be considered in conservatorship and child-access decisions. The period begins five years before suit filing or when the parties began living separately, whichever is earlier, and also includes conduct or orders during the suit; the changes apply to suits pending on the effective date or filed afterward.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes family-court standards for considering family violence and abuse when deciding conservatorship and child access.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and applies to qualifying suits in trial courts statewide.

affected_groups.group: Parents and other parties in suits affecting the parent-child relationship
affected_groups.explanation: The expanded period may affect conservatorship decisions and whether a parent may have access to a child.

affected_groups.group: Children involved in parent-child relationship suits
affected_groups.explanation: Their conservatorship and access decisions may take account of a longer history of family violence or abuse.

major_effects.label: Expanded period for considering violence and protective orders
major_effects.explanation: Courts would consider relevant conduct and Chapter 85 protective orders from a period beginning five years before filing or when the parties began living separately, whichever is earlier, as well as during the suit.

major_effects.label: Child-access restriction for qualifying family-violence history
major_effects.explanation: A court may not allow parental access when the specified family-violence history is shown by a preponderance of the evidence within the expanded period or during the suit.

agencies.name: the court
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the evidence and time period courts must consider in suits affecting the parent-child relationship. The bill does not identify a specific court category that can be mapped to a canonical registry entry.

HB307.summary: HB 307 would require the Texas Cyber Command to establish at least one intrastate information-sharing organization and would authorize it to establish an interstate organization. The center, coordinating with the digital forensics laboratory, would operate each organization, which would provide forums for the specified public, higher-education, and private-sector participants. Participants would have to assert any applicable state or federal public-disclosure exception for shared information, and Section 552.007 would not apply to that information.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands cybersecurity threat-information sharing and specifies how participants must respond to public-disclosure requests for shared information.
The bill changes the Command's authority to establish information-sharing organizations and the center's operational responsibility for them.
Local governments are expressly included in the forum created by the required intrastate organization.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The required intrastate organization includes entities in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Texas state agencies and local governments
affected_groups.explanation: They are among the participants for whom the required intrastate organization provides a forum.

affected_groups.group: Public and private institutions of higher education and private-sector entities in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: They are expressly included in the intrastate organization's forum.

affected_groups.group: Participants in organizations established under the section
affected_groups.explanation: They must assert applicable public-disclosure exceptions in response to requests for shared information.

major_effects.label: Intrastate and optional interstate organizations
major_effects.explanation: The Command must establish at least one intrastate organization and may establish an interstate organization for sharing cybersecurity information.

major_effects.label: Expanded operations by the center
major_effects.explanation: The center's duty changes from operating the organization to operating each organization established under the section.

major_effects.label: Disclosure-exception procedure for shared information
major_effects.explanation: Participants in any organization established under the section must assert available state or federal exceptions when disclosure is requested; this does not make all shared information categorically confidential.

agencies.name: Texas Cyber Command
agencies.explanation: Chapter 2063 defines “Command” as the Texas Cyber Command established under the chapter; the bill directs the Command to establish at least one intrastate information sharing and analysis organization. No matching registry entry is supplied, so no registry ID is supported.

HB308.summary: The bill would prohibit a governmental entity in Texas from requiring a person to install or use an intelligent speed assistance device on a motor vehicle. The definition excludes speed-control technology provided by a vehicle manufacturer as a component of a new motor vehicle.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes requirements concerning motor vehicles and speed-assistance devices.
The prohibition limits governmental entities in Texas, including local governments, from requiring use or installation of the device.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The prohibition applies to governmental entities throughout Texas.

affected_groups.group: People who might be required to install or use an intelligent speed assistance device
affected_groups.explanation: They would be protected from a governmental entity requiring installation or use of the defined device.

affected_groups.group: Governmental entities in Texas, including local governments
affected_groups.explanation: They would be prohibited from requiring installation or use of the device.

major_effects.label: Prohibits governmental device mandates
major_effects.explanation: Governmental entities could not require a person to install or use a defined intelligent speed assistance device on a motor vehicle; manufacturer-provided technology that is a component of a new vehicle is excluded from the definition.

HB309.summary: The bill would designate the golden-cheeked warbler, instead of the mockingbird, as the state bird of Texas.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The designation concerns the state bird.

major_effects.label: State symbol designation
major_effects.explanation: Would replace the mockingbird with the golden-cheeked warbler as the designated state bird.

HB310.summary: The bill would add a liability shield for owners, lessees, and occupants of nonagricultural land for injury or property damage arising from specified events involving entry onto the land. The shield would not cover harm arising from the landholder’s willful or wanton act or gross negligence, and would apply only to causes of action accruing on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the liability rules for owners, lessees, and occupants of nonagricultural land.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The proposed Texas law would apply to qualifying nonagricultural land statewide.

affected_groups.group: Owners, lessees, and occupants of nonagricultural land
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive the liability protection for specified injuries and property damage, subject to the bill’s exception for their willful or wanton acts or gross negligence.

affected_groups.group: People seeking recovery for injury or property damage
affected_groups.explanation: Their claims may be limited when the injury or damage arises from the events specified in the bill.

major_effects.label: Limits landholder liability for specified events
major_effects.explanation: Would shield nonagricultural landholders from liability for harm arising from specified events, including peace or federal law enforcement officer actions or omissions when the officer enters or causes another person to enter the land, with or without permission; firefighter actions or omissions when the firefighter enters or causes another person to enter; trespass, unauthorized fence or gate damage, wildlife, and acts of God. The shield does not extend to harm arising from the landholder’s wil

HB311.summary: HB 311 would take effect only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment. It would reserve certain disaster and emergency business restrictions to the Legislature and limit the governor’s authority to suspend laws or continue certain disaster declarations.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the division of disaster and emergency powers among the Legislature, governor, and state agencies.
Revises the statutory distinction between disasters and force- or violence-related emergencies and changes emergency powers.
Reserves authority to impose certain category- or region-based business operating or occupancy restrictions to the Legislature during disasters and emergencies.
Limits the scope of local disaster declarations and emergency directives, and requires consultation with affected county judges for certain disaster-related business restrictions.
Restricts the governor’s authority to suspend specified Election Code provisions during a disaster, subject to stated exceptions.
Limits when the governor may suspend provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure and Penal Code during a declared disaster.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The business restriction provisions apply to businesses in this state.

locations.name: County or municipality for which an application was made
locations.explanation: A directive under the emergency provision is limited to the jurisdiction of the county or municipality that applied.

affected_groups.group: Businesses and business operators
affected_groups.explanation: Their operations or occupancy may be restricted by category or region only through legislative authority during a declared disaster or emergency.

affected_groups.group: Counties and municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Local disaster declarations and emergency directives are subject to new limits; the restriction on local disaster declarations applies unless expressly authorized by a proclamation or executive order issued by the governor. County judges must be consulted for certain disaster-related business restrictions affecting their counties.

affected_groups.group: State agencies affected by suspended statutes or rules
affected_groups.explanation: These agencies must publish the suspended statutes and rules on their websites.

affected_groups.group: Voters in disaster areas
affected_groups.explanation: The bill limits suspension of specified voting procedures while preserving a narrow ballot-delivery exception for voters registered at addresses in a disaster area.

major_effects.label: Legislative authority over business restrictions
major_effects.explanation: During a declared disaster or emergency, only the Legislature may impose category- or region-based business operation or occupancy restrictions. For disaster restrictions, the Legislature must consult affected county judges; the governor must convene a special session if the Legislature is not convened and the governor finds that authority should be exercised.

major_effects.label: Legislative role in certain disaster renewals
major_effects.explanation: For a disaster declaration described by the specified constitutional provision, the governor must convene the Legislature to respond if renewal is needed and the Legislature is not in session. The rule does not apply to renewals based solely on the listed fire, flood, wind, storm, wave action, drought, or extreme-heat declarations; the governor also may not re-declare a substantially similar disaster after legislative termination or nonrenewal.

major_effects.label: Limits on emergency suspensions of laws and rules
major_effects.explanation: The governor may not suspend Chapter 418 or Chapter 433, or suspend a law or rule in a way that continues an agency beyond its statutory abolishment date. Suspensions of provisions in the Code of Criminal Procedure, Election Code, or Penal Code are limited to the first 30 days; if the governor finds continued suspension necessary while the Legislature is not in session, the governor must convene a special session.

major_effects.label: Limits on suspending election procedures
major_effects.explanation: The governor generally may not suspend the specified early-mail-voting or voter-acceptance procedures. A narrow exception permits delivery of a marked ballot by a voter registered at a disaster-area address, and the voting period for early voting by mail may still be extended as necessary to address the disaster.

major_effects.label: Boundaries for local disaster declarations and emergency directives
major_effects.explanation: A local disaster declaration may not conflict with or change the scope of a state disaster declaration unless the governor expressly authorizes it. Emergency directives apply only within the jurisdiction of the county or municipality that applied.

major_effects.label: Online publication of suspended laws and rules
major_effects.explanation: The governor's office must publish its compiled list online, and each state agency affected by a suspension must publish its own list; agency lists must be updated within 24 hours of a suspension and be readily accessible from the agency homepage.

major_effects.label: Revised disaster and emergency categories
major_effects.explanation: The statutory disaster definition excludes causes related to force or violence, including civil unrest, riots, or insurrection; the emergency provisions include a natural or man-made disaster related to force or violence.

agencies.name: governor's office
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the governor's office a website publication duty; the supplied canonical registry does not identify a matching entry.

HB312.summary: HB 312 would allow a person who will be 18 years of age or older by the next general election for state and county officers to register for the primary election to determine a political party’s nominees, if the person satisfies the requirements of Subsection (a) except for age. The Secretary of State would prescribe implementation procedures, and a voter registrar could notify these registrants that they cannot vote in other elections until age 18. The bill would take effect only if the proposed constitutional amendment is approved and takes effect; otherwise, the bill has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes registration and primary-voting eligibility for people who will be 18 by the next general election.
Authorizes a voter registrar to send an eligibility notice; whether this is a local-government impact depends on the statutory identity of the registrar.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The registration change applies to voting in this state.

affected_groups.group: People under 18 who will be 18 by the next general election for state and county officers
affected_groups.explanation: They may qualify to register and vote in a primary before turning 18, but remain ineligible for other elections until age 18.

affected_groups.group: Voter registrars
affected_groups.explanation: Registrars may send a written notice explaining the limited election eligibility of registrants under the new provision.

major_effects.label: Registration and primary-voting eligibility before age 18
major_effects.explanation: A person who will be 18 by the next general election may register for primary-election purposes and vote in a primary if the person meets the other voter qualifications; the change does not make the person eligible to vote in other elections before turning 18.

major_effects.label: Election implementation procedures
major_effects.explanation: The Secretary of State must prescribe procedures for implementing the new provisions; for primary voting, the Secretary must consult the specified political-party chairs.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The Secretary of State is directed to prescribe procedures to implement the new registration and primary-voting provisions.

HB313.summary: The bill would prohibit state agencies from adopting, enforcing, or maintaining rules that require applicants for agency permits, licenses, benefits, and other listed actions to prove U.S. citizenship or residency, unless another statute expressly authorizes the requirement. A rule violating the prohibition would be void and unenforceable.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes a general restriction on state agencies' adoption, enforcement, and maintenance of rules.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies to state agencies generally rather than to a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for state-agency permits, licenses, registrations, benefits, exemptions, contracts, grants, or loans
affected_groups.explanation: These applicants would be covered by the restriction on agency rules requiring proof of U.S. citizenship or residency, unless another statute expressly authorizes the requirement.

major_effects.label: Restricts agency documentation rules
major_effects.explanation: Agencies generally could not adopt, enforce, or maintain rules requiring the specified proof, unless another statute expressly authorizes the requirement.

major_effects.label: Makes violating rules unenforceable
major_effects.explanation: A rule that violates the prohibition would be void and unenforceable.

agencies.name: State agencies
agencies.explanation: The bill directly restricts state agencies as a class; it does not identify particular agencies.

HB314.summary: HB 314 would bar the public school financial accountability rating system from counting amounts a school district is required to spend to comply with Chapter 49 when calculating its assets-to-liabilities ratio, if the district is required to reduce its local revenue under Section 48.257. The change would apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes a measure used in the public school financial accountability rating system.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change concerns school districts covered by the statewide Education Code provision.

affected_groups.group: School districts required to reduce their local revenue level under Section 48.257
affected_groups.explanation: Their Chapter 49-required spending would be excluded from the specified assets-to-liabilities calculation.

major_effects.label: Adjusts financial rating calculation
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying districts, the rating system could not include Chapter 49-required spending when determining the assets-to-liabilities ratio.

HB315.summary: The bill would let a peace officer or county or municipal animal-control officer apply for a warrant to seize a cruelly treated animal in the county or municipality where the animal is located. If the animal is on property with a property line within 400 feet of another county’s or municipality’s boundary, it would also allow an application in that other county or municipality.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes where an officer may apply for a warrant to seize an animal alleged to have been cruelly treated.
Expands the county and municipal court venues available for applications by officers, including specified nearby jurisdictions.

locations.name: County or municipal boundary areas where the property line is within 400 feet of another jurisdiction’s boundary
locations.explanation: The bill makes the other county or municipality an eligible venue when the property line meets the 400-foot boundary condition.

affected_groups.group: Peace officers and county or municipal animal-control officers
affected_groups.explanation: These officers may apply for a warrant in additional jurisdictions under the specified boundary conditions.

affected_groups.group: People whose animals are subject to cruelty-seizure warrant applications
affected_groups.explanation: The bill expands the court venues where an officer may seek a warrant to seize an animal alleged to be cruelly treated.

major_effects.label: Expands eligible warrant venues
major_effects.explanation: Allows applications in the county or municipality where the animal is located and, when the property line is within 400 feet of another jurisdiction’s boundary, in that other jurisdiction.

agencies.name: justice court or magistrate
agencies.explanation: The bill directly makes these court venues available for warrant applications in the stated circumstances, but does not identify a specific court or establish a canonical agency identity.

HB316.summary: HB 316 would require each general academic teaching institution to add a class-wide average grade—or, when all students receive letter grades, the median—to a student's transcript beside the student's grade for each attempted class. Pass/fail-only or independent-study classes and classes with grades reported for 10 or fewer students would be excluded, and the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board would adopt implementing rules. The requirement would apply beginning with the 2027 fall semester.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes transcript requirements for covered postsecondary institutions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to covered institutions under the Texas Education Code; the precise institution category is defined by referenced state law.

affected_groups.group: Students at covered general academic teaching institutions
affected_groups.explanation: Their transcripts would display the applicable class average or median for attempted classes, subject to the stated exclusions.

affected_groups.group: General academic teaching institutions
affected_groups.explanation: These institutions would have to add class-level grade information to student transcripts.

major_effects.label: Class-level grade information on transcripts
major_effects.explanation: For each attempted class, transcripts would include the class average or, when all students receive letter grades, the median, placed beside the student's individual grade. The requirement excludes pass/fail-only or independent-study classes and classes with grades reported for 10 or fewer students.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board must adopt rules to administer the requirement.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The board must adopt rules to administer the new transcript requirement.

HB317.summary: The bill would authorize religious organizations to establish 24-hour faith-based facilities for children in the department’s conservatorship, subject to requirements including care planning, staff training, mental-health services, committee oversight, and faith-family programs. These facilities would be exempt from Chapter 42 licensing and rules for licensed child-care facilities, but the department would set minimum standards, periodically evaluate facilities, and integrate them into the foster-care system. The bill would also establish a grant program, using available funds or private donations, to help religious organizations establish facilities.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires contracted mental and behavioral health services for children in the facilities and requires those services to meet professional-care standards.
The bill creates a category of child-care facility exempt from ordinary Chapter 42 licensing and licensed-facility rules, with separate minimum standards and evaluations.
The bill requires a grant program for facility establishment, funded using available funds or private donations.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill provides for integration of these facilities into the state foster-care system.

affected_groups.group: Foster youth in the department’s conservatorship
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive care in these facilities and participate in the associated faith-family and mental-health programs.

affected_groups.group: Religious organizations establishing faith-based child-care facilities
affected_groups.explanation: They may establish and operate facilities and would have planning, training, oversight, and program responsibilities; they may also receive grants.

affected_groups.group: Licensed mental health services providers
affected_groups.explanation: A facility’s establishing organization must contract with a licensed provider to provide services to youth in its care.

affected_groups.group: Child-placing agencies
affected_groups.explanation: They may place children in facilities established under the bill.

major_effects.label: Faith-based foster-care facilities
major_effects.explanation: Religious organizations could establish 24-hour facilities for children in the department’s conservatorship, and the department would integrate them into the foster-care system.

major_effects.label: Separate licensing and oversight framework
major_effects.explanation: Facilities would be exempt from Chapter 42 licensing and rules for licensed facilities, while remaining subject to department-adopted minimum standards and periodic evaluation.

major_effects.label: Facility establishment grants
major_effects.explanation: The department would administer grants to religious organizations using available funds or private donations.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department duties to integrate these facilities into foster care, adopt standards, evaluate facilities, and administer grants. The source does not identify which department the generic term refers to, so no canonical registry identity is assigned.

HB318.summary: The bill requires the attorney general to defend a school district in lawsuits alleging that an expulsion based on a student's threat to safety violates state or federal law; the attorney general may settle those cases. The state must indemnify the district for related damages, settlements, and other costs, but the change applies only to actions filed on or after the effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds legal-defense and indemnification provisions for lawsuits arising from school-district student expulsions.
School districts receive a required state-provided defense and indemnification in the specified cases.
The state must cover specified damages, settlements, and other costs or expenses arising from the covered actions.
The bill assigns the attorney general a defense duty and authority to settle a defined category of lawsuits.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply generally to school districts under the Texas Education Code and do not identify a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts receive attorney general representation and state indemnification in the specified lawsuits.

affected_groups.group: Students expelled on a safety-threat basis who bring covered legal actions
affected_groups.explanation: Their lawsuits alleging that the expulsion violates state or federal law are subject to the new defense and indemnification provisions.

major_effects.label: Attorney general defense and settlement role
major_effects.explanation: Requires the attorney general to defend a district in the covered actions and allows the attorney general to settle them.

major_effects.label: State indemnification
major_effects.explanation: Requires the state to indemnify the district for damages, settlement amounts, and other costs or expenses arising from a covered action.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the attorney general a duty to defend school districts in the specified actions and permits the attorney general to settle them.

HB319.summary: The bill would require the state to compensate a county for the cost of confining, pending trial, a defendant charged with a felony who is not released on bail. The requirement applies to confinement costs incurred on or after January 1, 2028, even if the confinement began before that date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes compensation for county-jail confinement of felony defendants who are not released on bail pending trial.
Requires compensation to counties for specified county-jail confinement costs.
Creates a state payment obligation for qualifying county-jail confinement costs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The compensation requirement applies to counties generally; no particular county or place is specified.

affected_groups.group: County governments
affected_groups.explanation: Counties would receive compensation for qualifying confinement costs.

affected_groups.group: Felony defendants held in county jail pending trial without release on bail
affected_groups.explanation: Their confinement costs would qualify for state compensation to the county.

major_effects.label: State compensation to counties
major_effects.explanation: Requires the state to compensate counties for the cost of qualifying confinement; the requirement applies to costs incurred on or after January 1, 2028, regardless of when confinement began.

HB320.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, HB 320 would expand school-district reports on counseling programs to include campus counselor counts, average time spent on program and non-program duties, and findings about compliance with district policy. The report would also have to evaluate the district’s counseling program based on that information; time spent interpreting assessment data is excluded from the specified assessment-related time accounting.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes reporting requirements for school-district counseling programs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide Texas Education Code requirements applicable to school districts.

affected_groups.group: Texas school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would have to include additional counseling-program information and an evaluation in the report.

affected_groups.group: School counselors
affected_groups.explanation: Their campus-level numbers and average work hours would be reported.

major_effects.label: Expanded counseling-program reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires reports to include counselor counts by campus, average hours for counseling-program and other duties, district policy-compliance assessment findings, and a program evaluation based on the reported information. Assessment-data interpretation time is excluded from the specified assessment-related time accounting.

HB321.summary: HB 321 would require a provider that offers a discounted cash price to an uninsured patient to offer that same price to other patients for the service or supply, regardless of coverage, and disclose the price in writing. It would also bar covered health-plan contracts from prohibiting those offers and disclosures.

policy_tags.explanation: Sets price-offer and written-disclosure requirements for health care services and supplies.
Regulates provider pricing practices and restricts provisions in health-plan issuer/provider contracts.
Expressly applies the contract restrictions to the state Medicaid program, including Medicaid managed care.
Expressly applies the contract restrictions to county employee health benefits and coverage provided by locally created risk pools.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The provider definition covers authorizations issued by the state, and the bill establishes Texas-wide requirements.

affected_groups.group: Health care practitioners and facilities authorized by Texas
affected_groups.explanation: They must offer and disclose the discounted cash price when the statutory triggering condition applies, and may face license or authorization suspension or revocation for violations.

affected_groups.group: Patients, including patients with and without health-benefit coverage
affected_groups.explanation: Patients may receive the same discounted cash price for a service or supply and a written disclosure of that price when the provider offers the price to a patient without coverage.

affected_groups.group: Health-benefit plan issuers and covered plan participants
affected_groups.explanation: Covered plan contracts may not prohibit providers from making the required offers and disclosures; the covered plans include specified Medicaid coverage.

affected_groups.group: County employee health-plan participants and local risk-pool participants
affected_groups.explanation: The contract restrictions apply to specified county employee health benefits and coverage provided by local-government risk pools.

major_effects.label: Discounted cash-price offer and disclosure
major_effects.explanation: When a provider gives a discounted cash price for a service or supply to a patient without health-benefit coverage, it must offer that same price to each other patient for that service or supply, regardless of coverage, and disclose the price in writing.

major_effects.label: Health-plan contract restriction
major_effects.explanation: Covered health-benefit plan contracts may not prohibit the provider offers and disclosures; the covered plans include Medicaid and specified county employee benefits and local risk-pool coverage.

major_effects.label: Provider license and authorization enforcement
major_effects.explanation: The appropriate state regulatory authority must suspend or revoke a provider's license or other authorization for a violation of the new subchapter.

major_effects.label: HHSC implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: The Health and Human Services Commission's executive commissioner must adopt rules necessary to implement the new subchapter.

major_effects.label: Conditional federal authorization
major_effects.explanation: If, before implementing a provision, a state agency determines that a federal waiver or authorization is necessary, it must request it and may delay implementing that provision until it is granted.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is directed to adopt rules to implement the new discounted-cash-price subchapter.

agencies.name: appropriate state regulatory authority
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns this authority provider-license enforcement, but does not identify which body is responsible for each provider type.

HB322.summary: The bill would require a taxing unit to apply a property owner's tax payment to the tax due before penalties or interest, unless the owner gives written instructions for a different application. It would also cap a person's total liability for penalties and interest on delinquent taxes at five percent of the delinquent tax.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes how property tax payments are applied and limits penalties and interest on delinquent taxes.
The bill changes the payment-application duty of collectors for taxing units.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Tax Code and applies to property tax payments and delinquent taxes under that state law.

affected_groups.group: Property owners who make tax payments
affected_groups.explanation: Their payments would be applied to tax due before penalties or interest unless they provide different written instructions.

affected_groups.group: People liable for delinquent property taxes
affected_groups.explanation: Their total liability for penalties and interest would be capped at five percent of the delinquent tax.

affected_groups.group: Taxing units and their collectors
affected_groups.explanation: Collectors would have to apply payments to tax before penalty or interest, unless the property owner provides written instructions for a different application.

major_effects.label: Payment application order
major_effects.explanation: A collector must apply a property owner's payment to tax due before penalties or interest, unless the owner provides written instructions for a different application.

major_effects.label: Cap on delinquent-tax penalties and interest
major_effects.explanation: Total penalties and interest for a person on a delinquent tax could not exceed five percent of the delinquent tax, regardless of the amount otherwise incurred or accrued.

HB323.summary: The bill designates the first seven days of August as Back to School Immunization Awareness Week to highlight immunization’s importance for students, families, and school communities. The week may be observed through programs and activities that educate about immunization and encourage families to consult health care providers before the school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Designates an immunization awareness observance and permits activities promoting education about immunization.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes the observance in Texas law without limiting it to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Students, families, and school communities
affected_groups.explanation: The awareness week is intended to promote immunization awareness for these groups.

affected_groups.group: Families
affected_groups.explanation: Families are encouraged to consult health care providers about immunization before the school year.

major_effects.label: Awareness-week designation
major_effects.explanation: Designates the first seven days of August as an immunization awareness week; programs and activities may be used to observe it.

HB324.summary: HB 324 would require private schools seeking approval for the education savings account program to post information about services and accommodations for students with disabilities and disclose that they are not required to follow a student's IEP or Section 504 plan. It also updates statutory cross-references used to determine whether tutors, therapists, and teaching-service employees are disqualified. The changes would apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility requirements for providers participating in an education program.
Changes requirements for private schools seeking to participate in the education savings account program.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes concern participation in the state education savings account program and specify no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Private schools seeking approval for the education savings account program
affected_groups.explanation: These schools would have to post the specified disability-services information to meet the stated approval requirements.

affected_groups.group: Students with disabilities and their families
affected_groups.explanation: The required website disclosures address services and accommodations for students with disabilities and whether the school must follow an IEP or Section 504 plan.

affected_groups.group: Private tutors, therapists, and teaching-service employees
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes statutory cross-references used for their disqualification and registry criteria; whether the criteria themselves change is unclear from the bill text.

major_effects.label: Private-school participation disclosures
major_effects.explanation: Adds website disclosures about disability-related services and accommodations, including that the school is not required to provide services as prescribed by an IEP or Section 504 plan, to the private-school approval requirements.

major_effects.label: Updated personnel disqualification references
major_effects.explanation: Replaces statutory citations used for tutor, therapist, and teaching-service employee disqualifications; the text alone does not show whether the referenced criteria change.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The Comptroller approves education service providers and vendors, so the new private-school website condition would be applied as part of that approval.

HB325.summary: HB 325 would let a municipality where a majority of voters favored adoption or reauthorization in each of the last two consecutive elections, and whose tax has not expired since the first, call an election for an 8- or 10-year reauthorization; otherwise, reauthorization is for four years. It would allow tax revenue to maintain and repair municipal streets or sidewalks, and water, wastewater, or stormwater systems only when located within the width of a municipal street. The new expiration rules apply only to taxes adopted or reauthorized after the effective date, and the revised ballot language applies only to elections ordered after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes reauthorization periods and ballot language for a municipal sales and use tax.
Changes the tax-election options and permissible uses of revenue for municipalities.
Changes the authorized use of local tax revenue for municipal street and sidewalk maintenance and repair.
Permits revenue to be used for specified municipal water, wastewater, and stormwater systems within a municipal street's width of way.

locations.name: Statewide, in municipalities imposing the Chapter 327 tax
locations.explanation: The bill establishes rules for qualifying municipalities under the statewide municipal tax statute; it names no particular place.

affected_groups.group: Municipal governments imposing the Chapter 327 tax
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible municipalities may choose a longer reauthorization period, and municipalities may use the tax revenue for the specified maintenance and repair purposes.

affected_groups.group: Voters in municipalities holding a tax adoption or reauthorization election
affected_groups.explanation: Voters decide whether to reauthorize the tax, including whether it continues for a longer term where eligible.

major_effects.label: Longer municipal tax reauthorization options
major_effects.explanation: A municipality meeting the two-election majority-support and no-expiration conditions may call an election for an 8- or 10-year term instead of four years; the longer term is not automatic and depends on the election.

major_effects.label: Expanded permitted uses of tax revenue
major_effects.explanation: Revenue may be used for maintenance and repair of municipal streets or sidewalks and of water, wastewater, or stormwater systems located within the width of a municipal street; this does not authorize use for those systems outside that area.

HB326.summary: HB326 would require the Texas Historical Commission to establish a program to identify, restore, maintain, and preserve Rosenwald School structures and protect their historic and architectural integrity, with the program first implemented in the south central region of Texas. The commission could acquire property and accept donations; the Legislature could appropriate funds, but the bill does not itself appropriate money, and restored structures could be used as community learning centers.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a program and assigns its administration to the Texas Historical Commission.
The program is focused on restoring and preserving historic structures and protecting their architectural integrity.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The program covers Rosenwald School structures located in the state.

locations.name: South central region of Texas
locations.explanation: The commission must first implement the program in this region.
