affected_groups.group: Employees, former employees, and contractors of developers or deployers
affected_groups.explanation: Protected from specified adverse personnel actions for good-faith reporting or assistance with an investigation or proceeding.

major_effects.label: Human oversight and override requirements
major_effects.explanation: Developers must provide, test, and document oversight mechanisms; deployers must maintain controls that enable human monitoring and intervention, with additional controls proportionate to the nature and risk of system actions.

major_effects.label: Testing of oversight mechanisms
major_effects.explanation: Deployers must test required mechanisms before deployment, at least annually, after specified material changes, and after a material failure before resuming affected operations.

major_effects.label: Protection for good-faith reporting
major_effects.explanation: Bars specified adverse personnel actions against employees, former employees, or contractors for good-faith reporting or assistance concerning alleged violations.

major_effects.label: Attorney General enforcement and technical consultation
major_effects.explanation: Makes violations subject to Attorney General enforcement under Subchapter C and allows temporary injunctive relief before notice only when continued unlawful operation poses an immediate and substantial risk of serious harm. The Attorney General must consult the Department of Information Resources on technical compliance.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: A violation is subject to enforcement by the Attorney General under Subchapter C. The bill also permits the Attorney General to seek temporary injunctive relief in the specified urgent-risk circumstances and requires consultation with the department when evaluating technical compliance.

agencies.name: Department of Information Resources
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly defines “Department” as the Department of Information Resources and requires the Attorney General to consult it and provide relevant reports and technical documentation for compliance evaluations. The bill does not authorize the department to bring enforcement actions.

HB511.summary: The bill would require each intended parent and gestational mother in a gestational agreement to be a U.S. citizen and would prohibit specified foreign-adversary citizens and people acting for a designated foreign terrorist organization from participating. A court could validate an agreement only if neither the intended parent nor the gestational mother is prohibited, and the changes would apply only to petitions filed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill makes U.S. citizenship and specified foreign-affiliation status conditions for participating in a gestational agreement.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The amendments to the Texas Family Code establish rules for gestational agreements across Texas.

affected_groups.group: Intended parents and gestational mothers seeking to enter a gestational agreement
affected_groups.explanation: Their eligibility would depend on citizenship and the specified foreign-adversary and terrorist-organization restrictions.

affected_groups.group: People who are not U.S. citizens or who fall within the specified foreign-affiliation restrictions
affected_groups.explanation: They would be barred from participating as an intended parent or gestational mother under the bill’s qualifications.

major_effects.label: Gestational-agreement party qualifications
major_effects.explanation: The bill would require intended parents and gestational mothers to be U.S. citizens and exclude the specified foreign-adversary citizens and people acting for designated foreign terrorist organizations; courts could validate agreements only if the parties meet these restrictions.

agencies.name: court
agencies.explanation: For a court to validate a gestational agreement under Subsection (c), it must find that neither intended parent nor the gestational mother is prohibited under Section 160.754(b-1) from entering into the agreement.

HB512.summary: HB 512 would add an offense requiring an attorney to register as a sex offender under Chapter 62 to the offenses that trigger court-ordered suspension while appeals are pending and disbarment after final conviction. The changes would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act's effective date; an offense with any element occurring before then would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Makes convictions for offenses requiring sex-offender registration a basis for mandatory attorney discipline.
Expands the district courts' mandatory duties to order attorney suspension and disbarment for the added offense category.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Texas Government Code and applies the change to covered cases statewide.

locations.name: County of the convicted attorney's residence
locations.explanation: The bill assigns the relevant suspension and disbarment orders to the district court of that county.

affected_groups.group: Attorneys convicted of an offense requiring sex-offender registration
affected_groups.explanation: Their ability to practice law would be subject to suspension during appeals and disbarment after final conviction.

major_effects.label: Expanded mandatory attorney discipline
major_effects.explanation: Adds the covered offenses as grounds for suspension during appeals and disbarment after final conviction; the amendments apply only to offenses committed on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Conviction record in disbarment actions
major_effects.explanation: For the added offense category, the record of conviction is conclusive evidence of the attorney's guilt in a disbarment action.

agencies.name: district court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns suspension and disbarment order duties to the district court, but does not identify a specific court or establish a canonical registry mapping.

HB513.summary: The bill would make the cited federal conviction-based exclusion inapplicable when determining eligibility for Chapter 31 financial assistance or SNAP. These changes would apply only to initial eligibility decisions or redeterminations made on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes eligibility for Chapter 31 financial assistance, potentially affecting who can receive public-benefit payments.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The eligibility changes apply to the Texas benefit programs statewide, with no geographic limitation stated.

affected_groups.group: People seeking Chapter 31 financial assistance or SNAP whose convictions fall within the cited federal exclusion
affected_groups.explanation: Their eligibility would be evaluated without applying the cited federal provision, subject to the bill's timing rule for initial determinations and redeterminations.

major_effects.label: Chapter 31 financial assistance eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Makes 21 U.S.C. Section 862a(a) inapplicable when determining eligibility for financial assistance.

major_effects.label: SNAP eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Makes 21 U.S.C. Section 862a(a) inapplicable to SNAP eligibility and repeals Human Resources Code Section 33.018(b) and (c).

major_effects.label: Conditional federal authorization process
major_effects.explanation: If an affected state agency determines before implementation that federal authorization is necessary, it must request it and may delay implementation of that provision until authorization is granted.

agencies.name: agency affected by the provision
agencies.explanation: If a state agency determines that federal authorization is needed for implementation, the bill requires the affected agency to request it. The bill does not identify that agency by name.

HB514.summary: HB 514 would establish that a surface-estate owner has an inherent, nonseverable right to capture and use wind energy, directly or through a wind-energy developer, and would subject wind-energy agreements to the same rules as other agreements involving interests in or use of real property. When an agreement expires or is terminated, the developer holding it at that time must record a release; if it does not, the owner may request one, subject to the bill’s good-faith-claim qualification and response process. The bill would not affect the validity of agreements entered into before its effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes a surface-estate owner’s right to capture and use wind energy and regulates agreements for wind-powered generation.
The bill defines a right attached to the surface estate and establishes requirements for releasing recorded agreements affecting land.
The bill imposes release-recording and related response requirements on wind-energy developers after an agreement expires or is terminated.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill adds generally applicable provisions to the Texas Utilities Code and does not limit them to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Owners of surface estates
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive the stated wind-energy right and may request a release when a developer fails to record one.

affected_groups.group: Wind-energy developers and successors to their interests
affected_groups.explanation: Developers holding an expired or terminated agreement would have release-recording duties, with related duties applying when an owner requests a release or identifies a successor.

major_effects.label: Surface-estate wind-energy right
major_effects.explanation: Establishes an inherent right to capture and use wind energy, directly or through a developer under an agreement, and makes that right inseparable from the surface estate.

major_effects.label: Release of expired or terminated agreements
major_effects.explanation: Requires the developer holding the agreement at expiration or termination to record a release. If the developer fails to do so, an owner may request one; absent a good-faith claim that the agreement remains in force, the recipient must record the release or provide successor information within the bill’s response period.

HB515.summary: For health benefit plans and policies delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028, the bill removes the requirement that noncontracting dentists receive the same payment or reimbursement as contracting dentists. It instead requires plans to offer at least one payment method that provides the dentist 100 percent of the contracted amount without requiring the dentist to pay a fee to access it; plans issued, delivered, or renewed before that date remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes payment and reimbursement requirements for dental services under certain health benefit plans and policies.
Imposes payment-method requirements on employee benefit plans and health insurance policies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Insurance Code and sets requirements applicable to covered plans and policies across the state.

affected_groups.group: Dentists providing dental care services
affected_groups.explanation: Dentists must have access to at least one payment method that provides the contracted amount without an access fee; the prior same-payment rule for noncontracting dentists is removed.

affected_groups.group: Employee benefit plans and health insurance policies
affected_groups.explanation: Covered plans and policies must provide the specified payment method for applicable plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: Dental payment and reimbursement rules
major_effects.explanation: Removes the equal-payment requirement for noncontracting dentists and requires at least one payment method that provides the dentist the contracted amount without an access fee.

HB516.summary: The bill would designate the portion of Farm-to-Market Road 1960 in Liberty County as the Corporal David Eugene King Memorial Highway, in addition to any other designation. Subject to Transportation Code Section 225.021(c), it would require the department to design and erect markers for the designation.

policy_tags.explanation: Designates a state highway segment and requires markers along it.

locations.name: Portion of Farm-to-Market Road 1960 in Liberty County
locations.explanation: This is the specific highway segment covered by the designation.

affected_groups.group: Road users traveling on the designated portion of Farm-to-Market Road 1960
affected_groups.explanation: Travelers on the segment would encounter markers identifying its memorial designation.

major_effects.label: Memorial highway designation
major_effects.explanation: Adds the Corporal David Eugene King Memorial Highway designation to the specified road segment, in addition to any other designation.

major_effects.label: Designation markers
major_effects.explanation: Subject to Section 225.021(c), requires the department to design, construct, and erect markers along the highway.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns marker-design and installation duties to “the department,” but does not identify the department by name in the supplied text.

HB517.summary: HB 517 would expand the definition of “first responder” for the Governor's Interoperable Radio Communications Program to expressly include engineers and wastewater treatment plant employees whose duties include responding rapidly to an emergency. The duty condition remains; the bill does not classify all employees in those roles as first responders.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes which emergency-response personnel fall within the program-specific first-responder definition.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The definition applies to the Governor's Interoperable Radio Communications Program, rather than to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Engineers and wastewater treatment plant employees with rapid emergency-response duties
affected_groups.explanation: They would be expressly included in the program-specific first-responder definition when their duties include responding rapidly to an emergency.

major_effects.label: Expanded program-specific first-responder definition
major_effects.explanation: Adds engineers and wastewater treatment plant employees to the definition only when their duties include rapid emergency response; this changes classification for the program, not automatic receipt of a benefit.

agencies.name: Administering state body for the Governor's Interoperable Radio Communications Program
agencies.explanation: The program-specific definition would affect the state body administering the program, but the bill does not identify that body.

HB518.summary: HB 518 would extend the school-meal restriction on specified food additives to meals offered for sale during the instructional day by school districts and open-enrollment charter schools, as well as to free or reduced-price meals. The restriction would not apply to food sold by a restaurant under contract with a school or through a vending machine, and it would apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the food restrictions that apply to meals offered by school districts and open-enrollment charter schools.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools across the state.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: These schools would be subject to the additive restriction for meals offered for sale during the instructional day and for covered free or reduced-price meals.

affected_groups.group: Students who buy or receive school meals
affected_groups.explanation: Food in covered meals could not contain the listed additives or substantially similar additives.

affected_groups.group: Restaurants contracting with schools and vending-machine food sellers
affected_groups.explanation: Food sold through these channels is excluded from the section's restriction.

major_effects.label: Extends additive restrictions to meals sold during the school day
major_effects.explanation: Covered school meals offered for sale during the instructional day would be subject to the listed-additive restriction, alongside free or reduced-price meals; contracted restaurant sales and vending-machine sales are excluded.

HB519.summary: For a main election, an application for a ballot by mail would also serve as an application for a ballot in any resulting runoff election. The applicant could request not to receive a runoff ballot.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how applications for mail ballots cover resulting runoff elections.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas election law and applies statewide.

affected_groups.group: Voters applying for a mail ballot for a main election
affected_groups.explanation: Their application would also cover a resulting runoff unless they request otherwise.

major_effects.label: Runoff mail-ballot applications
major_effects.explanation: A main-election mail-ballot application would also apply to any resulting runoff, unless the applicant requests not to receive a runoff ballot.

HB520.summary: The bill directs the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to establish a grant program for counties to reduce illegal scrap-tire disposal in waters, on rights-of-way, and on other land. It creates a dedicated account to support grants and program administration, and requires rules and an annual report to the Legislature; the program must be established by January 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a program aimed at reducing illegal scrap-tire disposal in waters and on land.
Authorizes grants to counties for enforcement, public information, and tire removal and disposal.
Creates a dedicated account funded in part by legislative appropriations and restricts its uses to grants and program administration.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The grant program is established for counties without a stated geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: Texas counties
affected_groups.explanation: Counties may receive grants for identifying and prosecuting violators, public information, and removal and proper disposal of illegally disposed tires.

affected_groups.group: Members of the public
affected_groups.explanation: The program may fund public information discouraging illegal tire disposal, and aims to reduce such disposal.

major_effects.label: County scrap-tire remediation grants
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to establish a program awarding grants to counties to reduce illegal scrap-tire disposal; the commission must establish it by January 1, 2029.

major_effects.label: Dedicated grant account
major_effects.explanation: Creates a dedicated general revenue account funded by legislative appropriations, donations and investment interest; money may be used only for grants and program administration.

major_effects.label: Annual report to the Legislature
major_effects.explanation: Requires an annual written report with recommendations for addressing illegal scrap-tire disposal.

major_effects.label: Program administration rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to adopt rules for administering the grant program.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission responsibility for establishing the grant program; it also requires the commission to administer the program, report to the Legislature, and adopt rules.

HB521.summary: HB 521 would create the Housing Texas Fund in the state treasury, administered by the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs. It would direct annual fund spending to grants for affordable rental housing and housing-stability services, with specified shares and priorities for certain people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates grant funding for affordable rental housing and services to secure stable housing and prevent or address homelessness.
Creates a state treasury fund and directs how annual expenditures from it must be allocated.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill creates a state treasury fund administered by a state department, without limiting the grant program to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Nonprofit developers of multifamily affordable rental housing
affected_groups.explanation: Would be eligible for grants to develop, maintain, and manage rental housing for low-income individuals and families.

affected_groups.group: Nonprofit entities providing housing placement and homelessness-prevention services
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive grants for stable housing placements, homelessness prevention, and transitions to stable housing.

affected_groups.group: People experiencing or at risk of homelessness, including specified families, children, and people recently released from confinement
affected_groups.explanation: These populations would be served by the grant programs, with specified groups prioritized for some housing-placement grants.

major_effects.label: Creates the Housing Texas Fund
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a special fund in the state treasury, administered by the department, to support the specified housing grants.

major_effects.label: Directs annual grant allocations
major_effects.explanation: Requires annual expenditures to be divided among affordable rental housing, stable housing placements, and one-time homelessness prevention or transition grants.

major_effects.label: Requires rules for grant qualifications and fund use
major_effects.explanation: Requires department rules to establish proficiency for certain grant recipients and provide for use of fund assets, subject to the bill's limits.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department responsibility to administer the fund, allocate expenditures and grants, and adopt rules governing use of fund assets.

agencies.name: the board
agencies.explanation: The bill provides for money transferred by a board to be deposited in the fund, but the supplied text does not identify which board.

HB522.summary: The bill would prohibit specified insurers and county mutual insurance companies from charging an annual premium for the liability portion of an automobile policy that exceeds the total loss value of the covered vehicle or vehicles. The limit would apply only to policies delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill would impose a premium ceiling on specified automobile insurers.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law with no narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: Insureds with covered automobile liability policies
affected_groups.explanation: Their annual premium for the liability portion of a covered policy would be subject to the bill's ceiling.

affected_groups.group: Insurers described by Insurance Code Section 1952.001 and county mutual insurance companies
affected_groups.explanation: These insurers would be subject to the premium limit for applicable policies.

major_effects.label: Annual premium ceiling
major_effects.explanation: For applicable policies, the liability-coverage premium could not exceed the total loss value of the covered vehicle or vehicles.

HB523.summary: Requires medical schools to include Ehlers-Danlos syndrome identification and treatment in medical-degree curricula, with an exception for students who entered before fall 2028 that expires January 1, 2034. Physicians applying to renew a license on or after January 1, 2029 must complete related continuing medical education under rules adopted by the Texas Medical Board.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds a required subject to medical-degree curricula.
Requires physicians renewing their licenses to complete continuing education on identifying and treating the syndrome.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to medical schools and physician license renewals under Texas law, without a narrower geographic limit.

affected_groups.group: Medical schools and students pursuing medical degrees
affected_groups.explanation: Medical schools must add the training to degree curricula; the requirement does not apply to degree-program requirements for students who entered before fall 2028, and that exception expires January 1, 2034.

affected_groups.group: Physicians seeking license renewal
affected_groups.explanation: Physicians with renewal applications filed on or after January 1, 2029 must complete the specified continuing medical education.

major_effects.label: Medical-degree curriculum requirement
major_effects.explanation: Requires medical schools to include training on identifying and treating Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, subject to the stated student-entry exception.

major_effects.label: Continuing education for license renewal
major_effects.explanation: Makes syndrome-related continuing medical education a requirement for physician renewal applications filed on or after January 1, 2029.

major_effects.label: Rules for continuing education
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Texas Medical Board to adopt rules specifying the required education hours and content.

agencies.name: Texas Medical Board
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly assigns the Texas Medical Board responsibility for adopting rules implementing the new physician continuing-education requirement.

HB524.summary: The bill would prohibit covered health maintenance organizations and insurers from requiring preauthorization for specified services, including emergency care, certain acute outpatient care, some outpatient mental health and substance use treatment, and specified preventive care; exceptions include prescription drugs or intravenous infusions for the outpatient treatment category and otherwise-agreed terms for qualifying capitated services. It would limit payment denials or reductions and prohibit retrospective review of services for which preauthorization is not required, unless the health maintenance organization or insurer has reasonable cause to suspect a basis for denial under Subsection (a). It would require notice if a preauthorization request is submitted anyway and apply only to requests under plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028; CHIP and Medicaid plan

policy_tags.explanation: Changes preauthorization and payment-review rules for specified health care services.
Imposes requirements on covered insurers, health maintenance organizations, and their preauthorization contractors.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies to qualifying plans governed by Texas insurance statutes, without limiting its reach to a particular place in the state.

affected_groups.group: Participating physicians and providers
affected_groups.explanation: Would not have to obtain preauthorization for the listed services and would receive protections against payment denials or reductions and retrospective review, subject to statutory conditions: payment may be denied or reduced if an applicable exception under Section 4201.705(a) applies, including the stated knowing and material misrepresentation with intent to deceive and obtain an unlawful payment; retrospective review is permitted only if the HMO or insurer has reasonable cause to suspect a §

affected_groups.group: Health maintenance organizations, insurers, and their preauthorization contractors
affected_groups.explanation: Would be subject to the preauthorization restrictions and related payment-review and notice requirements for covered plans.

affected_groups.group: Patients enrolled in covered health benefit plans
affected_groups.explanation: May receive listed services without a required preauthorization; Medicaid and CHIP plans are excluded.

major_effects.label: Preauthorization restrictions for specified services
major_effects.explanation: Bars covered plans from requiring preauthorization for the listed services, subject to the bill's stated exceptions.

major_effects.label: Payment and retrospective-review limits
major_effects.explanation: Generally bars denial or reduction of payment for services exempt from preauthorization, with exceptions for intentional material misrepresentation or failure to substantially perform; retrospective review is allowed only when there is reasonable cause to suspect such a basis for denial.

major_effects.label: Notice when a preauthorization request is submitted
major_effects.explanation: Requires a covered plan to promptly notify a physician or provider that preauthorization is not required for the service and state the plan's payment requirements.

HB525.summary: HB 525 would create a Texas Workforce Commission-administered program that matches eligible employers’ contributions toward employees’ child-care costs; participating employers must contribute at least 20% of those costs. Match amounts would vary with household income. Approval of agreements and issuance of matching payments require sufficient money in the program fund and an appropriation for that purpose, although the bill also permits use of other commission money available for the purpose.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates an employer-based child-care contribution benefit for participating employees.
Creates a dedicated fund for the program and authorizes state matching payments subject to appropriation and fund availability.
Requires confidentiality protocols for participant information, including written consent before disclosing an employee’s personal information.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The program is intended to support families in this state.

affected_groups.group: Employers providing child-care assistance as an employment benefit
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible employers may participate but must contribute at least 20% of an employee’s child-care cost.

affected_groups.group: Employees and their families seeking child care
affected_groups.explanation: Employees may receive an income-based state match toward eligible child-care costs and remain responsible for costs not covered by contributions and the match.

affected_groups.group: Child-care providers
affected_groups.explanation: Providers must meet commission-set quality criteria and enter an agreement to receive program money.

major_effects.label: Child-care contribution partnership program
major_effects.explanation: Directs the commission to establish and administer a program that encourages employer contributions and provides state matching funds.

major_effects.label: Employer contributions and income-based state matches
major_effects.explanation: Participating employers contribute at least 20% of costs; the match is equal to the employer contribution for employees at or below the state median household income and is reduced by income tiers above that level. Matching payments require sufficient appropriated funds.

major_effects.label: Program fund and small-employer priority
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a dedicated fund and directs that, to the greatest extent practicable, at least 25% of annual appropriations from it go to agreements with employers having fewer than 50 full-time employees.

major_effects.label: Program effectiveness reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires biennial public reports to the legislature on program funding, participation, providers, costs, and participant demographics.

major_effects.label: Participant information confidentiality
major_effects.explanation: Requires confidentiality protocols and written employee consent before disclosing an employee’s personal information.

major_effects.label: Penalty for intentional false information
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes a civil penalty of up to $500 per violation for intentionally providing false information to obtain program benefits.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission is assigned responsibility to establish and administer the program, and the bill names the Texas Workforce Commission as responsible for adopting its implementing rules.

HB526.summary: The bill would prohibit toll operators from charging tolls or related fees for a tow truck and its towed vehicle while the truck travels to respond to, or transports the vehicle from, an incident-management tow initiated by a peace officer. The exemption ends when the vehicle reaches its initial destination for release, storage, or other lawful disposition; operators may require proof of the officer’s request and must refund or credit charges for covered travel.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes toll-payment rules for qualifying incident-management tows and applies the exemption under multiple toll-facility provisions.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill changes toll rules in the statewide Transportation Code rather than identifying a particular toll facility or locality.

affected_groups.group: Tow-truck owners and operators performing qualifying incident-management tows, and people whose vehicles are being towed
affected_groups.explanation: Their covered travel would be exempt from tolls and related fees, subject to the initial-destination limit; owners may need to provide proof if an operator requests it.

affected_groups.group: Public and private toll operators
affected_groups.explanation: They could not charge for covered travel, may request documentation, and must refund or credit charges collected for it.

major_effects.label: Limited toll exemption for qualifying incident tows
major_effects.explanation: Covered tow-truck and towed-vehicle travel is exempt while responding to or transporting a vehicle from an incident-management tow initiated by a peace officer. The exemption ends at the vehicle’s initial destination, and related amendments apply it under other toll-facility provisions.

major_effects.label: Optional documentation to verify a tow
major_effects.explanation: A toll operator may require the tow-truck owner to submit documentation of the peace officer’s request; the bill does not require every owner to submit documentation.

major_effects.label: Refund or credit for covered travel charges
major_effects.explanation: Toll operators must refund or credit tolls or related fees charged for travel covered by the exemption.

HB527.summary: HB 527 would require the Comptroller to study whether consolidating the human-resources functions of executive-branch state agencies into a centralized or shared-services model is feasible, cost-effective, and practical; the bill’s definition excludes institutions of higher education. Covered agencies would provide requested information, and the Comptroller would report findings and legislative recommendations to state leaders and relevant legislative committee chairs—the bill commissions a study, not the consolidation itself.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires a study of how state agencies organize and administer human-resources functions, with agency cooperation and a report of findings.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The study and cooperation duty cover the state agencies defined by the Act.

affected_groups.group: Executive-branch state agencies, excluding institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: Covered agencies must cooperate and provide information requested for the study.

major_effects.label: Centralized human-resources feasibility study
major_effects.explanation: Requires evaluation of agency HR expenditures, duplicated infrastructure, potential costs and savings, and practical effects; it does not itself consolidate HR functions.

major_effects.label: Agency information and study report
major_effects.explanation: Covered agencies must provide requested study information, and the Comptroller must report findings and legislative recommendations to state leaders and relevant committee chairs.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The Comptroller is assigned the study and must submit its findings and recommendations.

agencies.name: State agencies
agencies.explanation: Agencies within the Act’s defined class must cooperate and provide requested information; the bill does not identify each covered agency by name.

HB528.summary: The bill would extend appointed counsel to eligible indigent defendants raising claims under Article 11.073, revise the scientific-evidence standards and procedures for postconviction habeas relief, and require written merits decisions on those claims. It would allow the Court of Criminal Appeals to consider certain otherwise-ineligible subsequent capital habeas applications when justice requires, and create a limited district-court petition route for seeking relevant documents. The changes would apply only to habeas applications filed on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes criminal postconviction habeas procedures, counsel eligibility, and access to documents.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes Texas criminal procedure and applies to qualifying habeas applications statewide.

affected_groups.group: Eligible indigent defendants raising Article 11.073 claims
affected_groups.explanation: They would be entitled to appointed counsel for a habeas proceeding raising such a claim.

affected_groups.group: People seeking postconviction habeas relief, including capital applicants
affected_groups.explanation: Their scientific-evidence claims and, for capital applicants, certain subsequent applications would be subject to the revised procedures.

affected_groups.group: Texas-licensed attorneys seeking relevant postconviction documents
affected_groups.explanation: They could petition a district court for a writ seeking relevant documents, subject to the bill's stated prerequisites.

major_effects.label: Appointed counsel for specified habeas claims
major_effects.explanation: Eligible indigent defendants would be entitled to appointed counsel in a habeas proceeding when they raise a claim governed by Article 11.073.

major_effects.label: Revised scientific-evidence relief standards
major_effects.explanation: The bill revises which scientific evidence may support relief and replaces the prior outcome standard with a reasonable-likelihood test for whether the evidence could have affected conviction or sentence. The specified subsequent-application restrictions apply to a covered claim only if it was previously presented in an application filed by an attorney.

major_effects.label: Written merits decisions on scientific-evidence claims
major_effects.explanation: The Court of Criminal Appeals could not deny relief on an Article 11.073 claim without a written decision addressing its merits.

major_effects.label: Discretion to consider subsequent capital applications
major_effects.explanation: The Court of Criminal Appeals could consider a subsequent application that fails the usual requirements if it finds justice requires consideration; otherwise it must dismiss the application as an abuse of the writ. If the court makes that finding, the convicting court may take further action.

major_effects.label: Petitions seeking relevant documents
major_effects.explanation: The bill creates a limited district-court petition route for an eligible attorney to seek a writ requiring issuance of relevant documents; it does not guarantee that documents will be issued.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Court of Criminal Appeals must issue written merits decisions on Article 11.073 claims, and district courts receive jurisdiction over the new document-petition process.

agencies.name: Office of Capital and Forensic Writs
agencies.explanation: The amended appointment cross-reference reaches the new justice-based pathway for considering subsequent applications, under which the Office may be appointed if it represented the applicant previously or accepts the appointment.

HB530.summary: The bill would require eligible campus food vendors to seek authorization to accept SNAP benefits, and would establish a statewide hunger-free campus program, campus designation criteria, and a competitive grant program subject to available funding. It would also direct the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to convene a work group and produce reports, and allow the commission to adopt rules providing a SNAP work-requirement exemption for certain students enrolled in postsecondary education.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates campus hunger programs, designation criteria, and vendor-contract requirements at postsecondary institutions.
Creates competitive grants to institutions, contingent on money being appropriated or otherwise available.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The campus hunger program applies to institution campuses in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Students at postsecondary educational institutions
affected_groups.explanation: Students may benefit from campus food solutions and, if enrolled in at least 12 semester credit hours, may be covered by rules providing a SNAP work-requirement exemption.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: Institutions may seek campus designation and grants, with grant awards subject to money appropriated or otherwise available; they must report grant use if awarded, and include the specified term in covered food-vendor contracts.

affected_groups.group: Food vendors contracting to serve campus food
affected_groups.explanation: A vendor must be required by its contract to seek SNAP retailer authorization and accept benefits if eligible.

major_effects.label: Campus food-vendor contract requirement
major_effects.explanation: New contracts for selling or providing food on campus must require an eligible vendor to seek SNAP retailer authorization and accept benefits.

major_effects.label: Hunger-free campus program and designation
major_effects.explanation: Establishes campus hunger solutions, designation criteria, and a work group to develop best-practice guidelines.

major_effects.label: Competitive campus hunger grants
major_effects.explanation: Creates grants for designated campuses, subject to available money, with priority based on institutions' enrolled Pell-grant recipient percentages.

major_effects.label: Possible SNAP work-requirement exemption
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes the commission to adopt rules consistent with federal law providing an exemption for a student enrolled in at least 12 semester credit hours; it does not itself grant an exemption to every such student.

major_effects.label: Program and grant reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires work-group recommendations and grant-use reporting, plus a report evaluating the grant program and its effects.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The board is assigned responsibility for the hunger-free campus program, designation criteria, work group, grants, rules, and reports; a later provision names it as the body establishing the work group.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Agriculture
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department a coordination role in establishing the campus hunger grant program.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission is named as a collaborator on strategies to increase student SNAP enrollment.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The commission may adopt rules for an exemption from SNAP work requirements, but the bill does not identify this commission by name.

HB531.summary: HB 531 would redirect filing fees and petitions in lieu of a fee for convention nominations: statewide or district office submissions would go to the state chair rather than the secretary of state, and county or precinct office submissions to the county chair rather than the county judge. It would also repeal Election Code Section 181.0311(c) and (d), but their contents are not included in the supplied text.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes who receives candidate filing fees and fee-in-lieu petitions for nomination by convention.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill addresses filings for statewide and district offices as well as county and precinct offices.

affected_groups.group: Candidates seeking nomination by convention
affected_groups.explanation: Their filing fees or petitions in lieu of fees would be directed to different recipients.

affected_groups.group: State and county chairs
affected_groups.explanation: They would become the designated recipients of the relevant fees and petitions.

affected_groups.group: County judges
affected_groups.explanation: They would no longer be the designated recipients for county or precinct office filings under this provision.

major_effects.label: Change in filing-fee and petition recipients
major_effects.explanation: Would replace the Secretary of State and county judge with the state chair and county chair, respectively, as recipients for the specified convention-nomination filings.

major_effects.label: Repeal of two related subsections
major_effects.explanation: Repeals Election Code Section 181.0311(c) and (d); the supplied bill text does not show what provisions those subsections contain.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The bill removes the Secretary of State as the recipient of filing fees and petitions for statewide or district offices, replacing that role with the state chair.

HB532.summary: The bill would require certain notices to unsecured creditors to enclose a blank claim form that, when completed, satisfies applicable statutory requirements, and explain that creditors may use that form or existing statutory methods to present a claim. A creditor who returns the enclosed form before the 121st day after receiving notice would be treated as having given the required notice of the claim; the Texas Supreme Court would add this form to those it may promulgate, as it considers appropriate. These changes would apply only to estates of decedents who die on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands the Texas Supreme Court’s probate-form responsibilities and changes the statutory process for presenting certain estate claims.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes govern Texas estate administration and apply to estates of decedents who die on or after the Act’s effective date.

affected_groups.group: Unsecured creditors of estates
affected_groups.explanation: They may use the enclosed claim form to present a claim, and timely return of the form counts as giving the required notice of the claim.

affected_groups.group: Personal representatives and independent executors
affected_groups.explanation: They must enclose a blank claim form that, when completed, satisfies the applicable statutory requirements; independent executors receive claims submitted using the form.

major_effects.label: Alternative method to present a claim
major_effects.explanation: A creditor may use the enclosed form instead of the specified statutory methods; returning it before the 121st day after receiving notice counts as giving the required notice of the claim.

major_effects.label: Probate creditor-claim form
major_effects.explanation: Adds a form for creditor notices and claims to the forms the supreme court shall promulgate as it considers appropriate.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The bill adds a probate creditor-notice and claim form to the forms the supreme court shall promulgate as it considers appropriate. The named court is represented by the Texas Judicial Branch registry entry.

HB533.summary: HB533 would create a limited exception to the Penal Code prohibition on possessing a weapon at a polling place on election day or during early voting. The exception would allow a person to possess a licensed concealed handgun and no other covered weapon only when state law does not otherwise prohibit concealed handguns at that location.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the rules for concealed handgun possession at polling places on election day and during early voting.
Creates a qualified exception to a restriction on carrying weapons at polling places.
Narrows the conduct subject to a Penal Code offense by adding a conditional exception.

locations.name: Premises of polling places
locations.explanation: The change applies at polling places on election day or while early voting is in progress.

affected_groups.group: People licensed to carry concealed handguns
affected_groups.explanation: They may qualify for the new exception at a polling place, subject to the weapon and location limits.

affected_groups.group: People at polling places
affected_groups.explanation: The change concerns weapon possession at polling places during elections and early voting.

major_effects.label: Qualified polling-place handgun exception
major_effects.explanation: Adds an exception to the offense prohibition for a licensed concealed handgun, with no other covered weapon, only where state law does not otherwise prohibit concealed handgun possession.

HB534.summary: HB 534 would require covered hotels to maintain carbon monoxide detectors in regularly used sleeping rooms and to provide hearing-accessible detectors when requested, extending the existing detector-related offense to those requirements. The duties would not apply to a hotel certified by the local fire marshal as having no carbon monoxide-producing sources, if the certificate is publicly displayed; the bill would also include carbon monoxide detectors in the state fire marshal’s detector-listing process.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds carbon monoxide detection and related offense provisions for hotels.
Imposes detector maintenance and guest-accommodation requirements on hotel operators.
Makes certification by the local fire marshal a condition for the hotel exemption.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The hotel requirements apply statewide to hotels within the bill’s definition; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: Hotel operators
affected_groups.explanation: Must maintain carbon monoxide detectors in sleeping rooms and provide hearing-accessible detectors as specified.

affected_groups.group: Hotel patrons who are hearing-impaired
affected_groups.explanation: May request a room with hearing-accessible smoke and carbon monoxide detectors; the operator must assign an equipped room or install portable detectors.

affected_groups.group: Local fire marshals
affected_groups.explanation: May certify that a hotel has no carbon monoxide-producing sources, enabling the stated exemption if the certificate is publicly displayed.

major_effects.label: Hotel detector requirements
major_effects.explanation: Adds carbon monoxide detectors to the working-order requirement for sleeping rooms and to the hearing-accessible detector requirements. The hearing-accessible inventory is one of each type per 60 rooms or fraction, capped at five of each; requested equipment may be provided through an equipped room or portable detectors. The section does not apply when the local fire marshal provides the specified no-source certification and the hotel displays it.

major_effects.label: Offense provisions extended
major_effects.explanation: Extends the existing offense for specified hotel detector failures to include the added carbon monoxide detector requirements.

major_effects.label: Detector qualification and listing
major_effects.explanation: Adds carbon monoxide detectors to the devices that must be listed after effectiveness testing by the state fire marshal or an approved testing laboratory.

HB535.summary: Official mail-ballot carrier envelopes would have to be prepared so they can be mailed without U.S. postage, state that return postage is prepaid, and exclude indicia from third parties such as campaigns or voter-registration organizations; the secretary of state would adopt implementing rules. These changes apply only to elections ordered on or after the Act's effective date; earlier-ordered elections remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes requirements for official carrier envelopes used to return early voting ballots by mail.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to official mail-ballot carrier envelopes generally, rather than to a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: Voters returning early voting ballots by mail
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes the postage arrangements and information on the envelopes used to return their ballots.

affected_groups.group: Early voting clerks and election administrators
affected_groups.explanation: Official carrier envelopes must meet the new postage and envelope-marking requirements.

affected_groups.group: Campaigns and third-party voter registration organizations
affected_groups.explanation: These entities may not place their indicia on officially prescribed carrier envelopes.

major_effects.label: Postage-free return envelopes
major_effects.explanation: Official carrier envelopes must be prepared to be mailed without U.S. postage and must indicate that return postage is prepaid.

major_effects.label: Restriction on third-party indicia
major_effects.explanation: Official carrier envelopes may not include indicia from third-party entities, including campaigns and third-party voter registration organizations.

major_effects.label: Secretary of state rules
major_effects.explanation: The secretary of state must adopt rules to administer the postage requirement.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The secretary of state is expressly assigned rulemaking responsibility to administer the postage requirement.

HB536.summary: The bill would update which organizations may certify covered school personnel and student athletic trainers in CPR and AED use. It would require public school campuses to provide enough AEDs to support emergency care within three minutes of notification, with the requirement met by the first instructional day of the 2029–2030 school year. It would also direct the commissioner to establish grants for districts and schools implementing cardiac emergency response plans, prioritizing those with at least 50 percent educationally disadvantaged students.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes requirements for covered school personnel and campus AED availability, and creates a grant program for districts and schools.
The bill addresses CPR, AED use, and emergency care for cardiac arrest at schools.
The bill directs the commissioner to establish a grant program awarding grants to schools and districts.
School districts would have campus AED duties and may receive grants under the bill.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill concerns covered schools in this state.

affected_groups.group: Covered school personnel and student athletic trainers
affected_groups.explanation: Those required to participate in CPR/AED instruction would be subject to the revised certification-organization wording.

affected_groups.group: Public school districts and campuses
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would need to make the required number of AEDs available at each campus.

affected_groups.group: Districts and schools with at least 50 percent educationally disadvantaged students
affected_groups.explanation: These districts or schools would receive priority when grants are awarded.

affected_groups.group: People experiencing cardiac arrest at school campuses
affected_groups.explanation: The campus AED availability requirement is intended to facilitate timely emergency care for people in cardiac arrest.

major_effects.label: CPR and AED certification standards
major_effects.explanation: The bill changes the description of organizations from which covered people may obtain and maintain CPR/AED certification.

major_effects.label: Campus AED availability and placement
major_effects.explanation: Districts would provide the number of AEDs needed for access from any campus location to support emergency care within three minutes of notification; placement must consider emergency cardiovascular care guidance and devices must be clearly marked.

major_effects.label: Cardiac emergency response plan grants
major_effects.explanation: The commissioner would establish grants to help districts and schools implement cardiac emergency response plans, prioritizing those with at least 50 percent educationally disadvantaged students.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commissioner a grant-program duty, but the excerpt does not identify the office or agency; the Education Code context may indicate the Commissioner of Education.

HB537.summary: HB 537 would require health benefit plans that provide prescription-drug benefits—including specified state plans and Medicaid, including Medicaid managed care—to cover a GLP-1 receptor agonist to treat obesity. The requirement would apply only to plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028; if an affected state agency determines a federal waiver or authorization is necessary, it must request one and may delay implementing that provision until it is granted.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires coverage of a medication used to treat obesity under qualifying health benefit plans.
The coverage subchapter expressly applies to the state Medicaid program, including Medicaid managed care.
Imposes a prescription-drug coverage requirement on issuers of qualifying health benefit plans.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies to qualifying health benefit plans and the state Medicaid program under Texas law.

affected_groups.group: Enrollees in qualifying health benefit plans seeking treatment for obesity
affected_groups.explanation: Their plans would be required to cover the specified medication when they provide prescription-drug benefits.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid enrollees, including Medicaid managed-care enrollees
affected_groups.explanation: The bill expressly includes the state Medicaid program and its managed-care program within the subchapter's scope.

affected_groups.group: Issuers of qualifying health benefit plans
affected_groups.explanation: Covered plan issuers would have to provide the required medication coverage if their plans provide prescription-drug benefits.

major_effects.label: Required coverage for an obesity medication
major_effects.explanation: Plans within the subchapter's scope that provide prescription-drug benefits must cover a GLP-1 receptor agonist to treat obesity. The requirement applies to plans delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028, and implementation of a provision may be delayed while a necessary federal waiver or authorization is sought.

agencies.name: agency affected by the provision
agencies.explanation: The bill conditionally directs an affected state agency to request a federal waiver or authorization if it determines one is necessary. The bill does not identify which agency would have this role.

HB538.summary: HB 538 would require Medicaid reimbursement for doula services provided to recipients, in addition to existing reimbursement for doula case-management services, from pregnancy confirmation by a medical professional through the 12th month after pregnancy ends. It directs the Health and Human Services Commission to seek a state Medicaid plan amendment; if the commission or another state agency determines a federal waiver is necessary, that agency must request it and may delay the affected provision until the waiver is granted.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds Medicaid reimbursement for doula services and sets the period during which the reimbursement applies.
The bill changes coverage of doula services for medical assistance recipients during and after pregnancy.
The bill requires medical assistance reimbursement for an additional category of services.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill concerns the state Medicaid plan and medical assistance reimbursement under Texas law.

affected_groups.group: Medical assistance recipients during and after pregnancy
affected_groups.explanation: Recipients would have doula services reimbursed beginning when pregnancy is medically confirmed and through the 12th month after pregnancy ends.

affected_groups.group: Doulas
affected_groups.explanation: Doula services provided to medical assistance recipients would qualify for reimbursement.

major_effects.label: Medicaid reimbursement for doula services
major_effects.explanation: Requires reimbursement for doula services, in addition to reimbursement already available for doula case-management services, within the specified pregnancy-related period.

major_effects.label: Federal Medicaid implementation
major_effects.explanation: Requires seeking a state Medicaid plan amendment; if an agency determines a federal waiver is necessary, it must request one and may delay the affected provision until the waiver is granted.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is directed to seek a state Medicaid plan amendment to implement the new reimbursement provision. The commission also may determine that a federal waiver is necessary.

HB539.summary: HB 539 would make the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November the uniform date for general or special elections, subject to Election Code exceptions, and generally require elections to be held on Tuesdays, except for an election under Section 41.0011 or as provided by Section 203.004(b). It would require political subdivisions holding officer elections on another date to move them to the November uniform date by December 31, 2025, and revise runoff election schedules.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes uniform election dates and requirements for runoff and other election schedules.

Requires political subdivisions, including those previously excluded from this subsection, to change the date of their general officer elections if they are not held on the November uniform election date.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The election-date requirements apply to elections held in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions and their governing bodies
affected_groups.explanation: Those holding general officer elections on a date other than the November uniform election date would have to change the date.

affected_groups.group: Voters and candidates participating in runoff elections
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes the timing and day-of-week requirements for runoff elections, subject to the exceptions in Subsection (d) and elsewhere in the Election Code.

major_effects.label: Uniform election dates
major_effects.explanation: Makes the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November the uniform date for general or special elections, subject to applicable exceptions, and generally requires elections to be held on Tuesdays, except for an election under Section 41.0011 or as provided by Section 203.004(b).

major_effects.label: Political subdivision election-date changes
major_effects.explanation: Requires a political subdivision holding its general officer election on another date to move it to the November uniform election date by December 31, 2025.

major_effects.label: Runoff and specified election schedules
major_effects.explanation: Requires designated runoff elections to be held on Tuesdays, moves the runoff primary election to the second Tuesday in May, and requires elections under Section 203.013 to be held on Tuesdays within their existing timing windows.

major_effects.label: Exception for certain time-limited special elections
major_effects.explanation: For a special election subject to Section 41.001(a), if a non-constitutional law outside the Election Code requires it to be held within a particular period and no uniform election date within that period affords enough time to hold it as required by law, Section 41.001(a) does not apply.

HB540.summary: The bill would designate the second Saturday in October as Hospice and Palliative Care Day to raise awareness of hospice and palliative care’s role in improving quality of life for seriously ill patients and their families. The day may be observed with appropriate ceremonies and activities.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill designates an awareness day focused on hospice and palliative care.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The designation applies statewide.

affected_groups.group: Seriously ill patients and their families
affected_groups.explanation: The awareness day highlights hospice and palliative care’s role in their quality of life.

major_effects.label: Designates Hospice and Palliative Care Day
major_effects.explanation: Designates the second Saturday in October for awareness of hospice and palliative care; appropriate ceremonies and activities may be held.

HB541.summary: The bill would require school district procedures to provide for a holistic mental and physical health assessment within a reasonable time after a student receiving special education services is restrained. It would also require the district’s notice to the student’s parent to report whether the screening occurred and its results, and require a copy of the screening and results in the student’s special education eligibility records.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required procedures and records for school districts concerning restraint of students receiving special education services.
Requires mental and physical health screening as part of an assessment after a restraint incident.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply generally to school districts under state law.

affected_groups.group: Students with disabilities receiving special education services who are restrained
affected_groups.explanation: Subject to Subsection (j), the required procedures would require a district to conduct an overall health assessment after a restraint incident; the screening would be documented in the student's special education eligibility records.

affected_groups.group: Parents or persons standing in parental relation to affected students
affected_groups.explanation: Their restraint notification would include whether the screening occurred within a reasonable time and the screening results.

affected_groups.group: School districts and qualified district professionals
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would be required to arrange the assessment, including mental and physical health screenings by qualified professionals.

major_effects.label: Post-restraint health assessment
major_effects.explanation: District procedures would have to require an overall assessment with mental and physical health screenings after a restraint incident, within a reasonable time determined by the commissioner.

major_effects.label: Parent notification and student records
major_effects.explanation: The restraint notice would include whether the screening was conducted within a reasonable time and its results; a copy of the screening and results would also be placed in the student's special education eligibility records.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commissioner responsibility for adopting procedures that require the assessment and for determining assessment standards and timing. The text does not identify the commissioner by canonical agency name.

HB542.summary: HB 542 would require the General Land Office, working with a working group, to study establishing and implementing a distributed-ledger title registry pilot, including a potential pilot involving at least one rural and one urban county. It would require rules to administer the study and a report to the Legislature; it does not itself establish or implement the pilot.

policy_tags.explanation: The required study evaluates distributed-ledger technology for title records and must consider data privacy and fraud protections; the bill does not establish the technology pilot.
The study concerns recording real-property title transfers and liens, without changing property rights or existing recording requirements.
The bill assigns the General Land Office a study, rulemaking, and legislative reporting duties.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The study includes estimating the cost of converting to a statewide system, although the bill does not require statewide implementation.

locations.name: Rural counties
locations.explanation: The contemplated pilot must include a rural county, defined by its location outside specified metropolitan statistical areas.

locations.name: Urban counties
locations.explanation: The contemplated pilot must include an urban county, defined by its location partly or wholly within a primary metropolitan statistical area.

affected_groups.group: Texas counties, including rural and urban counties
affected_groups.explanation: The study must consider a pilot with both county types and assess potential impacts on them and counties generally; it does not require counties to participate.

affected_groups.group: Title insurance, banking, and blockchain industries
affected_groups.explanation: Representatives of these industries are included in the working group that discusses and provides feedback on the study.

affected_groups.group: Parties to real estate transactions
affected_groups.explanation: The study is to obtain regulator input on guidance that could protect parties to transactions recorded using distributed-ledger technology; the bill does not itself create those protections.

major_effects.label: Study of a proposed title-registry pilot
major_effects.explanation: Requires the General Land Office and working group to study a possible distributed-ledger recording pilot, including county impacts, costs, security, and privacy. The study does not itself authorize or implement the pilot.

major_effects.label: Working group and regulator input
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Office to establish a working-group framework with specified stakeholder and agency representation and to engage appropriate regulators for study input.

major_effects.label: Rules to administer the study
major_effects.explanation: Requires the General Land Office to adopt rules necessary to administer the study.

major_effects.label: Report to the Legislature
major_effects.explanation: Requires a report of study findings and recommendations for legislative or other action.

agencies.name: General Land Office
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the Office as the General Land Office and assigns it the study, working-group, rulemaking, and reporting responsibilities.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Insurance
agencies.explanation: The bill names the department as a required source of representation on the study working group.

agencies.name: Department of Information Resources
agencies.explanation: The bill names the department as a required source of representation on the study working group; the supplied canonical registry does not list a matching entry.

HB543.summary: HB 543 would add child pornography to the material a social media platform must address after receiving notice, defining it as visual material depicting a child engaging in sexual conduct or sexual performance. The platform would have to remove reported material and known copies or identical content within 48 hours of the user's report when the content qualifies as explicit deep fake material or child pornography.

policy_tags.explanation: Imposes a content-removal deadline and related compliance duty on social media platforms.
Changes how social media platforms must handle reported content and known copies on their services.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and has statewide relevance.

affected_groups.group: Social media platforms
affected_groups.explanation: Platforms receiving notice must remove qualifying reported content and known copies or identical content within the specified period.

affected_groups.group: Users who report qualifying content
affected_groups.explanation: Their report starts the removal deadline for content that meets the bill's specified categories.

affected_groups.group: Children depicted in child pornography
affected_groups.explanation: The bill extends the platform removal requirement to material depicting a child engaging in sexual conduct or sexual performance.

major_effects.label: Expands required content removal
major_effects.explanation: After notice, platforms must remove reported content and known copies or identical content within 48 hours of the user's report if it constitutes explicit deep fake material or child pornography.

HB544.summary: The bill directs the Texas Education Agency to study whether school districts building new campuses could be required to choose from a set of 10 standardized building designs, including potential cost savings. The agency must report the study's results to specified state officials and legislative education committee chairs by September 1, 2028; the bill does not itself require districts to use standardized designs.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires a study concerning standardized building designs for public schools and their potential cost effects on school districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The study concerns public schools and school districts generally, without limiting its scope to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: School districts building new campuses
affected_groups.explanation: The study must examine the feasibility of standardized designs for new campuses and the cost savings to districts building them.

major_effects.label: Study of standardized school building designs
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Texas Education Agency to assess the feasibility of 10 standardized designs that a school district would choose from when building a new campus, and potential cost savings for districts building new campuses; it does not require districts to adopt them.

major_effects.label: Report study results
major_effects.explanation: Requires the agency to submit the study results to specified state officials and legislative education committee chairs by September 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill defines “agency” as the Texas Education Agency and assigns it the study and reporting duties.

HB545.summary: The bill bars a person with an intellectual disability from being sentenced to death and creates a process for deciding that question in a capital case. It also makes the state’s appeal of a Chapter 46D order a direct appeal to the Court of Criminal Appeals for expedited review. The changes apply to trials beginning on or after the Act’s effective date, regardless of when the alleged offense occurred.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes capital-case sentencing rules and criminal-court procedures for determining intellectual disability.

locations.name: Statewide in Texas
locations.explanation: The bill changes state criminal procedure for qualifying trials, rather than limiting the changes to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Defendants in capital cases who may have an intellectual disability
affected_groups.explanation: They may seek a determination under the new process and, if found to have an intellectual disability, may not be sentenced to death.

affected_groups.group: Attorneys representing defendants in capital cases
affected_groups.explanation: A defendant's attorney may request the intellectual-disability hearing, and the state may offer rebuttal evidence.

affected_groups.group: Trial judges and juries in capital cases
affected_groups.explanation: They conduct or decide the intellectual-disability determination under the new procedure.

major_effects.label: Death-penalty ineligibility
major_effects.explanation: A defendant determined to have an intellectual disability may not be sentenced to death.

major_effects.label: Intellectual-disability determination process
major_effects.explanation: Creates a capital-case process for requesting a hearing and determining intellectual disability before trial; if the defendant is not found to have an intellectual disability, the trial proceeds as if the hearing had not been held.

major_effects.label: Direct appellate review
major_effects.explanation: Routes the state's appeal of a Chapter 46D order directly to the Court of Criminal Appeals, which must review it expeditiously.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Court of Criminal Appeals is assigned direct, expedited review of the state's appeals of orders under Chapter 46D.

HB546.summary: Beginning January 1, 2028, HB 546 would exempt qualifying educational materials bought by teachers employed by public schools or open-enrollment charter schools from Texas sales and use taxes, if they present a completed exemption certificate at purchase. Covered items include supplies and books used primarily for education, technology used exclusively for education or a purpose related to teacher employment, and other learning tools used exclusively for classroom education; the last category is capped at $500 per calendar year. The Comptroller and Texas Education Agency must develop and publish the certificate form, which must require an educational-purpose description for that last category.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a sales and use tax exemption for qualifying educational materials purchased by eligible teachers.
The exemption is limited to educational materials purchased by public school and open-enrollment charter school teachers.

locations.name: Statewide (Texas)
locations.explanation: The exemption is created in the Texas Tax Code and applies to taxes imposed under the chapter.

affected_groups.group: Teachers employed by public schools or open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: These teachers may claim the exemption for qualifying educational materials by presenting the required certificate at purchase.

major_effects.label: Teacher educational-materials tax exemption
major_effects.explanation: Exempts qualifying purchases from sales and use taxes for eligible public and charter school teachers who present the certificate; the $500 annual cap applies only to other learning tools used exclusively in the classroom.

major_effects.label: Exemption certificate administration
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Comptroller and Texas Education Agency to develop and publish a certificate, including a requirement to describe the educational purpose of specified classroom learning tools.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: Must coordinate on developing the exemption certificate and make it available on the Comptroller's website.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
