agencies.explanation: Must coordinate on developing the exemption certificate and make it available on the agency's website.

HB548.summary: HB 548 would allow a qualifying taxing unit—one other than a school district, county, municipality, or junior college district—to limit annual ad valorem taxes on a homestead owned by a disabled or 65-or-older individual whose household income is no more than 200 percent of the federal poverty level, but only if that taxing unit establishes the specified constitutional limitation. It sets a tax baseline with an adjustment for certain improvements, provides for qualifying surviving spouses and later homesteads, and changes related appraisal and tax-rate calculations. The bill takes effect January 1, 2028, only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise, it has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a conditional limitation on ad valorem taxes for certain eligible homesteads and adjusts related tax calculations.
Changes the tax authority and tax calculations of qualifying taxing units, which exclude school districts, counties, municipalities, and junior college districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law for qualifying taxing units across the state; it does not identify a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Low-income homeowners who are disabled or at least 65 years old
affected_groups.explanation: Their homestead taxes may be limited if household income does not exceed 200 percent of the federal poverty level and the qualifying taxing unit establishes the constitutional limitation.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying taxing units
affected_groups.explanation: Units other than school districts, counties, municipalities, and junior college districts may establish the specified limitation and have related tax calculations affected.

affected_groups.group: Eligible surviving spouses
affected_groups.explanation: A surviving spouse may retain the limitation if disabled or at least 55, eligible under the income definition, and continuing to use the homestead as a residence.

affected_groups.group: Appraisal and tax officials
affected_groups.explanation: The bill assigns appraisal, eligibility-verification, certificate, and tax-correction tasks related to the new limitation.

major_effects.label: Conditional homestead tax limitation
major_effects.explanation: For an eligible disabled or 65-or-older individual, a qualifying unit may not raise annual taxes above the applicable baseline once it establishes the constitutional limitation. Certain value-enhancing improvements may increase the amount, after which the limitation applies to the increased amount.

major_effects.label: Surviving-spouse continuation and homestead transfer
major_effects.explanation: A qualifying surviving spouse may retain the limitation while continuing to occupy the homestead. An eligible individual or qualifying surviving spouse may also receive a calculated limitation on a subsequently qualified homestead in the same taxing unit.

major_effects.label: Related appraisal and tax-rate calculations
major_effects.explanation: The bill excludes homestead values qualifying for the new limitation from specified current- and prior-year taxable-value calculations and extends related separate-appraisal and tax-bill treatment for cooperative housing.

HB550.summary: HB 550 would require Texas-licensed physicians and health care practitioners who prescribe a defined fall-risk-increasing drug to a patient age 65 or older to disclose the risk to the patient or legal guardian and document the disclosure in the medical record. It would direct the Health and Human Services Commission’s executive commissioner to create and annually post a list of these drugs, and make violations subject to review and disciplinary action by the relevant licensing agency.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates patient disclosure and medical-record documentation requirements related to prescription drug risks.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to covered practitioners licensed to practice in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Patients age 65 or older who are prescribed a fall risk increasing drug
affected_groups.explanation: They must receive information about the increased fall risk.

affected_groups.group: Legal guardians of covered patients
affected_groups.explanation: The disclosure may be made to the patient's legal guardian.

affected_groups.group: Physicians and health care practitioners licensed in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: Covered prescribers must disclose the risk and document that disclosure.

major_effects.label: Patient disclosure and documentation
major_effects.explanation: Covered prescribers must disclose the increased fall risk to the patient or legal guardian and document the disclosure in the medical record.

major_effects.label: Annual drug-risk list
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must develop and annually post a list; the bill says the commissioner may consider the cited drug criteria when developing it.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules and procedures
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must adopt rules necessary to implement the chapter, and the disclosure and documentation must follow the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner.

major_effects.label: Licensing review and discipline
major_effects.explanation: A covered physician or practitioner may be reviewed and disciplined by the relevant licensing agency for violating the chapter.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is assigned implementation rulemaking and responsibility for developing and annually posting the drug list.

agencies.name: State licensing agency with regulatory authority over the physician or health care practitioner
agencies.explanation: The bill makes violations subject to agency review and discipline, but does not identify the licensing agencies by name.

HB551.summary: The bill would direct the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs to establish a pilot offering housing assistance and landlord incentives for people facing homelessness, fleeing specified violence, or otherwise at high risk of housing instability. Selected local entities could provide up to $3,500 per household in assistance, but financial assistance under that provision is limited to people receiving a housing voucher. The department would report on program outcomes by January 1, 2032, and the program would expire September 1, 2032.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a housing-readiness program that may fund housing search and other costs of obtaining housing, as well as landlord incentives.
Local governmental entities may receive program funding and administer the pilot.
Directs the department to provide program funding, including assistance administered by selected local entities.
Creates a time-limited state-administered pilot and assigns the department program administration, rulemaking, and reporting duties.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The pilot is established by the state for administration through local entities, with rural service expressly considered.

affected_groups.group: Individuals and families experiencing homelessness, fleeing specified violence, or at risk of housing instability
affected_groups.explanation: These groups are the intended recipients of the program; financial assistance under the local-assistance provision is available only to those receiving a housing voucher.

affected_groups.group: Local governmental entities and nonprofit organizations
affected_groups.explanation: They may contract with the department for program funding, and selected local governmental entities may administer the pilot.

affected_groups.group: Landlords
affected_groups.explanation: The program may provide incentives to landlords who provide housing and may cover certain inspection costs.

major_effects.label: Creates a tenant-readiness pilot
major_effects.explanation: Directs the department to establish a pilot that funds local entities and nonprofit organizations to assist specified populations with obtaining housing.

major_effects.label: Housing assistance and landlord incentives
major_effects.explanation: Selected local administrators may provide qualified assistance up to $3,500 per household, only to eligible people receiving a housing voucher; qualified costs may also include landlord payments and inspection costs.

major_effects.label: Program eligibility rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to adopt necessary program rules, including eligibility requirements.

major_effects.label: Pilot outcomes report
major_effects.explanation: Requires a report to the legislature covering participant demographics, assistance, housing outcomes, administrator experiences, and rural service.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
agencies.explanation: The bill names the department and assigns it responsibility for establishing and implementing the pilot, adopting rules, and reporting outcomes.

HB552.summary: HB 552 would create a plumbing service technician license for people who meet board-set requirements, complete at least 2,000 supervised apprentice hours, pass an examination, and perform limited repair or replacement work in one- or two-family homes. It would also change the Plumbing Examiners Board’s administrative powers, protections, and reimbursement rules, and authorize certain agreements with higher education institutions and acceptance of gifts and grants.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a new occupational license and adds service technicians to the plumbing licensing and examination framework.
Sets training and apprenticeship requirements for a new plumbing credential and authorizes higher education agreements supporting workforce development.
Authorizes agreements with institutions of higher education for student services, education, outreach, and testing resources, subject to approval by the coordinating board.
Changes the plumbing board’s reimbursement, immunity, order-delegation, and resource-acceptance provisions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes Texas plumbing licensing requirements administered by a state board.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for plumbing service technician licenses and plumbing apprentices
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants would be subject to the new training, supervised-hours, examination, and work-scope requirements.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education and their students
affected_groups.explanation: The board could enter agreements with institutions for workforce development and student support services.

affected_groups.group: Plumbing board members, executive director, and employees
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes member expense reimbursement, provides good-faith liability protection, and allows delegation of certain order approvals.

major_effects.label: New plumbing service technician license
major_effects.explanation: Creates a license with supervised apprenticeship, examination, and board-set training and eligibility requirements; authorized work is limited to non-gas plumbing repairs and replacements in one- or two-family dwellings.

major_effects.label: Licensing and implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the board to adopt service technician eligibility requirements and implementing rules for the bill’s changes.

major_effects.label: Additional board powers and agreements
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes higher education memoranda of understanding and delegation to the executive director of approval authority for certain contested-case orders.

major_effects.label: Gifts and grants
major_effects.explanation: Allows the board to solicit and accept gifts, grants, donations, or other items of value to pay for activities under the chapter.

major_effects.label: Good-faith liability protection
major_effects.explanation: Provides immunity from liability for board members, the executive director, and employees for good-faith actions or omissions in performing covered duties.

major_effects.label: Board member reimbursement
major_effects.explanation: Replaces the per-diem and transportation-only provisions with reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses, subject to applicable General Appropriations Act limits.

agencies.name: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the board new licensing and rulemaking responsibilities and changes its administrative powers. No matching canonical registry identity is supplied.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The bill requires the coordinating board to approve a memorandum of understanding made under the new provision.

HB553.summary: The bill would prohibit commercial motor vehicles from parking at any time on qualifying signed streets within residential subdivisions, or on adjacent streets within 1,000 feet of a residence, school, place of worship, park, or retail area. It would require the county or municipality where a subdivision is located to post signs, allow specified parking for up to two hours, and authorize immediate towing of vehicles parked in violation.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes parking restrictions and towing rules for commercial motor vehicles on specified streets.
Assigns counties or municipalities a sign-posting duty and allows them to condition posting on payment by subdivision residents.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide Texas law governing qualifying streets in residential subdivisions.

locations.name: Residential subdivisions and qualifying adjacent streets
locations.explanation: The restrictions apply within subdivisions and on adjacent streets within 1,000 feet of specified properties, where the other statutory conditions are met.

affected_groups.group: Commercial motor vehicle operators and owners
affected_groups.explanation: Their parking is restricted on qualifying signed streets, subject to specified exceptions; violating vehicles may be towed immediately.

affected_groups.group: Counties and municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: They must post the signs required for the parking restrictions and may condition posting on residents paying the cost.

affected_groups.group: Residents of residential subdivisions
affected_groups.explanation: Residents are affected by the parking restrictions and may be required to pay sign costs if the county or municipality makes posting conditional on payment.

major_effects.label: All-times parking restriction
major_effects.explanation: On signed streets maintained by a county or municipality, commercial motor vehicle parking is prohibited within a subdivision or on qualifying adjacent streets, without the former overnight-only limit.

major_effects.label: Local sign-posting duty
major_effects.explanation: The county or municipality where a subdivision is located must post signs; it may condition posting on residents paying the sign costs.

major_effects.label: Limited parking exceptions
major_effects.explanation: Parking is permitted for no more than two hours when the operator remains in the vehicle during a rest or other legally mandated break, or when the vehicle is making a delivery or performing work and remains only as long as necessary.

major_effects.label: Immediate towing
major_effects.explanation: A commercial motor vehicle parked in violation of the restriction may be towed immediately.

HB554.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, each school district must give each student’s parent a physical copy of written information about mental-health resources available to the student. The information must cover counseling, suicide-prevention or crisis hotlines, family resources, and relevant resources from the list under Section 38.253; districts may use information compiled by the agency or the Health and Human Services Commission.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a new school-district requirement to provide information to parents of enrolled students.
Assigns a new information-distribution duty to school districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to each school district.

affected_groups.group: Parents of students enrolled in public school districts
affected_groups.explanation: They must be provided the written mental-health resource information.

affected_groups.group: Students enrolled in school districts
affected_groups.explanation: The information provided to their parents concerns resources available to the students.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Each district must provide the information at the beginning of each school year.

major_effects.label: Annual distribution of mental-health resource information
major_effects.explanation: Requires each district to provide parents a physical copy of written information covering specified mental-health resources; a district may use information compiled by the agency or HHSC.

HB555.summary: HB 555 would repeal subsection (c) of Alcoholic Beverage Code Section 14.05, a provision concerning sales of distilled spirits to ultimate consumers by holders of distiller’s and rectifier’s permits. Because the bill does not include the text of that subsection, the specific rule being removed cannot be determined from the supplied text.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill repeals a provision concerning regulated sales of distilled spirits by permit holders; the specific rule removed is not shown.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code, so the change is statewide in scope.

affected_groups.group: Holders of distiller’s and rectifier’s permits
affected_groups.explanation: The repealed subsection concerns their sales of distilled spirits to ultimate consumers; the precise effect on those sales is unclear without the subsection’s text.

affected_groups.group: Ultimate consumers of distilled spirits
affected_groups.explanation: The bill concerns sales of distilled spirits to ultimate consumers, though the specific change to those sales cannot be determined from the supplied text.

major_effects.label: Repeal of a distilled-spirits sales provision
major_effects.explanation: Repeals Alcoholic Beverage Code Section 14.05(c), which concerns sales to ultimate consumers by distiller’s and rectifier’s permit holders. The omitted subsection text prevents specifying the rule removed.

HB556.summary: The bill would require a transportation network company to notify both the driver and the ride requester when a ride’s starting or ending point requires the driver’s vehicle or the requester to enter a designated bicycle lane. The notice, sent when the driver accepts the ride, must identify the bicycle-lane entry and advise both people to watch for bicyclists.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a bicycle-lane notification requirement for digitally arranged rides.
Imposes a new notification duty on transportation network companies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The new requirement is added to Texas law and is not limited to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Transportation network companies
affected_groups.explanation: Must provide the specified notification through their digital networks when the condition applies.

affected_groups.group: Drivers and people requesting digitally prearranged rides
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive the notification when the driver accepts a ride that requires bicycle-lane entry.

affected_groups.group: Bicyclists
affected_groups.explanation: The notice must advise the driver and requester to be alert for bicyclists.

major_effects.label: Bicycle-lane notifications for rides
major_effects.explanation: When a ride’s starting or ending point requires entry into a designated bicycle lane, the company must notify the driver and requester at ride acceptance and advise them to watch for bicyclists.

HB557.summary: HB 557 would align wine-only package-store hours for off-premises sales of malt beverages, wine, and vinous liquors with malt-beverage hours, removing the separate restriction on Sundays and late-night sales of wine and vinous liquors over 17% alcohol. It would also permit wholesalers to sell, offer for sale, or deliver liquor to retailers anytime except Christmas Day, and set local distributors’ hours by reference to the hours prescribed for malt-beverage sale and delivery.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes permitted hours for alcohol sales and deliveries by package stores, liquor sellers, wholesalers, and local distributors.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code rules without specifying a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Holders of wine-only package store permits
affected_groups.explanation: Their allowable hours for covered off-premises sales would follow malt-beverage hours.

affected_groups.group: Persons selling, offering for sale, or delivering liquor
affected_groups.explanation: The general hours restriction for liquor would be tied to malt-beverage hours, subject to listed holidays and statutory exceptions.

affected_groups.group: Liquor wholesalers
affected_groups.explanation: Wholesalers could sell or deliver liquor to retailers at any time except Christmas Day.

affected_groups.group: Local liquor distributors and retailers receiving their deliveries
affected_groups.explanation: Local distributor sales and deliveries to retailers would follow malt-beverage hours, except on days package stores cannot sell liquor.

major_effects.label: Wine-only package-store hours
major_effects.explanation: Covered off-premises sales would use malt-beverage hours, replacing the separate Sunday and late-night restriction for wine and vinous liquor over 17% alcohol.

major_effects.label: General liquor sale hours
major_effects.explanation: Liquor sales, offers for sale, and deliveries would be barred outside malt-beverage hours, with New Year's Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day prohibitions retained, subject to existing statutory exceptions.

major_effects.label: Wholesale and local-distributor schedules
major_effects.explanation: Wholesalers could supply retailers anytime except Christmas Day; local distributors would follow malt-beverage sale and delivery hours, except on days package stores may not sell liquor.

HB558.summary: HB 558 would require each institution of higher education covered by the incorporated Education Code definition, as part of its comprehensive prevention and outreach program, to post in every campus restroom a sign carrying the same written notice adopted by HHSC. An institution could comply by printing and displaying a publicly available digital version of that notice.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds a campus restroom sign requirement for covered institutions of higher education.

locations.name: Campuses of covered institutions of higher education
locations.explanation: The signs must be posted in restrooms located on each covered institution's campus.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education covered by Education Code Section 61.003
affected_groups.explanation: These institutions would have to post the notice in campus restrooms.

affected_groups.group: People using covered campus restrooms
affected_groups.explanation: They would have access to the posted notice, which the bill identifies as facilitating reporting and preventing specified incidents.

major_effects.label: Required campus restroom signs
major_effects.explanation: Covered institutions would have to post a sign in each campus restroom, at least 8.5 by 11 inches, with content identical to the HHSC-adopted notice.

major_effects.label: Digital notice option
major_effects.explanation: An institution may comply by printing and displaying a publicly available digital version of the required notice.

agencies.name: institution of higher education
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the sign-posting duty to institutions in this defined class, but does not name a specific institution or registry body.

HB559.summary: The bill would allow a child-care facility to provide information about the share of attending children and employed adults who are immunized, along with the facility’s infection-prevention handwashing policy. It would permit these disclosures but would not require facilities to provide the information.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes what health-related immunization and infection-prevention information a child-care facility may provide.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision amends Texas law governing child-care facilities and is not limited to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Child-care facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Facilities may provide the specified immunization and handwashing-policy information.

affected_groups.group: Children attending child-care facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The permitted information may include the percentage of attending children who are immunized.

affected_groups.group: Adults employed by child-care facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The permitted information may include the percentage of employed adults who are immunized.

major_effects.label: Permissive health-information disclosure
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes a child-care facility to provide specified immunization percentages and its infection-prevention handwashing policy; it does not require disclosure.

HB560.summary: The bill would bar political subdivisions from adopting or enforcing minimum parking-space requirements for bars holding one of the listed alcohol permits and lacking a food and beverage certificate. It would not limit local regulation of accessible parking for persons with disabilities under state or federal law.

policy_tags.explanation: Restricts political subdivisions' authority to impose minimum parking requirements for covered bars.
Removes a local regulatory requirement for businesses meeting the bill's definition of a bar.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The restriction applies generally to political subdivisions in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Bars holding one of the listed alcohol permits and lacking a food and beverage certificate
affected_groups.explanation: These establishments would no longer be subject to local minimum parking-space requirements under the bill.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions
affected_groups.explanation: Their authority to require minimum parking spaces for covered bars would be restricted, while their authority to regulate accessible parking would remain.

major_effects.label: Limits local minimum parking requirements for covered bars
major_effects.explanation: Political subdivisions could not adopt or enforce minimum parking-space requirements for covered bars; the bill preserves their ability to regulate accessible parking for persons with disabilities under state or federal law.

HB562.summary: HB 562 would prohibit a health benefit plan from requiring prior authorization for medication-assisted treatment of opioid or substance use disorders when the plan covers that treatment, except as needed to minimize fraud, waste, or abuse. The rule would apply to specified plans covering Texas residents, but not Medicaid or CHIP, and only to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028; it would not itself require plans to cover the treatment.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes access conditions for covered treatment of opioid or substance use disorders.
Sets a conduct requirement for issuers and providers of specified health benefit plans.

locations.name: Statewide (Texas residents)
locations.explanation: The rule applies to group health plan coverage provided to Texas residents, regardless of where the group policy is issued or renewed.

affected_groups.group: Enrollees with opioid or substance use disorders
affected_groups.explanation: Enrollees receiving covered medication-assisted treatment would no longer face prior authorization for that treatment, subject to the fraud, waste, and abuse exception.

affected_groups.group: Issuers and providers of covered health benefit plans
affected_groups.explanation: Plans within the subchapter’s scope would have to follow the prior-authorization limitation for covered treatment, except as needed to minimize the opportunity for fraud, waste, and abuse.

major_effects.label: Limits prior authorization
major_effects.explanation: For treatment that a plan covers, prior authorization is barred except as needed to minimize fraud, waste, or abuse.

major_effects.label: Limits which plans are covered
major_effects.explanation: The subchapter excludes Medicaid and CHIP coverage; the new rule applies only to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Insurance
agencies.explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Code and changes a requirement for health benefit plans. It does not expressly assign the department a new duty.

HB563.summary: The bill would lower the annual limit on increases to a residence homestead’s appraised value from 10 percent to 3 percent, while retaining the existing formula’s treatment of new improvements and the market-value ceiling. It would apply to tax years beginning on or after its effective date, and would take effect only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise, it would have no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the appraised-value limitation used for ad valorem taxation of residence homesteads.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The appraisal limitation applies to residence homesteads statewide.

affected_groups.group: Owners of residence homesteads
affected_groups.explanation: The limit on increases to the appraised value of their homes would be reduced, if the constitutional amendment is approved.

affected_groups.group: Appraisal offices
affected_groups.explanation: These offices apply the limit when appraising residence homesteads for taxation.

major_effects.label: Lower homestead appraisal-growth limit
major_effects.explanation: Reduces the annual percentage component of the appraised-value cap from 10 percent to 3 percent. The change applies only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment.

HB564.summary: The bill would require institutions of higher education to give entering freshman and undergraduate transfer applicants information about eligibility and enrollment for public health coverage, including Medicaid and the child health plan program. The Health and Human Services Commission would develop current, easy-to-understand eligibility materials to support that information; the requirement would apply beginning with the 2027 fall semester.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates information-distribution duties for institutions of higher education toward specified admission applicants.
Requires information about eligibility and enrollment for public health benefits coverage.
Specifically includes Medicaid coverage in the required eligibility information; the bill does not change Medicaid eligibility itself.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply generally to institutions of higher education and their covered applicants in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for freshman or undergraduate transfer admission at institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive information about public health benefit eligibility and enrollment.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: They would distribute the required information, tailored to their student population.

major_effects.label: Public health coverage information for applicants
major_effects.explanation: Institutions would distribute information explaining relevant eligibility and enrollment procedures; the bill does not change who qualifies for coverage.

major_effects.label: Eligibility materials developed by HHSC
major_effects.explanation: HHSC would prepare supporting eligibility materials that are current and clear and easy to understand.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: Must develop current, clear informational material on public health benefit eligibility.

HB565.summary: HB 565 would define advanced air mobility around electric aircraft weighing at least 300 pounds that transport passengers or cargo, or provide services in an urban or regional setting. It would require the department to plan for vertiports, electric-aircraft charging and related aviation infrastructure, and generally bar political subdivisions from regulating advanced-air-mobility aircraft, their ownership or aerial operation. The restriction is subject to an exception requiring the political subdivision to be an airport operator and at least one additional condition; the supplied excerpt does not show that further condition.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes statewide aviation planning and technical-support duties concerning advanced air mobility.
It limits political subdivisions' authority to regulate advanced air mobility, while preserving a narrow airport-operator exception.
It assigns the department new statewide planning, technical-assistance and public-official education responsibilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill requires a statewide aviation plan and resources intended to support uniform provisions across Texas.

locations.name: Geographic boundaries of an airport operated by a political subdivision
locations.explanation: The airport-operator exception is limited to regulation of aircraft activity within the airport's geographic boundaries and takeoffs or landings there.

affected_groups.group: Local and regional governmental entities
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive planning guidance and technical resources concerning aviation technology.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions, including airport operators
affected_groups.explanation: Their authority to regulate advanced air mobility would be restricted. The stated exception requires the political subdivision to be an airport operator and at least one additional condition, which is not shown in the supplied excerpt.

affected_groups.group: Owners and operators of qualifying advanced-air-mobility aircraft
affected_groups.explanation: The bill limits local regulation of aircraft ownership and aerial operation within its defined scope.

major_effects.label: Statewide aviation planning and support
major_effects.explanation: The department would develop or update a statewide plan covering vertiports, electric-aircraft charging and other aviation infrastructure, and provide related resources and public-official education.

major_effects.label: Limits on local regulation, with an airport exception
major_effects.explanation: Political subdivisions generally could not regulate advanced air mobility, aircraft ownership or aerial operations. An airport-operator political subdivision could regulate operations within that airport's boundaries and aircraft takeoffs or landings there.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department new aviation-planning and support duties, but the supplied text does not identify which state agency the generic term denotes. Its placement in the Transportation Code suggests a transportation agency, but that identity is not verified here.

HB566.summary: For identification cards issued on or after January 1, 2028, HB 566 would require health maintenance organization cards to display “HMO” and insurer cards subject to Chapter 1301 to display “PPO.” The bill would also state that those labels do not ensure access to discounts for out-of-network services or to other discounts available through the network.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required information on health plan identification cards and adds statements about access to network-related discounts.
Imposes new identification-card content requirements on health maintenance organizations and insurers subject to the specified Insurance Code chapter.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to covered identification cards under the Texas Insurance Code, without a narrower geographic limit.

affected_groups.group: Health maintenance organization enrollees and insured individuals
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive cards displaying the applicable acronym and a statement about access to network-related discounts.

affected_groups.group: Health maintenance organizations and insurers regulated by the Insurance Code and subject to Chapter 1301
affected_groups.explanation: They would have to include the new acronym and related disclosure on covered identification cards issued from January 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: HMO and PPO identification-card content
major_effects.explanation: Requires covered HMO and insurer cards to display the relevant acronym and states that the label does not ensure access to out-of-network discounts or other network fee discounts. Applies only to cards issued on or after January 1, 2028.

HB567.summary: HB 567 would allow community supervision and corrections officers and juvenile probation officers to carry authorized weapons while off duty, subject to the applicable certification and approval requirements and, for juvenile probation officers, at least one year of employment. It would prohibit establishments serving the public from restricting authorized carry by those officers and qualifying retired law-enforcement officers, and add juvenile probation officers to the group protected by the offense for taking or attempting to take specified weapons from certain personnel.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes when specified officers and qualifying retired law-enforcement officers may carry weapons, including at public-serving establishments.
Adds juvenile probation officers to the personnel covered by the offense for taking or attempting to take specified weapons.
Prohibits establishments serving the public from restricting specified officers' and qualifying retired officers' authorized weapon carry on their premises.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The weapon-carrying exemptions apply in this state.

affected_groups.group: Community supervision and corrections department officers
affected_groups.explanation: May carry authorized weapons regardless of whether they are discharging their duties, subject to certification and department-director approval.

affected_groups.group: Juvenile probation officers
affected_groups.explanation: May carry firearms outside official duties if statutory requirements are met, and are added to the group covered by the weapon-taking offense.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying retired peace officers and other qualified retired law-enforcement officers
affected_groups.explanation: May carry authorized weapons at establishments serving the public without those establishments prohibiting or restricting the carry.

affected_groups.group: Establishments serving the public
affected_groups.explanation: May not prohibit or otherwise restrict the specified officers' and qualifying retired officers' authorized carry on their premises.

affected_groups.group: People who take or attempt to take specified weapons from protected personnel
affected_groups.explanation: The weapon-taking offense's protected group is expanded to include juvenile probation officers.

major_effects.label: Off-duty weapon carry
major_effects.explanation: Allows community supervision and corrections officers to carry under the section regardless of duty status if certified and approved by the department director. Juvenile probation officers may carry regardless of duty status if certified, authorized by their department's chief for official-duty carry, and employed by the department for at least one year.

major_effects.label: Carry at public-serving establishments
major_effects.explanation: Bars public-serving establishments from prohibiting or restricting authorized carry by the specified officers and qualifying retired law-enforcement officers.

major_effects.label: Expanded weapon-taking offense coverage
major_effects.explanation: Adds juvenile probation officers to the group from whom taking or attempting to take specified weapons is an offense; the bill does not specify a change to the offense's penalty level.

HB568.summary: HB 568 would require the Texas Department of Transportation to reimburse grant recipients for construction costs exceeding the grant amount when the department manages the project, but only for projects in counties with fewer than 25,000 people or municipalities with fewer than 15,000 people. The requirement would apply only to grants awarded on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes reimbursement rules for grants to construct transportation projects.
It requires the department to reimburse qualifying recipients for eligible costs above the grant amount.

locations.name: Counties with populations under 25,000 and municipalities with populations under 15,000
locations.explanation: The reimbursement provision is limited to transportation projects in counties or municipalities meeting the stated population thresholds.

affected_groups.group: Recipients of qualifying transportation-project grants
affected_groups.explanation: Recipients may receive reimbursement for qualifying construction costs above the grant amount when the department manages construction.

major_effects.label: Reimbursement of excess construction costs
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying projects in the specified small counties or municipalities, the department must reimburse costs above the grant amount if it manages construction. The requirement applies only to grants awarded on or after the Act’s effective date.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department a mandatory reimbursement duty; the bill identifies the department as the Texas Department of Transportation.

HB569.summary: The bill adds the National Sexual Assault Hotline and a youth crisis support service designated by the Texas Education Agency to the information required on public-school student ID cards for students in grade six or higher. The change applies to cards issued on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes information requirements for student identification cards issued by public schools.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement concerns student identification cards issued by public schools, without a narrower geographic limit.

affected_groups.group: Public-school students in grade six or higher
affected_groups.explanation: Their student identification cards must include the added hotline and youth crisis support information, for cards issued on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Additional student ID card information
major_effects.explanation: Requires the National Sexual Assault Hotline and a designated youth crisis support service to be included on covered student ID cards.

major_effects.label: Youth crisis support service designation
major_effects.explanation: Directs the Texas Education Agency to designate a service for the card-information requirement.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the agency the duty to designate a youth crisis support service for the student-card requirement.

HB570.summary: The bill would allow people to distribute sealed, unbranded water to voters waiting in line at a polling place, provided the distribution is nonpartisan and does not interfere with voting. Election officials would have to ensure compliance and could remove a person who violates the requirements.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill sets conditions for distributing water to voters at polling places and assigns compliance responsibilities to election officials.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The amendment applies to polling places under the statewide Texas Election Code.

affected_groups.group: Voters waiting in line at polling places
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive water under the bill's stated conditions.

affected_groups.group: People distributing water at polling places
affected_groups.explanation: They must follow the restrictions on the water, manner of distribution, attire, and displayed materials.

affected_groups.group: Election officials
affected_groups.explanation: They must ensure compliance and may remove violators from the polling place.

major_effects.label: Conditional permission to distribute water
major_effects.explanation: Allows water distribution to voters waiting in line only when the water and distribution meet the bill's nonpartisan and noninterference requirements.

major_effects.label: Polling-place compliance and removal authority
major_effects.explanation: Requires election officials to ensure compliance and permits them to remove a person found in violation.

HB571.summary: The bill authorizes an institution of higher education to adopt a policy prohibiting cigarette, e-cigarette, or tobacco-product use on its campus grounds or in campus buildings. It does not itself prohibit that use; a prohibition would apply only if an institution adopts such a policy.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the policy authority of institutions of higher education regarding conduct on their campuses.

locations.name: Grounds and buildings on an institution of higher education's campus
locations.explanation: The authorized policies may cover the institution's campus grounds and buildings.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: These institutions may choose whether to adopt a policy prohibiting the specified uses on campus.

affected_groups.group: People using institution campuses
affected_groups.explanation: Campus users could be subject to a prohibition if an institution adopts the authorized policy.

major_effects.label: Optional campus-use prohibition
major_effects.explanation: An institution may adopt a policy prohibiting cigarette, e-cigarette, or tobacco-product use on campus grounds or in campus buildings; the bill does not impose a prohibition automatically.

agencies.name: Texas Division of Emergency Management
agencies.explanation: Section 61.003 includes other agencies of higher education within the defined term and specifically lists the Texas Division of Emergency Management as one. The bill authorizes an institution of higher education to adopt the described campus policy.

HB572.summary: HB 572 would increase the franchise and insurance premium tax credit cap for rehabilitation of a certified historic structure from 25% to 33% of eligible costs when the structure is in a distressed county and at least half its internal square footage is primarily residential when placed in service. A distressed county is one with median household income no greater than 80% of the state median, measured using the Census Bureau’s most recent five-year American Community Survey estimate; the bill also adds county-status information to the eligibility certification process. The changes apply only to tax reports due and certificates issued on or after the Act’s effective date, with a process for certain applicants whose certificate requests are still pending.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the maximum tax credit available for qualifying historic rehabilitation costs.
Uses a larger tax credit to encourage rehabilitation investment in qualifying historic structures, subject to county and residential-use conditions.

locations.name: Texas counties meeting the distressed-county income test
locations.explanation: The enhanced credit applies to a structure in a county whose median household income is no more than 80% of the Texas median, determined using the specified Census Bureau estimate.

affected_groups.group: Entities incurring eligible costs to rehabilitate certified historic structures
affected_groups.explanation: These entities may qualify for the increased credit cap when the county and residential-use conditions are met.

affected_groups.group: Entities with certificate requests pending when the Act takes effect
affected_groups.explanation: Certain entities that applied before the effective date and have not yet received a certificate may certify the structure’s distressed-county status for Commission verification.

major_effects.label: Higher credit cap for qualifying rehabilitation
major_effects.explanation: Raises the maximum credit from 25% to 33% of eligible costs for a structure in a distressed county if at least 50% of its internal square footage is primarily residential when placed in service.

major_effects.label: Distressed-county status in eligibility certification
major_effects.explanation: Adds county status to the information and certificate determinations; certain applicants with pending requests may submit written certification, which the Commission must verify before indicating the status on the certificate.

agencies.name: Texas Historical Commission
agencies.explanation: The Commission’s eligibility-certificate process must address distressed-county status, and it must verify qualifying information from certain applicants with pending requests and indicate the status on the certificate when verified.

HB573.summary: The bill increases from two to five the maximum years of qualifying career or technology field work experience that count as teaching experience for salary-step credit. It also allows eligible members to establish up to five years of equivalent Teacher Retirement System service credit for that experience, beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes salary-step credit rules for certified public school career or technology education teachers.
Changes qualifying work experience counted toward teacher salary steps and retirement service credit.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes state education and retirement-credit rules applying to the specified teachers and eligible members across Texas.

affected_groups.group: Certified public school career or technology education teachers
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying work experience may count for up to five years of salary-step credit.

affected_groups.group: Eligible Teacher Retirement System members who are certified career or technology education teachers with qualifying work experience in a career or technological field
affected_groups.explanation: They may establish equivalent membership service credit for up to five years of qualifying experience.

major_effects.label: Expanded salary-step credit
major_effects.explanation: Raises the maximum qualifying career or technology field work experience counted as teaching experience for salary-step credit from two years to five.

major_effects.label: Expanded retirement service credit
major_effects.explanation: Allows eligible members to establish equivalent membership service credit for up to five years of experience that qualifies for salary-step credit.

agencies.name: Teacher Retirement System of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill expands the maximum qualifying work experience for which an eligible member may establish equivalent service credit in the system named in the bill.

HB574.summary: HB 574 would require polling places to provide accessible restroom access to voters, election workers, and volunteers during voting hours, with visible signage and restroom-access information in election materials. If a polling place lacks a permanent restroom accessible to the public, the responsible county or political subdivision would have to provide a temporary restroom that complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act and is readily accessible to voters.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates restroom-access requirements for polling places and election materials.
Assigns a conditional temporary-restroom duty to the county or political subdivision responsible for a polling place.
Requires accessible restroom access at polling places, including an ADA-compliant temporary facility when the stated condition applies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The new requirements apply to polling places under the statewide Election Code provision.

affected_groups.group: Voters, including voters needing accessible facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Would receive accessible restroom access during polling-place voting hours.

affected_groups.group: Election workers and volunteers
affected_groups.explanation: Would be included among those provided restroom access at polling places.

affected_groups.group: Counties and political subdivisions responsible for polling places
affected_groups.explanation: Would have to provide a temporary restroom when the polling place lacks a permanent restroom accessible to the public.

major_effects.label: Accessible restroom access at polling places
major_effects.explanation: Requires restroom access for voters, election workers, and volunteers during voting hours; if no permanent public-access restroom is maintained, the responsible local entity must provide a temporary ADA-compliant restroom readily accessible to voters. Polling places must also post restroom-location signage and election materials must include restroom-access information.

HB575.summary: HB 575 would define an “individual” to include an unborn child from fertilization until birth and apply Penal Code homicide and assault provisions equally to offenses against unborn and born victims. It would repeal specified Penal Code and civil provisions while adding exceptions for unintentional injury or death resulting from qualifying lifesaving procedures or spontaneous miscarriage. The Penal Code changes would apply only to offenses committed on or after the effective date, while the civil changes generally apply prospectively.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the reach of homicide and assault provisions to include offenses against unborn victims, subject to specified exceptions.
Extends equal application of the specified criminal-law protections to unborn victims and revises related civil-law treatment.
Creates a liability exception tied to lifesaving procedures for a pregnant mother, subject to steps to save the unborn child and an unintentional outcome.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes without limiting their application to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Unborn children
affected_groups.explanation: The bill includes unborn children from fertilization within the definition of an individual and applies the specified criminal chapters equally to them as victims.

affected_groups.group: Pregnant mothers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill expressly addresses unintentional outcomes of procedures undertaken to save a pregnant mother's life, with a specific condition concerning reasonable and available steps to save the unborn child.

affected_groups.group: People whose conduct causes injury or death to an unborn child, including those involved in lifesaving procedures
affected_groups.explanation: The criminal provisions apply to offenses against unborn victims, while the bill specifies exceptions for certain unintentional outcomes.

major_effects.label: Criminal coverage of unborn victims
major_effects.explanation: Applies the homicide and assault chapters equally to offenses against unborn and born victims; the new exclusions cover specified unintentional injury or death from lifesaving procedures or spontaneous miscarriage.

major_effects.label: Civil-law changes and exception
major_effects.explanation: Amends the civil subchapter's treatment of unintentional injury or death of an unborn child and repeals the specified existing subsection; the bill text does not state the full content of the repealed subsection.

HB576.summary: The bill would prohibit a person subject to registration under Chapter 62 from purchasing a firearm if the registration requirement is based on an offense committed on or after September 1, 2027. It would also require the restriction to be included in specified release and registration-verification notices.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a firearm-purchase prohibition for a defined group of people required to register as sex offenders.
Amends the criminal-procedure registration framework by adding a prohibition and related notices for people required to register under Chapter 62.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to Chapter 62 registration and local law enforcement authorities generally, without limiting the requirements to a named place.

affected_groups.group: People required to register under Chapter 62 based on an offense committed on or after September 1, 2027
affected_groups.explanation: These people would be subject to the firearm-purchase prohibition and related notices.

affected_groups.group: Officials of penal institutions
affected_groups.explanation: Before release, an official must inform the person of the new firearm-purchase prohibition when the specified offense-date condition is met.

affected_groups.group: Local law enforcement authorities
affected_groups.explanation: Authorities that provide registration-verification forms must include a statement describing the prohibitions under Articles 62.064 and 62.066.

major_effects.label: Firearm-purchase prohibition
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits a person subject to Chapter 62 registration from purchasing a firearm when the registration requirement is based on an offense committed on or after the Act's effective date.

major_effects.label: Release and verification notices
major_effects.explanation: Adds the prohibition to the information officials provide before release and to statements included with registration-verification forms.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: The bill adds a pre-release notice about the firearm prohibition for officials of penal institutions. TDCJ is named in the surrounding release provision, but the new notice duty is assigned to a penal-institution official rather than expressly to the department.

agencies.name: Texas Juvenile Justice Department
agencies.explanation: The bill adds a pre-release notice about the firearm prohibition for officials of penal institutions. The department is named in the surrounding release provision, but the new notice duty is assigned to a penal-institution official rather than expressly to the department.

HB577.summary: The bill would require public or private facilities with capacity for at least 100 people and gatherings where at least 100 people are reasonably expected to have an accessible automated external defibrillator, with signage and maintenance requirements for facilities. A gathering organizer need not provide a separate defibrillator if the location already provides one meeting the requirements; compliance is not required until January 1, 2028, and the HHSC executive commissioner must adopt implementing rules by December 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates requirements for ready access to automated external defibrillators at qualifying facilities and gatherings.
Requires emergency-response equipment to be accessible at certain public-facing facilities and large gatherings.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to qualifying facilities and gatherings generally under Texas law, without a specified local boundary.

affected_groups.group: Owners and operators of qualifying high-occupancy facilities
affected_groups.explanation: They would have to provide, locate, sign for, and maintain an AED while the facility is open to the public or occupied.

affected_groups.group: Organizers of public or private gatherings expected to have at least 100 attendees
affected_groups.explanation: Organizers would have to ensure an accessible AED is available throughout the gathering, unless the location already provides one meeting the requirements.

major_effects.label: AED availability requirements
major_effects.explanation: Requires an accessible AED at qualifying facilities and large gatherings; gathering organizers may rely on a qualifying AED provided by the location.

major_effects.label: HHSC implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the HHSC executive commissioner to adopt implementing rules by December 1, 2027.

major_effects.label: Delayed compliance
major_effects.explanation: The new facility and gathering requirements do not require compliance before January 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The HHSC executive commissioner is authorized to adopt implementing rules and is required to adopt rules by December 1, 2027.

HB578.summary: The bill would allow a convicting court, for good cause and after notice and an opportunity for the state’s attorney to be heard, to grant an initial 90-day extension and further 90-day extensions if each later request is made before the preceding extension expires. A later application would be subject to limits on merits review after final disposition of an initial application, or if treated as subsequent under Subsection (f); a court could not consider its merits or grant relief unless specified factual grounds are established.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes habeas corpus procedures in death penalty cases, including extension requests and judicial review of subsequent applications.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide criminal procedure governing habeas applications.

affected_groups.group: People sentenced to death seeking habeas relief
affected_groups.explanation: Their ability to seek extensions and obtain merits review of subsequent applications is affected.

affected_groups.group: Attorneys representing the state in capital habeas cases
affected_groups.explanation: They receive notice and an opportunity to be heard on initial and subsequent extension requests.

major_effects.label: Initial and subsequent extensions
major_effects.explanation: For good cause and after notice and an opportunity for the state’s attorney to be heard, a convicting court may grant an initial 90-day extension and subsequent 90-day extensions requested before the preceding extension expires. The amendment applies only to qualifying applications whose filing is not untimely under the stated deadline provisions on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Review of subsequent applications
major_effects.explanation: The limits apply after final disposition of an initial application or when an application is considered subsequent under Subsection (f); a court may not reach the merits or grant relief unless the statutory grounds are established. This amendment applies only to applications filed on or after the effective date.

agencies.name: convicting court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly changes the court’s authority over extension requests and its ability to consider certain subsequent applications. The source uses a generic court description rather than identifying a particular court or canonical registry body.

HB579.summary: The bill would require the state's classification officer to review state information technology positions at least every two years and revise the classification plan to align titles and work descriptions with the private sector and emphasize job skills over degree and certification requirements. The officer would consult the Department of Information Resources and, by October 1, 2028, report on the initial review and revisions to the governor and each legislator.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how state information technology jobs are classified and described, including emphasizing competencies over degree and certification requirements.
Creates recurring review, revision, and reporting duties for the state's position classification plan.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill concerns the state's position classification plan for information technology positions, rather than a particular geographic place.

affected_groups.group: State information technology employees and applicants
affected_groups.explanation: Their job titles, classifications, and descriptions may be revised, including the stated emphasis on competencies rather than degree and certification requirements.

major_effects.label: Recurring review and revision of IT job classifications
major_effects.explanation: Requires review at least every two years and any plan changes needed for private-sector alignment and competency-focused descriptions.

major_effects.label: Initial review report
major_effects.explanation: Requires a written report to the governor and each legislator summarizing the initial review and any revisions by October 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Department of Information Resources
agencies.explanation: The department is a required consultation participant in reviews, and its recommendations must be considered; the bill does not require it to make recommendations.

HB580.summary: HB 580 would require private schools seeking approval as providers or vendors in the education savings account program to demonstrate compliance with federal laws on educational services for children with disabilities, including IDEA, ADA Title II, and Section 504. It also updates statutory references in existing tutor, therapist, and teaching-service eligibility checks. These changes apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility requirements for providers participating in the education savings account program.
Changes which private schools may qualify as providers or vendors in an education savings account program.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes eligibility rules for a Texas education savings account program and specifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Private schools seeking approval as education savings account providers or vendors
affected_groups.explanation: They must demonstrate compliance with the added federal disability-services requirement to qualify.

affected_groups.group: Children with disabilities served by participating private schools
affected_groups.explanation: The new eligibility condition concerns federal requirements for providing educational services to children with disabilities.

affected_groups.group: Private tutors, therapists, and teaching-service employees serving participating children
affected_groups.explanation: The bill updates statutory references used in their existing eligibility exclusions and registry checks.

major_effects.label: Private-school provider eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Adds compliance with federal laws governing educational services to children with disabilities as a condition for private-school participation.

major_effects.label: Updated tutor screening references
major_effects.explanation: Replaces references in existing tutor, therapist, and teaching-service eligibility criteria with Sections 22A.157 and 22A.151.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The Comptroller approves education service providers and vendors, so it must apply the added private-school eligibility requirement.

HB581.summary: HB 581 would require the Department of State Health Services to develop and implement a maternal health care workforce campaign, focusing on training, workforce growth, and improving access in rural and professional-shortage areas. The Health and Human Services Commission’s executive commissioner would adopt implementing rules; the campaign would also support services for women from underserved racial or ethnic minority groups.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a campaign to expand maternal health care capacity and improve access to services.
The campaign is expressly aimed at increasing the maternal health care workforce and supporting its training.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The campaign concerns the state's maternal health care workforce and capacity.

locations.name: Rural areas and areas with a shortage of maternal health care professionals
locations.explanation: The campaign is designed to improve access and increase workforce numbers in these areas.

affected_groups.group: Maternal health care professionals, including doulas and providers of nonmedical support
affected_groups.explanation: The campaign targets this workforce with outreach, continuing education, and training.

affected_groups.group: Women of underserved racial or ethnic minority groups
affected_groups.explanation: The campaign would facilitate maternal health care programs serving this population.

affected_groups.group: Maternal health care professionals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups
affected_groups.explanation: The campaign is designed to increase their representation in the workforce.

major_effects.label: Maternal health care workforce campaign
major_effects.explanation: Requires a public outreach campaign to expand the workforce and access, including training, programs, and capacity-building efforts.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Health and Human Services Commission’s executive commissioner to adopt rules necessary to implement the campaign.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department responsibility for developing and implementing the campaign; Section 2 identifies it as the Department of State Health Services.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission’s executive commissioner is assigned to adopt rules implementing the campaign.

HB582.summary: The bill would make it a misdemeanor to possess a burning tobacco product or smoke tobacco inside or on the grounds of a state-owned building where a state agency office is located. A conviction would be punishable by a fine of up to $50; the bill’s definition of “state agency” excludes university systems and institutions of higher education.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a misdemeanor offense and establishes its maximum fine.
Establishes a conduct restriction for qualifying state-owned buildings containing state agency offices.

locations.name: Statewide: qualifying state-owned buildings
locations.explanation: The restriction applies across the state to state-owned buildings where a state agency office is located.

affected_groups.group: People at qualifying state-owned buildings
affected_groups.explanation: Anyone inside or on the grounds of a covered building would be subject to the new prohibition.

major_effects.label: Misdemeanor prohibition and fine
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits possessing a burning tobacco product or smoking tobacco in covered buildings or on their grounds, with a misdemeanor fine capped at $50.

HB583.summary: The bill requires the Department of State Health Services to use available resources to develop and implement an e-cigarette and tobacco prevention and cessation program, including a counseling hotline and information about services for pregnant or postpartum women. The department must prioritize and accept all eligible applicants who are pregnant or gave birth in the preceding year; it may partner with a nonprofit organization.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a tobacco and e-cigarette prevention and cessation program with counseling and related health-service information.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The program is assigned to a Texas state department without a narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: Pregnant people and people who gave birth in the preceding year who are eligible applicants
affected_groups.explanation: The department must prioritize and accept all eligible applicants in these groups.

affected_groups.group: People seeking e-cigarette or tobacco cessation support
affected_groups.explanation: The program must provide a hotline with cessation counseling.

major_effects.label: Prevention and cessation program
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to create and implement a program that includes a cessation counseling hotline and information about available services for pregnant or postpartum women.

major_effects.label: Priority for pregnant and recently postpartum applicants
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to prioritize and accept all eligible program applicants who are pregnant or gave birth in the preceding year.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department responsibility for developing and implementing the program and prioritizing eligible applicants.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the executive commissioner to adopt implementing rules. Health and Safety Code §1001.001 defines “Executive commissioner” as the executive commissioner of the Health and Human Services Commission.

HB584.summary: The bill authorizes counties, alone or regionally, to establish family-violence courts for defendants and victim-services courts for victims who voluntarily participate; defendant programs may charge a capped, ability-to-pay-based fee. Some participants who complete a defendant program may qualify for dismissal and expunction, and some graduates may petition for nondisclosure of related criminal-history information after two years if they meet specified conditions.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates local court programs and changes eligibility for dismissal, expunction, and nondisclosure related to family-violence cases.
The defendant-court program includes interventions to end abusive behavior and consideration of alleged victims' safety.
County commissioners courts may establish programs, regional programs may be shared by counties, and counties may accept gifts for victim-services programs.
Family-violence court programs are added to the specialty-court category considered for grant funding; this does not itself award a grant.
Eligible program graduates may obtain an order restricting public disclosure of criminal-history information related to the program offense.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill authorizes programs in counties statewide, but establishment is optional and regional programs involve participating counties.

affected_groups.group: Defendants arrested for and charged with misdemeanor offenses involving family violence
affected_groups.explanation: They may participate in a county program, may owe a program fee based on ability to pay, and some may qualify for dismissal, expunction, or later nondisclosure.

affected_groups.group: Victims of alleged family-violence offenses
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible victims may voluntarily join a victim-services court program and may withdraw at any time.

affected_groups.group: County governments
affected_groups.explanation: County commissioners courts may establish defendant or victim-services programs, alone or in regional arrangements.

major_effects.label: Family-violence defendant court programs
major_effects.explanation: Counties may establish programs for people charged with qualifying misdemeanor offenses; two or more counties may establish a regional program.

major_effects.label: Victim-services court programs
major_effects.explanation: Counties may establish programs for eligible victims who agree voluntarily; participation can be ended by the participant.

major_effects.label: Program funding options
major_effects.explanation: Defendant programs may charge a reasonable fee up to $1,000, based on ability to pay and used only for program purposes; counties may also accept contributions for victim-services programs.

major_effects.label: Specialty-court grant consideration
major_effects.explanation: Family-violence court programs are added to the specialty-court category whose grant applications are evaluated; inclusion does not guarantee funding.

major_effects.label: Dismissal and expunction after program completion
major_effects.explanation: A participant who was not convicted or placed on deferred adjudication may receive a case dismissal after successful completion if the family-violence court finds dismissal is in the interest of justice; expunction remains subject to the stated process and state-attorney consent.

major_effects.label: Criminal-history nondisclosure
major_effects.explanation: Some program graduates may petition on or after the second anniversary of completion, subject to specified criminal-history limits and a court determination that an order is in the best interest of justice.

agencies.name: Specialty Courts Advisory Council
agencies.explanation: The Council's grant-review and best-practices scope is expanded to include family-violence court programs.

agencies.name: Governor’s Criminal Justice Division
agencies.explanation: Family-violence court programs enter the specialty-court grant-review framework, under which funding recommendations are made to this division.

HB586.summary: The bill would require medical directors subject to Section 242.151(a)(2) to hold a specified medical director certification or an equivalent set by commission rule, and to complete a commission-developed course on legal compliance, quality improvement, infection control, and resident care management. An institution in a medically underserved rural area would be excused from the certification requirement if it makes a good-faith effort but cannot recruit a compliant medical director. These requirements would apply only to medical directors hired on or after March 1, 2028; the executive commissioner must adopt implementing rules and develop the course by January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes certification and training qualifications for medical directors at covered care institutions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to covered institutions under Texas law, subject to the rural-area exception.

locations.name: Medically underserved rural area
locations.explanation: Institutions in this area may use the recruitment exception if they make a good-faith effort but cannot recruit a compliant medical director; the commission defines the area by rule.

affected_groups.group: Medical directors hired on or after March 1, 2028, at covered institutions
affected_groups.explanation: They would be subject to the certification and training requirements; directors hired earlier remain governed by prior law.

affected_groups.group: Institutions subject to Section 242.151, Health and Safety Code
affected_groups.explanation: They must have a qualifying medical director, except that an institution in a medically underserved rural area may use the stated exception when unable to recruit one despite a good-faith effort.

major_effects.label: Medical director certification and training requirements
