major_effects.explanation: Covered medical directors hired on or after March 1, 2028, must meet the certification and course requirements, subject to the rural-area exception for institutions unable to recruit a compliant director despite a good-faith effort.

major_effects.label: Medical director training course
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must develop the required course, covering the specified operational and care-management topics.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules and determinations
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must adopt implementing rules; for medical directors subject to Section 242.151(a)(2), commission rules will determine equivalent certification and define the medically underserved rural area.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is assigned duties to adopt implementing rules and develop the required medical director training course.

HB587.summary: The bill would prohibit construction of specified industrial or offensive land-use facilities in a county’s unincorporated area unless the person first obtains a permit from the county commissioners court. Counties would establish a review process with at least two public hearings, consider community and environmental impacts, and could impose mitigation conditions or suspend or revoke a permit in specified circumstances.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates county permitting, review, and enforcement authority over covered facilities in unincorporated areas.
Requires covered facility constructors to obtain a county permit and allows permit conditions.
Requires counties to consider air, water, and soil impacts and authorizes permit conditions to mitigate them.
Requires consideration of public health and safety and allows conditions for safety measures and emergency-service support.
Includes electric generation, wind, solar, and battery storage facilities among facilities potentially subject to county permits.
Specifically includes data centers among industrial facilities subject to the new county permit requirement.

locations.name: Unincorporated areas of counties
locations.explanation: The permit requirement applies to covered facilities proposed for construction in a county’s unincorporated area.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Must establish the permitting procedure and conduct facility permit reviews; they may impose conditions and enforce permits.

affected_groups.group: Persons proposing covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: A person may not construct a covered facility in a county’s unincorporated area unless the person first obtains a permit from that county’s commissioners court.

affected_groups.group: County residents and other stakeholders
affected_groups.explanation: Their comments and input must be considered in permit decisions, which also require public hearings.

major_effects.label: County facility permitting
major_effects.explanation: Requires county commissioners courts to create a permit review process, hold at least two public hearings, and decide covered construction applications.

major_effects.label: Permit conditions and oversight
major_effects.explanation: Permits may include conditions to mitigate negative effects; a county may suspend or revoke a permit for violations or undue harm to the surrounding area or community.

HB588.summary: Creates a grant program for Texas hospitals and health care facilities to use artificial intelligence to scan medical images for cancer, with grants capped at $250,000 and limited to no more than five qualified applicants. Applicants must provide matching funds and a physician-review plan; recipients must report outcomes, and the program expires September 1, 2037.

policy_tags.explanation: Establishes grants supporting AI-assisted cancer detection in medical imaging.
Creates a grant program specifically to support use of artificial intelligence technology in cancer detection; the bill does not otherwise establish privacy rules.
Authorizes grant awards and permits use of a portion of money appropriated to the commission for program administration.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The grant program is for qualified applicants located in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Hospitals and health care facilities providing medical imaging services, including federally qualified health centers
affected_groups.explanation: These Texas facilities may apply for grants to support AI cancer detection.

affected_groups.group: Physicians reviewing AI-identified cancer results
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants must plan for a physician to review each result identified as a cancer case through AI.

major_effects.label: AI cancer-detection grant program
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to establish and administer a grant program for qualified medical imaging providers.

major_effects.label: Grant limits and matching funds
major_effects.explanation: Grant awards are capped at $250,000, may not be awarded to more than five qualified applicants, and applications must show matching funds of at least 10 percent of the award.

major_effects.label: Recipient outcome reports
major_effects.explanation: Grant recipients must report on images scanned, cancer cases identified, detection outcomes, comparative effectiveness, and recommendations. Reporting does not itself require use of the technology beyond the grant program.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the executive commissioner to adopt rules necessary to implement the chapter.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission responsibility for establishing and administering the grant program, processing applications, and receiving recipient reports. The executive commissioner is assigned rulemaking; the bill text alone does not verify the commission's canonical identity.

HB589.summary: HB 589 would apply a new definition of “dispatchable” throughout Utilities Code Chapter 34, including treating facilities that use petroleum, natural gas, coal, geothermal, hydroelectric, or nuclear energy as dispatchable. This could expand which facilities serving the ERCOT power region qualify for Texas energy fund loans or construction completion grants; the existing 100-megawatt loan thresholds and exclusions for electric energy storage facilities would remain.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which electric generating facilities may qualify for financing through the Texas energy fund.
Changes eligibility for loans and grants from an existing state fund; it does not appropriate new funds.

locations.name: ERCOT power region
locations.explanation: The loan and grant provisions concern facilities providing power for, or constructed in, the ERCOT power region.

affected_groups.group: Applicants seeking Texas energy fund loans or completion bonus grants for electric generating facilities serving ERCOT
affected_groups.explanation: Facilities classified as dispatchable under the expanded definition could qualify, subject to the applicable existing loan or grant conditions.

major_effects.label: Expands which facilities may qualify for energy fund financing
major_effects.explanation: Facilities using the listed primary energy sources would be considered dispatchable for Chapter 34, potentially qualifying for loans or construction completion grants. Existing 100-megawatt loan thresholds and the exclusions for electric energy storage facilities remain.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission a role in providing fund loans and completion bonus grants, but does not identify it by formal name.

HB590.summary: Beginning with the 2028–2029 school year, school districts and open-enrollment charter schools may offer a mindfulness elective to middle school, junior high school, and high school students. The course must cover specified techniques, and a high school version must qualify for elective credit under existing law.

policy_tags.explanation: Authorizes an optional school elective and specifies its instructional content.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The authorization applies to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools under Texas law, with no narrower geographic limit stated.

affected_groups.group: Middle school, junior high school, and high school students
affected_groups.explanation: May be offered the elective; high school students receive elective credit only if the course meets existing credit requirements.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: May choose whether to offer the course.

major_effects.label: Optional mindfulness elective
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes districts and open-enrollment charter schools to offer the elective; it does not require them to do so.

major_effects.label: Course content and credit requirements
major_effects.explanation: Any course offered must teach techniques addressing focus, stress, emotional regulation, self-awareness, and compassion; the high school course must meet existing elective-credit requirements.

HB591.summary: HB 591 would require school districts to adopt a policy allowing certain classroom teachers with limited service at their current district to take up to 12 weeks of parental leave, if they meet service and work-hour requirements across Texas districts. Leave would be limited to the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child; teachers must first use available applicable paid vacation and sick leave, and the remainder is unpaid. The changes apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires school districts to adopt a parental-leave policy for classroom teachers.
Establishes parental-leave eligibility and conditions for classroom teachers employed by school districts.
Imposes a policy-adoption duty on school district boards of trustees.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The policy concerns school districts in Texas and recognizes qualifying classroom-teacher service with any district in the state.

affected_groups.group: Classroom teachers employed by Texas school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Certain teachers may qualify for up to 12 weeks of parental leave based on their service and work hours across districts.

affected_groups.group: Texas school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Each district's board of trustees must adopt a policy providing the specified leave eligibility.

major_effects.label: Parental leave for qualifying teachers
major_effects.explanation: Requires district policies to allow eligible teachers up to 12 weeks of leave for a child's birth, adoption, or foster placement. Teachers must first use available applicable paid vacation and sick leave; any remaining leave is unpaid.

HB593.summary: HB 593 would require the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to arrange translation into Arabic, Hindi, Mandarin, Tagalog, and Urdu of information in its public online complaint-file system and the form used to submit complaints online. The requirement applies to complaint-file information and the online submission form identified in Water Code Section 5.176.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes access to the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality's complaint-file information and online complaint submission form.

affected_groups.group: Users of the online complaint system who use Arabic, Hindi, Mandarin, Tagalog, or Urdu
affected_groups.explanation: The bill would make specified complaint-file information and the online submission form available in these languages.

major_effects.label: Translation of online complaint materials
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to provide translations of specified online complaint-file information and the complaint submission form in five languages.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill identifies the commission as the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and assigns it the translation duty.

HB594.summary: The bill would require each school district, open-enrollment charter school, and private school to adopt and implement a policy regarding respiratory-distress medication at each campus. The policy must require the school or district to maintain and make available a supply of the medication at each campus, and require each campus to have school personnel or volunteers authorized and trained to administer it present during regular school hours. Schools must provide parents or guardians written notice of each policy implemented under the subchapter.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires each school district, open-enrollment charter school, and private school to adopt and implement a campus policy on maintaining, administering, and disposing of medication for respiratory distress, and to provide parents or guardians written notice of policies implemented under the subchapter.
Requires schools to maintain and make available medication for respiratory distress and provide for its administration.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to school districts, open-enrollment charter schools, and private schools across the state.

affected_groups.group: School districts, open-enrollment charter schools, and private schools
affected_groups.explanation: Must adopt and implement policies and maintain medication at each campus.

affected_groups.group: School personnel and school volunteers
affected_groups.explanation: May administer medication if authorized and trained, and are subject to school training duties.

affected_groups.group: Students and their parents or guardians
affected_groups.explanation: People experiencing respiratory distress may receive medication under the policy, and parents or guardians of enrolled students must receive written notice of policies.

major_effects.label: Mandatory school medication policies and campus coverage
major_effects.explanation: Requires a policy and available medication at each campus, provides for administration by authorized and trained personnel or volunteers, and requires trained coverage during regular school hours.

major_effects.label: Removes policy-based condition on respiratory-medication rules
major_effects.explanation: Removes the former condition that respiratory-medication rules apply only at campuses subject to a policy; the bill separately makes school policies mandatory.

major_effects.label: Parent and guardian notice
major_effects.explanation: Requires written notice of each policy implemented under the subchapter to a parent or guardian of each enrolled student.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner must adopt rules on epinephrine delivery systems at campuses subject to a policy under Subsection (a). The bill deletes the parallel condition for rules on respiratory-distress medication.

agencies.name: commissioner of education
agencies.explanation: The bill requires this office to be consulted on the rules, but does not identify its agency affiliation.

HB595.summary: HB 595 would require the Public Utility Commission of Texas to study the costs, potential savings, and technologies associated with burying existing overhead power lines within 150 miles of the Gulf of Mexico, and to evaluate the potential benefits of an environmental feasibility study. The commission would report its results and any recommendations to the governor and legislative leaders by September 1, 2028; the Act expires October 31, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires a state utility regulator to study the costs, savings, and technology involved in burying power lines.

locations.name: Study area: within 150 miles of the Gulf of Mexico coast in Texas
locations.explanation: The bill defines the geographic area covered by the required study.

affected_groups.group: Electricity customers in the defined study area
affected_groups.explanation: The study considers potential reductions in weather-related outages affecting the area; it does not itself require power lines to be buried or create a customer entitlement.

major_effects.label: PUC study and report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to evaluate specified costs, savings, technologies, and the potential benefits of an environmental feasibility study, then report results and recommendations. It does not itself require undergrounding power lines.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The Act defines the commission as the Public Utility Commission of Texas and assigns it the study and reporting duties.

HB596.summary: The bill repeals the exception that let students satisfy the foundation high school program’s foreign-language credit requirement with computer programming language credits. The revised requirement applies to students entering ninth grade in the 2027–2028 school year or later; students entering a grade above ninth grade that year remain under the prior law, and exceptions under Subsections (b-13) and (b-14) remain.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the language-credit requirement in the foundation high school program.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The curriculum requirement is assigned to the State Board of Education for the foundation high school program, with no locality limitation.

affected_groups.group: Public school students entering ninth grade in the 2027–2028 school year or later
affected_groups.explanation: These students are subject to the amended language-credit requirement.

affected_groups.group: Students entering a grade above ninth grade during the 2027–2028 school year
affected_groups.explanation: These students remain subject to the prior version of the law.

major_effects.label: Foreign-language credit requirement
major_effects.explanation: Removes the computer-programming-language exception from the two-credit requirement for the same language other than English, while retaining the exceptions in Subsections (b-13) and (b-14). The change applies to the specified incoming ninth-grade cohorts.

agencies.name: State Board of Education
agencies.explanation: The bill changes a curriculum requirement that the State Board of Education must require by rule, including two credits in the same language, except as provided under Subsections (b-13) and (b-14).

HB597.summary: The bill adds procedures for Attorney General examinations of filing entities: requests must be written and state their legal or governing-document basis, entities must be given a reasonable time to respond, and inspections must minimize interference with operations. An entity may petition a district court within 45 days to extend, modify, or set aside a request; the response deadline is suspended while that petition is pending, and forfeiture of business privileges or an offense for noncompliance is subject to these procedures.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the procedures and protections governing state examinations of filing entities and foreign filing entities.
Sets requirements for how the Attorney General requests and conducts records examinations.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The provisions govern examinations under state law and refer to an entity's right to do business in this state.

locations.name: Travis County
locations.explanation: A district court in Travis County is one venue option for a petition challenging or seeking an extension of a request.

locations.name: County where the parties reside
locations.explanation: A district court in the county where the parties reside is an alternative venue for the petition.

affected_groups.group: Filing entities and foreign filing entities
affected_groups.explanation: These entities receive procedural protections and may petition a district court concerning an Attorney General records request.

affected_groups.group: Managerial officials and other individuals authorized to manage entity affairs
affected_groups.explanation: The bill makes the existing offense for refusing an examination subject to the new request procedures.

major_effects.label: Requirements for Attorney General examinations
major_effects.explanation: The Attorney General must make a written request, state its legal or governing-document basis, allow a reasonable response time, and conduct the examination to minimize interference with the entity's operation.

major_effects.label: Judicial review of requests
major_effects.explanation: An entity may seek an extension, modification, or setting aside of a request for good cause; filing the petition suspends the response deadline while the court considers it.

major_effects.label: Noncompliance consequences subject to new procedures
major_effects.explanation: Forfeiture of the right to do business and the related offense for refusing an examination are made subject to Section 12.152's request procedures.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill directly changes the Attorney General's procedures and constraints when requesting and conducting examinations of entity records.

HB599.summary: HB 599 would establish a program to connect students and recent graduates with career opportunities in state agencies. The commission would partner with higher education institutions, educate students about state careers and benefits, coordinate agency workforce needs, and refer candidates to opportunities, including internships that may lead to full-time jobs.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a state workforce pathways program to connect students and recent graduates with state employment opportunities.
Creates a program for state-agency workforce recruitment and coordination.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The program is directed to students in this state and career opportunities with state agencies.

affected_groups.group: Students and recent graduates of institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: They are the intended participants and potential referrals for state career opportunities.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: The commission would establish program partnerships with these institutions.

affected_groups.group: State agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Their workforce needs would be identified through the program's coordination with the commission.

major_effects.label: State employee pathways program
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a program to promote state careers, identify agency workforce needs, and refer students and recent graduates to opportunities, including internships that may lead to full-time placement.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to adopt rules necessary to implement the program.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission responsibility for establishing and administering the program and adopting implementing rules, but the supplied text does not identify which commission this means.

agencies.name: State agencies defined by Government Code § 651.007, excluding institutions of higher education
agencies.explanation: The definition includes boards, commissions, councils, committees, departments, offices, agencies, and other governmental entities in the executive, legislative, or judicial branch of state government, but excludes institutions of higher education. The bill directs the commission to coordinate with these agencies to determine workforce needs; it does not expressly impose a separate duty on each agency.

HB601.summary: HB 601 would require the Public Utility Commission of Texas to study the potential costs and savings of burying existing overhead power lines within 150 miles of the Gulf of Mexico coast, including the use of specified federal-program technologies. The commission would submit the study results and any recommendations to state leaders by September 1, 2028; the study does not itself require power lines to be buried, and the Act would expire October 31, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a study of undergrounding electric power lines and related costs, outage savings, and technology.

locations.name: Study area: the area within 150 miles of the Gulf of Mexico coast
locations.explanation: The bill defines the geographic area covered by the study.

major_effects.label: Power-line undergrounding study and report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to assess potential undergrounding costs, maintenance and repair costs, outage-related savings, and use of specified technologies, then report results and any recommendations. It does not require undergrounding.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The Act defines the commission as the Public Utility Commission of Texas and assigns it the study and reporting duties.

HB602.summary: The bill would let governing bodies of specified facilities adopt a policy allowing a physician to temporarily detain a person who wants to leave before treatment is complete, if the person meets the stated mental-illness and serious-risk criteria and there is not enough time to seek formal emergency detention or a protective-custody order. The policy would require notice and documentation, and the person must be released within four hours unless a peace officer takes custody or a judge or magistrate issues a protective-custody order; the bill would also authorize peace officers to take into custody people admitted to listed facilities and protect good-faith, nonmalicious detention decisions from civil or criminal liability.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes temporary detention authority and procedures for people receiving or seeking care at specified mental-health, hospital, and emergency-care facilities.
Changes peace-officer custody authority and permits limited detention when the physician believes there is a serious risk of harm.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and sets rules for covered facilities and peace officers without limiting them to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: People with mental illness seeking or receiving treatment at covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: They may be temporarily detained under a facility policy if the bill's conditions are met, with notice and a four-hour limit unless custody or a protective-custody order follows.

affected_groups.group: Physicians, facility staff, and governing bodies of covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Governing bodies may adopt the detention policy, while physicians and staff would be subject to its notice, documentation, and release procedures.

affected_groups.group: Peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: They may take into custody a patient admitted to a facility listed in the new section.

major_effects.label: Facility physician temporary-detention authority
major_effects.explanation: A covered facility may adopt a policy allowing a physician to detain a person who seeks to leave before care is complete, only when the stated mental-illness, risk, and timing conditions are met.

major_effects.label: Notice, documentation, and time-limited detention
major_effects.explanation: A policy must provide notice and medical-record documentation and require release within four hours unless peace-officer custody or a protective-custody order intervenes.

major_effects.label: Peace-officer custody of admitted patients
major_effects.explanation: A peace officer may take into custody under the existing section a person admitted as a patient to a facility listed in the new section.

major_effects.label: Good-faith liability protection
major_effects.explanation: Physicians, facility staff, and facilities acting in good faith and without malice are protected from civil or criminal liability for detaining or not detaining under a policy; facilities are also protected regarding the decision to adopt or not adopt one.

HB603.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, the bill would allow school districts to adopt local policies addressing eloping by students with autism or another intellectual or developmental disability. Such policies would emphasize behavioral supports, staff training and nonpunitive responses; they could not treat eloping as intentionally fleeing for an unlawful purpose, and districts could collaborate with law enforcement and emergency services on safe recovery protocols.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill authorizes public school districts to adopt policies concerning student supports, staff training, and responses to eloping.
The bill gives school districts, as local public entities, discretion to adopt and implement a local policy.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The authorization applies to school districts under the statewide Education Code, beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

affected_groups.group: Students with autism or another intellectual or developmental disability who elope
affected_groups.explanation: They are the students whose eloping behavior the authorized policies would address.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts may adopt and implement the local policies and may collaborate on recovery protocols.

affected_groups.group: School staff
affected_groups.explanation: Policies may emphasize training on causes of eloping, de-escalation, and safety measures.

major_effects.label: Optional district policy authority
major_effects.explanation: Districts may adopt policies emphasizing behavioral supports and staff training, and may collaborate with law enforcement and emergency services on safe recovery protocols.

major_effects.label: Limits on adopted policies
major_effects.explanation: A district policy adopted under this section may not classify eloping as intentional flight for an unlawful purpose and is to emphasize nonpunitive treatment of incidents.

HB604.summary: HB 604 would establish a temporary advisory committee under the Health and Human Services Commission to study access to, funding for, quality of, and workforce capacity for services and supports for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities, and to recommend improvements to the Legislature. The committee would issue biennial reports; the commission would report by December 1, 2030, on whether it should continue, and the committee and subchapter would expire September 1, 2031.

policy_tags.explanation: The committee would study gaps in access to acute and long-term care services and supports for people with intellectual or developmental disabilities.
The bill creates a state advisory committee and assigns it study and reporting duties.
Committee members would be entitled to reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses, and the commission would provide administrative support using existing resources.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The committee's review includes services and supports provided in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities who receive services or supports
affected_groups.explanation: Their service access, needs, and the quality of available supports are central subjects of the committee's study and recommendations.

affected_groups.group: Disability services providers, professionals, caregivers, and managed care organizations
affected_groups.explanation: These stakeholders are included in committee membership, and the study would examine workforce capacity and service delivery models.

affected_groups.group: Local intellectual and developmental disability authorities
affected_groups.explanation: Their representatives would be included on the committee, which would evaluate their role and capacity in coordinating services.

major_effects.label: Temporary disability services advisory committee
major_effects.explanation: The commission would establish a committee to study access gaps and make recommendations to the Legislature.

major_effects.label: Study and recurring reports
major_effects.explanation: The committee would evaluate service, funding, workforce, and program issues and submit biennial findings and recommendations; the commission would separately recommend whether the committee should continue by December 1, 2030.

major_effects.label: Limited committee expense support
major_effects.explanation: Members would not receive compensation but would be entitled to reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses; the commission's administrative support would use existing resources.

major_effects.label: Sunset
major_effects.explanation: The committee and the subchapter would expire September 1, 2031.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission must establish and support the committee; its executive commissioner appoints members, and the commission must submit a report on whether the committee should continue.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The committee's required membership includes Department of State Health Services representatives; the bill does not separately assign the department a duty.

HB606.summary: The bill would make it a Class A misdemeanor for a person younger than 21 to knowingly purchase or possess a firearm. It would also make knowingly transferring a firearm to someone younger than 21 an offense; the offense would be a state jail felony if the firearm is a handgun.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill restricts firearm purchase, possession, and transfer by age.
The bill creates criminal liability and sets misdemeanor and felony classifications.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Penal Code and establishes generally applicable state criminal law.

affected_groups.group: People younger than 21
affected_groups.explanation: They would be prohibited from knowingly purchasing or possessing firearms and would be protected from firearm transfers under the amended transfer offense.

affected_groups.group: People who sell, rent, lease, give, or otherwise transfer firearms
affected_groups.explanation: They could face criminal liability for knowingly transferring a firearm to a person younger than 21; transfer of a handgun carries a state jail felony classification.

major_effects.label: Under-21 firearm purchase or possession offense
major_effects.explanation: Knowingly purchasing or possessing a firearm while younger than 21 would be a Class A misdemeanor.

major_effects.label: Criminal penalties for firearm transfers to people under 21
major_effects.explanation: Knowingly transferring a firearm to someone younger than 21 would be an offense; it is a state jail felony if the firearm is a handgun.

HB607.summary: The bill would revise law-enforcement diversion and criminal-court procedures for people experiencing mental health crises or substance-use issues, and for defendants who may be incompetent to stand trial. It would change competency-restoration and release pathways, create additional mental health court options, and expand procedures for court-ordered medication and release from residential care.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes criminal-case diversion, competency determinations and restoration, release, and dismissal procedures.
Changes procedures for mental-health treatment, competency-restoration services, and court authorization of psychoactive medication.
Assigns reporting and program responsibilities to local law-enforcement agencies and counties, and makes counties responsible for specified hearing costs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply across Texas, including the reporting requirement for each local law-enforcement agency in the state.

affected_groups.group: Defendants with mental illness, intellectual or developmental disability, or substance-use issues
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes diversion, competency, treatment, and release procedures that apply to these defendants.

affected_groups.group: Local law-enforcement agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Agencies must adopt diversion plans and submit annual reports to local governing bodies and the state commission.

affected_groups.group: Counties and municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Local governments receive diversion reports; counties also have mental health court program and specified cost responsibilities.

affected_groups.group: Primary care providers
affected_groups.explanation: A treating primary care provider may apply on behalf of the state for an order authorizing psychoactive medication despite a patient's refusal when the provider believes the patient lacks capacity to decide about the medication.

major_effects.label: Diversion plans and annual reports
major_effects.explanation: Local law-enforcement agencies would adopt diversion plans and report annually, including plan changes, to the governing bodies of served counties or municipalities and to the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement.

major_effects.label: Dismissal based on lack of capacity
major_effects.explanation: On a motion or on the court's own motion, a judge or justice would determine whether probable cause supports a finding that a defendant lacks capacity and is unfit to proceed; after notice to the state, the court may dismiss the complaint.

major_effects.label: Competency-restoration and release pathways
major_effects.explanation: The bill ties restoration procedures to the authorized restoration period and broadens the lower-offense bail and outpatient pathway to certain Class A misdemeanors without bodily injury, provided the defendant has no qualifying bodily-injury conviction in the preceding two years. If an outpatient program is unavailable or timely placement cannot be made, dismissal and proceedings under Subchapter F are available only through the specified motion and court procedures.

major_effects.label: Reassessment when proceedings are delayed
major_effects.explanation: If criminal proceedings do not resume within the specified period after a competency finding, a party may move to raise competency again, and the court may do so on its own motion if it suspects the defendant may no longer be competent.

major_effects.label: Residential-care release and community living plans
major_effects.explanation: For defendants committed to residential care, the court would consider release requests and may require a community-based living plan if the statutory findings about placement and available services are met. If a plan is ordered, the court designates the local intellectual and developmental disability authority to supervise it.

major_effects.label: Expanded county mental health court programs
major_effects.explanation: Counties may establish programs for persons subject to court-ordered outpatient mental health services under Chapter 574, Health and Safety Code, including assisted outpatient treatment court programs; counties with populations over 200,000 must establish a program under criminal-court supervision.

major_effects.label: Medication-order applications by primary care providers
major_effects.explanation: A treating primary care provider, as defined in the bill, may apply for a court order authorizing psychoactive medication for a patient who meets the stated conditions, including refusal to take the medication voluntarily.

major_effects.label: County payment of specified hearing costs
major_effects.explanation: The county where criminal charges are pending or were adjudicated would pay specified costs for a medication hearing for a person under criminal-court jurisdiction.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Law Enforcement
agencies.explanation: The bill makes the commission a recipient of annual reports from local law-enforcement agencies.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The bill refers to a commission in connection with designated facilities and transportation reimbursements, but does not identify it by name.

HB608.summary: The bill would require specified health benefit plans—including Medicaid and certain school-district and county plans—that cover inpatient physical therapy to cover medically necessary services to maintain function, prevent or slow its loss, or reduce secondary health risks. It would also bar denial solely because improvement is not expected and expand the statutory definition and scope of physical therapy; the insurance changes would apply to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates physical-therapy coverage requirements and broadens the statutory definition and practice of physical therapy.
Expressly includes the state Medicaid and Medicaid managed care programs within the chapter's applicability.
The coverage mandate applies to group health coverage made available by school districts.
The mandate applies to county employee group health benefits and health and accident coverage provided by local-government risk pools.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds requirements to the Texas Insurance Code and Occupations Code for the specified plans and physical-therapy practice.

affected_groups.group: People enrolled in covered health benefit plans who need physical therapy
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive medically necessary therapy to maintain function, prevent or slow functional decline, or reduce secondary health risks, even when improvement is not expected.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plan issuers and sponsors
affected_groups.explanation: Plans within the chapter's scope would have to provide the required coverage when they cover inpatient physical therapy.

affected_groups.group: Physical therapists
affected_groups.explanation: The bill expands the statutory definition of physical therapy and the described scope of practice to include maintaining function and slowing functional decline.

major_effects.label: Expanded physical-therapy coverage
major_effects.explanation: Specified plans that cover inpatient physical therapy would also cover medically necessary services for maintaining function, preventing or slowing decline, or reducing secondary risks; issuers could not deny required coverage solely because improvement is not expected.

major_effects.label: Broader definition and practice of physical therapy
major_effects.explanation: Adds maintenance of existing function and slowing the progress of dysfunction or disability to the statutory definition and practice of physical therapy.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: Inferred because the bill expressly subjects state Medicaid, including managed care, to the coverage requirements; the bill does not name the agency responsible for administering those provisions.

HB609.summary: The bill would make every offense under Penal Code Section 46.13 a Class A misdemeanor, replacing the Class C classification and removing the subsection (e) qualification. The change would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act’s effective date; earlier offenses would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill increases the criminal classification for the offense.
The increased penalty concerns making a firearm accessible to a child.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Texas Penal Code, with no narrower geographic area specified.

affected_groups.group: People who commit the offense of making a firearm accessible to a child
affected_groups.explanation: They would face a Class A misdemeanor classification for offenses committed on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Increases offense classification
major_effects.explanation: Changes the offense classification from Class C to Class A and repeals subsection (e); the change applies only to offenses committed on or after the effective date.

HB610.summary: The bill would make it an offense to intentionally or knowingly sell, rent, lease, give, or offer to sell, rent, lease, or give a firearm to someone younger than 21, while retaining the under-18 restriction for clubs and location-restricted knives. The parental-consent affirmative defense would apply only to that latter category; firearm-transfer offenses would generally be Class A misdemeanors, but the offense would be a state jail felony if the firearm is a handgun.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill restricts intentional or knowing firearm transfers and offers to people younger than 21.
The bill establishes an offense and specifies misdemeanor and felony punishment for violations.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a Texas Penal Code offense, establishing a state-level rule rather than a place-specific one.

affected_groups.group: People younger than 21
affected_groups.explanation: The bill addresses firearm transfers to this age group.

affected_groups.group: People who sell, rent, lease, give, or offer firearms
affected_groups.explanation: These actions can constitute the new offense when the recipient is younger than 21 and the actor acts intentionally or knowingly.

affected_groups.group: Children younger than 18 and their parents or legal custodians
affected_groups.explanation: The bill retains a restriction on transfers of clubs and location-restricted knives to children under 18 and limits the related affirmative defense to that category.

major_effects.label: Firearm transfers to people under 21
major_effects.explanation: Intentionally or knowingly selling, renting, leasing, giving, or offering to sell, rent, lease, or give a firearm to a person younger than 21 would be an offense.

major_effects.label: Misdemeanor and felony punishment
major_effects.explanation: The offense is generally a Class A misdemeanor; the under-21 firearm offense is a state jail felony when the firearm is a handgun.

major_effects.label: Affirmative defense limited to under-18 category
major_effects.explanation: The parental-consent affirmative defense is tied to transfers under subsection (a)(2)(A), not the new firearm offense under subsection (a)(2)(B).

HB611.summary: HB 611 would establish an Office of Defender General, funded through legislative appropriations and the fair defense account, with administrative support and staffing provided through the Office of Capital and Forensic Writs. The new office could represent appellants in criminal appellate proceedings, participate as amicus curiae, and decline specified appointments for stated reasons.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a state office and establishes its administrative arrangement, leadership, and staffing.
Provides for appropriated funds and fair defense account funds to cover the new office's personnel costs and expenses.
Authorizes representation and amicus participation in criminal appellate matters and permits declining certain criminal-defense appointments for specified reasons.

locations.name: Texas (statewide)
locations.explanation: The bill creates a state office and concerns criminal appellate representation before the Court of Criminal Appeals; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: Appellants in criminal cases
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive representation from the new office in specified appellate matters, subject to the office's authority to decline appointments in stated circumstances.

affected_groups.group: Criminal-law attorneys and other personnel
affected_groups.explanation: The bill provides for hiring attorneys and other personnel, and requires office attorneys to have at least five years of criminal-law practice experience in Texas.

major_effects.label: Creates the Office of Defender General
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a new office with appellate representation and amicus functions.

major_effects.label: Provides funding for the new office
major_effects.explanation: The office is to receive appropriations and fair defense account funds for personnel costs and expenses not covered by those appropriations.

major_effects.label: Authorizes criminal appellate representation
major_effects.explanation: Allows the office to represent appellants in specified appellate matters and to decline covered appointments for conflicts, insufficient resources, professional-conduct limitations, or other good cause.

agencies.name: Office of Defender General
agencies.explanation: The bill creates the office, assigns it appellate representation and amicus functions, and provides for its funding. No matching canonical registry entry is supplied.

agencies.name: Office of Capital and Forensic Writs
agencies.explanation: Section 78.001 defines the Office of Capital and Forensic Writs as the office established under Subchapter B. The bill assigns it administrative-support and supervisory-hiring duties, but the supplied evidence does not identify it with a canonical registry entity.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals is named as a forum in which the new office may represent appellants and participate as amicus; the bill does not assign the court a new duty.

HB612.summary: HB 612 would prohibit a person required to register under Chapter 62 from possessing a firearm when the registration requirement is based on an offense committed on or after September 1, 2027. It would also require pre-release officials to notify people of the prohibition and local law enforcement authorities to include it in registration-verification materials; people required to register solely because of a pre-effective-date conviction or adjudication remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds a firearm-possession restriction to the sex-offender registration requirements in the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The new restriction bars specified registrants from possessing firearms.
Local law enforcement authorities must include the prohibition in registration-verification forms they provide.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Chapter 62 registration requirements without limiting them to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: People required to register under Chapter 62 based on a qualifying offense
affected_groups.explanation: Those whose registration is based on an offense committed on or after the effective date would be subject to the firearm prohibition; the bill preserves prior law for the specified pre-effective-date cases.

affected_groups.group: Local law enforcement authorities
affected_groups.explanation: Authorities providing registration-verification forms must add a statement describing the new prohibition.

affected_groups.group: Officials of penal institutions
affected_groups.explanation: Before release, officials must inform covered people about the firearm prohibition.

major_effects.label: Firearm-possession prohibition
major_effects.explanation: Bars covered Chapter 62 registrants from possessing a firearm. The prohibition applies to registration based on an offense committed on or after the effective date; the bill continues prior law for people required to register solely on the basis of a pre-effective-date conviction or adjudication.

major_effects.label: Notice of the prohibition
major_effects.explanation: Adds pre-release notice to the information given to covered people and requires local authorities to describe the prohibition in registration-verification forms.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: The pre-release duties apply before the release of a person who will be subject to registration under this chapter. The new notice is assigned to an official of the penal institution, and the bill does not specify which institutions' officials must provide it.

agencies.name: Texas Juvenile Justice Department
agencies.explanation: The pre-release duties apply before the release of a person who will be subject to registration under this chapter. The new notice is assigned to an official of the penal institution, and the bill does not specify which institutions' officials must provide it.

HB613.summary: HB 613 would allow a licensed firearms dealer to transfer a firearm without the bill’s new conditions; a nondealer could transfer one to a licensed dealer or, before delivery to another recipient, request a national instant criminal background check through a licensed dealer and verify that the recipient may lawfully possess a firearm. A dealer receiving a check request would have to conduct the check and notify the seller of the results, and violating the transfer requirements would be a Class A misdemeanor.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill makes firearm transfers subject to a background check and verification that the recipient may lawfully possess a firearm.
The bill creates a criminal offense for violating its firearm-transfer requirements.
The bill regulates conditions for private firearm transfers and assigns duties to licensed firearms dealers responding to background-check requests.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The proposed requirements apply under the Texas Business & Commerce Code without a narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: People who sell or transfer firearms without being licensed firearms dealers
affected_groups.explanation: They would have to meet the bill’s transfer conditions, including requesting a check and verifying lawful possession when transferring to a recipient rather than a dealer.

affected_groups.group: People receiving firearms through covered transfers
affected_groups.explanation: Their eligibility to lawfully possess a firearm would be checked as part of a covered transfer.

affected_groups.group: Licensed firearms dealers
affected_groups.explanation: Dealers receiving a check request would have to conduct the background check and notify the seller of its results; they may charge a reasonable fee.

major_effects.label: Conditions on nondealer firearm transfers
major_effects.explanation: A nondealer may transfer a firearm to a licensed dealer, or to another recipient only after requesting a dealer-conducted national instant criminal background check and verifying lawful possession.

major_effects.label: Dealer background-check duties
major_effects.explanation: A licensed dealer receiving a request must conduct the check and notify the seller of its results; the dealer may collect a reasonable fee.

major_effects.label: Class A misdemeanor
major_effects.explanation: A person who violates the proposed transfer requirements would commit a Class A misdemeanor.

HB614.summary: Only if voters approve the specified 2027 constitutional amendment, HB 614 would change certain transfer adjustments among the State Highway Fund, Economic Stabilization Fund (ESF), and Grow Texas Fund when projected amounts fall below the statutory threshold. It would also allow the Legislature to appropriate Grow Texas Fund money for grants to build or maintain roads, schools, health care facilities, and other infrastructure in areas significantly affected by oil and gas production. The bill repeals Government Code Section 316.092(b), which provides that Section 316.092 expires December 31, 2042; removing that sunset would allow the subsection (a) threshold calculation—7 percent of certified general revenue-related appropriations—to continue beyond that date. If voters do not approve the amendment, the bill would have no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how specified constitutional transfers are adjusted and authorizes legislative appropriations from the Grow Texas Fund for a grant program.
The transfer adjustment can reduce the amount allocated to the State Highway Fund, and grants may fund road construction or maintenance.
Creates an infrastructure grant program targeted to areas the commission identifies as significantly affected by oil and gas production.

locations.name: Areas of Texas determined by the commission to be significantly affected by oil and gas production
locations.explanation: The grant program is limited to infrastructure in areas selected by the commission under this criterion.

affected_groups.group: Applicants selected for Grow Texas Fund grants
affected_groups.explanation: Selected applicants may receive grants for eligible infrastructure construction or maintenance.

affected_groups.group: Communities in areas significantly affected by oil and gas production
affected_groups.explanation: Those areas may receive infrastructure improvements funded through the grant program.

major_effects.label: Adjusts specified constitutional transfers
major_effects.explanation: When the specified sum is below the threshold, the bill changes the shortfall adjustment: the pre-2043 provision proportionately reduces specified highway and Grow Texas-related amounts to increase the ESF allocation, while the provision for biennia beginning on or after September 1, 2043, reduces the ESF-to-Grow Texas transfer and increases the ESF allocation correspondingly. Separately, repealing Section 316.092(b) removes the section’s December 31, 2042 expiration, allowing the subsection (a)

major_effects.label: Creates a Grow Texas infrastructure grant program
major_effects.explanation: The Legislature may appropriate fund money for grants; the commission selects applicants and establishes eligibility and grant guidelines, while the comptroller administers applications, monitoring, and rules.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The comptroller's transfer-adjustment duties are changed, and the comptroller is assigned grant-administration and rulemaking duties.

agencies.name: Grow Texas fund commission
agencies.explanation: The commission is assigned grant-selection and program-design responsibilities; the supplied registry does not identify a canonical registry entry for it.

HB616.summary: The bill adds benzimidazole-opioids, also known as nitazenes, to Penalty Group 1-B; this change applies only to offenses committed on or after the Act's effective date. It replaces “Fentanyl” with “Opioid” in required death-certificate terms when a lethal amount or concentration of a Penalty Group 1-B substance is found and autopsy results are consistent with an opioid overdose; the change applies to deaths occurring on or after the effective date, and earlier deaths discovered on or after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds a class of opioids to a criminal-law penalty group, with the change applying prospectively to offenses.
The bill changes required medical-certification terminology for qualifying deaths.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes with statewide application.

affected_groups.group: People subject to offenses involving benzimidazole-opioids
affected_groups.explanation: These substances are added to Penalty Group 1-B for offenses committed on or after the effective date.

affected_groups.group: Medical certifiers completing qualifying death certificates
affected_groups.explanation: They must use the specified opioid terminology when the listed toxicology and autopsy conditions are met.

major_effects.label: Adds nitazenes to Penalty Group 1-B
major_effects.explanation: Benzimidazole-opioids are added to the group; the change applies only to offenses committed on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Updates death-certificate terminology
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying deaths, certification must use “Opioid Poisoning” or “Opioid Toxicity” rather than the former fentanyl terms. This applies to deaths on or after the effective date and earlier deaths discovered on or after it.

HB617.summary: HB 617 would delete the former “subject to Subsection (c)” qualification to the prohibition on limiting, denying, or reducing coverage based on a health professional’s choice of platform, and repeal Insurance Code §1455.004(c). The repeal applies to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028; earlier plans remain governed by prior law. The bill’s title describes services provided only by synchronous or asynchronous audio, but the supplied text does not state what subsection (c) provides.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes health benefit plan coverage rules for telemedicine, teledentistry, and telehealth services.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Insurance Code provisions and applies to covered health benefit plans under those provisions.

affected_groups.group: Covered patients
affected_groups.explanation: Their plan coverage may be affected by the change to platform-based coverage limits.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plans
affected_groups.explanation: Plans within the provision are subject to the amended coverage rule, with the repeal applying prospectively as specified.

affected_groups.group: Preferred or contracted health professionals
affected_groups.explanation: The platform-choice coverage rule concerns services they deliver to covered patients.

major_effects.label: Platform-based coverage limits
major_effects.explanation: Removes subsection (c) as a qualification to the prohibition on limiting, denying, or reducing coverage based on the professional’s choice of platform; the precise effect of repealing subsection (c) is not shown in the supplied text.

major_effects.label: Prospective application
major_effects.explanation: The repeal applies to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028; plans from before that date remain governed by prior law.

HB618.summary: HB 618 would create an offense for knowingly buying or receiving a detachable magazine while prohibited under state or federal law from possessing the type of firearm for which it is designed. It would restrict sellers from transmitting, using, or preserving information collected incidentally to such a sale for a firearm-related registry or database, with exceptions for specified background-check and crime-information databases; the changes apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a criminal offense involving the purchase or receipt of a magazine by a person prohibited from possessing the corresponding type of firearm.
Adds a restriction concerning magazine transfers to people prohibited from possessing the corresponding type of firearm.
Limits sellers’ use, transmission, and preservation of information collected incidentally to covered sales for firearm-related registries or databases, subject to stated exceptions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Penal Code and establishes no narrower geographic scope.

affected_groups.group: People prohibited from possessing the type of firearm for which a magazine is designed
affected_groups.explanation: Knowingly purchasing or receiving such a magazine would be covered by the new offense.

affected_groups.group: Sellers of magazines
affected_groups.explanation: They would be restricted in transmitting, using, or preserving information collected incidentally to covered sales for firearm-related registries or databases.

major_effects.label: New magazine-purchase and receipt offense
major_effects.explanation: Creates an offense for knowingly purchasing or receiving a magazine when prohibited from possessing the type of firearm for which it is designed.

major_effects.label: Limits on seller information use
major_effects.explanation: Bars covered seller-collected information from being transmitted, used, or preserved for firearm-related registries or databases, while allowing specified database uses.

HB619.summary: The bill would allow a university system governing board to establish and operate a public law school in Cameron County or Hidalgo County, subject to available funding. If more than one system seeks to establish one, the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board would choose which system may proceed; before establishment, it would also prepare a requested feasibility study on steps needed for accreditation.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates authority for a university system to establish a law school and offer customary law degrees.

locations.name: Cameron County
locations.explanation: The law school may be established in this county.

locations.name: Hidalgo County
locations.explanation: The law school may instead be established in this county.

affected_groups.group: University system governing boards
affected_groups.explanation: They may establish and operate a law school, subject to available funding and selection if multiple systems seek to do so.

affected_groups.group: Prospective law students
affected_groups.explanation: If a law school is established, it may offer courses and customary law degrees.

major_effects.label: Conditional authority to establish a law school
major_effects.explanation: A university system governing board may establish and operate a law school in Cameron or Hidalgo County, but only subject to available funding.

major_effects.label: Coordinating Board selection when multiple systems apply
major_effects.explanation: If the Coordinating Board receives notices from more than one governing board, it must determine which board may establish a law school.

major_effects.label: Accreditation feasibility study
major_effects.explanation: Before establishment, a governing board must request a study of the actions needed to obtain accreditation; the Coordinating Board must provide copies to specified recipients.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the Board proposal-selection responsibility if multiple university system governing boards notify it, and requires it to prepare a requested feasibility study before establishment.

agencies.name: governing board of a university system
agencies.explanation: A university system governing board may establish and operate the law school, subject to funding and the Board's selection if multiple systems seek to establish one. The bill does not identify a particular system or governing board.

HB620.summary: The bill directs the Office of Court Administration to develop and periodically review a statewide model citation and addendum for fine-only offenses, with plain-language court information and details about available assistance and options for fines and costs. Law enforcement agencies must adopt conforming forms by September 1, 2029, but may keep issuing citation books they already possess until those books are used up. The forms provide information about relief options; the bill does not itself create eligibility for fine relief.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a standardized citation and addendum for fine-only offenses, including information about court appearances and resolving a citation.
Imposes form-adoption and implementation duties on covered law enforcement agencies, which may be agencies of political subdivisions.
Assigns the Office of Court Administration responsibility for developing, distributing, and periodically reviewing a standardized government form.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The model is distributed to law enforcement agencies across the state, and municipal and justice courts statewide receive notice of updates.

affected_groups.group: People issued citations for fine-only offenses
affected_groups.explanation: They receive standardized court, response, and citation-resolution information, along with information about resources for attending court.

affected_groups.group: People unable to afford court-imposed fines or costs
affected_groups.explanation: The addendum must provide details about payment plans, deferrals, community service, and waiver or reduction options; this is an information requirement, not a change to eligibility.

affected_groups.group: State and political-subdivision law enforcement agencies authorized to employ peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: Covered agencies must adopt, implement, and maintain citation and addendum forms that conform to the statewide model.

major_effects.label: Statewide model citation and addendum
major_effects.explanation: The Office of Court Administration must create and disseminate a model for fine-only citations. The citation must include specified court and resolution information, and the addendum must describe available assistance and options related to fines and costs.

major_effects.label: Agency adoption, with transition for existing citation books
major_effects.explanation: Covered law enforcement agencies must adopt forms conforming to the model by September 1, 2029, but need not issue compliant forms until they use the remainder of citation books they already possess.

major_effects.label: Recurring review and outcomes reporting
major_effects.explanation: The Office of Court Administration must periodically review the model, conduct user tests, and report on data outcomes and practices; it may modify or update the designs.

agencies.name: Office of Court Administration
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the article's “Office” as the Office of Court Administration and assigns it duties to design, adopt, disseminate, and review the model citation and addendum.

agencies.name: State and political-subdivision agencies authorized by law to employ peace officers
agencies.explanation: The bill defines this covered category to include state or political-subdivision agencies authorized to employ peace officers and requires each covered agency to adopt and implement conforming forms.

HB621.summary: For specified vehicle-title forms, or a substantially equivalent form designated by the department, the bill limits what the department may require as a condition of acceptance when the form is electronically signed and transmitted in compliance with existing requirements. In those circumstances, the department may not require the electronic signature to be printed or affixed to the form, or require evidence that a superseded or invalidated title was stamped invalid.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes requirements for documentation used in motor vehicle title transfers.
Changes the state department's conditions for accepting specified electronic forms.

locations.name: Texas (statewide)
locations.explanation: The provision amends a Texas Transportation Code requirement administered by a state department; the bill identifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: People submitting or using covered electronic motor vehicle title forms
affected_groups.explanation: Their forms are subject to the limits on acceptance conditions when electronically signed and transmitted in compliance with the existing requirements.

major_effects.label: Limits on electronic title-form acceptance conditions
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying electronically signed and transmitted forms, the department may not condition acceptance on printing or affixing the electronic signature or on evidence of stamped invalidation of the prior title.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles
agencies.explanation: The bill directly limits this department's conditions for accepting covered electronic forms. The supplied text does not identify the department by its canonical agency name.

HB622.summary: The bill would bar a toll project entity from collecting or attempting to collect an unpaid toll after two years from when it was incurred if the entity failed to solicit payment during those two years because of a billing or other error not attributable to the person. The restriction would apply to unpaid tolls pending when the Act takes effect, including tolls incurred before, on, or after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill restricts toll collection by toll project entities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision applies to toll project entities under Texas law without limiting its reach to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: People with unpaid tolls
affected_groups.explanation: They would be protected from collection after the two-year anniversary when the entity failed to solicit payment because of an error not attributable to them.

affected_groups.group: Toll project entities
affected_groups.explanation: They would be barred from collecting or attempting to collect tolls in the specified circumstances.

major_effects.label: Limit on collection of certain unpaid tolls
major_effects.explanation: Bars collection after the second anniversary only when the entity failed to solicit payment during the two-year period because of a billing or other error not attributable to the person.

HB623.summary: The bill would designate the specified portion of Interstate Highway 2 in Hidalgo County as the Officer Domingo Jasso III Memorial Highway, in addition to any other designation. Subject to Transportation Code Section 225.021(c), the department would have to design and construct markers and place them at both ends of the segment and at appropriate intermediate sites.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill designates a highway segment and requires markers identifying that designation.

locations.name: Portion of Interstate Highway 2 in Hidalgo County between Farm-to-Market Road 1015 in Weslaco and Farm-to-Market Road 493 in Donna
locations.explanation: This is the highway segment covered by the designation and marker requirements.

affected_groups.group: Drivers and other users of the designated highway segment
affected_groups.explanation: They would encounter the memorial designation and its markers on this segment.

major_effects.label: Memorial highway designation and markers
major_effects.explanation: Designates the specified segment by name and, subject to Section 225.021(c), requires markers at each end and at appropriate intermediate sites.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department marker-design and construction duties. The supplied text does not verify which state agency the generic term “the department” identifies.

HB624.summary: The bill would require the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement to establish an evidence-based training program of at least two hours on interacting with people with autism spectrum disorder, and would require officers to complete it as part of minimum curriculum requirements. The completion requirement would apply only to officers who first begin satisfying those requirements on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required training in how peace officers interact with people with autism spectrum disorder.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes a Texas officer-training requirement without limiting it to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: Officers would have to complete the training as part of minimum curriculum requirements, subject to the stated applicability cutoff.

affected_groups.group: People with autism spectrum disorder
affected_groups.explanation: The training is designed to guide officer interactions with this population, including communication, de-escalation, and safety.

major_effects.label: Autism interaction training
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to establish and maintain an evidence-based training program of at least two hours, and requires officers to complete it as part of minimum curriculum requirements, subject to the stated applicability cutoff.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Directs the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement to adopt rules necessary to implement the changes.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Law Enforcement
agencies.explanation: The commission is assigned responsibility for establishing and maintaining the training program and adopting implementing rules.

HB625.summary: The bill would require businesses operating for a commercial purpose to clearly label their use of a “heightened scrutiny” artificial intelligence system in a consumer-accessible area of the business or on a website or social media site they maintain. The attorney general could sue to stop violations and seek other public-interest relief, including a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation and restitution to a victim.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill creates a consumer-facing disclosure requirement for businesses' use of specified artificial intelligence systems.
The bill imposes a labeling duty on businesses operating for a commercial purpose and provides for enforcement.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill is enacted by the Texas Legislature and establishes a statewide business requirement.

affected_groups.group: Businesses operating for a commercial purpose
affected_groups.explanation: These businesses would have to label their use of covered artificial intelligence systems in specified consumer-accessible locations.

affected_groups.group: Consumers of goods or services
affected_groups.explanation: Consumers would be the audience for the required labels, which must be displayed in areas or online spaces accessible to them.

major_effects.label: Consumer-facing AI labeling
major_effects.explanation: Commercial businesses would have to clearly and conspicuously disclose their use of covered artificial intelligence systems in a physical business area accessible to consumers or on a maintained website or social media site.

major_effects.label: Attorney general enforcement and remedies
major_effects.explanation: The attorney general could sue to enjoin violations and seek public-interest relief, including civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation and victim restitution.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The attorney general may bring an enforcement action and request public-interest relief for violations.

HB626.summary: The bill would establish a dedicated account in the state treasury, administered by the department, to provide financial assistance for transportation projects. Assistance would be limited to projects outside the unified transportation program that a member of the legislature has designated as a priority.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a funding mechanism for qualifying transportation projects.
Creates a dedicated state treasury account and specifies sources of money that may be deposited in it and the purposes for which it may be used.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The fund is expressly identified as statewide and is established in the state treasury.

affected_groups.group: Transportation project sponsors or entities seeking financial assistance
affected_groups.explanation: Projects may receive assistance only if they are outside the unified transportation program and designated as a priority by a legislator.

major_effects.label: Creates a transportation improvement fund
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a dedicated account in the state treasury administered by the department.

major_effects.label: Limits eligible project assistance
major_effects.explanation: Fund assistance is restricted to transportation projects outside the unified transportation program that a member of the legislature has designated as a priority.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
