affected_groups.explanation: They would have to follow the new complaint, notice, advisor, and disciplinary-process requirements. An institution may not take disciplinary action against a currently or formerly enrolled student unless its disciplinary process complied with this subchapter.

affected_groups.group: People adversely affected by an institution's noncompliance
affected_groups.explanation: They could bring an action for specified relief against the institution.

major_effects.label: Sworn complaint required
major_effects.explanation: An institution could not initiate an investigation or disciplinary process against a current or former student without a written, sworn complaint signed by a person with personal knowledge; the complaint must describe the alleged misconduct with reasonable specificity and be kept as an institutional record.

major_effects.label: Student notice and advisor protections
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying disciplinary processes, students could designate a third party to receive notice and would be allowed an advisor; institutions would provide advisor training and, with written student consent, process updates.

major_effects.label: Compliance condition and civil relief
major_effects.explanation: An institution could not take disciplinary action unless its process complied with the subchapter. An adversely affected person could seek declaratory or injunctive relief and other relief authorized by law; sovereign immunity would be waived only to the extent of liability created by this section.

agencies.name: institution of higher education
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns disciplinary-process duties to institutions of higher education. The source uses a statutory category rather than naming specific institutions, and the registry has no matching entry.

HB705.summary: The bill bars the HHSC executive commissioner from modifying or deleting immunizations listed in Education Code §38.001(a) or requiring additional immunizations for elementary or secondary school admission. It requires the Department of State Health Services to prepare an annual list of immunizations required under subsection (a) for public-school admission, removing the reference to recommended additional immunizations.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes immunization requirements and information posted for public-school admission.
Changes statutory immunization requirements and limits governmental immunization mandates.
Requires school districts that maintain websites to post specified immunization information.
Establishes a general limit on governmental compulsion to receive immunizations, with statutory exceptions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies to immunization requirements for children throughout Texas and to governmental entities.

affected_groups.group: Children subject to school or child-care immunization requirements
affected_groups.explanation: Their applicable immunization requirements are tied to the diseases listed in Education Code §38.001.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts maintaining websites must post specified immunization, clinic, and exemption information.

affected_groups.group: Individuals subject to governmental immunization requirements
affected_groups.explanation: Governmental entities generally may not compel them to receive immunizations, except where specified statutes require them.

major_effects.label: Limits authority to change school immunization requirements
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner may not alter the Education Code list or add school-admission immunization requirements, but may recommend additions to the Legislature.

major_effects.label: Restricts governmental immunization mandates
major_effects.explanation: Governmental entities generally may not compel immunization; the restriction does not apply to immunizations required by the cited statutes.

major_effects.label: Aligns child immunization requirements with the statutory list
major_effects.explanation: Statewide and child-care requirements refer to the diseases listed in Education Code §38.001; the child-care provisional-admission qualification remains.

major_effects.label: Revises public immunization information
major_effects.explanation: The annual list is limited to required immunizations, and school-district website postings include required immunizations, known district influenza clinics, and an exemption-information link.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner is barred from changing the school immunization list or adding school admission requirements and may recommend additions to the Legislature.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: Its annual list is limited to immunizations required under Education Code §38.001, rather than also including recommended immunizations.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the child-care immunization requirement assigned to “the department” in Human Resources Code §42.043(b), but this excerpt does not identify that department.

HB706.summary: The bill would bar a municipality or its contracting entity from entering into a Chapter 380 economic-development agreement for a covered data center unless the municipality holds at least five public hearings and voters in the covered area support the agreement at an election. It also requires public notice and opportunities for participation, and applies only to agreements entered into on or after the Act takes effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates approval requirements for covered data-center development agreements.
Imposes hearing, notice, and election-related requirements on municipalities and limits when they or their contracting entities may enter covered agreements.
Requires voter approval at an election before a covered agreement may be entered into.
Changes the conditions for entering into agreements under Chapter 380 economic development programs.

locations.name: Areas within municipalities, limited-purpose annexed areas, and municipal extraterritorial jurisdictions
locations.explanation: The requirements apply only to areas in a municipality, annexed by a municipality for limited purposes, or in a municipality's extraterritorial jurisdiction.

affected_groups.group: Municipal governing bodies and their program-administration contracting entities
affected_groups.explanation: For covered data-center agreements in areas subject to this section, the municipality or its contracting entity may not enter the agreement unless the statutory conditions are met. One stated condition is that the municipal governing body hold at least five public hearings.

affected_groups.group: Residents and qualified voters in areas covered by the section
affected_groups.explanation: Residents are invited to hearings, and qualified voters in the covered area may vote on the agreement.

affected_groups.group: Data-center developers and other agreement counterparties
affected_groups.explanation: The agreement counterparty is invited to hearings, and the agreement cannot be entered into unless the hearing and election prerequisites are met.

affected_groups.group: Businesses affected by a covered development agreement
affected_groups.explanation: Affected businesses in the covered area are invited to the public hearing.

major_effects.label: Prerequisites for covered data-center agreements
major_effects.explanation: A municipality or its program-administration contracting entity may enter a covered agreement only after at least five public hearings and voter support at an election.

major_effects.label: Public hearing and notice process
major_effects.explanation: Requires public notice for each hearing, an opportunity for interested parties to be heard, and invitations to specified affected persons and entities.

HB707.summary: The bill extends the existing videoconference meeting condition to county boards of park commissioners. When such a board meets by videoconference, the presiding member must be physically present at a meeting location open to the public during open portions of the meeting.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the conditions under which county boards of park commissioners may meet by videoconference.
Changes the meeting procedures that apply to a governmental body conducting a videoconference meeting.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change applies to county boards of park commissioners across Texas.

affected_groups.group: County boards of park commissioners and their members
affected_groups.explanation: When these boards meet by videoconference, the presiding member must be physically present at a qualifying public meeting location.

affected_groups.group: Members of the public attending open portions of these meetings
affected_groups.explanation: The physical meeting location must be open to the public during the meeting's open portions.

major_effects.label: Conditions videoconference meetings by county park boards
major_effects.explanation: Adds county boards of park commissioners to the bodies whose videoconference meetings require the presiding member to be physically present at a location open to the public during open portions.

HB709.summary: The bill would reduce by 10 percent a school district’s required payment to purchase attendance credit if the district elects to use the payment method specified in law and pays the total amount by February 15 of the school year. The reduction would apply after any other reductions the district is entitled to receive.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes a payment requirement under the public school finance system.
Changes the amount school districts must pay when purchasing attendance credit.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision adds a general rule to the Texas public school finance statutes and does not specify a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts that elect the specified payment method and pay the total amount by February 15 would receive the 10 percent reduction.

major_effects.label: Conditional 10% payment reduction
major_effects.explanation: Reduces the amount required for attendance-credit purchases by 10 percent for districts meeting the payment-method and timing conditions; other applicable reductions are applied first.

HB710.summary: The bill would add procedures for impeachment investigations and trials, including sworn testimony in open sessions, committee-material review periods, family-member voting exclusions, and a specified order for selecting the presiding officer in a trial of the governor or lieutenant governor. It would require the House and Senate to account for and report impeachment-related costs, and limit removal of state and specified local officers to acts committed while holding an elected or appointed office. The changes apply only to proceedings commenced on or after the effective date and take effect only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise, the act has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes procedures for impeachment proceedings and trials, including testimony, voting, cost reporting, and who may preside in certain trials.
The bill changes removal grounds for general-law municipal, county, and precinct officers.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill applies to officers in this state and amends state and local laws governing their removal.

affected_groups.group: Public officers subject to impeachment or removal
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes procedures affecting officers who are the subject of impeachment or removal proceedings.

affected_groups.group: Members of the Texas House and Senate
affected_groups.explanation: Members receive committee materials, follow new proceeding requirements, and may be barred from voting when related to the officer or the officer's former spouse.

affected_groups.group: General-law municipal, county, and precinct officers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill limits removal under the specified local-government laws to acts committed while holding an elected or appointed office.

major_effects.label: Testimony and open-session requirements
major_effects.explanation: Witnesses, including the officer who is the subject, must testify under oath in sessions open to the relevant House members, committee members, or senators. A committee must allow the subject officer to testify in the officer's defense with counsel present, but the officer may not cross-examine other witnesses.

major_effects.label: Committee-material review and House vote timing
major_effects.explanation: For a committee-conducted proceeding, members must receive the committee report and related materials at least 72 hours before deliberations, and the House may not vote during the 72 hours after deliberations conclude.

major_effects.label: Family-member voting exclusions
major_effects.explanation: House members may not vote in an impeachment proceeding, and senators may not vote on removal or disqualification, if they are related within the third degree or are the former spouse of the officer or individual concerned.

major_effects.label: Impeachment cost accounting and reports
major_effects.explanation: The House and Senate must account for impeachment-related costs and deliver reports to specified recipients within 60 days after the relevant proceeding or trial concludes. The House must update its report if the Senate conducts a trial.

major_effects.label: Presiding officer for trials of the governor or lieutenant governor
major_effects.explanation: The bill sets an order of judicial officers who may preside, beginning with the Texas Supreme Court chief justice and providing substitutes if that justice or later designees recuse or are unavailable.

major_effects.label: Limits grounds for removal
major_effects.explanation: Removal of state officers and specified local officers is limited to acts committed while holding an elected or appointed office, replacing prior language about acts before election; the municipal provision also deletes its public-record-or-known-to-voters qualification.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The comptroller is a required recipient of the House and Senate reports on impeachment costs.

agencies.name: Legislative Budget Board
agencies.explanation: The Legislative Budget Board is a required recipient of the House and Senate reports on impeachment costs; no matching registry ID is supplied.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Texas Supreme Court chief justice is first in line to preside over an impeachment trial of the governor or lieutenant governor; the bill provides court-judge substitutes if the chief justice is unavailable or recuses.

HB711.summary: The bill would require the Winkler County commissioners court to pay additional annual compensation to all members of the county juvenile board, in an amount set by the court and paid monthly from county funds. This replaces a discretionary arrangement that specified $1,200 for the chair and allowed compensation of up to $1,200 for other members. It would also add Human Resources Code Section 152.0003 to the provisions that do not apply to the board.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes required compensation paid by Winkler County and imposes a payment duty on its commissioners court.

locations.name: Winkler County
locations.explanation: The bill specifically concerns the Winkler County Juvenile Board and its commissioners court.

affected_groups.group: Members of the Winkler County Juvenile Board
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive required additional annual compensation, with the amount determined by the commissioners court.

affected_groups.group: Winkler County commissioners court and county government
affected_groups.explanation: The commissioners court would set the compensation amount and pay it from county funds.

major_effects.label: Required board-member compensation
major_effects.explanation: Requires the county commissioners court to pay additional annual compensation to board members; the court determines the amount, and payments are made monthly from county funds.

major_effects.label: Additional statutory nonapplication
major_effects.explanation: Adds Human Resources Code Section 152.0003 to the provisions that do not apply to the Winkler County Juvenile Board; the bill text does not state the underlying effect of that provision.

HB712.summary: The bill authorizes municipalities and counties to regulate or prohibit carrying firearms on the premises of libraries they establish and operate. That authority would not extend to people described by specified Penal Code provisions or people otherwise authorized to carry under a license or commission issued under Chapter 1702, Occupations Code.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds municipal and county authority to regulate or prohibit firearm carrying at libraries those local governments operate.
The bill concerns local regulation of firearm carrying at municipal and county libraries, subject to specified exceptions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes the authority of municipalities and counties under Texas law, without limiting the change to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Municipal and county governments
affected_groups.explanation: They may regulate or prohibit firearm carrying at libraries they establish and operate.

affected_groups.group: People carrying firearms at municipal or county libraries
affected_groups.explanation: Their carrying may be subject to local regulation or prohibition, except for the people excluded by the bill's exceptions.

major_effects.label: Local authority over firearms at libraries
major_effects.explanation: Municipalities and counties may regulate or prohibit firearm carrying at libraries they establish and operate, except as to the persons identified in the bill's exceptions.

HB713.summary: The bill would raise the basic-allotment calculation basis from 130 to 200 students in average daily attendance for qualifying districts with fewer than 200 students that offer kindergarten through grade 12. The existing attendance and distance qualifications would remain in place.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the Foundation School Program allotment calculation for certain school districts.
Raises the student-count basis used to calculate state basic allotments for qualifying districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change applies to qualifying school districts under the statewide Education Code provision.

affected_groups.group: School districts offering kindergarten through grade 12 with fewer than 200 students in average daily attendance
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying districts would receive a basic allotment calculated on a 200-student basis, subject to the existing attendance or distance qualifications.

major_effects.label: Higher allotment calculation basis
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying districts with fewer than 200 students in average daily attendance, the basic allotment would be calculated on the basis of 200 students instead of 130.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill does not name the agency, but the revised Foundation School Program allotment basis implies an impact on administration of school-funding calculations.

HB714.summary: The bill would establish the Office of Rural Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Services within the governor’s office, serving counties with fewer than 120,000 people and supporting community-based mental health care and community centers in those rural communities. The governor would hire the office’s director, the Governor’s Committee on People with Disabilities would oversee it, and the director would submit a biennial report; the office would use money appropriated or otherwise available for that purpose.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a state office focused on strengthening access to community-based mental health care in rural communities.
Establishes a new office, assigns administrative oversight, and provides for its director and staff.
Provides for operating the new state office with money appropriated or otherwise available for that purpose, but does not specify a dollar appropriation.

locations.name: Counties with populations under 120,000 (rural communities)
locations.explanation: The bill defines the rural communities served by the office using county population.

affected_groups.group: Community centers serving rural communities
affected_groups.explanation: The office is tasked with promoting their development, addressing barriers to financial viability, and assisting with grant procurement.

affected_groups.group: Residents of rural communities seeking community-based mental health care
affected_groups.explanation: The office’s purposes include strengthening the rural community-based mental health care system and improving access.

major_effects.label: Creates a rural mental health office
major_effects.explanation: Establishes an office within the governor’s office to support community-based mental health care and community centers in rural communities.

major_effects.label: Sets governance and operational authority
major_effects.explanation: The Governor’s Committee on People with Disabilities oversees administration; the governor employs the director, who manages the office and may hire staff.

major_effects.label: Provides for office resources
major_effects.explanation: The office uses money appropriated or otherwise available for its purpose and may accept gifts, grants, or loans; the bill makes no specified dollar appropriation.

major_effects.label: Requires biennial reporting
major_effects.explanation: The director must submit a report describing the office’s findings, recommendations, and legislative recommendations to the governor, legislature, and Legislative Budget Board.

agencies.name: Office of Rural Mental Health and Intellectual Disability Services
agencies.explanation: The bill creates this office and assigns it purposes and powers.

agencies.name: office of the governor
agencies.explanation: The new office is placed within it, and it is directed to implement the changes made by the Act.

agencies.name: Governor's Committee on People with Disabilities
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the committee oversight of the new office’s administration.

HB715.summary: The bill would prohibit a public institution of higher education from awarding an associate or baccalaureate degree unless the student has completed at least three semester credit hours of economics, with equal time devoted to macroeconomics and microeconomics. This requirement would apply only to students who enroll in those degree programs on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes an economics coursework condition for associate and baccalaureate degrees at public institutions of higher education.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to public institutions of higher education across Texas.

affected_groups.group: Students enrolling in associate or baccalaureate degree programs at public institutions of higher education on or after January 1, 2028
affected_groups.explanation: These students would need the specified economics coursework for the institution to award their degree.

affected_groups.group: Public institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: These institutions would be prohibited from awarding covered degrees unless the student meets the economics coursework requirement.

major_effects.label: Economics coursework required for covered degrees
major_effects.explanation: For students who enroll in the covered programs on or after January 1, 2028, an institution may not award an associate or baccalaureate degree unless the student has at least three semester credit hours or equivalent in an economics course that dedicates equal time to macroeconomics and microeconomics.

HB716.summary: The bill adds a municipality that is the county seat of a county with more than 10,000 people and a state park featuring sandhills to the municipalities covered by Tax Code Section 351.1066. This expands which municipalities qualify for that section’s rules governing municipal hotel occupancy tax revenue.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands which municipal governments are covered by the statutory rules for municipal hotel occupancy tax revenue.
The amendment changes which municipalities qualify under a Tax Code section concerning use of hotel occupancy tax revenue.

locations.name: Municipality that is the county seat of a county with more than 10,000 people containing a state park featuring sandhills
locations.explanation: The new eligibility category is defined by municipal and county characteristics rather than a named place.

affected_groups.group: Municipal governments meeting the new county-seat and state-park criteria
affected_groups.explanation: These municipalities would newly fall within the municipalities covered by Section 351.1066.

major_effects.label: Expands municipal eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Adds a municipality meeting the stated county-seat and state-park criteria to the municipalities covered by Section 351.1066’s rules concerning municipal hotel occupancy tax revenue.

HB717.summary: HB 717 would raise the population limit for a county to qualify for the rural ambulance service grant program from 68,750 to 200,000. It would allow counties with populations from 10,000 through 200,000 to qualify for grants of up to $350,000, while leaving the existing $500,000 cap for counties under 10,000 unchanged.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands county eligibility for a grant program identified as supporting rural ambulance services.
The expanded eligibility allows more counties to qualify for awards under a state grant program; the bill does not change the award caps.
The bill expands which counties may qualify for grant awards.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a statewide Texas grant program and sets eligibility by county population.

affected_groups.group: Counties with populations up to 200,000
affected_groups.explanation: Counties above the former population ceiling and up to 200,000 would newly qualify for the grant program.

affected_groups.group: Rural ambulance services
affected_groups.explanation: The grant program supports rural ambulance services, and expanded county eligibility could extend access to grant awards in additional areas.

major_effects.label: Expanded county eligibility for ambulance grants
major_effects.explanation: Raises the qualifying county population ceiling to 200,000; grant caps remain up to $500,000 for counties under 10,000 and up to $350,000 for counties from 10,000 to 200,000.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The Comptroller awards grants under the section, whose county eligibility is expanded by the bill.

HB718.summary: The bill lets courts prohibit remotely controlling electronic devices affecting a protected person's residence, vehicle, or property in specified protective orders, emergency orders, bond conditions, and family-law temporary restraining orders. It also creates an intent-based offense, generally a Class B misdemeanor, with higher classifications for specified repeat offenses and conduct targeting court employees or judges, and adds remote control to conduct that can violate covered orders. The order-related amendments apply under prospective transition rules keyed to the order, release, or offense date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a criminal offense and adds remote control to conduct that may violate covered orders or bond conditions.
Allows specified court orders and bond conditions to prohibit remote control of devices affecting protected people’s property.
Regulates remote control of electronic devices affecting another person’s property and makes specified intentional conduct criminal.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes without limiting the changes to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: People protected by orders and their family or household members
affected_groups.explanation: Their property may be protected by an order prohibiting remote control of an electronic device.

affected_groups.group: People whose electronic-device control is restricted by an order or bond condition
affected_groups.explanation: The bill adds remote control to conduct courts or magistrates may prohibit in specified orders or release conditions.

affected_groups.group: Judges and court employees
affected_groups.explanation: Specified offenses against people the actor knows are judges or court employees carry enhanced classifications.

major_effects.label: Remote-control prohibitions in orders and bond conditions
major_effects.explanation: Allows specified courts and magistrates to prohibit remote control of electronic devices affecting a protected person's or party's residence, vehicle, or property.

major_effects.label: New offense and enhanced classifications
major_effects.explanation: Creates an intent-based offense, generally a Class B misdemeanor, with increased classifications for specified prior convictions and victims who are court employees or judges; also adds remote control to conduct that can violate covered orders.

agencies.name: court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly changes what a court may prohibit in specified orders, but the provisions refer generically to a court and do not identify a particular court system.

HB719.summary: For executive-branch state agencies, notices for proposed rules would have to certify that the governor—or, when an agency is governed by elected state officers, an elected officer of that agency—reviewed and approved the rule. Emergency rules would have to be submitted for approval within 10 days after adoption; if not approved, they could not be renewed or replaced by a substantially similar rule through the specified regular-rule process. These changes apply only to rules proposed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes approval and notice procedures for rules proposed by executive-branch state agencies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill governs rulemaking by state agencies in the executive branch, without limiting the requirements to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Executive-branch state agencies proposing covered rules
affected_groups.explanation: These agencies would have to obtain the specified approval and include the required certification in proposed-rule notices.

affected_groups.group: Governor and elected state officers who govern an agency
affected_groups.explanation: They would review and approve covered proposed rules, including emergency rules.

major_effects.label: Approval of proposed rules
major_effects.explanation: Covered rule notices must certify approval by the governor or, for an agency governed by elected state officers, an elected officer of that agency.

major_effects.label: Emergency-rule approval and limits
major_effects.explanation: Agencies must submit covered emergency rules for approval within 10 days after adoption. If the rule is not approved, it cannot be renewed or replaced by a substantially similar rule under the specified regular-rule sections.

agencies.name: state agency in the executive branch of state government
agencies.explanation: The bill directly imposes rule-approval and notice duties on this class of agencies, but does not identify particular agencies by name.

HB720.summary: The bill would raise the population limit for counties authorized to own, operate, and maintain a cemetery from 8,200 to 15,000. Eligible counties could also sell the right of burial in the cemetery.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands which counties may exercise authority over a county-owned cemetery and sell burial rights.

locations.name: Texas counties with a population of 15,000 or less
locations.explanation: The authority applies to counties meeting the stated population threshold.

affected_groups.group: County governments with a population of 15,000 or less
affected_groups.explanation: These counties would be eligible to own, operate, and maintain a cemetery and sell burial rights.

major_effects.label: Expands county cemetery authority
major_effects.explanation: Raises the population ceiling from 8,200 to 15,000 for counties authorized to own, operate, and maintain a cemetery and sell the right of burial.

HB721.summary: HB 721 would make the commission and advisory panel, rather than the department acting with them, responsible for preparing the biennial report on regional mental-health bed allocation. It would expand the report to cover the allocation methodology, service capacity and demand, patient outcomes, state funding, and grant applications denied because of funding limits; it would not itself change bed allocations or funding.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands statutory reporting about regional mental-health beds and state-funded mental-health services, without changing the services or bed allocations themselves.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The report includes statewide mental-health funding and statewide recommendations.

locations.name: Regions covered by the bed-day allocation methodology
locations.explanation: The bill requires regional reporting but does not name or define the regions in this text.

affected_groups.group: Patients using state-funded inpatient mental-health beds
affected_groups.explanation: The report must assess outcomes for patients who occupied a state-funded bed and discuss the use of those beds.

affected_groups.group: State-funded mental-health facilities and program operators
affected_groups.explanation: The report must break down facilities and programs by region and assess their capacity, demand, waitlists, funding, and service gaps.

affected_groups.group: Entities applying for state-funded mental-health grants
affected_groups.explanation: The report must include entities denied grants because of funding limits and information about their grant requests.

major_effects.label: Expanded biennial mental-health bed allocation report
major_effects.explanation: Adds analysis of the methodology, regional services and capacity, state funding, patient outcomes, and grant applications denied because of funding limitations.

major_effects.label: Report-preparation responsibility
major_effects.explanation: Removes the department from the report-preparation requirement and assigns preparation to the commission and advisory panel.

agencies.name: commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the commission responsibility for preparing the report and calculating regional bed-day values; the bill does not give its full formal name.

HB722.summary: HB 722 would let courts and magistrates prohibit remote control of electronic devices affecting specified property of protected people, including through protective orders, emergency orders, temporary restraining orders, and bond conditions. It would also expand existing criminal offenses to cover specified remote-control conduct when the existing requirements for violating an order or committing harassment are met; the amendments apply prospectively based on when the relevant order is issued or offense is committed.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands conduct covered by existing criminal offenses involving violations of certain orders and harassment.
Adds a potential protective-order and bond restriction addressing conduct affecting protected people and their property.
Creates restrictions and criminal-offense coverage for remotely controlling electronic devices affecting another person's specified property.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes and has statewide scope.

affected_groups.group: People protected by orders and their family or household members
affected_groups.explanation: The new order provisions address remote control of devices affecting their residences, vehicles, or property.

affected_groups.group: People subject to protective orders, emergency orders, or bond conditions
affected_groups.explanation: Courts or magistrates may prohibit this conduct, and a bond condition may require a defendant to refrain from it.

affected_groups.group: Individuals whose property is affected by another person's remote control
affected_groups.explanation: The harassment provision would cover remote control of devices affecting property owned, leased, occupied, or possessed by another person, subject to its existing intent requirement.

major_effects.label: Adds remote-control restrictions to court orders and bond conditions
major_effects.explanation: Courts and magistrates may prohibit remote control affecting specified property in several types of orders; a magistrate may also require a defendant charged with family violence to refrain from it as a bond condition.

major_effects.label: Expands criminal-offense coverage
major_effects.explanation: Adds specified remote control to conduct covered by the order-violation offense and the harassment offense, while retaining the existing requirements for those offenses.

HB723.summary: HB 723 would replace average daily attendance with average enrollment as the central measure for public-school finance and revise related funding and eligibility calculations across the Education Code. When a commissioner-defined emergency or crisis causes a statewide enrollment decrease among districts funded under the chapter—or a decrease limited to a specific region—the commissioner would have to modify or waive affected requirements and adopt safeguards.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the measure used throughout public-school finance and related Education Code calculations.
Changes the enrollment basis used to calculate state aid and per-student school funding; it does not specify a net change in total state spending.
Updates enrollment-based calculations and criteria in the existing educational assistance program, including account funding and whether a child is counted for public-school funding.
Changes the measure used in funding calculations for school districts, which are local education entities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to Texas public-school finance, including statewide and region-specific enrollment adjustments.

affected_groups.group: Public school districts
affected_groups.explanation: District funding and related calculations would use average enrollment rather than average daily attendance.

affected_groups.group: Open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: The revised measure applies to charter-school funding and other enrollment-based calculations.

affected_groups.group: Students counted for public-school funding
affected_groups.explanation: The measure used to count students for funding changes from attendance to enrollment.

affected_groups.group: Children participating in the educational assistance program
affected_groups.explanation: Program account funding and public-school enrollment-status criteria are tied to average enrollment.

major_effects.label: Enrollment-based school finance
major_effects.explanation: Uses average enrollment instead of average daily attendance in the core school-finance measure and related district, charter, and per-student funding calculations; the bill does not specify the net fiscal effect.

major_effects.label: Enrollment calculation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commissioner to adopt rules, including a method for calculating average enrollment.

major_effects.label: Emergency and crisis adjustments
major_effects.explanation: If a commissioner-defined emergency or crisis causes a statewide enrollment decrease among districts funded under the chapter, or a regional decrease among districts in the affected region, the commissioner must modify or waive applicable requirements and adopt safeguards.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The commissioner receives calculation, rulemaking, and adjustment responsibilities under the Education Code; the responsible education agency is inferred from that context.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The comptroller's approval criteria for providers in the educational assistance program refer to whether children are counted using average enrollment.

agencies.name: Texas Juvenile Justice Department
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the student-count measure used for the department's state available school fund apportionment.

HB724.summary: The bill repeals Section 4 of a 2005 act concerning Star of Texas Award recipients. Its caption connects the change to peace officers, firefighters, and emergency medical first responders killed or seriously or fatally injured in the line of duty before September 1, 2003, but the supplied text does not show what the repealed provision required or how its removal changes recipient eligibility.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill concerns Star of Texas Award recipients among first responders killed or seriously or fatally injured in the line of duty.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: This is a Texas legislative enactment concerning the Star of Texas Award; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: Peace officers, firefighters, and emergency medical first responders killed or seriously or fatally injured in the line of duty before September 1, 2003
affected_groups.explanation: The bill's caption identifies these first responders as the subject of the recipient-related change; the effect on their eligibility is not shown in the supplied text.

major_effects.label: Repeal of a recipient-related provision
major_effects.explanation: Repeals a section of the 2005 act. The caption links the bill to Star of Texas Award recipients in pre-September 1, 2003 line-of-duty cases, but the supplied text does not establish the rule being removed or the resulting change.

HB726.summary: The bill would let a law-enforcement agency chief ask the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement to waive a training-course or initial-licensure minimum standard that disqualifies an applicant solely because of a qualifying felony-theft deferred adjudication. Applicants would have to meet strict conditions, including committing the single qualifying offense before age 21 and having been dismissed and discharged at least 15 years before the request; the commission would have to make an individualized written determination. A waiver would not itself confer training enrollment, licensure, appointment, or employment, and would ordinarily apply only at the requesting agency unless the commission approves a transfer before separation.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes when an applicant may receive a waiver from a peace-officer training or licensure disqualification, subject to a finding that the waiver would not create an unreasonable risk to public safety.
Creates a limited waiver pathway for a disqualification based solely on a qualifying felony-theft deferred adjudication.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes concern Texas peace-officer training and licensure standards administered by the state commission.

affected_groups.group: Applicants with qualifying felony-theft deferred adjudications seeking peace-officer training or initial licensure
affected_groups.explanation: They may be considered for a limited waiver if they satisfy the bill's eligibility conditions and demonstrate rehabilitation.

affected_groups.group: Law-enforcement agencies seeking to employ eligible applicants as full-time peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: The agency chief may request a waiver, and a waiver ordinarily limits the person's appointment or employment as a peace officer to that agency.

major_effects.label: Conditional waiver of a training or licensure disqualification
major_effects.explanation: Allows a law-enforcement agency chief to request a waiver for a disqualification based solely on the specified deferred-adjudication felony theft, subject to extensive eligibility limits; the waiver does not itself guarantee enrollment, licensure, appointment, or employment.

major_effects.label: Individualized commission review
major_effects.explanation: The commission may grant a waiver only after an individualized review and a written determination of rehabilitation and that the waiver would not create the specified risks.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Directs the commission to adopt rules for the new waiver process, based on rules applicable to waivers involving disqualifying misdemeanor offenses.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Law Enforcement
agencies.explanation: The commission may grant the new waivers after individualized review and must adopt implementing rules; the bill names the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement as the rulemaking body.

HB727.summary: The bill expands the statutory fraud-in-transaction provision from transactions involving corporate or joint-stock-company stock to transactions involving a broader range of business ownership interests in for-profit entities, including membership and partnership interests. The expanded provision applies only to claims based on a false representation or promise made after the Act’s effective date and related to a contract entered into after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: Broadens the types of business ownership transactions covered by the statutory fraud provision.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law without limiting the change to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Parties to contracts involving business ownership interests in for-profit entities
affected_groups.explanation: The expanded fraud provision may apply to claims involving false representations or promises made to induce these parties to contract.

major_effects.label: Broader covered business transactions
major_effects.explanation: Extends the statutory fraud provision from stock transactions to transactions involving defined business ownership interests, including membership and partnership interests.

major_effects.label: Prospective application
major_effects.explanation: The change applies only when both the false representation or promise and the related contract occur after the Act’s effective date.

HB728.summary: The bill would prohibit a private entity from exercising eminent domain to develop or operate high-speed rail, as defined in specified Transportation Code sections. It would also make Transportation Code Chapter 131, Subchapter B inapplicable to high-speed rail.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes rules applicable to high-speed rail.
The bill limits private entities' eminent-domain authority for high-speed rail.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Transportation Code without limiting its application to a particular area.

affected_groups.group: Private entities developing or operating high-speed rail
affected_groups.explanation: These entities would be barred from using eminent domain for high-speed rail purposes and would not be subject to Chapter 131, Subchapter B.

affected_groups.group: Property owners whose property could otherwise be taken for high-speed rail
affected_groups.explanation: The restriction would limit private entities' ability to acquire property through eminent domain for high-speed rail development or operation.

major_effects.label: Limits high-speed rail eminent domain
major_effects.explanation: Although the general railroad-company authority remains, a private entity may not exercise eminent domain to develop or operate high-speed rail.

major_effects.label: Excludes high-speed rail from Chapter 131, Subchapter B
major_effects.explanation: The bill makes that subchapter inapplicable to high-speed rail; it does not specify the subchapter's individual provisions here.

HB730.summary: HB 730 would restrict a utility operating solely outside ERCOT from recovering from other customers the cost of generation primarily serving a single-site customer above 75 megawatts, unless the commission makes findings that include net customer benefit and specified cost and rate safeguards. A certificate could be granted only after those findings or with a condition barring recovery until the findings are made; the bill would also require interconnection rules for new or expanded single-site loads above 75 megawatts, with authority to set a lower threshold and standards for customer disclosures, study fees, site control, and financial commitments.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes electric-utility cost recovery for dedicated generation and establishes standards for large-load interconnections.
Requires standards and financial commitments for customers seeking large-load electric service.

locations.name: Areas outside the ERCOT power region
locations.explanation: The dedicated-generation provisions define the covered utility as operating solely outside the ERCOT power region.

affected_groups.group: Large-load customers and entities seeking large-load interconnections
affected_groups.explanation: The bill covers generation facilities primarily serving a single-site customer whose load exceeds or is projected to exceed 75 megawatts, and new or expanded interconnections above the applicable threshold.

affected_groups.group: Electric utilities operating outside ERCOT
affected_groups.explanation: Utilities constructing, acquiring, or contracting for generation primarily to serve a large-load customer would be subject to the new cost-recovery safeguards.

affected_groups.group: Other utility customers, particularly residential and small commercial customers
affected_groups.explanation: The cost-allocation findings must protect these classes from rates exceeding what they would have paid without the dedicated facility.

major_effects.label: Limits recovery of dedicated-generation costs
major_effects.explanation: For rate-change proceedings initiated on or after the Act's effective date, utilities may not recover these facility costs from other customers unless the commission makes the required findings, including net benefit and cost-allocation protections.

major_effects.label: Conditions certificates for dedicated generation facilities
major_effects.explanation: For certificate applications filed on or after the Act's effective date, the commission must make the required findings or condition the certificate on no recovery from other customers unless the commission later makes those findings in a proceeding described by Section 36.053(f).

major_effects.label: Requires large-load interconnection standards
major_effects.explanation: The commission must set standards for new or expanded interconnections with an electric utility subject to this subchapter, where the total load at a single site would exceed 75 megawatts, or a lower threshold the commission determines is necessary. The standards are not limited to requests made after their effective date.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly assigns the Commission rulemaking for large-load interconnection standards; it also assigns commission findings and certificate decisions concerning dedicated generation facilities.

HB731.summary: Only if voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment abolishing ad valorem taxes, the bill would establish a temporary legislative committee to study replacing lost local ad valorem revenue with local sales and use taxes. Beginning January 1, 2033, it would repeal Title 1 of the Tax Code and prohibit the state and political subdivisions from imposing ad valorem taxes.

policy_tags.explanation: Conditionally repeals Title 1 of the Tax Code and prohibits state and political-subdivision ad valorem taxes beginning in 2033.
Political subdivisions would be barred from imposing ad valorem taxes, and the committee would study replacement revenue for local government.
Establishes a temporary joint legislative committee with a study and reporting assignment.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The tax prohibition applies to the state and its political subdivisions.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions
affected_groups.explanation: If voters approve the proposed amendment and ad valorem taxes are abolished, political subdivisions would lose local tax revenue; the committee would study replacing that lost revenue with local sales and use tax revenue.

affected_groups.group: Persons liable for ad valorem taxes
affected_groups.explanation: The bill preserves liability that accrued before January 1, 2033, for collection and enforcement.

affected_groups.group: Appointed House and Senate committee members
affected_groups.explanation: Five members of each chamber would be appointed to the temporary joint interim committee.

major_effects.label: Conditional abolition of ad valorem taxes
major_effects.explanation: If voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment, the state and political subdivisions could not impose ad valorem taxes beginning January 1, 2033. Liability accrued before that date remains in effect for collection and enforcement.

major_effects.label: Temporary legislative study committee
major_effects.explanation: Creates a joint interim committee to study how local sales and use tax revenue could replace revenue lost from abolishing ad valorem taxes.

major_effects.label: Study report to the legislature
major_effects.explanation: Requires the committee to submit its study results and recommendations to the legislature.

agencies.name: state agency
agencies.explanation: A state agency must provide information and assistance if the committee requests it; the bill does not identify which agencies may be asked.

HB732.summary: HB 732 defines data centers to include facilities used for cryptocurrency or blockchain computation and AI, while excluding specified public, higher-education, business-site and telecommunications facilities. It would bar tax abatements, certain municipal and county incentives, and tax-increment support for data centers, and make data-center projects ineligible for specified state economic-development support; comparable governmental services and qualifying general public works remain allowed. The restrictions apply to agreements entered into and plans adopted or amended on or after the effective date, with certain renewals, extensions and benefit-increasing amendments treated as new agreements.

policy_tags.explanation: Defines data centers and restricts their access to several incentive programs.
Changes eligibility for local economic-development incentives and state project-support programs.
Restricts municipal, county and reinvestment-zone incentive programs and use of local funds.
Makes certain data-center projects ineligible for Texas Enterprise Fund grants.
Prohibits tax abatements and limits tax-increment financing support for data centers.

locations.name: Statewide in Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide Texas tax and local-government laws.

locations.name: Municipalities and their extraterritorial jurisdictions
locations.explanation: Municipal incentive restrictions cover data centers in the municipality or its extraterritorial jurisdiction.

locations.name: Counties
locations.explanation: County incentive restrictions apply to data centers located in the county.

locations.name: Reinvestment zones
locations.explanation: The bill limits project costs and payments funded through a reinvestment zone.

affected_groups.group: Data-center owners and operators
affected_groups.explanation: Their projects would be barred from specified tax and public-money incentives, subject to the bill's definition and exclusions.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities, counties and reinvestment-zone boards
affected_groups.explanation: These local bodies would face restrictions on incentive agreements and use of tax-increment funds for data centers.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for state economic-development support
affected_groups.explanation: Projects consisting of or including a data center would be ineligible for the specified JETI and Texas Enterprise Fund support.

major_effects.label: Exclude data-center projects from specified state incentives
major_effects.explanation: Data centers would be excluded from the JETI eligible-project definition, and projects consisting of or including a data center would be ineligible for Texas Enterprise Fund grants.

major_effects.label: Restrict tax abatements and tax-increment support
major_effects.explanation: Taxing units could not grant the specified abatements for data-center property, and tax-increment plans and funds could not support projects or payments primarily benefiting or conditioned on a data center. Public works serving the zone generally remain permitted if not constructed primarily to serve a data center; violating agreements and plans are void to the extent specified.

major_effects.label: Bar specified municipal and county incentives
major_effects.explanation: Municipalities and counties could not provide covered loans, grants, rebates, refunds or other payments tied wholly or partly to data-center construction, operation, location or tax and fee amounts. The bill preserves governmental services provided on the same terms as for similarly situated commercial property.

agencies.name: Governor
agencies.explanation: The bill directly prohibits the Governor from awarding a Texas Enterprise Fund grant for a project consisting of or including a data center. The supplied registry has no matching Governor entry.

HB733.summary: HB 733 would require notaries to determine before a notarization whether the person for whom it is performed is associated with a comptroller-listed foreign terrorist organization. Performing a notarization for such an organization or one of its members with criminal negligence would be a state jail felony; notaries applying or reapplying on or after December 1, 2027, would also have to sign an acknowledgment, with earlier applicants signing at their first reappointment on or after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a criminal offense, classified as a state jail felony, for specified notarizations performed with criminal negligence.
Adds state administration duties for notary acknowledgment forms, lists, and implementation rules.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Government Code provisions governing notaries public statewide.

affected_groups.group: Notaries public
affected_groups.explanation: Must screen before notarizing, and covered applicants must sign an acknowledgment; violations meeting the criminal-negligence standard carry felony consequences.

affected_groups.group: Foreign terrorist organizations and their members seeking notarization
affected_groups.explanation: Notarizations for an organization or its member are subject to the new prohibition and criminal offense provision.

major_effects.label: Notary screening and acknowledgment
major_effects.explanation: Notaries must determine whether a person for whom they notarize is associated with a listed organization. The acknowledgment applies to applications submitted on or after December 1, 2027; earlier applicants must sign it when applying for their first reappointment on or after that date.

major_effects.label: State jail felony for specified notarizations
major_effects.explanation: A notary commits the offense when, with criminal negligence, the notary performs a notarization for a foreign terrorist organization or its member.

major_effects.label: Secretary of State implementation
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Secretary of State to adopt necessary rules and make the acknowledgment form available to notaries.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The Secretary of State must provide notaries a current list, provide the acknowledgment form, and adopt implementation rules.

HB734.summary: The bill defines data center agreements to include local development agreements with benefits tied to data centers, including facilities used for cryptocurrency mining or AI model training or operation, subject to specified exclusions. For covered agreements, local governments must submit a complete copy, including schedules, exhibits, and amendments, except for information the attorney general has determined is exempt under Section 552.110, and must provide the supporting decision for each redaction. A local government that does not comply may not provide agreement benefits until it does, and benefits that accrue during noncompliance are forfeited; these changes apply only to agreements entered into on or after the effective date, including specified renewals, extensions, and amendments.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes disclosure rules specifically for local development agreements tied to data center construction, expansion, operation, or location, and defines which facilities count.
The bill imposes agreement-submission requirements on local governments and restricts their provision of benefits when they do not comply.
The bill changes disclosure and compliance conditions for local economic development agreements and makes benefits accruing during noncompliance forfeitable.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to local governments entering covered agreements across Texas.

affected_groups.group: Local governments entering data center agreements
affected_groups.explanation: They must submit the required complete agreement copy and may lose the ability to provide benefits while noncompliant.

affected_groups.group: Data center owners and operators receiving local development benefits
affected_groups.explanation: Their agreements are subject to the disclosure rules, and benefits accruing during a local government's noncompliance are forfeited.

affected_groups.group: People seeking public information about local data center agreements
affected_groups.explanation: The required electronic copies must be complete and generally unredacted, subject to the stated exception.

major_effects.label: Complete agreement disclosure
major_effects.explanation: Requires the electronic copy of a covered agreement to include schedules, exhibits, and amendments, with redactions limited to information determined by the attorney general to be exempt under Section 552.110; supporting decisions must accompany redactions.

major_effects.label: Withholding and forfeiture of benefits
major_effects.explanation: Until a local government complies, it may not provide payments, abatements, or other agreement benefits; benefits that would have accrued during noncompliance are forfeited.

HB735.summary: HB 735 would repeal Subsection J of Chapter 29 of the Education Code, which the bill identifies as Texas’ education savings account program. The proposal is therefore directed at ending that program.

policy_tags.explanation: The proposal repeals an Education Code provision identified as the education savings account program.
The bill targets the education savings account program, a school-choice program.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill identifies the affected education savings account program as Texas’ program.

affected_groups.group: Current and prospective education savings account program participants
affected_groups.explanation: Repealing the program would affect people who use or seek to use it.

major_effects.label: Education savings account program repeal
major_effects.explanation: The bill proposes repealing the Chapter 29 provision it identifies as the education savings account program.

HB736.summary: The bill would create new care, safety, recordkeeping, disclosure, and family-contact duties for operators of detention facilities in Texas, including facilities on land subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the United States, to the extent permitted by 28 U.S.C. Section 5001 or other federal law; it would not apply to the federal government or its employees acting within their employment. It would allow civil actions for death or serious bodily injury and for specified failures involving custody records or family contact, with damages and other remedies available to prevailing claimants.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes duties and civil liability concerning people held in detention facilities, whether or not their custody relates to a criminal charge or conviction.
Creates protections for people in custody, including care and safety duties and a child's right to communicate with adults taken into custody with the child, subject to a court order.
Requires detention facility operators to exercise ordinary care to provide necessary medical care, mental health care, and medication to people in custody.
The new duties apply to operators regardless of whether they are governmental entities, so local governments that operate detention facilities are covered.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The chapter applies to detention facilities located in Texas, with application to facilities on land under exclusive federal jurisdiction only to the extent permitted by federal law.

affected_groups.group: Detention facility operators, including governmental and contracted operators and providers of custodial, medical, mental health, or security services
affected_groups.explanation: Operators would be subject to the new duties and potential civil liability; the chapter excludes the federal government and its personnel acting within their employment.

affected_groups.group: People held in custody at detention facilities
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive the new care and safety protections and may bring an action for qualifying death, injury, or records-related violations.

affected_groups.group: Children held in custody with adults and their family members or guardians
affected_groups.explanation: The bill sets requirements for records, certain out-of-state transfers, and communication between a child and adults taken into custody with the child. The communication requirement does not apply if a court has ordered otherwise.

major_effects.label: Care, safety, and family-contact duties
major_effects.explanation: Requires ordinary care for specified health, basic-needs, supervision, and safety matters, and requires daily communication for a child with each adult taken into custody with the child unless a court orders otherwise.

major_effects.label: Custody records and disclosure
major_effects.explanation: Requires operators to create and retain custody records and disclose covered information on request; it also requires specified notice before certain transfers of children out of state.

major_effects.label: Civil liability and remedies
major_effects.explanation: Creates civil claims for death or serious bodily injury caused by breach of the care duty and for specified record or family-contact failures; prevailing claimants may recover damages, and courts must award costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: An operator may transfer a child from a detention facility to a location outside Texas only if, before the transfer, the operator records the identity and last known location of each adult taken into custody with the child and provides that information and notice of the transfer to the Attorney General and, if known, to a parent or legal guardian of the child.

HB737.summary: The bill would require the vital statistics unit to furnish a certificate of state-registry search results no later than the 10th day after receiving a request, replacing the existing requirement to furnish it on request. The new deadline would apply only to requests made on or after the Act’s effective date; earlier requests would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the deadline for a state unit to provide a certificate in response to registry-search requests.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill concerns searches of the state registry of paternity, without limiting the change to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Individuals, courts, and agencies requesting registry searches
affected_groups.explanation: These requestors would receive the certificate under the specified response deadline.

major_effects.label: Deadline for search-result certificates
major_effects.explanation: The unit would have to furnish the certificate no later than the 10th day after receiving a request. The new deadline applies only to requests made on or after the Act’s effective date.

agencies.name: Vital statistics unit
agencies.explanation: The bill directly changes this unit’s deadline for furnishing search-result certificates, but the supplied text does not identify its parent agency or verify a canonical identity.

HB738.summary: HB 738 would require the Health and Human Services Commission to adopt minimum standards for Texas civil detention facilities, including standards for care, safety, communication, and children; facilities already regulated under specified chapters and compliant with those standards would be treated as compliant, federal actors are excluded, and the bill would not require a license or authorize the Commission to prohibit facility operation or decide where someone is held. Beginning September 1, 2028, counties and municipalities could request facility assessments, with local health authorities able to conduct them and receive reimbursement if the Commission misses the deadline; operators would have incident and quarterly reporting duties, public reporting would be required, and failures to report could result in civil penalties.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires minimum facility standards covering medical and mental health care, medication, nutrition, sanitation, and communicable disease.
The facility standards apply to covered civil detention facilities holding people pending or following federal immigration-status determinations; the bill does not change those determinations.
Required standards must address protecting people in custody from violence, sexual abuse, and self-harm.
The standards must address access to legal counsel, communication with family, and interpretation and translation services for people in custody.
Counties and municipalities may request assessments, and a local health authority may conduct an assessment if the Commission misses the deadline.
The Commission must reimburse a local health authority for reasonable assessment costs if the Commission fails to conduct a requested assessment on time.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The chapter applies to civil detention facilities located anywhere in Texas, subject to its stated exclusions and compliance provisions.

locations.name: County or municipality where a civil detention facility is located
locations.explanation: The assessment-request authority and related local health authority duties depend on the county or municipality where the facility is located.

affected_groups.group: People held in civil detention, including children
affected_groups.explanation: They would be covered by facility standards for care, safety, communication, and child-adult contact, and some incidents involving them must be reported.

affected_groups.group: Operators of civil detention facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Operators would be subject to the standards and reporting duties, and may face civil penalties for reports not made; federal operators are excluded.

affected_groups.group: Counties, municipalities, and their local health authorities
affected_groups.explanation: Local governing bodies could request assessments, and local health authorities could conduct them and receive reimbursement in the specified circumstance.

major_effects.label: Minimum facility standards
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must adopt standards for care, living conditions, safety, communication, interpretation, and children. Compliant facilities regulated under the listed chapters are treated as compliant, and the standards may not exceed the specified comparator; the chapter does not require a license or allow the Commission to prohibit operation.

major_effects.label: Assessments on local request
major_effects.explanation: A county or municipality may request an assessment of standards compliance and local public-health conditions. If the Commission does not conduct it within the prescribed period, the requesting jurisdiction's local health authority may do so, with reasonable costs reimbursed by the Commission.

major_effects.label: Incident and quarterly reporting
major_effects.explanation: Operators must report specified deaths, serious injuries, disease outbreaks, and child separations, as well as quarterly population, capacity, child-custody, and incident information; the Commission must publish quarterly information. Local assessment reports must also be delivered and published.

major_effects.label: Civil penalties for missing reports
major_effects.explanation: An operator may be liable for a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for each report not made, recoverable through an action brought by the attorney general or a listed local prosecutor.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the Commission as the Health and Human Services Commission and assigns it rulemaking, assessment, reporting, and reimbursement duties.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The attorney general is authorized to bring an action to recover the bill's civil penalty.

HB739.summary: The bill would allow a perpetual care cemetery to inter cremated remains of a deceased person’s previously owned pet in the person’s casket or beside the person’s cremated remains in a columbarium, and to include pet information on the person’s memorial; euthanizing a pet for this purpose would be prohibited. It would extend the property tax exemption to qualifying cemetery property used for human and pet burial, provided the property is not held for profit. The Finance Commission of Texas would adopt rules to implement the changes.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes what services perpetual care cemeteries may provide by authorizing specified interments of pet remains with human remains.
The bill extends a cemetery property tax exemption to qualifying property used for human and pet burial.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply generally to perpetual care cemeteries under Texas law, without specifying a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Perpetual care cemetery operators and owners
affected_groups.explanation: They may allow the specified pet interments and memorial information under the bill.

affected_groups.group: People arranging interment for a deceased individual and the individual’s previously owned pet
affected_groups.explanation: They may arrange for qualifying pet remains to be interred with the human remains or have pet information included on the memorial, subject to the prohibition on euthanizing a pet for this purpose.

affected_groups.group: Owners of qualifying cemetery property
affected_groups.explanation: Property owners may qualify for the cemetery property tax exemption when the property is used for human and pet burial in accordance with the bill and is not held for profit.

major_effects.label: Authorization for pet interment
major_effects.explanation: Perpetual care cemeteries may allow remains of a previously owned pet to be buried in a deceased individual’s casket or placed beside the individual’s cremated remains in a columbarium, and may include pet information on the memorial.

major_effects.label: Limit on pet interment
major_effects.explanation: A pet may not be euthanized for the purpose of interring its remains with a deceased individual.

major_effects.label: Cemetery property tax exemption
major_effects.explanation: The exemption would cover qualifying property used for human and pet burial, so long as the property is not held for profit.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: The Finance Commission of Texas must adopt rules necessary to implement the bill’s changes.

agencies.name: Finance Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the commission rulemaking responsibility. No matching canonical registry entry is supplied, so the registry ID is left null.

HB740.summary: The bill would increase mail-theft penalties based on the number of addressees and revise felony levels and an elderly-or-disabled-addressee enhancement for certain mail theft involving identifying information. It would also increase penalties for assaults against employees or contractors of common carriers or delivery services performing mail-delivery duties, and these changes would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes criminal offense classifications and penalties for mail theft and assaults against mail-delivery workers.
The bill adds enhanced criminal penalties for assaults against workers performing mail-delivery duties.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Penal Code provisions applicable to offenses committed in the state; it identifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Employees and contractors of common carriers or delivery services performing mail-delivery duties
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive the benefit of enhanced assault penalties when targeted while performing mail-delivery duties.

affected_groups.group: Mail addressees, including elderly or disabled individuals
affected_groups.explanation: Mail-theft offense levels depend on the number of addressees, and a specified enhancement applies when the actor knew or had reason to believe an addressee was elderly or disabled.

major_effects.label: Raises base mail-theft penalties
major_effects.explanation: The bill makes theft of mail from fewer than 10 addressees a state jail felony, theft from 10 to 29 a third-degree felony, and theft from 30 or more a second-degree felony.

major_effects.label: Revises penalties for certain identity-related mail theft
major_effects.explanation: When appropriated mail contains identifying information and the offense is intended to facilitate an offense under Section 32.51, the specified tiers are third degree for 10–19 addressees, second degree for 20–49, and first degree for 50 or more. The next-category enhancement for knowing or having reason to believe an addressee is elderly or disabled applies to the specified (d)(1) and (d)(2) categories.

major_effects.label: Enhances penalties for assaults against mail-delivery workers
major_effects.explanation: Assault against a qualifying mail-delivery employee or contractor while performing mail-related duties becomes a third-degree felony; the specified aggravated-assault circumstance makes the offense a first-degree felony.
