major_effects.explanation: If the jury recommends community supervision for an offense whose minimum prison term is increased under the bill, the judge must set a minimum supervision period of five years.

major_effects.label: Limits on deferred adjudication
major_effects.explanation: Adds covered listed felonies to the offenses for which deferred-adjudication community supervision is unavailable when the judge makes the specified firearm finding.

major_effects.label: Parole eligibility floor
major_effects.explanation: Sets a five-year minimum before parole eligibility for the specified sentences, while retaining a two-year floor for other offenses covered by the subsection; the subsection’s other eligibility calculation remains in place.

HB774.summary: The bill would cap contributions per election to candidates for statewide office or the Legislature, and to certain committees supporting or opposing them, at $5,000 for an individual contributor and $10,000 for a political committee. It would lower the aggregate amount a judicial candidate or officeholder may accept from a general-purpose committee for a statewide judicial election from $25,000 to $10,000; the changes apply only to contributions made on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes campaign contribution limits for candidates and committees in specified elections.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill covers candidates for statewide office and statewide judicial offices.

affected_groups.group: People contributing to candidates for statewide office or the Legislature
affected_groups.explanation: Their contributions would be subject to a $5,000 per-election limit.

affected_groups.group: Political committees and specific-purpose committees supporting or opposing covered candidates
affected_groups.explanation: Political committees would face a $10,000 per-election contribution limit, and specific-purpose committees are among the permitted recipients covered by the limits.

affected_groups.group: Judicial candidates and officeholders
affected_groups.explanation: For statewide judicial elections, the aggregate amount they may accept from a general-purpose committee would be reduced.

major_effects.label: Campaign contribution caps
major_effects.explanation: Sets per-election limits of $5,000 for contributors other than political committees and $10,000 for political committees for contributions to covered candidates or supporting/opposing specific-purpose committees. The changes apply to contributions made on or after the Act’s effective date.

major_effects.label: Lower limit for statewide judicial campaigns
major_effects.explanation: Reduces the aggregate contribution limit a judicial candidate or officeholder may accept from a general-purpose committee for a statewide judicial election from $25,000 to $10,000.

HB775.summary: The bill would require a county commissioners court to designate a polling place on the main campus of a qualifying general academic teaching institution in the county if the institution has at least 5,000 enrolled students. Personal-appearance voting at that location would be conducted during the same hours as voting at the main early voting polling place and on election day.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a requirement for campus polling-place designation and specifies voting hours at the designated location.
Assigns a polling-place designation duty to county commissioners courts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to counties across the state when a qualifying institution is located in the county.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Must designate the required campus polling place when the enrollment condition is met.

affected_groups.group: Students and other voters using qualifying campuses
affected_groups.explanation: Personal-appearance voting would be available at the designated campus polling place under the specified hours requirement.

affected_groups.group: General academic teaching institutions with at least 5,000 enrolled students
affected_groups.explanation: Their main campuses would be subject to the county polling-place designation requirement if located within the county.

major_effects.label: Campus polling-place designation
major_effects.explanation: Requires a county commissioners court to designate a polling place on the main campus of a qualifying institution in the county when at least 5,000 students are enrolled.

major_effects.label: Voting hours at designated campus locations
major_effects.explanation: Requires personal-appearance voting at a designated campus location during the same hours as voting at the main early voting polling place and on election day.

HB777.summary: HB 777 would extend the public-school self-administration framework to students with seizure disorders and prescribed anti-seizure medicine, subject to prescription, demonstrated-skill, and parent/provider documentation requirements. For seizure-disorder students, self-administration may follow the seizure management and treatment plan under Section 38.032; the Texas Education Agency would update and post the plan form to request self-administration instructions when applicable. The changes apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes public-school students' rights concerning possession and self-administration of prescription anti-seizure medicine and changes the required seizure-plan form.
Changes school-based administration requirements for prescribed anti-seizure medicine and information in students' seizure management plans.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes concern public schools statewide; the self-administration provisions apply on school property and at school-related events or activities.

affected_groups.group: Public-school students with seizure disorders
affected_groups.explanation: They would gain the specified entitlement to possess and self-administer prescribed anti-seizure medicine when the stated conditions are met.

affected_groups.group: Parents or guardians of students with seizure disorders
affected_groups.explanation: A parent must provide written authorization and a signed health-care-provider statement for student self-administration.

affected_groups.group: Public-school districts and personnel
affected_groups.explanation: They would use seizure plans that, when applicable, include instructions for a student's self-administration of anti-seizure medication.

major_effects.label: Student self-administration entitlement
major_effects.explanation: Extends the school-setting entitlement to students with seizure disorders for prescribed anti-seizure medicine, subject to the bill's conditions, including demonstrated ability and required parent/provider documentation.

major_effects.label: Seizure-plan form update
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Texas Education Agency to update and post the form, adding a request for anti-seizure self-administration instructions when applicable.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly requires the agency to update and post the seizure management and treatment plan form.

HB778.summary: The bill would treat a defendant as convicted for purposes of Code of Criminal Procedure Article 42.08(a) if the defendant was adjudged guilty or pleaded guilty or nolo contendere in return for deferred adjudication, even if no sentence was imposed or the defendant was later discharged from supervision. This changes which offenses may be considered when determining whether sentences run concurrently or consecutively, and applies only to offenses committed on or after the effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how convictions, including pleas resulting in deferred adjudication, are treated when determining whether sentences may run concurrently or consecutively.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas criminal procedure and establishes a sentencing rule for offenses governed by that law statewide.

affected_groups.group: Defendants whose sentences are subject to a concurrent-or-consecutive sentencing decision, including those with deferred-adjudication pleas
affected_groups.explanation: Their deferred-adjudication pleas would qualify as convictions for purposes of Article 42.08(a), even if the sentence was not imposed or supervision ended in discharge.

major_effects.label: Treatment of deferred-adjudication pleas in sentencing
major_effects.explanation: For purposes of Article 42.08(a), the bill counts a guilty or nolo contendere plea made in return for deferred adjudication as a conviction, regardless of whether a sentence was imposed or the defendant was later discharged from supervision. The change applies only to offenses committed on or after the effective date.

HB779.summary: HB 779 would add a population-based alternative to existing exemptions from specified public-beach lifeguard requirements. The added alternative covers municipalities with fewer than 1,000 residents located in a county with more than 32,000 and fewer than 40,000 residents, and counties with more than 32,000 and fewer than 40,000 residents; existing adjacency-based exemption criteria remain.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which municipalities and counties qualify for exemptions from statutory requirements.
The exemptions concern requirements for using lifeguards on public beaches.

locations.name: Municipalities and counties meeting the specified population criteria
locations.explanation: The added exemptions apply to municipalities in counties and counties within the stated population range.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities with fewer than 1,000 residents located in counties with populations over 32,000 and under 40,000
affected_groups.explanation: These municipalities would qualify for the added exemption from the specified lifeguard requirement.

affected_groups.group: County governments with populations over 32,000 and under 40,000
affected_groups.explanation: These counties would qualify for the added exemption from the specified lifeguard requirement.

major_effects.label: Adds population-based lifeguard exemptions
major_effects.explanation: Adds an alternative to existing adjacency-based exemptions for municipalities under 1,000 residents in counties with populations over 32,000 and under 40,000, and for counties in that population range.

HB780.summary: The bill adds an identification card from a Texas public institution of higher education to the acceptable forms of photo identification for voting. The card must be unexpired or have expired no more than four years before presentation, and must show the holder’s photograph, date of birth, and full legal name.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds a qualifying form of photo identification that voters may present.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The newly accepted identification must be issued by a public institution of higher education located in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Voters with identification cards from Texas public institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: They may use a qualifying card as acceptable photo identification when voting.

major_effects.label: Acceptable voting identification
major_effects.explanation: Adds qualifying Texas public higher education identification cards to the acceptable photo ID list, subject to the expiration and personal-information requirements.

HB781.summary: HB 781 would authorize commissioners courts in a county meeting specified population and geographic criteria to impose a hotel occupancy tax. The county tax rate could not exceed 7%, or 2% for hotels where specified municipal hotel taxes apply; revenue could also fund county airport repairs or improvements, subject to a 20-year revenue cap and cutoff.

policy_tags.explanation: Authorizes a qualifying county to impose a hotel occupancy tax and sets limits on its rate.
Gives a qualifying county authority to impose the tax and use some revenue for its airport.
Adds county airport repairs and improvements as an allowable use of the qualifying county's hotel-tax revenue.

locations.name: County meeting the criteria in Tax Code Section 352.002(a)(30)
locations.explanation: The bill defines the county eligible for the new tax authority by population and geographic features but does not name it.

locations.name: Guadalupe River
locations.explanation: The river is part of the geographic criterion defining the eligible county.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts in the county meeting the new criteria
affected_groups.explanation: They may choose by order or resolution to impose the hotel occupancy tax and may use qualifying revenue for airport work.

affected_groups.group: Hotels and people paying for hotel rooms in the qualifying county
affected_groups.explanation: The tax applies to qualifying hotel-room payments; lower county-rate limits apply at hotels where specified municipal taxes apply.

affected_groups.group: County airport operators and users
affected_groups.explanation: They may be affected by tax-funded airport repairs and improvements.

major_effects.label: New county hotel-tax authority
major_effects.explanation: Allows a commissioners court in the specifically defined county to impose a hotel occupancy tax; that county is excluded from the general Gulf-border county category.

major_effects.label: County hotel-tax rate limits
major_effects.explanation: Caps the county tax at 7%, with a 2% cap for hotels in a municipality with an applicable Chapter 351 tax or in a municipality's qualifying extraterritorial jurisdiction.

major_effects.label: Hotel-tax revenue for county airport work
major_effects.explanation: Allows revenue to fund or reimburse county airport repairs and improvements, limited in total to hotel revenue reasonably attributable to airport travelers over the 20-year period beginning with first use, and bars use after that period.

HB782.summary: The bill would allow voters to deliver mail-ballot applications in person to a registrar or volunteer deputy registrar by the existing application deadline, and would authorize deputies to distribute and accept those applications. It also sets application-routing duties, requires the secretary of state to update election-law training and adopt timely-delivery rules, and bars forwarding a mail-ballot application submitted with a voter-registration application until the registration application is accepted.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how voters may submit mail-ballot applications and how election officials distribute, receive, and route them.
Assigns application-handling duties to registrars and volunteer deputy registrars operating at the county level.

locations.name: Texas (statewide)
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Election Code and establishes procedures for use statewide.

affected_groups.group: Voters applying for a ballot to be voted by mail
affected_groups.explanation: May deliver an application in person to a registrar or volunteer deputy registrar by the existing deadline.

affected_groups.group: Registrars and volunteer deputy registrars
affected_groups.explanation: Receive, distribute, and route mail-ballot applications under the bill's new procedures.

major_effects.label: In-person application submission and distribution
major_effects.explanation: Allows eligible applicants to deliver a mail-ballot application in person to a registrar or volunteer deputy registrar; deputies may distribute and accept applications, and registrars or deputies may distribute official forms.

major_effects.label: Application routing and safeguard
major_effects.explanation: Requires deputy registrars to deliver applications to the registrar and registrars to route them to the early voting clerk; when a voter submits a registration application with the ballot application, forwarding is barred until the registration application is accepted.

major_effects.label: Statewide delivery rules and training standards
major_effects.explanation: Requires the secretary of state to adopt rules ensuring timely delivery and to include receipt of mail-ballot applications in election-law training standards.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The secretary of state must adopt rules for timely delivery and expand election-law training standards to cover receipt of mail-ballot applications.

HB783.summary: HB 783 would let judges determine reasonable court-coordinator compensation without commissioners court approval and require counties to fund that compensation through the county budget process. District-court judges would generally have to submit raise orders before budget adoption (unless the commissioners court permits otherwise); raises above 10% would require approval from each county served, subject to a compensation-increase cap for judges serving counties with at least one million people, and a newly appointed coordinator’s pay could not exceed the predecessor’s in the following fiscal year.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes county responsibilities and commissioners-court authority concerning court-coordinator compensation and county budget funding.
The bill changes how compensation for court coordinators is determined and limits judges’ authority to increase it.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The compensation rules apply generally to covered courts and counties across Texas; no particular county is named.

locations.name: Counties with a population of one million or more
locations.explanation: A population-based compensation-increase cap applies to district judges serving counties in this defined group.

affected_groups.group: Court coordinators
affected_groups.explanation: Their compensation is set by judges and is subject to limits on increases, including a first-year cap after a new appointment.

affected_groups.group: District and statutory county court judges
affected_groups.explanation: Judges determine reasonable coordinator compensation; district judges are subject to new procedures and limits for increases.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts and counties
affected_groups.explanation: Counties must provide funding through the county budget process for compensation determined under Subsection (a). Judges determine reasonable compensation; except as provided by Subsection (e), an increase exceeding 10% requires approval by the commissioners court of each county served.

major_effects.label: Judges determine coordinator compensation, with approval required for increases exceeding 10%
major_effects.explanation: The bill removes commissioners court approval from the general determination of reasonable compensation for court coordinators. However, a district court judge may increase annual compensation by more than 10% only if the commissioners court of each county served by the court approves the increase.

major_effects.label: County budget funding
major_effects.explanation: The county must provide, through its budget process, the funding necessary for compensation determined by the judges.

major_effects.label: Procedures and approval for raises
major_effects.explanation: A district judge generally must submit an order before the county budget is adopted, unless the commissioners court permits otherwise; increases above 10% require approval from each county served, subject to the population-based provision.

major_effects.label: Limits on coordinator pay increases
major_effects.explanation: For a judge serving a county with at least one million people, an increase may not exceed the average percentage increase in county-employee compensation in each served county of that size; in the fiscal year after a new appointment, pay may not exceed the predecessor’s compensation.

agencies.name: district or statutory county court judges
agencies.explanation: The bill directly changes judges’ authority over court-coordinator compensation, but refers only to generic court types rather than identifying a particular court or registry body.

HB784.summary: For specified criminal proceedings, the bill raises from younger than 13 to younger than 18 the age threshold for applying Code of Criminal Procedure Article 38.071 when a court determines a child would be unavailable to testify in the defendant’s presence. The change applies only to proceedings that commence on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which child witnesses qualify for a criminal-procedure article in proceedings concerning specified offenses.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The amendment is to the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure and applies to qualifying proceedings statewide.

affected_groups.group: Child witnesses younger than 18
affected_groups.explanation: Children in proceedings involving the listed offenses may fall within Article 38.071’s scope at the higher age threshold if the court determines they would be unavailable to testify in the defendant’s presence.

affected_groups.group: Criminal defendants in proceedings involving the listed offenses
affected_groups.explanation: The change concerns whether Article 38.071 applies in proceedings where a child is determined unavailable to testify in the defendant’s presence.

major_effects.label: Raises the age threshold for Article 38.071 applicability
major_effects.explanation: Extends the covered age range from children younger than 13 to children younger than 18, when the court determines the child would be unavailable to testify in the defendant’s presence and the proceeding concerns a listed offense.

HB786.summary: The bill would require the State Board of Education, in consultation with the Texas School Safety Center, to add evidence-based instruction on bullying and harassment and on bodily autonomy to the required health curriculum. The changes would apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required health-curriculum content for public school students.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The curriculum change applies to Texas public school students beginning with the specified school year.

affected_groups.group: Public school students
affected_groups.explanation: Students would receive the added required health-curriculum instruction.

affected_groups.group: Public school curriculum authorities and educators
affected_groups.explanation: They would implement the additional required health-curriculum content.

major_effects.label: Adds required health-curriculum content
major_effects.explanation: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt evidence-based health-curriculum skills addressing bullying and harassment and instruction on bodily autonomy.

agencies.name: State Board of Education
agencies.explanation: The board must adopt the specified essential knowledge and skills for the health curriculum.

agencies.name: Texas School Safety Center
agencies.explanation: The board's curriculum adoption must be in consultation with the Center, suggesting a substantive consultation role; the bill does not specify a separate duty for the Center.

HB787.summary: If voters approve the required constitutional amendment, a county commissioners court may adopt an exemption for the part of a property's appraised value attributable to installing a rainwater harvesting or graywater system; the exemption applies to every taxing unit that taxes the property. The bill applies to tax years beginning on or after its effective date and has no effect if voters reject the amendment.

policy_tags.explanation: Authorizes a property-tax exemption for the value attributable to specified water conservation systems, if the required constitutional amendment is approved.
Gives county commissioners courts authority to adopt the exemption, which applies across taxing units taxing the property.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The authority is framed for the commissioners court of any county, with no narrower geographic area specified; it is conditional on voter approval of the constitutional amendment.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: May choose by order whether to adopt the exemption, if the required amendment is approved.

affected_groups.group: Property owners with rainwater harvesting or graywater systems
affected_groups.explanation: May receive an exemption for the portion of appraised value attributable to installing a qualifying system in or on their property.

affected_groups.group: Taxing units that tax qualifying property
affected_groups.explanation: The exemption adopted by a commissioners court applies to each taxing unit that taxes the property.

major_effects.label: County authority to adopt an exemption
major_effects.explanation: If voters approve the required constitutional amendment, the Act takes effect January 1, 2028, and a county commissioners court may adopt the exemption by order. If voters do not approve the amendment, the Act has no effect.

major_effects.label: Optional property-tax exemption for qualifying systems
major_effects.explanation: The exemption covers only the portion of appraised value attributable to installing a rainwater harvesting or graywater system and applies to all taxing units taxing the property; it has no effect if voters reject the amendment.

HB788.summary: The bill would let a county commissioners court, by order, require county approval for constructing or reconstructing a commercial sign adjacent to and visible from four specified Ranch-to-Market Roads. When such approval is required, the department could not issue a permit under the chapter unless the person has obtained it.

policy_tags.explanation: Counties would gain authority to require approval for certain commercial signs.
The approval and permit conditions apply to commercial signs along specified roads and permits under the Transportation Code chapter.
The bill would add a county approval requirement for construction or reconstruction of certain commercial signs.

locations.name: Ranch-to-Market Road 12
locations.explanation: The bill applies to signs adjacent to and visible from this road.

locations.name: Ranch-to-Market Road 150
locations.explanation: The bill applies to signs adjacent to and visible from this road.

locations.name: Ranch-to-Market Road 967
locations.explanation: The bill applies to signs adjacent to and visible from this road.

locations.name: Ranch-to-Market Road 1826
locations.explanation: The bill applies to signs adjacent to and visible from this road.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: A commissioners court could choose by order whether to require county approval for qualifying signs.

affected_groups.group: People constructing or reconstructing commercial signs along the specified roads
affected_groups.explanation: They may need county approval if the county adopts an order, and the department could not issue the chapter permit without that required approval.

major_effects.label: County approval authority
major_effects.explanation: A county commissioners court could require approval by order for commercial sign construction or reconstruction adjacent to and visible from the listed roads.

major_effects.label: Permit conditioned on required county approval
major_effects.explanation: If county approval is required under the section, the department could not issue a chapter permit until the person obtains that approval.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The department may not issue a chapter permit when the applicant is required to obtain county approval under this section unless the applicant has obtained that approval.

HB789.summary: The bill would require the commissioner to establish and administer grants to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools for training educators and administrators in best practices for teaching historically underserved students. Grant funds could be used only for that training, and the act would apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a grant program for training public school educators and administrators.
Creates a state-administered grant program that awards money to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools.
School districts are eligible recipients of the grant funds.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The grant program is established in state law for school districts and open-enrollment charter schools, without a narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: They may apply for and receive grants under the program.

affected_groups.group: Public school educators and administrators
affected_groups.explanation: The grants are limited to providing them training on best practices for teaching historically underserved students.

affected_groups.group: Historically underserved students
affected_groups.explanation: They are the intended beneficiaries of the training supported by the grant program.

major_effects.label: Educator training grant program
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commissioner to establish and administer grants to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools for the specified training.

major_effects.label: Grant program rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules covering applicant eligibility, application procedures, and grant-amount guidelines.

major_effects.label: Restricted grant use
major_effects.explanation: Grant money may be used only for the specified educator and administrator training.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commissioner responsibility for establishing, administering, and making rules for the grant program, but the supplied text does not identify the commissioner's canonical agency.

HB790.summary: HB 790 would add an intent requirement to two parts of the definition of a diversity, equity, and inclusion office, narrowing which offices meet that definition. It would remove the grant-or-accreditation context from the provision protecting support for first-generation, low-income, and underserved students, while deleting the separate express protection for statements certifying compliance with antidiscrimination laws.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes rules governing diversity, equity, and inclusion offices and student support at institutions of higher education.
Alters the statutory definition of covered offices in provisions addressing race- and sex-related hiring practices and differential treatment.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to covered institutions of higher education across Texas, rather than to a named place.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education and their employees
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes the definition used in rules governing DEI offices and revises what the section protects institutions and employees from being limited or prohibited from doing.

affected_groups.group: First-generation, low-income, and underserved students
affected_groups.explanation: The revised provision expressly protects institutional support for these student groups.

major_effects.label: Narrowed DEI-office definition
major_effects.explanation: Adds an intent requirement to the definition's hiring-practices and differential-treatment clauses; the other listed parts of the definition are not changed.

major_effects.label: Revised protection for student support
major_effects.explanation: Removes the grant-or-accreditation context from the protection for supporting the listed student groups and deletes the separate express protection for statements certifying compliance with antidiscrimination laws.

HB791.summary: For reports required to be filed on or after January 1, 2028, candidates and officeholders required to file with the Texas Ethics Commission must file electronically if, in a calendar year, their political contributions or political expenditures exceed $25,000 in aggregate. The requirement does not apply to candidates or officeholders for judicial offices subject to Subchapter F, Chapter 253.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the filing method for certain political contribution and expenditure reports.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The Election Code filing requirement applies statewide to covered candidates and officeholders.

affected_groups.group: Candidates and officeholders required to file reports with the Texas Ethics Commission
affected_groups.explanation: They must file electronically when their calendar-year political contributions or expenditures exceed $25,000 in aggregate.

affected_groups.group: Candidates and officeholders for judicial offices subject to Subchapter F, Chapter 253
affected_groups.explanation: They are excluded from the new electronic filing requirement.

major_effects.label: Electronic filing above a contribution or expenditure threshold
major_effects.explanation: Covered candidates and officeholders must file electronically if their contributions or expenditures exceed $25,000 in aggregate during a calendar year; the requirement excludes the specified judicial offices and applies to reports required on or after January 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Texas Ethics Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directs certain candidates and officeholders to submit reports electronically to the commission, changing the filing method for reports it receives.

HB792.summary: HB 792 would require the Commission on Jail Standards to study living conditions and safety in the Harris County jail and report its findings and recommendations to the Legislature by December 1, 2028. The Act would expire September 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires a study of conditions and safety for people confined in a county jail.

locations.name: Harris County
locations.explanation: The study concerns the Harris County jail; the bill does not identify a more specific site.

affected_groups.group: People confined in the Harris County jail
affected_groups.explanation: Their living conditions and safety are the subject of the required study.

major_effects.label: Jail conditions study and legislative report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Commission on Jail Standards to evaluate jail living conditions and safety and submit study results and recommendations to the Legislature.

agencies.name: Commission on Jail Standards
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the Commission the study and reporting duties. No canonical registry entry is supported by the supplied registry.

HB793.summary: The bill would require the Railroad Commission of Texas to require owners or operators of its jurisdictional oil or gas pipelines constructed or expanded in the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone to submit and comply with water pollution abatement plans. This requirement would apply only when construction or expansion begins on or after the Act’s effective date. The bill also directs the Railroad Commission and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to adopt related practices and a joint consultation process, authorizes limited plan-review and inspection fees, and makes the new requirements enforceable through existing remedies, subject to the conditions provided in Chapters 81 and 85.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates water pollution abatement plan requirements and water-protection practices for certain pipelines in the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone.
Regulates construction, expansion, and operation of certain oil or gas pipelines.
Imposes plan-submission and compliance duties, and may authorize fees, for affected pipeline owners or operators.

locations.name: Edwards Aquifer recharge zone
locations.explanation: The plan requirements apply to covered pipelines constructed or expanded in this area.

affected_groups.group: Owners or operators of Railroad Commission-jurisdiction oil or gas pipelines in the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone
affected_groups.explanation: For qualifying new construction or expansion, they must submit and comply with a water pollution abatement plan and may be subject to plan-review or inspection fees.

major_effects.label: Water pollution abatement plans
major_effects.explanation: Requires owners or operators of oil or gas pipelines subject to the Railroad Commission’s jurisdiction and constructed or expanded in the recharge zone to submit and comply with plans; applies only when construction or expansion begins on or after the Act’s effective date.

major_effects.label: Water-protection practices and agency coordination
major_effects.explanation: Directs the Railroad Commission, in consultation with TCEQ, to adopt temporary best management practices by rule, and requires the agencies to establish a joint consultation process and implementation memorandum of understanding by rule.

major_effects.label: Plan and inspection fees
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes, but does not require, the Railroad Commission to impose fees for plan processing and pipeline inspection, subject to the manner and limitations provided by Section 26.0461.

major_effects.label: Enforcement of new requirements
major_effects.explanation: Extends the Railroad Commission’s enforcement authority to Section 26.136 and rules adopted under it, including existing civil-penalty and injunctive-relief remedies.

major_effects.label: Aquifer boundary information
major_effects.explanation: Requires digital boundary-line copies, when available, to be made available to the Railroad Commission for administering the new section, in addition to the public.

agencies.name: Railroad Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: Must require plans for owners or operators of oil or gas pipelines subject to its jurisdiction and constructed or expanded in the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone. It may impose fees for processing a water pollution abatement plan or amendment only when the plan or amendment is subject to review and approval under rules adopted under this section; it may also charge for inspecting covered pipeline construction and maintenance.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: Must consult with the Railroad Commission on temporary best management practices and jointly develop a consultation process and adopt an implementation memorandum of understanding by rule.

HB794.summary: The bill would create an offense for a person age 17 or older who fails to report a defined sexual offense against a child and also engages in conduct intended to hinder its investigation or prosecution. The offense would generally be a third-degree felony, elevated to a second-degree felony if the failure to report enables or facilitates the offender’s subsequent sexual offense against a child; specified identities would remain confidential until charges are filed. The change would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a felony offense for specified conduct that hinders investigation or prosecution of sexual offenses against children.
Makes specified names confidential and exempt from public disclosure until charges are filed.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Penal Code without limiting the offense to a particular area.

affected_groups.group: People age 17 or older who fail to report and hinder investigation or prosecution
affected_groups.explanation: They could be subject to the new felony offense when both elements are met.

affected_groups.group: Children who are victims of the specified sexual offenses
affected_groups.explanation: Their names would be confidential under the new provision.

major_effects.label: New felony offense
major_effects.explanation: Creates a third-degree felony for qualifying failure to report combined with intentional hindering; the offense becomes a second-degree felony if the failure enables or facilitates a subsequent sexual offense against a child.

major_effects.label: Confidentiality of specified identities
major_effects.explanation: Protects the child victim’s name, the actor’s name until the actor is charged, and the suspected offender’s name until that person is charged with the applicable offense.

HB795.summary: HB 795 would allow motorcycle operators to travel between lanes of same-direction traffic for a safe distance and to pass a stopped or very slow vehicle in its lane, but only under specified highway, speed, and safety conditions. It also expressly leaves in place the prohibition on passing a school bus in a manner barred by existing law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes rules governing motorcycle movement and passing on roadways.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Transportation Code rules governing roadway conduct.

affected_groups.group: Motorcycle operators
affected_groups.explanation: Would gain conditional authority to travel between same-direction lanes and pass a motor vehicle in the same lane subject to the stated only-if conditions, including being on a divided highway with at least two lanes of traffic in each direction.

affected_groups.group: Operators of other motor vehicles
affected_groups.explanation: Their roadway interactions with motorcycles would be affected by rules entitling motorcycles to full use of a lane except as otherwise provided by Subdivision (2), which includes same-lane passing only if its stated conditions are met.

major_effects.label: Conditional motorcycle lane travel and passing
major_effects.explanation: Allows travel between same-direction traffic lanes for a safe distance and same-lane passing only on a divided highway with at least two lanes in each direction, when the passed vehicle is stopped or moving at no more than 10 mph, the motorcycle is moving at no more than 20 mph, and the pass is safe. This does not authorize passing a school bus contrary to existing law.

HB796.summary: The bill would establish a consortium of eligible in-state historically Black colleges and universities to provide civic education to Texas residents at no cost to students. It would create a grant program, using money appropriated or otherwise available, to support the consortium and its community partners, with offerings directed to urban and rural communities statewide. The bill also provides for oversight and evaluation of the consortium, and applies beginning with the 2027-2028 academic year.

policy_tags.explanation: Establishes a higher-education consortium and grant program to provide civic education.
Creates a state grant program funded from money appropriated or otherwise available for the purpose.
Municipalities and counties are identified as possible community partners and must be represented on the oversight committee.
Establishes a committee to monitor the consortium and grant program and evaluate the civic education provided.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: Civic education under the grant program must be available across Texas, with resources directed to urban and rural communities.

affected_groups.group: Texas residents and students
affected_groups.explanation: Residents are the intended recipients of civic education, which must be provided at no cost to students.

affected_groups.group: Eligible in-state historically Black colleges and universities
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible colleges and universities may participate in the consortium and receive grants to provide civic education.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities, counties, community organizations, and public libraries
affected_groups.explanation: These entities are among the possible community partners for grant recipients; municipalities and counties are also represented on the oversight committee.

major_effects.label: Civic education consortium and grants
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a consortium of eligible colleges and universities and a grant program for no-cost civic education, including through community partnerships.

major_effects.label: Grant funding
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes grants from money appropriated or otherwise available for the purpose, with specified permitted uses related to civic education.

major_effects.label: Progress reporting and evaluation
major_effects.explanation: Grant recipients must regularly report progress, and the consortium must arrange independent evaluation on the oversight committee’s evaluation schedule.

major_effects.label: Program oversight
major_effects.explanation: Requires an oversight committee to monitor the consortium and grant implementation, evaluate civic education, and approve consortium recommendations before related grant funds may be spent.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: Texas Education Code Section 61.003 defines “Board” as the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board. The bill assigns the board grant-program and oversight-committee responsibilities.

HB797.summary: The bill would require the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to set maximum ground-level hydrogen sulfide concentrations, with different limits depending on the use of affected downwind property. It would also require the commission to review health studies and reevaluate the limits at least every five years, and to classify violations as having major significance under the Water Code.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill would establish regulatory limits on hydrogen sulfide emissions and require review of those limits.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The proposed concentration standards are statewide in scope, applying to regulated hydrogen sulfide emissions and affected properties.

affected_groups.group: People using downwind property for residential, recreational, business, or commercial purposes
affected_groups.explanation: The bill sets a concentration ceiling for emissions when downwind concentrations affect property used for these purposes.

affected_groups.group: Operators of sources emitting hydrogen sulfide
affected_groups.explanation: Operators would be subject to the concentration limits established under the bill.

major_effects.label: Hydrogen sulfide concentration limits
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules establishing maximum allowable ground-level concentrations, with statutory ceilings that vary according to the use of affected downwind property.

major_effects.label: Periodic review of concentration limits
major_effects.explanation: Requires review of the latest health studies and reevaluation of the maximum allowable concentrations at least once every five years.

major_effects.label: Classification of violations
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to classify violations of the established limits as having major significance under the cited Water Code provision.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission duties to establish and periodically reevaluate concentration limits and classify violations; the bill identifies the commission as the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality.

HB798.summary: HB 798 would add any six-hour alcohol awareness program approved by the court as an option for minors placed on deferred disposition for listed offenses, and make the Section 106.115 program options apply to completion requirements following a minor’s conviction. In specified community-supervision and juvenile proceedings, it would remove an express TDLR-regulation qualification for alcohol awareness programs described by Section 106.115.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes court-ordered program options and conditions in criminal, community-supervision, and juvenile proceedings.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes and the changes apply statewide.

affected_groups.group: Minors placed on deferred disposition or convicted of the listed offenses
affected_groups.explanation: They may be required to complete a court-approved program from the expanded set of options; for repeat convictions, the court may require completion.

affected_groups.group: Defendants younger than 18 on community supervision and children in juvenile proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: Courts may use the Section 106.115 program options in specified supervision, deferred-prosecution, and adjudication proceedings.

affected_groups.group: Providers of court-approved alcohol awareness programs
affected_groups.explanation: Six-hour programs may be approved by a court as an additional option under the amended provisions.

major_effects.label: Adds a court-approved six-hour program option
major_effects.explanation: For the specified deferred-disposition cases, the court may require one of the listed programs, including any six-hour alcohol awareness program it approves.

major_effects.label: Applies the expanded options to conviction-related requirements
major_effects.explanation: A minor without a prior conviction must complete a program described by Section 106.115; for a minor with a prior conviction, the court may require one.

major_effects.label: Removes an express TDLR-regulation qualification
major_effects.explanation: Specified community-supervision and juvenile provisions no longer include the express requirement that Section 106.115 alcohol awareness programs be regulated by TDLR.

major_effects.label: Repeals two alcohol-awareness-program subsections
major_effects.explanation: The bill repeals subsections 106.115(b-1) and (b-2), but their contents are not included in the supplied text, so their specific effects cannot be determined here.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The bill deletes express requirements that certain alcohol awareness programs described by Section 106.115 be regulated by TDLR. The separate TDLR regulation requirement for substance misuse education remains in the cited provisions.

HB799.summary: HB 799 would require a county commissioners court to designate a polling place on the main campus of each general academic teaching institution in the county with at least 8,000 students enrolled. In-person voting at that location would have to be conducted during the same hours as voting at the main early voting polling place and on election day.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill requires a campus polling place for certain institutions and specifies voting hours there.
The bill assigns county commissioners courts a polling-place designation duty.

locations.name: Statewide, at qualifying campuses
locations.explanation: The requirement applies in any county containing a qualifying institution.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: They would be required to designate the campus polling place.

affected_groups.group: General academic teaching institutions with at least 8,000 students enrolled
affected_groups.explanation: Their main campuses would receive a designated polling place if located in the county.

affected_groups.group: Voters using designated campus polling places
affected_groups.explanation: In-person voting at those locations would be conducted during specified hours.

major_effects.label: Campus polling place designation
major_effects.explanation: County commissioners courts would have to designate a main-campus polling place in counties with an institution meeting the enrollment threshold.

major_effects.label: Voting hours at designated locations
major_effects.explanation: In-person voting at a location designated under this section must be conducted during the same hours as voting at the main early voting polling place and on election day.

HB801.summary: HB 801 would revise building-code rules for new construction in the unincorporated areas of counties covered by Subchapter F: except as provided by Subsection (b-1), residential construction would use the January 1, 2025 International Residential Code, and commercial construction the January 1, 2025 International Building Code. The definitions include certain additions or renovations that increase a building’s square footage or value by more than 50 percent; counties could adopt newer or stricter codes, charge enforcement fees, and would have to provide notice and public input opportunities for code changes. The changes would apply to construction commencing on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Revises building-code standards and inspection requirements for covered residential and commercial construction.
Authorizes counties to apply later versions of specified building codes, charge fees to defray enforcement costs, and adopt rules to administer and enforce the standards.

locations.name: Unincorporated areas of counties to which Subchapter F applies
locations.explanation: The building-code requirements apply in these unincorporated areas; the bill does not name the counties.

affected_groups.group: County governments and commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Counties may establish standards for new construction that exceed specified codes, and commissioners courts may adopt rules to administer and enforce those standards.

affected_groups.group: Builders of residential construction and general contractors for commercial construction
affected_groups.explanation: Covered projects are subject to inspections, and the bill specifies who must arrange inspections when a county does not use its own certified inspector.

affected_groups.group: People affected by proposed county building-code changes
affected_groups.explanation: They may provide testimony, and five or more written requests require a public hearing.

major_effects.label: Covered construction and code standards
major_effects.explanation: Applies the specified 2025 residential and building codes to covered construction. The definitions also include certain additions or renovations that increase square footage or value by more than 50 percent.

major_effects.label: County code-setting authority
major_effects.explanation: Commissioners courts may adopt later editions of either code or establish standards that exceed the codes’ standards.

major_effects.label: County enforcement fees
major_effects.explanation: A county may charge a fee to cover the cost of enforcing the subchapter’s standards.

major_effects.label: Code-adoption notice and public input
major_effects.explanation: Requires advance website notice and public testimony opportunities; a public hearing is required only if five or more people request one in writing.

major_effects.label: Inspections for residential and commercial construction
major_effects.explanation: Requires inspections for covered new construction. A county may use an ICC-certified building inspector to review plans and inspect, or require the applicable residential builder or commercial general contractor to contract for inspections with specified qualified inspectors.

major_effects.label: Residential inspection notices
major_effects.explanation: When a county requires it, the builder must report the final inspection’s compliance status for new residential construction. The bill does not impose that notice requirement for new commercial construction.

HB802.summary: The bill updates the residential and commercial building-code baselines adopted for Texas municipalities from versions in effect on May 1, 2012, to versions in effect on May 1, 2025; municipalities may review and consider later amendments. The changes apply only to covered construction or related work that begins under an agreement made on or after January 1, 2028, or, without an agreement, begins on or after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the editions of residential and commercial building codes adopted for municipal use.
The bill changes municipal building-code requirements and directs municipalities to take implementation actions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adopts the codes as municipal building codes in this state.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Municipalities must establish rules and take other actions to implement the revised code provisions.

affected_groups.group: Participants in residential and commercial construction and related work
affected_groups.explanation: The revised provisions govern covered construction and related work that begins on or after the specified 2028 threshold; earlier work remains governed by the law applicable when the agreement was made or the activity began.

major_effects.label: Updated municipal code baselines
major_effects.explanation: The adopted residential and commercial code editions are updated to those in effect on May 1, 2025; municipalities may review and consider later amendments.

major_effects.label: Municipal implementation
major_effects.explanation: Municipalities must establish rules and take other necessary implementation actions by December 1, 2027.

major_effects.label: Applicability transition
major_effects.explanation: The amended provisions apply to covered work beginning under agreements made on or after January 1, 2028, or beginning on or after that date without an agreement; earlier work remains governed by the law applicable at the relevant time.

HB803.summary: The bill requires the Texas Department of Criminal Justice to adopt indoor-temperature standards and emergency procedures for covered correctional facility buildings, with priority protections for medical units and certain inmates. For facilities that do not comply, the department must publish an implementation plan and submit an annual compliance report to the Legislature.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes temperature conditions and emergency procedures in correctional facilities.
The bill assigns the department new policy, implementation-planning, and compliance-reporting duties.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The policy applies to each covered department-operated or contracted correctional facility building, without limiting the requirement to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Inmates in covered correctional facilities, especially elderly, disabled, and pregnant inmates
affected_groups.explanation: The policy must prioritize heating and cooling in medical units and units housing specified groups of inmates.

affected_groups.group: Department staff, contractors, and visitors at covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The temperature policy covers buildings regularly used by these groups as well as inmates.

major_effects.label: Temperature standards and emergency response
major_effects.explanation: Requires a reasonable indoor temperature range, adequate heating and cooling, priority for specified units, and emergency measures when temperatures are outside the range.

major_effects.label: Facility implementation plans and compliance reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires public implementation plans for facilities that do not comply, including needed improvements, estimated costs, and timelines, plus an annual report to the Legislature on compliance and plan updates.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: The department must adopt the temperature policy, publish implementation plans for noncompliant facilities, and report compliance to the Legislature.

HB804.summary: HB 804 would revise eligibility for Agriculture Code grants by changing the required collection and transportation program to serve food banks in Texas, rather than a statewide network of food banks. It would also require grant recipients to make surplus agricultural products and other grant resources available to qualifying Texas-headquartered food banks.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes eligibility and resource-distribution conditions for grants involving surplus agricultural products.
The bill changes conditions for receiving grants and requires recipients to make grant resources available to qualifying food banks.

locations.name: Statewide in Texas
locations.explanation: The eligibility and resource-sharing conditions refer to food banks in Texas and food banks headquartered in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Nonprofit organizations seeking or receiving Chapter 21 grants
affected_groups.explanation: Subject to available funds, nonprofit organizations may qualify for Chapter 21 grants under the specified eligibility conditions; organizations that receive grants must make the specified resources available to food banks.

affected_groups.group: Texas-headquartered food banks with truckload storage capacity
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying food banks must be offered surplus products and other grant resources.

affected_groups.group: Local food programs
affected_groups.explanation: They are the recipients of agricultural products distributed free by qualifying food banks.

major_effects.label: Revised grant eligibility criteria
major_effects.explanation: The required collection and transportation program would serve food banks in Texas rather than a statewide network of food banks.

major_effects.label: Required sharing of grant resources with qualifying food banks
major_effects.explanation: Grant recipients would have to make surplus products and other grant resources available to Texas-headquartered food banks that meet the capacity and free-distribution conditions.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Agriculture
agencies.explanation: The bill changes eligibility conditions for grants awarded by the Department of Agriculture under Chapter 21.

HB805.summary: The proposed Act would create a temporary task force to study legal and societal barriers to equality for transgender people in Texas and recommend state actions, including in areas such as health care, education, housing, employment, and criminal justice. State agencies would have to assist the task force, the Texas Workforce Commission civil rights division would provide administrative support at its request, and the task force would report its findings and recommendations before being abolished on September 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a task force specifically to study barriers to transgender equality and recommend solutions; it does not itself change substantive rights.
Establishes a temporary state task force, assigns administrative support and cooperation duties, and requires a report to state officials.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The task force studies barriers and recommends state actions concerning transgender people in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Transgender people in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: They are the population whose equality and circumstances the task force would study.

affected_groups.group: State agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Named agencies supply task force representatives, and state agencies generally must assist the task force.

affected_groups.group: Task force members
affected_groups.explanation: Members would serve on the temporary task force and may receive reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses, but are not entitled to compensation for service.

major_effects.label: Temporary transgender equality task force
major_effects.explanation: Creates a task force to study barriers to equality and state actions that could improve transgender people's lives; it is abolished on September 1, 2029.

major_effects.label: Findings and recommendations report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the task force to submit a written report to the governor and legislature by December 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: Agency cooperation and administrative support
major_effects.explanation: Requires state agencies to assist the task force and assigns administrative support to the Texas Workforce Commission civil rights division when requested.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Banking
agencies.explanation: A representative of the department is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: A representative of the department is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Department of Family and Protective Services
agencies.explanation: A representative of the department is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Insurance
agencies.explanation: A representative of the department is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: A representative of the department is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: A representative of the agency is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: A representative of the commission is included in the task force composition.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The task force includes a representative from the commission's division of workforce development.

agencies.name: TWC Civil Rights Division
agencies.explanation: The division is represented on the task force and must provide administrative support at the task force's request.

HB806.summary: The bill would prohibit intentional or knowing transfers of semiautomatic rifles to people younger than 21, and of other firearms, clubs, or location-restricted knives to children younger than 18. The parental-permission defense would apply only to the under-18 category, and transferring a semiautomatic rifle to someone younger than 21 would be a state jail felony.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes age-based restrictions on transfers of firearms and other weapons.
The bill makes the specified semiautomatic-rifle transfer offense a state jail felony.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Penal Code and would apply statewide.

affected_groups.group: People younger than 21
affected_groups.explanation: They would be prohibited recipients of semiautomatic rifles under the bill's transfer offense.

affected_groups.group: Children younger than 18 and their parents or legal custodians
affected_groups.explanation: The bill addresses transfers to children under 18 and limits the parental-permission defense to that category.

affected_groups.group: People who sell, rent, lease, lend, give, or offer to transfer the covered weapons
affected_groups.explanation: The amended offense applies to intentional or knowing covered transfers or offers.

major_effects.label: Age-based weapon-transfer restrictions
major_effects.explanation: It would make covered intentional or knowing transfers to children younger than 18 an offense, except that semiautomatic rifles are addressed separately for recipients younger than 21. The parental-permission defense applies only to the under-18 category.

major_effects.label: Felony penalty for semiautomatic-rifle transfers to people under 21
major_effects.explanation: An offense under the new semiautomatic-rifle recipient provision would be a state jail felony.

HB807.summary: HB 807 would bar employers from asking about an applicant’s criminal history on the initial employment application. Employers could inquire into or consider that information only after determining the applicant is otherwise qualified and either conditionally offering employment or inviting the applicant to an interview; the restrictions would not apply when law requires consideration of criminal history.

policy_tags.explanation: Sets when employers may ask about or consider applicants’ criminal history during hiring.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill adds the restriction to the Texas Labor Code.

affected_groups.group: Employment applicants
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants would not be asked about criminal history on the initial application and would be subject to the later-stage timing rule, except where consideration is required by law.

affected_groups.group: Employers
affected_groups.explanation: Employers would be restricted in when they may ask about or consider an applicant’s criminal history.

major_effects.label: Delay criminal-history screening in hiring
major_effects.explanation: Bars criminal-history questions on initial employment application forms and permits inquiry or consideration only after the applicant is otherwise qualified and has received a conditional offer or an interview invitation. The restriction excludes positions for which consideration is required by law.

HB808.summary: HB 808 would require covered employers in Texas to provide paid sick leave that accrues at one hour per 30 hours worked and generally becomes usable after 60 days for reasons specified in the bill. It would establish a Texas Workforce Commission complaint process and protections against retaliation. The requirement applies to employees hired on or after January 1, 2028; employees hired earlier begin accruing leave then and generally may use it 90 days later unless the employer allows earlier use.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a paid sick leave entitlement and related workplace protections and enforcement requirements for covered employees.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The leave entitlement applies to employees in this state.

affected_groups.group: Employees of covered employers
affected_groups.explanation: Covered employees would accrue paid sick leave and may use accrued leave 60 calendar days after hire, unless the employer agrees to an earlier date, subject to the bill's other limits.

affected_groups.group: Employers engaged in an industry affecting commerce with one or more employees
affected_groups.explanation: Covered employers must provide qualifying paid leave, maintain records, give employee notices, and comply with the bill's protections and enforcement provisions.

major_effects.label: Paid sick leave entitlement
major_effects.explanation: Requires annual paid sick leave accruing at one hour per 30 hours worked, with specified permitted uses. Qualifying other paid leave can satisfy the requirement; a collective bargaining agreement may waive it through clear and unambiguous language, while agreements effective before January 1, 2028, are not preempted.

major_effects.label: Employer records and employee notices
major_effects.explanation: Requires employers to retain paid sick leave accrual and use records. Each employer subject to this chapter must provide hiring notices in English and Spanish describing leave entitlement, amount, and terms of use; additional-language notice is required when the stated workforce-language threshold is met.

major_effects.label: Commission implementation
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Texas Workforce Commission to prescribe the required notice and adopt rules to implement the chapter.

major_effects.label: Protection against retaliation
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits retaliation or discrimination against employees for requesting or using qualifying leave or filing a complaint.

major_effects.label: Complaint enforcement and remedies
major_effects.explanation: Provides for Commission investigations and administrative penalties, a civil penalty for willful violations, and employee civil actions to enforce the chapter.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the commission as the Texas Workforce Commission and assigns it complaint investigation, notice, rulemaking, and public information duties.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The attorney general is authorized to bring an action to collect the bill's civil penalty.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: District courts may hear appeals from Commission decisions and employee civil actions enforcing the new rights.

HB809.summary: HB 809 would require a judge discharging a person from felony community supervision, and the department for covered inmates and state jail defendants completing their sentences, to give written notice that the person may be eligible to register to vote. The requirements would apply only when a sentence is fully discharged or court-ordered probation is completed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates written notice requirements about potential eligibility to register to vote.
Adds notice duties tied to felony community supervision and completion of sentences by inmates and state jail defendants.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends state law and contains no narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: People discharged from felony community supervision
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive written notice that they may be eligible to register to vote.

affected_groups.group: Inmates and state jail defendants completing their sentences
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive the notice upon sentence completion, including completion of parole or mandatory supervision.

major_effects.label: Written notice about potential voter-registration eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Requires notice from the discharging judge for covered felony community-supervision defendants and from the department for covered offenders completing sentences; it does not itself determine eligibility or register anyone to vote.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department a written-notice duty for covered offenders. The supplied text does not identify the department by its canonical name.

HB810.summary: HB 810 would add protections against discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity or expression in public accommodations, employment, and housing. The public-accommodations chapter generally would not apply to religious organizations, except for qualifying for-profit activities subject to federal taxation, and it includes an exception for specified supportive services; the bill also authorizes civil remedies and extends specified housing-related intimidation offenses to these grounds. State agencies would have to require state contractors to adopt employment policies barring this discrimination, with administrative penalties after notice; that requirement applies to contracts first solicited on or after the Act's effective date, while the Labor Code and Property Code changes apply to later conduct and complaints, respectively.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds sexual orientation and gender identity or expression as protected grounds in public accommodations, employment, and housing, with civil remedies for public-accommodation violations.
Extends employment protections to employees and applicants across employers, employment agencies, labor organizations, and training programs.
Adds the protected grounds to prohibitions concerning dwelling sales and rentals and related real-estate services.
Expands the discrimination grounds relevant to local commissions and limits referrals of certain housing complaints to municipalities lacking applicable protections.
Extends an existing offense involving force or threats in specified housing-related contexts to intimidation based on the added protected grounds.
Sets employment-policy requirements for state contracts and requires state agencies to develop procedures to administer those requirements.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The public-accommodations prohibition expressly applies in this state, and the bill amends statewide Texas law.

affected_groups.group: People seeking or using public accommodations, employment, or housing who are protected by the added grounds
affected_groups.explanation: The bill adds protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity or expression in these settings.

affected_groups.group: Labor organizations, and employers, labor organizations, or joint labor-management committees controlling covered training programs
affected_groups.explanation: Section 21.053 covers labor-organization discrimination, including exclusion or expulsion from membership. Section 21.054 covers discrimination by controllers of specified training programs, unless the program is provided under a federally approved affirmative action plan. The supplied evidence does not support including employment agencies.

affected_groups.group: State contractors, subcontractors, their employees, and job applicants
affected_groups.explanation: Contractors and subcontractors must follow the required employment policy, and employees and applicants may complain to the contracting agency.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities and local commissions
affected_groups.explanation: Local commissions may address the expanded discrimination grounds, while certain complaints cannot be referred to municipalities without laws prohibiting the alleged discrimination.

affected_groups.group: Religious organizations
affected_groups.explanation: The new public-accommodations chapter generally excludes religious organizations, with an exception for specified qualifying for-profit activities.

major_effects.label: Expanded discrimination protections and civil remedies
major_effects.explanation: Adds sexual orientation and gender identity or expression as grounds for prohibiting discrimination in public accommodations, employment, and housing, and permits civil actions for violations of the new chapter.

major_effects.label: Contractor administrative penalties
major_effects.explanation: After notice of noncompliance, a state agency may impose a daily penalty for each affected employee or applicant, and an equivalent amount may be withheld from contract payments.

major_effects.label: Expanded housing-related intimidation offense
major_effects.explanation: Adds sexual orientation and gender identity or expression to the grounds for the existing offense involving force or threat of force in specified housing-related circumstances.

major_effects.label: Limits on municipal complaint referrals
major_effects.explanation: The commission may not refer a housing complaint alleging the added forms of discrimination to a municipality where the alleged discrimination occurred if that municipality lacks laws prohibiting it.

agencies.name: state agency
agencies.explanation: State agencies contracting under the specified subtitle must require contractors to adopt and apply the prescribed employment policy; each state agency must develop administration procedures. The bill uses the generic term, so the exact set of entities is not resolved here.

HB811.summary: HB 811 would create an offense for a driver restricted to an ignition-interlock vehicle who has another person provide a breath specimen and then drives without first providing the driver’s own specimen. It would also make it an offense to knowingly provide that specimen when knowing the restricted driver intends to drive without providing their own; penalties range from misdemeanors to a third-degree felony for the driver in specified circumstances.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates criminal offenses and establishes their classifications and penalties.
Criminalizes evading an ignition-interlock breath test and knowingly helping another person evade it before driving.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds an offense to the Texas Penal Code without limiting its application to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: People restricted to driving a motor vehicle equipped with an ignition interlock device
