affected_groups.explanation: A person eligible for more than one exemption under the relevant subsection may receive only one of those exemptions from the same subdivision or school district.

major_effects.label: Optional local homestead exemption
major_effects.explanation: Adds a parent-or-guardian condition to the optional local homestead exemption, which allows a subdivision to exempt at least $3,000 of homestead market value. As phrased, the owner must appear to be disabled as well as be the parent or guardian of a disabled person residing with them.

major_effects.label: Potential additional school-tax exemption
major_effects.explanation: Adds a co-resident parent or guardian of a disabled person to the class for which the Legislature may provide an additional homestead exemption of up to $60,000 by general law; the amendment does not itself grant that exemption.

major_effects.label: Choice among overlapping exemptions
major_effects.explanation: A person eligible for multiple exemptions under subsection (b) or (c) may receive only one under that subsection from the same subdivision or school district, while choosing which one.

HJR63.summary: HJR 63 proposes a Texas constitutional amendment allowing the Legislature, by general law, to exclude from real property's ad valorem market value improvements or features primarily made to comply with specified federal accessible-design standards. If voters approve the amendment on November 2, 2027, the Legislature may create the exclusion and set additional eligibility requirements; the resolution itself does not grant a tax exclusion to property owners.

policy_tags.explanation: The proposed amendment would authorize a future law excluding qualifying improvements or features from real property's market value for ad valorem tax purposes; it does not itself enact the exclusion.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The resolution proposes an amendment to the Texas Constitution for submission to voters statewide.

affected_groups.group: Owners of real property with qualifying accessibility improvements or features
affected_groups.explanation: They could benefit if voters approve the amendment and the Legislature later enacts an exclusion covering their property.

affected_groups.group: Texas voters
affected_groups.explanation: Voters will decide whether to approve the proposed constitutional amendment.

major_effects.label: Potential property-tax exclusion authority
major_effects.explanation: If voters approve the amendment, the Legislature may enact a general law excluding qualifying accessibility improvements or features from real property's ad valorem market value and may set additional eligibility requirements. The amendment alone would not create the exclusion.

HJR64.summary: If voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment, it would allow motor-vehicle registration revenues, motor-fuel tax revenues other than gross production and ad valorem taxes, and other revenue specifically dedicated by the Legislature for this purpose and not otherwise dedicated by the Constitution, to be used for constructing and maintaining roadways for seaports, airports, spaceports, land ports of entry, and international bridges, subject to legislative appropriation, allocation, and direction. It would also remove the existing provision authorizing payment of certain older county and road-district bond debt from the highway fund.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes constitutionally authorized uses of transportation revenues to include roadways for the listed port and airport facilities.
Expands the purposes for which specified state-dedicated revenues may be used, without itself making an appropriation.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The proposed change is to the Texas Constitution and is submitted to voters statewide.

affected_groups.group: Transportation infrastructure serving seaports, airports, spaceports, land ports of entry, and international bridges

major_effects.label: Expands eligible transportation uses of dedicated revenue
major_effects.explanation: Would allow specified revenues—including motor vehicle registration fees, motor-fuel taxes other than gross production and ad valorem taxes, and qualifying other dedicated revenue—to fund construction and maintenance of roadways for the listed facilities, subject to legislative appropriation, allocation, and direction.

major_effects.label: Removes a prior bond-debt payment provision
major_effects.explanation: Deletes the authorization for payment of principal and interest on specified older county and road-district bonds or warrants.

HJR65.summary: HJR 65 proposes a Texas constitutional amendment allowing the Legislature to provide by general law for a person to vote in a primary election if the person will be at least 18 by the subsequent general election for state and county officers and meets other applicable voting requirements. The amendment would take effect only if approved by voters; it would authorize the Legislature to provide for this voting eligibility, rather than itself establishing it.

policy_tags.explanation: The proposed amendment concerns eligibility to vote in a primary election.

locations.name: Statewide

major_effects.label: Authority to provide for primary voting by certain under-18-year-olds
major_effects.explanation: If voters approve the amendment, the Legislature may provide by general law for people who will be at least 18 by the subsequent general election to vote in a primary, subject to other applicable eligibility requirements. The amendment does not itself establish that eligibility.

HJR67.summary: HJR 67 proposes a constitutional amendment for voter consideration on November 4, 2025. If approved, it would bar a person from election to a statewide elected executive office, but not a judicial office, if by election day they had served in that same office during any part of 12 or more calendar years; service before January 1, 2027, would not count, and holdover service until a successor qualifies would remain permitted.

HJR68.summary: HJR 68 proposes a Texas constitutional amendment barring the Legislature from restricting an individual’s access to abortion or related health care when the individual chooses to obtain it in consultation with a licensed physician. The amendment would be adopted only if voters approve it at the November 4, 2025 election.

policy_tags.explanation: The proposal would protect access to abortion and related health care from legislative restriction, subject to the stated physician-consultation condition.

locations.name: Texas statewide

major_effects.label: Conditional constitutional access protection
major_effects.explanation: If approved by voters, the amendment would prohibit the Legislature from restricting the specified access when the individual chooses the care in consultation with a licensed physician.

HJR70.summary: HJR 70 would ask Texas voters to amend the constitution to require the state to provide medical assistance to every applicant for whom federal matching funds are available under the Affordable Care Act. If voters approve the amendment at the November 2, 2027 election, the requirement would take effect January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The proposed constitutional requirement would expand who must receive medical assistance under the federal Medicaid matching-funds condition.

SB100.summary: The bill would expand the definition of bullying to include targeting a student because of specified actual or perceived characteristics, and would expressly include artificial-intelligence applications among tools used for cyberbullying. It would require school districts to use more detailed investigation procedures and provide individualized supportive measures, and would expand incident reporting; the changes apply beginning with the 2027-2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes public-school bullying definitions, district policies, investigations, student supports, and reporting.

Assigns school districts new policy, reporting, investigation, and student-support duties.

locations.name: Statewide

affected_groups.group: School district employees
affected_groups.explanation: Employees must report qualifying bullying information they witness or receive in the course and scope of employment.

major_effects.label: Expanded bullying definitions
major_effects.explanation: Adds targeting based on specified actual or perceived characteristics as a bullying criterion and expressly includes AI applications among electronic communication tools for cyberbullying.

major_effects.label: District investigation procedures
major_effects.explanation: Requires notice, opportunities to provide information and review findings, an investigative report, and an appeal opportunity for impacted students.

major_effects.label: Individualized student supports
major_effects.explanation: Requires districts to provide nonpunitive, individualized supportive measures designed to protect safety and preserve access to education; they must be free and provided regardless of whether a student participates in an investigation.

major_effects.label: Bullying reporting requirements
major_effects.explanation: Adds employee reporting duties and requires annual campus-level incident counts to distinguish cyberbullying and incidents based on specified actual or perceived characteristics.

major_effects.label: Minimum standards
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Texas Education Agency to adopt or revise minimum standards for district bullying policies.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: Must adopt or revise minimum standards for school district bullying policies to comply with the bill.

SB101.summary: The bill would require a county commissioners court to designate at least one polling place on the main campus of an institution of higher education in the county when enrollment reaches 5,000 students. At 10,000 students, the court would have to designate two polling places, plus one additional polling place for every additional 10,000 students enrolled.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes requirements for designating campus polling places.
The bill assigns the polling-place designation duty to county commissioners courts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies in any county with an institution of higher education meeting the enrollment thresholds.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: They would be required to designate campus polling places when enrollment thresholds are met.

affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education and their students
affected_groups.explanation: A qualifying institution's main campus would receive polling places based on student enrollment.

affected_groups.group: Voters
affected_groups.explanation: The bill would require polling places on qualifying institutions' main campuses.

major_effects.label: Campus polling-place designation
major_effects.explanation: County commissioners courts would have to designate polling places on qualifying main campuses, with the number increasing at the specified enrollment thresholds.

SB102.summary: The bill revises the identification voters may present, adding photo and non-photo document options and new combinations of documents. It also updates the reasonable-impediment declaration and aligns provisional-ballot and in-person ballot-delivery procedures with the revised identification requirements.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes voter identification options and related voting and ballot-verification procedures.
Changes polling-place and voter-registration administration tasks carried out by election officers, election judges, and voter registrars.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Election Code requirements for voters and election administration across the state.

affected_groups.group: Voters
affected_groups.explanation: Voters may use revised forms and combinations of identification when offering to vote.

affected_groups.group: Voters unable to meet specified identification requirements
affected_groups.explanation: The bill revises the identification alternatives and declaration route available when a voter does not meet the specified requirements.

affected_groups.group: Election officers, election judges, and voter registrars
affected_groups.explanation: These officials carry out the revised declaration, identification-checking, and provisional-ballot procedures.

major_effects.label: Expanded voter identification options
major_effects.explanation: Adds acceptable photo documents and non-photo document combinations, including routes that require a declaration.

major_effects.label: Reasonable-impediment declaration process
major_effects.explanation: Updates when an election officer must offer the declaration route and which identification requirements and alternatives it covers.

major_effects.label: Related ballot-verification procedures
major_effects.explanation: Aligns identification checks for provisional ballots and in-person delivery of a marked ballot with the revised identification provisions.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The bill changes required contents of a declaration form that the Secretary of State must prescribe.

SB103.summary: SB 103 would make any qualified voter eligible to vote early by mail or in person, while requiring participants in the address confidentiality program to submit an application for early voting by mail by personal delivery. It would repeal certain criminal offenses concerning solicitation and distribution of mail-ballot applications, revise application and ballot-delivery rules, narrow the jail-based application procedure to specified confinement statuses, and change the conditions for late ballots. The changes would apply only to elections ordered on or after September 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility and procedures for early voting by mail, mail-ballot applications, ballot delivery, and late ballots.
Repeals certain criminal offenses concerning solicitation and distribution of mail-ballot applications.
Narrows the jail-based application procedure involving the authority in charge of a jail, affecting jail administration.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to qualified voters and elections under the Texas Election Code statewide.

affected_groups.group: Qualified voters
affected_groups.explanation: Would generally become eligible to vote early by mail without establishing one of the former statutory grounds.

affected_groups.group: Participants in the address confidentiality program
affected_groups.explanation: Participants must have submitted their voter-registration application by personal delivery; this is a necessary condition for eligibility to vote by mail.

affected_groups.group: Voters confined in jail
affected_groups.explanation: The jail-specific application procedure would apply only to applicants in the listed confinement statuses.

affected_groups.group: Voters with qualifying late-arising sickness or physical conditions
affected_groups.explanation: May qualify for a late ballot when the condition arises on or after the mail-ballot application deadline and prevents polling-place attendance without likely assistance or health injury.

major_effects.label: General eligibility for mail voting
major_effects.explanation: Would allow any qualified voter to vote early by mail, subject to the special personal-delivery voter-registration condition for address confidentiality program participants.

major_effects.label: Repeal of certain mail-ballot application offenses
major_effects.explanation: Would repeal certain criminal offenses concerning solicitation and distribution of applications to vote by mail.

major_effects.label: Application and ballot-delivery rules
major_effects.explanation: Would revise application and ballot-address rules to reflect the applicant's circumstances, including absence from the county on election day, specified living arrangements, and listed jail confinement statuses.

major_effects.label: Jail-based application procedure
major_effects.explanation: Would limit this section's jail-based application procedure to applicants in specified confinement statuses; submission by jail authority remains discretionary.

major_effects.label: Late-ballot qualification
major_effects.explanation: Would specify that a qualifying sickness or physical condition must arise on or after the day before the mail-ballot application deadline and prevent polling-place attendance without likely personal assistance or health injury.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The bill changes which overseas-mail-voting applicants trigger the existing ballot-timing provision, which includes notice to and monitoring and advice by the Secretary of State.

SB104.summary: SB104 would allow volunteer deputy registrars to serve throughout Texas regardless of which county appointed them, and to distribute and receive the Secretary of State’s prescribed application form statewide. It would also remove the county limitation from the appointment certificate, revise county authorization of compensation, and require the Secretary of State to prescribe implementation procedures.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the statewide service area and application-handling authority of volunteer deputy registrars.
Changes the county-level authorization required for compensation of volunteer deputy registrars.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill expressly authorizes service and application distribution throughout the state.

affected_groups.group: Volunteer deputy registrars
affected_groups.explanation: They would be authorized to serve statewide and distribute or receive the specified applications statewide.

affected_groups.group: County governments and commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: A county's commissioners court may authorize compensation paid by that county to a volunteer deputy registrar; the registrar may not receive that compensation unless the court authorizes it.

major_effects.label: Statewide registrar authority
major_effects.explanation: Volunteer deputy registrars could serve statewide regardless of their appointing county and handle the prescribed application form statewide.

major_effects.label: County compensation authorization
major_effects.explanation: Compensation from any county would require authorization by that county's commissioners court.

major_effects.label: Implementation procedures
major_effects.explanation: The Secretary of State would prescribe procedures to implement the new provisions.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The Secretary of State is expressly directed to prescribe procedures to implement the statewide service and application provisions.

SB105.summary: The bill would require the state registrar, local registrars, and county clerks to provide a homeless individual a certified copy of the individual's birth record without charge upon request. It requires the executive commissioner to establish a process to verify homeless status and prescribe documentation for issuance to individuals whose status is verified.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes procedures for verifying eligibility and issuing certified birth records.
Requires local registrars and county clerks to issue qualifying copies without a fee.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to the state registrar and local registrars and county clerks handling requests across Texas.

affected_groups.group: Homeless individuals seeking certified copies of their birth records
affected_groups.explanation: They may request a fee-free certified copy. The definition includes people lacking an adequate regular nighttime residence or using specified temporary or nonresidential places, but excludes people imprisoned or detained unless they met the conditions at the time of arrest.

affected_groups.group: State and local vital-records officials, including county clerks
affected_groups.explanation: These officials are responsible for issuing qualifying copies and observing the physical-address restriction.

major_effects.label: Fee-free certified birth records
major_effects.explanation: A homeless individual may request a certified copy without charge; people imprisoned or detained are excluded unless they met the homelessness conditions at arrest.

major_effects.label: Status verification and documentation rules
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must establish a process for verifying homeless status and prescribe the documentation needed for issuance to individuals verified through that process.

major_effects.label: No physical-address requirement
major_effects.explanation: The listed officials may not require a homeless individual to provide a physical residential address to satisfy this section.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The executive commissioner of the commission is directed to adopt rules establishing the verification process and documentation requirements.

agencies.name: state registrar
agencies.explanation: The state registrar must issue qualifying certified copies without a fee and may not require a physical residential address; the supplied material does not identify the state registrar's agency.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The department is barred from requiring a physical residential address for purposes of this section, but its identity is not established by the supplied materials.

SB106.summary: SB 106 would repeal the education savings account program and abolish its fund, transferring unencumbered money to general revenue; money obligated under contracts made before the effective date would be held for distribution under those contracts, subject to transfer to general revenue if the Comptroller determines it will not be distributed as contracted. Transfers already made for the 2026–27 school year would remain subject to the former program’s requirements. The bill also revises related educator-misconduct provisions and removes the Comptroller from the state agencies covered by Health and Safety Code Chapter 810.

policy_tags.explanation: Repeals the education savings account program and revises related educator-misconduct provisions.
Repeals the education savings account program.
Abolishes the program fund and transfers its unencumbered balance to the general revenue fund.
Changes which state agencies are covered by Health and Safety Code Chapter 810.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill changes statewide Texas education and state-agency law.

affected_groups.group: Recipients of education savings account transfers for the 2026–27 school year
affected_groups.explanation: Their transferred funds remain subject to the former program’s requirements.

affected_groups.group: Parties to contracts funded by the education savings account program
affected_groups.explanation: Money obligated by contract before the effective date is held for distribution under the contract, unless the Comptroller determines it will not be distributed as contracted.

affected_groups.group: Private schools and educational providers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill narrows the wording of Chapter 22A’s misconduct provisions and makes the reporting subchapter’s heading specific to private schools.

major_effects.label: Repeal education savings account program
major_effects.explanation: Repeals the Education Code subchapter establishing the program and related provisions.

major_effects.label: Close out the program fund
major_effects.explanation: Abolishes the fund and transfers its unencumbered balance to general revenue; pre-effective-date contract obligations are held for distribution under their terms, subject to the stated Comptroller determination.

major_effects.label: Preserve rules for 2026–27 transfers
major_effects.explanation: Transfers to accounts for the 2026–27 school year remain subject to the former subchapter and related Comptroller rules or procedures.

major_effects.label: Revise Chapter 22A misconduct provisions
major_effects.explanation: Removes Section 22A.302(c) from the reports listed for filing through the agency portal, revises the Subchapter G heading to refer to private schools, and narrows the confidentiality language by removing the reference to employees of or contractors for educational providers.

major_effects.label: Change Chapter 810 agency coverage
major_effects.explanation: Amends the list of state agencies to which Health and Safety Code Chapter 810 applies, removing the Comptroller.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The Comptroller is assigned trustee duties for contractually obligated program funds and is removed from Chapter 810’s list of covered agencies.

agencies.name: the board or agency under Chapter 22A
agencies.explanation: The bill changes which reports trigger preliminary review and which reports are filed through the agency portal, but the supplied text does not identify the responsible body by canonical name.

SB107.summary: The bill directs the Teacher Retirement System of Texas to provide a one-time cost-of-living adjustment beginning with September 2027 annuity payments to specified eligible retirement and survivor-benefit annuitants and alternate payees. Eligibility generally depends on the member’s retirement, death, or annuity-election date being before January 1, 2027, with living-on-the-adjustment-date requirements for specified recipients; fixed statutory annuities and deferred retirement option plan account payments are excluded. The increase is limited to the lesser of 3 percent of the monthly benefit subject to the increase or $200 per month, and the board of trustees determines eligibility and amount.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires an increase in specified monthly retirement and survivor benefits paid through the state retirement system.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The change concerns benefits administered by the statewide Teacher Retirement System of Texas.

affected_groups.group: Eligible Teacher Retirement System annuitants, including retirees, beneficiaries, and alternate payees
affected_groups.explanation: Specified annuitants may receive the one-time adjustment subject to the bill’s eligibility dates, living requirements where applicable, and exclusions.

major_effects.label: One-time annuity adjustment
major_effects.explanation: Provides a one-time increase beginning with September 2027 annuity payments, capped at the lesser of 3 percent of the monthly benefit or $200 per month.

major_effects.label: Eligibility limits and exclusions
major_effects.explanation: Limits eligibility based on recipient and member dates and, for specified recipients, being alive on the adjustment’s effective date; excludes listed fixed statutory annuities and deferred retirement option plan account payments.

agencies.name: Teacher Retirement System of Texas
agencies.explanation: The system is directed to make the adjustment, and its board of trustees must determine eligibility and the amount.

SB108.summary: SB 108 would provide qualifying employee-class annuitants a monthly cost-of-living adjustment beginning in January 2028, with rates of 2% to 8% based on retirement, death, or alternate-payee election dates; eligibility cutoffs and living-status requirements apply, and elected-class benefits are excluded. It would also provide qualifying annuitants a one-time payment of $2,500 to $10,000, but neither benefit may be paid unless the ERS board finds that legislative appropriations are sufficient without increasing the system’s unfunded actuarial liabilities; those appropriations must be in addition to amounts the state is otherwise required to contribute.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill establishes additional recurring and one-time retirement benefit payments, conditional on sufficient legislative appropriations.
The bill changes retirement benefits for qualifying members of the state employee retirement system and their beneficiaries.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions concern qualifying annuitants of the statewide Employees Retirement System of Texas.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying employee-class ERS annuitants, including retirees, disability and death-benefit recipients, beneficiaries, and alternate payees
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible recipients may receive the monthly adjustment, the one-time payment, or both, subject to the distinct eligibility and timing rules for each benefit.

major_effects.label: Limits eligibility for the benefit increases
major_effects.explanation: Eligibility is tied to annuitant status in December 2027 and category-specific date cutoffs, subject to Subsections (c) and (d); the COLA also requires certain annuitants to be living on its effective date.

major_effects.label: Monthly cost-of-living adjustment
major_effects.explanation: Beginning with the January 2028 annuity, qualifying monthly benefits receive a 2% to 8% adjustment, with the rate based on the applicable retirement, death, or election date.

major_effects.label: One-time supplemental payment
major_effects.explanation: Qualifying annuitants would receive a January 2028 payment ranging from $2,500 to $10,000, based on the relevant retirement, death, or alternate-payee election date.

major_effects.label: Payment conditioned on sufficient appropriations
major_effects.explanation: The system may make either benefit increase only if the board finds that legislative appropriations are sufficient to pay for it without increasing unfunded actuarial liabilities.

agencies.name: Employees Retirement System of Texas
agencies.explanation: The system is directed to make the supplemental payments, and its board determines eligibility and benefit amounts.

SB109.summary: If voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment requiring Medicaid expansion, the Act would require medical assistance for applicants for whom federal matching funds are available; the expanded eligibility applies only to initial eligibility determinations or recertifications made on or after January 1, 2028. It also directs the executive commissioner to adopt rules and requires annual reports on the expansion’s effects; if voters reject the amendment, the Act has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands medical assistance eligibility for applicants for whom federal matching funds are available, subject to voter approval of the proposed constitutional amendment.
Changes eligibility for medical assistance and requires reporting on coverage and health care costs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The eligibility expansion and related reporting concern individuals and costs in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for medical assistance who qualify for federal matching funds
affected_groups.explanation: Their eligibility for medical assistance would be expanded, subject to the Act’s voter-approval condition and implementation date.

affected_groups.group: Hospitals
affected_groups.explanation: The annual report must address the expansion’s effects on hospital charity care and uncompensated care costs.

major_effects.label: Expanded medical-assistance eligibility
major_effects.explanation: If voters approve the proposed constitutional amendment, the Commission must provide assistance to applicants for whom federal matching funds are available. The provision applies only to initial determinations or recertifications made on or after January 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: Rules for expanded assistance
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must adopt rules regarding provision of medical assistance under the expansion.

major_effects.label: Annual report on expansion effects
major_effects.explanation: The Commission must report annually to state leadership and legislative committees on effects including coverage, state and local health care costs, and hospital charity and uncompensated care costs.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The Commission is assigned the expanded medical-assistance and annual-report duties; its executive commissioner is also directed to adopt rules and take implementation steps.

SB110.summary: The bill would prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity, or military-veteran status in public accommodations, employment, and housing. It would create a Texas Workforce Commission complaint and enforcement process for public-accommodation claims and allow court-ordered relief and, in qualifying cases, civil penalties. It preserves specified veteran-preference programs and benefits, and excludes private clubs and other establishments not open to the public from the public-accommodation prohibition.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds sexual orientation, gender identity, and military-veteran status to discrimination protections in public accommodations, employment, and housing.
Expands protections against discrimination by employers, employment agencies, labor organizations, and training-program operators.
Extends fair-housing protections to sales, rentals, related services, and housing-related transactions.
Creates conduct requirements for businesses and other entities offering goods or services to the public.
Expands the discrimination grounds relevant to local commissions and limits referrals of certain complaints to municipalities without laws prohibiting the alleged discrimination.
Expands the protected grounds covered by an existing housing-related offense involving force or threats to intimidate or interfere with a person.
Assigns the Texas Workforce Commission new public-accommodation complaint, investigation, and alternative-dispute-resolution functions.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The public-accommodation prohibition applies in places of public accommodation throughout the state.

affected_groups.group: Individuals protected from discrimination based on sexual orientation, gender identity, or military-veteran status
affected_groups.explanation: These grounds are added to public-accommodation, employment, and housing protections.

affected_groups.group: Employers, employment agencies, labor organizations, and training-program operators
affected_groups.explanation: Their employment and training practices become subject to the expanded discrimination grounds.

affected_groups.group: Public-accommodation businesses and their customers
affected_groups.explanation: Businesses and other entities offering goods or services to the public must provide equal accommodation subject to stated exceptions.

affected_groups.group: People buying or renting housing and housing-related businesses
affected_groups.explanation: The expanded grounds apply to dwelling sales and rentals and to related transactions and services.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Municipalities may receive referred fair-housing complaints, but the commission may not refer specified complaints to a municipality lacking laws prohibiting the alleged discrimination.

major_effects.label: Expanded public-accommodation protections
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits discrimination on the listed grounds in public accommodations. The rule excludes private clubs and establishments not in fact open to the public, and allows specified benefits for people age 50 or older and veterans or their family members.

major_effects.label: Expanded employment and fair-housing protections
major_effects.explanation: Adds sexual orientation, gender identity, and military-veteran status to numerous employment and housing discrimination provisions. Specified veteran-preference programs remain unaffected.

major_effects.label: TWC complaint and dispute-resolution process
major_effects.explanation: Creates a public-accommodation complaint process administered by the Texas Workforce Commission, including investigation and an office of alternative dispute resolution.

major_effects.label: Court relief and conditional civil penalties
major_effects.explanation: Courts may order injunctions and equitable relief and award compensatory or punitive damages; punitive damages are limited to non-government respondents and require malice or reckless indifference. A civil penalty is available in qualifying attorney-general actions to vindicate the public interest and is subject to the referenced statutory cap.

major_effects.label: Limit on municipal complaint referrals
major_effects.explanation: The commission may not defer and refer a covered complaint to the municipality where the alleged discrimination occurred if that municipality lacks a law prohibiting the alleged discrimination.

major_effects.label: Expanded coverage of housing-related offense
major_effects.explanation: Adds the new protected grounds to an existing offense involving intentional intimidation or interference by force or threat of force in specified housing-related activities.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the commission as the Texas Workforce Commission and assigns it complaint processing, investigation, dispute-resolution, and enforcement functions.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The commission may request the attorney general to bring a civil action in specified pattern-or-practice or general-public-importance cases; qualifying actions may seek a civil penalty.

agencies.name: district courts
agencies.explanation: District courts are assigned proceedings for temporary relief, and courts may grant injunctions and other relief. The bill refers to district courts generically rather than naming a particular court.

SB111.summary: The bill would prohibit covered health benefit plan issuers from requiring prior authorization for prescription drugs prescribed to prevent HIV infection. It would apply to a broad range of plans, including Medicaid, the child health plan program, and county employee group health benefits, with an exception for certain older individual plans; the changes apply only to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028. If a state agency determines that federal authorization is necessary, the affected agency would have to request it and could delay implementation until it is granted.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes prescription drug coverage requirements for health benefit plans.
The bill expressly applies the coverage rule to the state Medicaid program, including Medicaid managed care.
The bill expressly includes county employee group health benefits among the plans subject to the rule.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The coverage rule applies to covered plans for state residents, including certain group plans regardless of where the policy or contract is issued or delivered.

affected_groups.group: Enrollees prescribed drugs to prevent HIV infection
affected_groups.explanation: Their covered prescription drug benefits would be exempt from prior authorization under applicable plans.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plan issuers
affected_groups.explanation: Issuers providing prescription drug benefits would be barred from requiring prior authorization for the specified drugs under covered plans.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid, child health plan, and county employee plan enrollees
affected_groups.explanation: The bill expressly includes these programs and county employee group health benefits in the plans subject to the subchapter.

major_effects.label: Prior-authorization prohibition
major_effects.explanation: Covered health benefit plan issuers could not require prior authorization for prescription drugs prescribed to prevent HIV infection.

major_effects.label: Covered-plan scope and timing
major_effects.explanation: The rule would reach the listed public and private plans, including Medicaid, the child health plan program, and county employee benefits. It would not apply to qualifying older individual plans, and the changes apply only to plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: Conditional federal authorization process
major_effects.explanation: If an affected state agency determines federal authorization is necessary, it must request it and may delay implementing the relevant provision until authorization is granted.

agencies.name: state agency affected by the provision
agencies.explanation: The bill gives the affected state agency a conditional duty to request federal authorization if it determines authorization is necessary, and permits it to delay implementation until approval. The bill does not identify which agency or agencies this refers to.

SB112.summary: The bill would require regular testing for lead, copper, and arsenic at every Texas Department of Criminal Justice correctional facility and county jail, in addition to tests required under federal law. If an outlet exceeds commission-set safe levels, the facility or jail must prevent its use until tests confirm the water is safe; the commission would set testing procedures and safety levels by rule in consultation with the Texas Department of Criminal Justice and county commissioners courts.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates recurring testing and safety thresholds for drinking water at specified facilities.
County jails must allow testing and prevent use of outlets exceeding safe levels; county commissioners courts also participate in rule development.

locations.name: Statewide in Texas
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to each TDCJ correctional facility and county jail in the state.

affected_groups.group: People held in TDCJ correctional facilities and county jails
affected_groups.explanation: Their access to potable water outlets could be restricted when testing finds unsafe levels of specified contaminants.

affected_groups.group: County governments and county jail operators
affected_groups.explanation: County jails must allow testing and restrict use of affected outlets, while county commissioners courts participate in rule development.

major_effects.label: Recurring water testing
major_effects.explanation: Requires regular testing for lead, copper, and arsenic at each covered correctional facility and county jail, in addition to federally required tests.

major_effects.label: Testing procedures and safety levels
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules establishing sample collection and testing procedures and the contaminant levels considered safe for human consumption.

major_effects.label: Restriction on unsafe outlets
major_effects.explanation: A covered facility or jail must prevent use of an outlet found above the rule-set safe level until tests confirm the water is safe.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The commission must arrange regular tests and adopt implementing rules; the bill title identifies it as the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: The department is expressly included in the rulemaking consultation required by the bill.

SB113.summary: SB 113 would provide statutory rules for selecting, organizing, staffing, and compensating the Texas Redistricting Commission and opening its work to public participation, including protection against retaliation for attending its meetings. It would let the commission make a statewide judicial-district reapportionment if the Judicial Districts Board misses its deadline and update the constitutional cross-reference governing county election-precinct boundary changes. The bill takes effect only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise it has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates statutory procedures for a commission that reviews and draws congressional and state legislative district maps.
Establishes selection, organization, staffing, meeting, and administrative procedures for the commission.
Adds a specific employment protection for employees attending or scheduled to attend commission meetings.
Updates the constitutional reference governing when county commissioners courts must adjust election precinct boundaries to implement a redistricting plan.
Provides commission members a per diem and reimbursement for expenses incurred performing their duties.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The commission’s work concerns statewide redistricting and participation by state residents.

affected_groups.group: Prospective commission applicants
affected_groups.explanation: The bill opens the application process to registered voters while prescribing conflict-of-interest exclusions and selection criteria.

affected_groups.group: Commission members
affected_groups.explanation: Members are selected and appointed under new procedures and receive per diem and expense reimbursement.

affected_groups.group: Texas residents and registered voters
affected_groups.explanation: Residents may submit maps or comments, and the process must solicit broad public participation.

affected_groups.group: Employees attending or scheduled to attend commission meetings
affected_groups.explanation: Employers may not retaliate against employees for attending or scheduling attendance at a commission meeting.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Their existing precinct-boundary adjustment requirement is linked to the constitutional redistricting-plan provision cited in the bill.

major_effects.label: Commission selection and operations
major_effects.explanation: Sets statutory procedures for applying, screening, selecting, and organizing commission members.

major_effects.label: Public transparency and participation
major_effects.explanation: Requires public access to redistricting information and maps and provides hearings and online participation opportunities; the hearing process is subject to public notice and promoted through outreach.

major_effects.label: Judicial-district reapportionment fallback
major_effects.explanation: If the Judicial Districts Board misses its deadline, the Texas Redistricting Commission must make the statewide reapportionment within 90 days after that deadline.

major_effects.label: Protection for meeting attendance
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits employers from taking specified retaliatory actions against employees because they attend or are scheduled to attend a commission meeting.

major_effects.label: Commission member compensation
major_effects.explanation: Provides members a $300 per diem, adjusted under the bill’s CPI formula, and expense reimbursement for commission duties.

major_effects.label: County precinct-boundary reference
major_effects.explanation: Updates the constitutional provision governing county precinct-boundary changes, which remain required only when necessary to give effect to the referenced redistricting plan.

agencies.name: Texas Redistricting Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill provides the commission’s membership, operating, public-participation, staffing, and compensation procedures, conditional on voter approval of the constitutional amendment.

agencies.name: state auditor
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the state auditor the commission-member application, screening, and selection-pool process, as well as temporary administrative support.

agencies.name: Texas Secretary of State
agencies.explanation: The bill requires the secretary of state to post notice of commission meetings on the Internet.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The commission’s procurement and contracting authority is subject to fiscal oversight from the comptroller.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: A commission member removed for substantial neglect or gross misconduct may be referred to the attorney general for criminal investigation.

SB114.summary: The bill would create an annual fine arts allotment for school districts for students in grades 6–12 enrolled in approved courses, with the allotment amount varying by grade. It would require approved courses to meet specified instructional criteria and direct portions of the funding to students in particular grade ranges, including a priority for certain compensatory-education-eligible students in grades 6–8.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a public school finance allotment for fine arts courses and specifies course and funding requirements.
Creates an annual funding entitlement in the public school finance system.
Provides the allotment to school districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The allotment is established for school districts under the statewide public school finance system, with no geographic limitation stated.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would receive the new annual fine arts allotment for qualifying students.

affected_groups.group: Students in grades 6–12 enrolled in approved fine arts courses
affected_groups.explanation: Their attendance in an approved course would determine eligibility for the allotment; course criteria include at least 225 minutes of instruction per week for a full-time student.

affected_groups.group: Students in grades 6–8 eligible for the compensatory education allotment
affected_groups.explanation: A portion of the funds for grades 6–8 must prioritize providing fine arts education to these students.

major_effects.label: Fine arts allotment
major_effects.explanation: Creates an annual per-student allotment based on the basic allotment, with grade-level multipliers; it also directs specified portions of the funds to students in particular grade ranges.

major_effects.label: Qualifying fine arts courses
major_effects.explanation: The agency would approve eligible courses, which must meet the stated fine arts, skill-development, and instructional-time criteria.

major_effects.label: Annual approved-course list
major_effects.explanation: Requires the agency to publish a list of approved fine arts courses each year.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns course-approval and annual publication duties to the agency, but does not identify it by a canonical name.

SB115.summary: The bill repeals the Education Code provision requiring the Ten Commandments to be displayed in public school classrooms.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill removes a statutory requirement applying to public school classrooms.
The repealed requirement concerns the display of a religious text in public schools, a matter involving religious expression in public institutions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The repeal concerns a statewide provision of the Texas Education Code applicable to public school classrooms.

affected_groups.group: Texas public schools and school districts
affected_groups.explanation: They would no longer be subject to the repealed classroom display requirement.

affected_groups.group: Public school students
affected_groups.explanation: Students would be affected by removal of the statutory requirement for the display in their classrooms.

major_effects.label: Repeals classroom display requirement
major_effects.explanation: Removes the Education Code requirement to display the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms.

SB116.summary: SB 116 would require Department of Agriculture standards to prohibit applying glyphosate or a neonicotinoid pesticide at a school building or other school district facility. The department would have to adopt standards reflecting the change as soon as practicable after the Act takes effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Adds a pesticide-use restriction specifically for school buildings and other school district facilities.
Restricts the application of two types of pesticides at the covered facilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The restriction applies to covered school buildings and school district facilities without a stated geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: School districts and operators of school facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The restriction applies at school buildings and other school district facilities.

affected_groups.group: Pesticide applicators working at covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Application of the specified pesticides would be prohibited at those facilities.

major_effects.label: School-site pesticide standards
major_effects.explanation: Requires Department of Agriculture standards to include a prohibition on applying glyphosate or neonicotinoid pesticides at covered school facilities, and directs the department to adopt the standards as soon as practicable after the Act takes effect.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Agriculture
agencies.explanation: The bill requires the department to adopt standards under the amended provision, which must include the specified pesticide-application prohibition.

SB117.summary: SB 117 would require health maintenance organizations, insurers, and utilization review agents to make appropriate personnel available by telephone 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including holidays. When personnel are unavailable due to circumstances beyond the entity’s reasonable control, the entity must maintain a call-handling system; verification and preauthorization calls, and specified utilization review calls, must receive a response as soon as possible and within two hours.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes telephone access and response standards for benefit verification, preauthorization, and utilization review involving patient care.
The bill imposes operational requirements on health maintenance organizations, insurers, and utilization review agents.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Insurance Code provisions without identifying a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Health maintenance organizations and health insurers
affected_groups.explanation: These entities would have expanded telephone availability and call-response requirements for verifications and preauthorizations.

affected_groups.group: Utilization review agents
affected_groups.explanation: These agents would have expanded telephone availability and response requirements for review calls.

affected_groups.group: Patients and callers seeking verification, preauthorization, or utilization review
affected_groups.explanation: Callers seeking verification, preauthorization, or utilization review are affected. The bill provides for 24/7 personnel availability for telephone review requests. For preauthorizations, it requires a system to accept or record calls during periods when personnel are unavailable due to circumstances beyond the health maintenance organization's reasonable control, with calls answered as soon as possible and within two hours.

major_effects.label: 24/7 telephone availability and call handling
major_effects.explanation: Requires appropriate personnel to be reasonably available by telephone around the clock, including holidays. If personnel are unavailable due to circumstances beyond the entity’s reasonable control, a system must accept or record calls; utilization review agents may also provide caller instructions.

major_effects.label: Two-hour response standard
major_effects.explanation: Requires responses as soon as possible and within two hours for verification and preauthorization calls, and for utilization review calls made during periods when personnel are unavailable under the stated circumstances.

SB118.summary: SB 118 would create a separate Occupations Code subchapter classifying specified efforts by defined mental health providers to change a child’s sexual orientation or reduce same-sex attractions as unprofessional conduct. It exempts specified supportive counseling and support for gender transition consistent with established standards of care, and makes covered providers subject to discipline by any state regulatory entity empowered to discipline them.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill sets a professional-conduct standard for mental health services provided to children.
The bill restricts covered providers from attempting to change a child's sexual orientation or gender identity or expression, subject to stated exceptions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill defines covered providers by state licensure or certification and applies the disciplinary provision to state regulatory entities.

affected_groups.group: Children younger than 18
affected_groups.explanation: The bill's conduct standard applies to services provided to a child, defined as an individual younger than 18.

affected_groups.group: Mental health providers covered by the bill
affected_groups.explanation: The bill covers specified licensed or certified health and counseling professionals and other state-licensed professional therapy or counseling providers.

major_effects.label: Unprofessional-conduct standard
major_effects.explanation: Defines attempts to change a child's sexual orientation, including attempts to change behavior or gender identity or expression, and attempts to reduce same-sex attractions or feelings as unprofessional conduct. Stated counseling exceptions remain.

major_effects.label: Disciplinary exposure
major_effects.explanation: Providers who commit the defined unprofessional conduct are subject to disciplinary action by a state regulatory entity that has authority over them.

agencies.name: any state regulatory entity with the power to take disciplinary action against that mental health provider
agencies.explanation: The bill makes covered providers subject to disciplinary action by whichever state regulatory entity has disciplinary authority over them, but it does not identify those entities by name.

SB119.summary: The bill extends the expiration date for the Bexar County family violence pretrial diversion pilot program from September 1, 2027, to September 1, 2031. It does not create a new program.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill extends the sunset for a pretrial diversion program related to family violence.
The extended program is specifically located in Bexar County.

locations.name: Bexar County
locations.explanation: The pilot program whose expiration date is extended is located in Bexar County.

affected_groups.group: Bexar County government
affected_groups.explanation: The bill extends the statutory period for the county-specific family violence pretrial diversion pilot program.

affected_groups.group: People involved in the Bexar County family violence pretrial diversion pilot
affected_groups.explanation: The program's expiration is extended, allowing it to continue beyond its former sunset date.

major_effects.label: Pilot program expiration extended
major_effects.explanation: Changes the expiration date from September 1, 2027, to September 1, 2031, extending the period before the statutory provision expires.

SB120.summary: SB 120 would repeal specified provisions in several codes and sections of a prior act concerning state preemption and the effect of state or federal law on certain municipal and county regulation. The bill does not identify the particular local rules or regulated activities affected; the practical consequences depend on the provisions being repealed and other applicable law.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill repeals provisions concerning state preemption of certain municipal and county regulation, changing the statutory framework for local regulatory authority.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill repeals provisions of Texas statutes and a prior Texas act without limiting the changes to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Municipal and county governments
affected_groups.explanation: Their regulatory authority may be affected by repeal of provisions concerning state preemption, though the precise consequences are not specified in the bill text.

major_effects.label: Repeal of provisions concerning local-regulation preemption
major_effects.explanation: The bill repeals the listed provisions associated with state preemption and the effect of state or federal law on certain local regulation; the resulting scope of local authority depends on the repealed provisions and other applicable law.

SB121.summary: The bill would require counties and municipalities that regulate boarding home facilities to report annually to the commission on local standards, accommodation requests and policies, complaints, facility closures, and support for operators. The executive commissioner could adopt implementing rules, and the first report would not be required until September 30, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill creates reporting and update-submission duties for counties and municipalities that regulate boarding home facilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply statewide to counties and municipalities that regulate boarding home facilities.

affected_groups.group: Counties and municipalities that regulate boarding home facilities
affected_groups.explanation: These local governments would prepare and submit annual reports and report later updates to applicable standards or ordinances.

major_effects.label: Annual local reports
major_effects.explanation: Regulating counties and municipalities would report local standards, accommodation-request information, complaints, closures, and operator-support activities. The first report is not required until September 30, 2028.

major_effects.label: Updates to local standards
major_effects.explanation: Counties and municipalities would also report updates to the standards or ordinances included in their annual reports.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner may adopt rules necessary to implement the reporting section.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: Chapter 260 defines “Commission” as the Health and Human Services Commission. The bill requires covered counties and municipalities to submit reports to the commission.

SB122.summary: Beginning with the 2027–2028 school year, each Texas senator and representative must substitute teach at a public school in the member’s district for at least one school day each school year. Members must report compliance to their house’s administration committee, which must maintain a public list of members who do not comply.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a substitute-teaching requirement at public schools.
Adds a duty for legislators to teach and report compliance, and for house administration committees to track noncompliance.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to members of both houses across their districts throughout Texas.

affected_groups.group: Members of the Texas Senate and House of Representatives
affected_groups.explanation: Each member must substitute teach in a public school in the member’s district and report compliance.

affected_groups.group: Public schools and students in legislators’ districts
affected_groups.explanation: Public schools are the sites where legislators must perform the substitute-teaching requirement.

major_effects.label: Annual substitute-teaching requirement
major_effects.explanation: Requires each senator and representative to substitute teach at a public school in the member’s district for at least one school day each school year.

major_effects.label: Compliance reporting and public noncompliance list
major_effects.explanation: Requires members to report compliance to their house’s administration committee; each committee must maintain a public list of members who do not comply.

SB123.summary: The bill directs the commissioner to provide available funds to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools for special education liaisons; after receiving the funds, those schools must employ a qualified liaison. Liaisons would support individualized education programs, legal compliance, and communication with families; if a district employs a liaison, the liaison serves as the district’s representative on the relevant committee.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates special education liaison positions and assigns them duties supporting students’ individualized education programs and special education services.
Directs distribution of available funds to support liaison employment at districts and open-enrollment charter schools.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools statewide.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: They receive funds for liaison employment, and after receiving funds must employ a qualified liaison.

affected_groups.group: Students with individualized education programs
affected_groups.explanation: Liaisons would assist with IEP development, compliance, case management, and certain behavioral assessments and interventions.

affected_groups.group: Special education teachers, staff, and students’ families
affected_groups.explanation: Liaisons would provide staff guidance and training and communicate with, assist, and respond to concerns from families.

major_effects.label: Funds for liaison employment
major_effects.explanation: The commissioner must provide available funds for special education liaisons, including funds identified for districts and open-enrollment charter schools.

major_effects.label: Special education liaison positions
major_effects.explanation: After receiving funds, a district or open-enrollment charter school must employ a qualified liaison to support IEP-related work, compliance, and communication with families. A district-employed liaison serves as the district’s committee representative.

agencies.name: commissioner of education
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commissioner duties to distribute funds and authorizes the commissioner to adopt implementing rules; the supplied text does not establish the canonical agency identity.

SB124.summary: SB 124 would require the Texas Education Agency’s standards for school electronic devices and software applications to provide exceptions allowing students with disabilities to use otherwise impermissible devices or applications when specified in an IEP or Section 504 plan as a reasonable accommodation or assistive technology. The change applies beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes standards governing electronic devices and software applications used by public schools, including an exception for disability-related accommodations.
Changes standards for permissible school electronic devices and software applications by requiring a disability-related exception; it does not change the bill’s existing data-collection standards.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The standards apply to school districts and open-enrollment charter schools statewide.

affected_groups.group: Students with disabilities
affected_groups.explanation: May use otherwise impermissible devices or software applications when an IEP or Section 504 plan provides for their use as a reasonable accommodation or assistive technology.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: Their use of electronic devices and software applications is governed by the standards that must provide the exception.

major_effects.label: Disability-related exceptions in school technology standards
major_effects.explanation: Requires the standards to allow otherwise impermissible devices or applications for a student with a disability when use is specified in an IEP or Section 504 plan as a reasonable accommodation or assistive technology.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill adds a requirement to the standards the agency adopts for school electronic devices and software applications.

SB125.summary: SB 125 would repeal Education Code Section 51.3525, identified by the bill as containing requirements concerning diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives at public institutions of higher education. It would also remove that section from the provisions for which the office receives and, when necessary, investigates institutional noncompliance complaints, while retaining the other listed provisions.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill repeals a requirement applicable to public institutions of higher education and changes which institutional compliance complaints are covered.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change concerns public institutions of higher education under Texas law and is not limited to a named place.

affected_groups.group: Public institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: The bill repeals a statutory requirement relating to these institutions and removes it from the listed complaint grounds.

major_effects.label: Repeal of DEI-related requirements
major_effects.explanation: Repeals Section 51.3525, which the bill describes as concerning requirements regarding diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives at public institutions of higher education.

major_effects.label: Complaint oversight scope narrowed
major_effects.explanation: Removes Section 51.3525 from the listed provisions for which the office receives and may investigate institutional noncompliance complaints.

agencies.name: the office
agencies.explanation: The bill removes Section 51.3525 from the provisions whose institutional noncompliance complaints the office receives and may investigate. The supplied text does not identify the office's canonical name.

SB126.summary: The bill requires specified power outage, AMBER, active shooter, Silver, missing suspect, missing adult, and severe-weather alerts to be provided in English, Spanish, and each language spoken by at least 10 percent of Texas residents, as determined by the most recent federal decennial census. The Department of Public Safety and the Texas Division of Emergency Management must adopt rules to implement the changes.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes language requirements for emergency and public-safety alerts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The alert-language threshold is based on residents of Texas, and the bill addresses statewide alert systems and advisories.

affected_groups.group: Texas residents who receive the specified alerts, including Spanish speakers and speakers of languages meeting the 10-percent threshold
affected_groups.explanation: Recipients of the listed alerts would receive the information in the required languages.

affected_groups.group: Electricity customers
affected_groups.explanation: Power outage alerts directed to electricity customers must meet the new language requirement.

major_effects.label: Multilingual emergency alert requirements
major_effects.explanation: Requires specified outage, missing-person, active-shooter, and severe-weather alert information to be in English, Spanish, and each language spoken by at least 10 percent of state residents, based on the most recent federal decennial census.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Department of Public Safety and the Texas Division of Emergency Management to adopt rules implementing the changes.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly requires the department to adopt rules implementing its changes.

agencies.name: Texas Division of Emergency Management
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly requires the division to adopt implementation rules and assigns it a role in coordinating multilingual severe-weather advisories.

SB127.summary: SB 127 would expand the required outreach about tuition and fee exemptions to include informational materials for facilities, caregivers or adoptive parents, and schools serving students in grades 9 through 12 who are in foster care or formerly in foster or other residential care. It would also require the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board and the Department of Family and Protective Services to create a streamlined eligibility and application process, including online applications and automatic delivery of eligibility documentation for students the department determines are eligible.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes outreach and the application process for tuition and fee exemptions for eligible students.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements cover the specified student groups and schools across the state, rather than a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Students in grades 9 through 12 in the conservatorship of the Department of Family and Protective Services
affected_groups.explanation: They are the subject of exemption outreach and the new application process.

affected_groups.group: Adopted students in grades 9 through 12 formerly in foster or other residential care
affected_groups.explanation: They are included in the exemption outreach and the streamlined process.

affected_groups.group: Caregivers, adoptive parents, residential child-care facilities, and schools serving students in grade nine or above
affected_groups.explanation: Outreach programs must provide them informational materials about the exemption.

major_effects.label: Expanded exemption outreach
major_effects.explanation: Existing outreach programs must include informational materials for specified facilities, caregivers or adoptive parents, and schools regarding exemptions for the covered student groups.

major_effects.label: Streamlined eligibility and application process
major_effects.explanation: The two agencies must jointly implement a process intended to reduce administrative burden, allow online applications, and automatically send required eligibility documentation to the institution selected by a student whom the department determines eligible.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: Must develop the exemption outreach programs.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: Must develop outreach programs and jointly design and implement the streamlined eligibility and application process.

agencies.name: Department of Family and Protective Services
agencies.explanation: Must jointly implement the streamlined process and submit eligibility documentation for students it determines eligible. The supplied canonical vocabulary does not provide a registry ID for this named department.

SB128.summary: The bill would require the Texas Department of Transportation to coordinate with local flood control authorities and add stormwater outfalls or other appropriate flood-control measures when constructing highway projects. In selecting those measures, the department would have to consider existing, proposed, and expected roadways reasonably near the project.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes requirements for the design and construction of the department's highway projects.
The bill requires flood-control measures, including stormwater outfalls, as part of highway projects.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill addresses the department's highway projects without specifying a narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Local flood control authorities
affected_groups.explanation: The department would be required to coordinate with these authorities on highway-project flood control.

major_effects.label: Flood-control requirements for highway projects
major_effects.explanation: The bill would require coordination and flood-control measures in highway projects, with nearby existing, proposed, and expected roadways considered in selecting measures.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the department requirements for flood control measures and coordination in its highway projects.

SB129.summary: The bill requires the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board to study causes of housing insecurity and instability among students at institutions of higher education and its effects on students. By May 1, 2028, the board must report its findings and any recommendations to state officials and each institution; the Act expires January 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a study and reporting requirement concerning students enrolled at institutions of higher education.
The required study examines student housing insecurity, including housing displacement, affordability, and housing availability.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The study concerns students at institutions of higher education statewide, with no narrower geographic area specified.

affected_groups.group: Students enrolled at institutions of higher education, particularly students experiencing housing insecurity or instability
affected_groups.explanation: Their housing circumstances and related academic, financial, and well-being outcomes are the subject of the study.

major_effects.label: Student housing study
major_effects.explanation: Requires a study of causes of student housing insecurity and instability and their effects on students.

major_effects.label: Study findings and recommendations report
major_effects.explanation: Requires the board to report the study's findings and any recommendations to specified state officials and each institution of higher education by May 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The Act defines the board as the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board and assigns it the study and reporting duties.

SB130.summary: SB 130 would allow a person whose conduct constitutes both forgery and another offense to be prosecuted under the forgery law, the other law, or both. The change would apply only to offenses committed on or after the Act’s effective date; earlier offenses would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the available prosecution options for conduct that constitutes forgery and another offense.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a Texas Penal Code provision governing prosecution, with no narrower geographic limitation stated.

affected_groups.group: People accused of conduct constituting both forgery and another offense
affected_groups.explanation: They could be prosecuted under the forgery law, the other law, or both, for offenses within the bill’s applicability period.

affected_groups.group: Prosecutors
affected_groups.explanation: They would have the option to prosecute qualifying conduct under both laws rather than choosing between them.

major_effects.label: Allows prosecution under both laws
major_effects.explanation: For qualifying offenses, prosecution may proceed under the forgery provision, the other applicable law, or both.

SB131.summary: The bill requires an institution admitting a transfer student to waive tuition and required fees for credit hours the institution does not count toward the student’s degree, or counts only as elective credit, when the credits are from specified core or field-of-study curricula or were awarded for qualifying Advanced Placement or International Baccalaureate work.
