affected_groups.group: Institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: Institutions are study collaborators, and the study examines program models at institutions inside and outside Texas.

major_effects.label: Study and report on support for former foster care students
major_effects.explanation: Requires a study of specified student and financial-assistance outcomes and successful program models, followed by a written report with findings and any recommendations.

major_effects.label: Limit use of personally identifiable student information
major_effects.explanation: The board may not request, require, or use personally identifiable student information for the study.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the board the study and reporting duties; the bill title identifies the board as the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The agency is required to collaborate with the board on the study.

agencies.name: Department of Family and Protective Services
agencies.explanation: The department is required to collaborate on the study and is also a report recipient. No matching canonical registry entry is supplied.

SB248.summary: Beginning September 1, 2027, the bill expands the child-custody-interference offense to cover a parent who knowingly entices or persuades a child under 18 to leave the custody of the other parent or a guardian, or a person standing in their stead. The offense is generally a Class C misdemeanor punishable by a $500 fine, but becomes a state jail felony if the defendant has at least two prior convictions under that subsection or entices the child to leave the state; the changes apply only to offenses committed on or after the effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the scope and punishment of a criminal offense.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Penal Code and sets rules for offenses under that code.

affected_groups.group: Parents
affected_groups.explanation: Parents may be subject to the expanded offense when they knowingly entice or persuade a child to leave specified custody.

affected_groups.group: Children under 18 and their custodians
affected_groups.explanation: The offense concerns a child leaving the custody of the other parent, a guardian, or a qualifying person standing in their stead.

affected_groups.group: People convicted of the offense
affected_groups.explanation: A conviction under subsection (b) carries a $500 fine as a Class C misdemeanor, with specified circumstances making it a state jail felony.

major_effects.label: Expanded child-custody-interference offense
major_effects.explanation: Removes the noncustodial-parent limitation and identifies custody of the other parent, a guardian, or a qualifying person standing in their stead.

major_effects.label: Penalty for subsection (b) offense
major_effects.explanation: Sets a $500 Class C misdemeanor penalty, elevated to a state jail felony for two or more prior subsection (b) convictions or when the child is enticed to leave the state.

SB249.summary: The bill would bar health maintenance organizations and insurers from requiring participating physicians and providers to obtain preauthorization for specified services, including emergency and certain urgent, outpatient mental health, preventive, and eye care; exceptions include some prescription drugs and infusions, and capitation arrangements where the provider agrees otherwise. It would limit payment denials and retrospective reviews for those services and require a notice if a provider submits a preauthorization request anyway. The changes would apply to requests under plans delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028, and would exclude CHIP and Medicaid plans.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes preauthorization and payment rules for specified health care services under covered health plans.
Imposes requirements and limits on health maintenance organizations, insurers, and certain contractors administering preauthorization.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Insurance Code provisions applicable to the covered plans; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: Patients enrolled in covered health plans
affected_groups.explanation: Patients enrolled in plans within the subchapter’s scope may receive specified services without a preauthorization requirement. The HMO-plan coverage excludes the child health plan program under Chapter 62 and the health benefits plan for children under Chapter 63; other applicability limits also apply.

affected_groups.group: Participating physicians and providers
affected_groups.explanation: They generally would not have to obtain preauthorization for covered service categories, except for services under a fully capitated risk-sharing or capitation arrangement when the participating physician or provider otherwise agrees. They would also be subject to the stated limits on payment denial and review.

affected_groups.group: Health maintenance organizations, insurers, and their preauthorization contractors
affected_groups.explanation: These entities would have to follow the new preauthorization, payment-review, and notice requirements for plans covered by the bill.

major_effects.label: Prohibits preauthorization for specified services
major_effects.explanation: Covered plans could not require preauthorization for the listed service categories. For outpatient mental health or substance use disorder treatment, this does not extend to the provision of prescription drugs or intravenous infusions. The fully capitated-services exception applies unless the participating physician or provider agrees otherwise.

major_effects.label: Limits payment denials and retrospective reviews
major_effects.explanation: Payment for services exempt from preauthorization generally could not be denied or reduced, except for knowing, material misrepresentation with specific intent to deceive and obtain unlawful payment or failure to substantially perform. Retrospective review would be allowed only with reasonable cause to suspect a basis for denial.

major_effects.label: Requires notice after an unnecessary preauthorization request
major_effects.explanation: If a physician or provider submits a request for a service that does not require preauthorization, the plan must promptly give written notice stating that preauthorization is not required and describing payment requirements.

SB250.summary: SB 250 would add breast cancer and cancers primarily specific to the female reproductive system to the cancers covered by Government Code Section 607.055 for firefighter and emergency medical technician benefits or compensation claims. The expansion would apply only to claims brought on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands the cancers covered for firefighter and emergency medical technician claims for benefits or compensation.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a Texas statute governing claims and has statewide scope.

affected_groups.group: Firefighters and emergency medical technicians
affected_groups.explanation: Their claims for benefits or compensation involving the added cancers fall within the expanded coverage.

affected_groups.group: Firefighters and emergency medical technicians with breast or female reproductive system cancers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill adds these cancers to the conditions covered by the section, for claims brought on or after the effective date.

major_effects.label: Expands covered cancers for claims
major_effects.explanation: Adds breast cancer and cancers primarily specific to the female reproductive system to the cancers covered by the section. The change applies only to claims brought on or after the effective date.

SB251.summary: For employees earning no more than the greater of the federal minimum wage or $15 an hour, the bill would prohibit employers (excluding public employers) from requiring noncompetes that restrict work for another employer by time, geographic area, or similar-work limits; those covenants would be void and unenforceable. The change would apply only to covenants entered into on or after the Act’s effective date, while earlier covenants would remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the employment restrictions employers may impose on employees within the bill’s earnings threshold.
Restricts covered employers’ use of specified noncompete covenants and makes those covenants unenforceable.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Business & Commerce Code and establishes a statewide rule rather than a locality-specific one.

affected_groups.group: Employees within the bill’s earnings threshold
affected_groups.explanation: Employees earning no more than the greater of the federal minimum wage or $15 an hour would be protected from the specified required noncompetes.

affected_groups.group: Employers other than public employers
affected_groups.explanation: Covered employers could not require qualifying employees to enter into the specified covenants; the bill’s definition excludes public employers.

major_effects.label: Prohibits specified noncompetes for qualifying employees
major_effects.explanation: Covered employers could not require covenants restricting work for another employer by time, geographic area, or similarity to the employee’s current work; the covenants would be void and unenforceable, and Section 15.51 would not apply to them.

major_effects.label: Adds the new rule to the exclusive and preemptive framework
major_effects.explanation: Section 15.502 would be included among the statutory criteria for noncompete enforceability that are exclusive and preempt other law, including common law.

major_effects.label: Applies prospectively
major_effects.explanation: Only covenants entered into on or after the Act’s effective date are covered by the change; earlier covenants remain governed by prior law.

SB252.summary: SB 252 would impose a fiduciary duty on pharmacy benefit managers administering pharmacy benefits for a plan toward individuals covered by that plan. The duty would require loyalty and care in covered individuals’ best interests, reasonable and full disclosure of fees, costs, and commissions, avoidance of self-dealing and conflicts, and transparency in related financial and contractual arrangements.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes duties for pharmacy benefit managers in connection with prescription drug benefits provided through a plan.
The bill establishes fiduciary and financial-conduct standards for pharmacy benefit managers.

affected_groups.group: Pharmacy benefit managers
affected_groups.explanation: They would be subject to the new fiduciary and related conduct duties.

affected_groups.group: Individuals covered by plans providing pharmacy benefits
affected_groups.explanation: They would be the individuals to whom the pharmacy benefit manager owes the new fiduciary duty.

major_effects.label: Fiduciary protections for covered individuals
major_effects.explanation: Pharmacy benefit managers would owe covered individuals duties of loyalty and care, disclosure, avoidance of conflicts, and transparency in plan-related financial and contractual arrangements.

SB253.summary: If voters approve the 2027 proposed constitutional amendment establishing an increased minimum wage and an annual inflation adjustment, the bill would require employers to pay the minimum wage established under the Texas Constitution instead of the federal minimum wage and would repeal Labor Code Section 62.151. It would take effect January 1, 2028, only if voters approve that amendment; otherwise, the bill would have no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill conditionally changes the minimum-wage standard employers must pay employees.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing the minimum wage, with no narrower geographic limitation stated.

affected_groups.group: Employees covered by the minimum-wage requirement
affected_groups.explanation: Their required minimum wage would be tied to the Texas constitutional standard if the amendment is approved.

affected_groups.group: Employers subject to the minimum-wage requirement
affected_groups.explanation: They would be required to pay the constitutional minimum wage if the amendment is approved.

major_effects.label: Minimum-wage standard
major_effects.explanation: If voters approve the specified amendment, the bill would replace the federal minimum-wage reference with the minimum wage established by the Texas Constitution.

major_effects.label: Repeal of Labor Code Section 62.151
major_effects.explanation: The bill repeals the section, but its subject and the practical effect of removing it are not shown in the bill text.

SB254.summary: The bill would require annual inflation-based adjustments to Teacher Retirement System of Texas service, disability, and death benefits, using the annual CPI-W increase as the adjustment rate. An increase could be withheld if the system is not actuarially sound or lacks funds; if funds are insufficient, the rate would be reduced to the largest amount the system can afford while maintaining actuarial soundness. The changes would apply only to benefits paid on or after January 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the amounts paid in retirement and related benefits, subject to the system's actuarial soundness and available funds.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change applies to benefits paid by the statewide Teacher Retirement System of Texas.

affected_groups.group: Recipients of Teacher Retirement System of Texas service retirement, disability retirement, or death benefits
affected_groups.explanation: Their benefit amounts may receive annual inflation-based adjustments, subject to actuarial soundness and available funds.

major_effects.label: Conditional inflation-based benefit adjustments
major_effects.explanation: Requires annual adjustments based on CPI-W increases, but only when the system is actuarially sound and has funds; if funds are insufficient, the adjustment is limited to the largest rate supportable while maintaining actuarial soundness.

agencies.name: Teacher Retirement System of Texas
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the amounts of benefits paid by the system under the relevant chapter, beginning with benefits paid on or after the stated date.

agencies.name: board of trustees
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the board of trustees duties to set the annual adjustment rate and increase benefit amounts; the source does not specify the board's canonical identity.

SB255.summary: The bill prohibits selling algorithmic device services or products for setting or recommending residential rent, and bars providers advising landlords from using nonpublic competitor data in algorithmic calculations. The chapter does not apply to a covered device using such data when nonpublic executed lease data is also available to the public in aggregated, anonymous form for no more than a reasonable charge; it also excludes certain periodic trade-association reports and products used to establish affordable-housing rent or income limits.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates restrictions on businesses providing algorithmic rent-setting services and treats violations as deceptive trade practices.
Regulates algorithmic services used to set or recommend residential rents.
Restricts algorithmic calculations using specified nonpublic competitor data.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The restrictions cover residential properties in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Landlords of residential premises
affected_groups.explanation: They are the intended recipients of rent advice covered by the restrictions.

affected_groups.group: Providers of algorithmic rent-setting services or products
affected_groups.explanation: Their sale and use of covered services or products would be restricted.

affected_groups.group: Residential tenants
affected_groups.explanation: The bill restricts covered tools used to determine or recommend the rent charged to them.

major_effects.label: Restrictions on algorithmic rent-setting
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits selling covered services or products to set or recommend residential rents and restricts covered providers from using nonpublic competitor data, subject to the chapter's applicability exception.

major_effects.label: Deceptive-trade-practice actionability
major_effects.explanation: Makes a violation of the new restrictions actionable as a deceptive trade practice under the specified existing law.

SB256.summary: SB 256 would broaden eligibility for organizations to register vehicles by removing the requirements that transported veterans’ disabilities result from military service and be service-connected. The vehicles must still be used exclusively to transport veterans with disabilities, and the veterans must not be charged for the transportation.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility to register motor vehicles under a state vehicle-registration provision.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a Texas Transportation Code registration provision with statewide application.

affected_groups.group: Veterans of the U.S. armed forces with disabilities who meet the stated compensation, vehicle, and disability criteria
affected_groups.explanation: The bill removes the service-connection and military-service relationship requirements while retaining the other eligibility conditions.

affected_groups.group: Organizations transporting veterans with disabilities without charge
affected_groups.explanation: Organizations may register qualifying transport vehicles when the veterans are not charged for transportation.

major_effects.label: Broader eligibility for vehicle registration
major_effects.explanation: Removes the service-connected and military-service requirements for veterans’ disabilities. Personal-use eligibility still requires the specified disability threshold, U.S. compensation because of the disability, and a qualifying owned vehicle; organizational registration remains limited to vehicles used exclusively for no-charge transportation of veterans with disabilities.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Motor Vehicles
agencies.explanation: The bill changes eligibility for vehicle registration and related plates, which implicates the state body administering motor-vehicle registration; the bill does not name that body.

SB257.summary: SB 257, also called Elliott’s Law, would expressly require emergency medical services providers to own or hold a long-term lease for visual communication equipment. It directs the Health and Human Services Commission’s executive commissioner to adopt rules requiring EMS personnel to have equipment that helps patients communicate pain, essential needs, and other information, including patients with specified communication barriers.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes equipment requirements for emergency medical services providers and communication with patients receiving emergency care.
Sets an equipment requirement for EMS personnel responding to emergencies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to each emergency medical services provider under the Texas statute.

affected_groups.group: Emergency medical services providers and personnel
affected_groups.explanation: Providers must own or hold a long-term lease for the required equipment and provide it to their personnel under rules adopted by the executive commissioner.

affected_groups.group: Patients who may have difficulty communicating during emergency care
affected_groups.explanation: The equipment is intended to help children without sufficient verbal skills, people not fluent in a language spoken by EMS personnel, patients whose medical crisis impedes communication, and people with specified communication disorders.

major_effects.label: Adds visual communication equipment to required EMS equipment
major_effects.explanation: EMS providers must own or hold a long-term lease for necessary equipment, with visual communication equipment expressly included.

major_effects.label: Requires rules for visual communication equipment
major_effects.explanation: The executive commissioner must adopt rules requiring providers to equip personnel with tools that support patient communication, including pointing to pain locations and conveying essential needs.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission’s executive commissioner is assigned rulemaking and implementation duties for the new equipment requirement.

SB258.summary: The bill would allow the commissioner of insurance to consider whether individual health benefit plan rates are affordable and whether issuers have taken effective steps to improve affordability when assessing whether rates are excessive. The change would apply only to coverage delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how rates for individual health benefit plans may be assessed for excessiveness.
Adds affordability considerations to the regulatory review of health plan issuer rates.

affected_groups.group: Individual health benefit plan issuers
affected_groups.explanation: Their affordability strategies may be considered in determining whether rates are excessive.

affected_groups.group: People covered by individual health benefit plans
affected_groups.explanation: Rates for their coverage would be subject to the revised review considerations when the coverage is delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2029.

major_effects.label: Adds affordability factors to rate review
major_effects.explanation: Permits the commissioner to consider rate affordability and issuers' effective affordability strategies when determining whether an individual health plan rate is excessive.

agencies.name: Commissioner of Insurance
agencies.explanation: The bill directly authorizes this official to consider affordability factors when reviewing rates; it does not identify the official's department by name.

SB259.summary: The bill would prohibit health care providers from charging facility fees for telehealth services and set claim-coding, patient-notice, and fee-charging requirements for specified facilities and services. At a provider-based outpatient facility or hospital-owned facility, a provider may not charge a patient or third-party payor a facility fee unless the provider provides notice as required by the section. It would also require the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston to study facility fees and report to the Legislature only if the Legislature specifically appropriates money for that purpose; without such an appropriation, the center may use other available money but is not required to conduct the study.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill regulates health care provider facility fees, claims, and patient disclosures.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill creates statewide Texas health-care requirements and expressly addresses facility fees charged in this state.

affected_groups.group: Health care providers, including hospitals and provider-based outpatient facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Providers would be subject to the facility-fee prohibition, claim coding, notice requirements, and potential penalties.

affected_groups.group: Patients receiving services or supplies at covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Patients would receive written notice of the facility fee amount or, if the exact service or supply is unknown, an explanation that they may incur cost-share or coinsurance unless the service or supply is provided by an independent physician or physician group.

affected_groups.group: Third-party payors
affected_groups.explanation: Payors would receive advance notice before a provider begins charging specified new facility fees, and claims must include a valid place-of-service code.

affected_groups.group: Independent physicians and physician groups
affected_groups.explanation: The bill includes independent physicians or groups in an aggregate cost comparison; the comparison of professional-fee charges applies when a health care facility fee is included in a patient's statement of charges.

major_effects.label: Prohibition on telehealth facility fees
major_effects.explanation: Providers may not charge facility fees for telehealth or telemedicine services, subject to the bill's definition of those services.

major_effects.label: Place-of-service coding on reimbursement claims
major_effects.explanation: Each reimbursement claim for a service provided by the health care provider must include a valid code indicating the setting where the service was provided.

major_effects.label: Facility-fee notice and charging requirements
major_effects.explanation: For the facilities and services specified in the bill, providers must give written patient notice and may not charge a patient or payor unless that notice is provided; specified new charges also require advance notice to contracted payors.

major_effects.label: Administrative penalties
major_effects.explanation: The Commission or a state regulatory authority with jurisdiction must assess a penalty of up to $1,000 per violation of the chapter or its rules.

major_effects.label: Conditionally required facility-fee study and report
major_effects.explanation: The study and report are required only if the Legislature specifically appropriates money for that purpose; without such an appropriation, the center may use other available money but is not required to do so.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the Commission as HHSC and authorizes it to assess administrative penalties and adopt implementing rules.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The department is to cooperate in the facility-fee study if conducted. The center is required to conduct the study only if the legislature specifically appropriates money; without that appropriation, it may, but is not required to, use other available money to do so.

agencies.name: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the institution the study and legislative-report duties, subject to the appropriation condition. The supplied registry does not identify a canonical entry for this institution.

agencies.name: Appropriate state regulatory authority with jurisdiction over a health care provider
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns penalty-assessment and rulemaking authority to a state regulatory authority with jurisdiction, but does not identify which authority or provider types it covers.

SB260.summary: The bill would generally make agreements unenforceable when they restrict grocery or drug stores, or limit their size, in qualifying shopping centers, subject to specified exceptions for store relocation and limits on the number of stores. Municipal or county authorities could establish good-cause procedures to modify some exception terms; the bill also requires notice of covered agreements and authorizes specified government attorneys to enforce the chapter. It would apply only to agreements executed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates enforceability limits and notice requirements for certain commercial agreements restricting grocery or drug stores.
Changes the treatment of agreements restricting the use of real property in qualifying shopping centers.
Allows municipal and county authorities to establish procedures for modifying certain exceptions and preserves local regulation of these agreements.

locations.name: Qualifying shopping centers in municipal areas or unincorporated county areas
locations.explanation: The chapter applies to qualifying shopping centers in areas where grocery or drug stores are allowed uses under municipal or county land-use regulations.

affected_groups.group: Parties to agreements restricting grocery or drug store uses in qualifying shopping centers
affected_groups.explanation: Subject to the exceptions in Sections 251.004 and 251.005, covered agreements may be unenforceable to the specified extent; parties entering covered agreements must also provide notice.

affected_groups.group: Grocery and drug store owners or operators
affected_groups.explanation: The bill limits restrictions on opening or sizing their stores in covered shopping centers, subject to exceptions.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities and counties
affected_groups.explanation: Their governing bodies may establish good-cause procedures for modifying certain exceptions, and they receive notice in specified circumstances.

major_effects.label: Limits enforceability of store-use restrictions
major_effects.explanation: In qualifying shopping centers, covered agreements are unenforceable to the extent they restrict use for a grocery or drug store or limit store size, except as provided for specified relocation and store-count agreements.

major_effects.label: Local good-cause procedures
major_effects.explanation: Municipal or county governing bodies may establish procedures allowing modification of specified relocation or store-count exception terms upon a showing of good cause.

major_effects.label: Notice of covered agreements
major_effects.explanation: A party entering a covered agreement must send written notice to the attorney general and, depending on the property's location, the municipality or county.

major_effects.label: Enforcement actions
major_effects.explanation: The attorney general, a city attorney, or a county attorney may bring an enforcement action in district court.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The attorney general must receive notice of covered agreements and may bring an action to enforce the chapter.

SB261.summary: Beginning with the 2026–2027 school year, school districts would have to offer prekindergarten to every child at least four years old and could offer it to any child at least three years old; classes offered under this section may not charge tuition. The bill would change how half-day and full-day prekindergarten attendance counts for school funding and remove a required free-prekindergarten-eligibility breakdown from annual early-education reports.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes public-school prekindergarten access and related reporting and attendance calculations.
Changes the average-daily-attendance calculation used in school funding for prekindergarten programs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes apply to school districts under the statewide Education Code rather than to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Children who are at least four years old and their families
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would be required to offer these children prekindergarten without tuition.

affected_groups.group: Children who are at least three years old and their families
affected_groups.explanation: Districts could offer prekindergarten to any child in this age group.

affected_groups.group: School districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: Districts receive the new offering duty; attendance calculations and early-education reporting also affect these education providers.

major_effects.label: Broader prekindergarten access
major_effects.explanation: Districts would have to offer classes to any child at least four years old and could offer them to any child at least three years old; classes under this section may not charge tuition.

major_effects.label: Prekindergarten attendance calculations
major_effects.explanation: For prekindergarten programs under Section 29.153(c), half-day programs count as one-half of the relevant average daily attendance and full-day programs count as the full amount. A half-day district or charter program is eligible for one-half ADA only if it provides at least 32,400 instructional minutes.

major_effects.label: Early-education report contents
major_effects.explanation: Annual reports would no longer be required to disaggregate third-grade reading or mathematics results by whether a student was eligible for free prekindergarten.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill changes the required contents of annual early-education reports produced by the agency, but the supplied text does not establish the agency's canonical identity.

SB262.summary: For construction projects contracted for less than one percent of a municipality’s most recently adopted budget, municipalities with populations under 20,000 would not have to ensure the contractor has workers’ compensation insurance or require a performance bond. A project includes work at one location within 12 months, and municipalities may not combine work from multiple projects to calculate the contract amount.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes contracting requirements for municipalities below the population threshold.
Relaxes insurance and performance-bond requirements for contractors on qualifying municipal projects.
Changes when municipalities must ensure workers’ compensation coverage for construction contractors.

locations.name: Texas municipalities with populations under 20,000
locations.explanation: The provision applies to municipalities meeting the population threshold.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities with populations under 20,000
affected_groups.explanation: These municipalities may use the exemptions for construction projects meeting the budget-based contract threshold.

affected_groups.group: Construction contractors and their workers on qualifying municipal projects
affected_groups.explanation: Contractors would not have to meet these municipal insurance and performance-bond requirements for qualifying projects; the insurance exemption may affect coverage for workers on those projects.

major_effects.label: Small-project contracting exemptions
major_effects.explanation: Qualifying municipalities would not be required to ensure contractor workers’ compensation coverage or require a performance bond for projects below the budget-based threshold. A project covers work at one location within 12 months, and work from multiple projects may not be aggregated to determine the contract amount.

SB263.summary: Subject to the existing subsection (a-1) exception, SB 263 would require groundwater-availability certifications for covered plat applications to comply with TCEQ rules, require TCEQ to set the certification’s form and content and define credible evidence of groundwater availability, and require municipal authorities and commissioners courts to disapprove applications that do not comply. It would broaden specified county exceptions to platting requirements and clarify that a county in a priority groundwater management area may adopt water-availability requirements notwithstanding Section 232.001(h), but only if needed to prevent current or projected water use from exceeding the county’s safe sustainable yield. The changes apply only to plat applications filed on or after the effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes county platting exceptions and requires municipal authorities and commissioners courts to disapprove noncompliant plat applications.
The bill changes when certain land subdivisions may be exempt from county plat-preparation requirements.
The bill adds TCEQ rules for groundwater-availability certifications and addresses county water-availability requirements tied to safe sustainable yield.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends generally applicable Texas statutes and does not confine the changes to a named locality.

locations.name: Land outside municipal limits
locations.explanation: The expanded county platting exceptions apply to qualifying tracts outside municipal limits.

locations.name: Priority groundwater management areas
locations.explanation: The county water-availability authority addressed by the bill applies in these areas.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for groundwater-supplied subdivisions
affected_groups.explanation: Covered applicants must provide a certification that complies with TCEQ rules, subject to the existing subsection (a-1) exception.

affected_groups.group: Municipal authorities
affected_groups.explanation: Municipal authorities must disapprove plat applications that fail to meet the section’s requirements.

affected_groups.group: County governments and commissioners courts
affected_groups.explanation: Commissioners courts must disapprove noncompliant applications and, in qualifying groundwater management areas, may adopt water-availability requirements subject to the safe-sustainable-yield condition.

affected_groups.group: Owners subdividing qualifying tracts outside municipal limits
affected_groups.explanation: Owners of specified agricultural-use tracts or subdivisions with all lots over 10 acres may qualify for broader exemptions from county plat-preparation requirements.

major_effects.label: Groundwater certification requirements
major_effects.explanation: For covered groundwater-supplied subdivisions, the attached certification must comply with TCEQ rules; the bill does not remove the existing subsection (a-1) exception.

major_effects.label: TCEQ groundwater certification rules
major_effects.explanation: TCEQ must establish certification form and content and define credible evidence of groundwater availability.

major_effects.label: Required disapproval of noncompliant plats
major_effects.explanation: Municipal authorities and commissioners courts must disapprove plat applications that fail to meet the applicable section’s requirements.

major_effects.label: Broader county platting exceptions
major_effects.explanation: For the specified agricultural-use tracts and subdivisions with all lots over 10 acres, the exception applies when the owner does not lay out a specified tract part or does not lay out public-use streets, parks, or similar parts.

major_effects.label: County water-availability requirements
major_effects.explanation: In a priority groundwater management area, a commissioners court may adopt water-availability requirements notwithstanding Section 232.001(h), if it determines they are necessary to prevent current or projected county water use from exceeding safe sustainable yield.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill directs TCEQ to adopt rules setting certification form and content and defining credible evidence of groundwater availability.

SB264.summary: For covered inactive-well fluid level or hydraulic pressure tests, operators would have to give at least three days’ notice to the Railroad Commission district office and the surface estate owner, and obtain the office’s approval before testing. The owner or representative would be entitled to witness the test, and operators would have to provide the owner results of unsuccessful tests; these changes apply to tests conducted on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes testing requirements for inactive wells subject to the Railroad Commission’s jurisdiction.
Adds notice, approval, and test-result duties for operators conducting covered tests.

locations.name: Statewide—wells subject to Railroad Commission of Texas jurisdiction
locations.explanation: The changes apply to covered inactive wells under the Commission’s jurisdiction, without limiting them to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Operators of covered inactive wells
affected_groups.explanation: Operators would have to provide advance notice, obtain approval before testing, and provide results of unsuccessful tests to the notified surface estate owner.

affected_groups.group: Surface estate owners and their representatives
affected_groups.explanation: Owners would receive advance notice, be entitled to witness the test, and receive results of unsuccessful tests; representatives are expressly entitled to witness.

major_effects.label: Advance notice and unsuccessful-test results
major_effects.explanation: Operators would notify the Commission district office and surface estate owner at least three days before a proposed test, and provide the owner results when a test is unsuccessful.

major_effects.label: Commission approval before testing
major_effects.explanation: An operator may not conduct a covered test without approval from the Commission office that receives the proposed-test notice.

major_effects.label: Surface owner’s opportunity to witness
major_effects.explanation: A surface estate owner, or the owner’s representative, who receives notice is entitled to witness the test.

agencies.name: Railroad Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: The Commission’s district office must receive notice and approve a covered test before it is conducted.

SB265.summary: SB 265 would define “personal communication device” broadly and require a youth camp operator that prohibits counselors from possessing such devices while serving as counselors to provide each counselor an operable two-way radio for contacting the camp’s administrative office. The operator would also have to require counselors to keep the radio active and with them while performing camp duties, and ensure they are trained in its proper use and maintenance.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill imposes equipment, use, and training requirements on youth camp operators that prohibit counselors from possessing personal communication devices.
It requires covered youth camps to equip counselors with a means of communicating with the camp administrative office while on duty.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to covered youth camp operators under Texas law, without limiting them to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Youth camp operators that prohibit counselors from possessing personal communication devices while acting as counselors
affected_groups.explanation: These operators would have to provide radios and ensure counselor radio use and training.

affected_groups.group: Youth camp counselors covered by the prohibition
affected_groups.explanation: They would be provided radios and required to keep them active and with them while performing camp duties, and to complete radio training.

major_effects.label: Two-way radios for covered counselors
major_effects.explanation: A covered operator must provide each counselor an operable radio for communication with the camp administrative office and require it to remain active and in the counselor’s possession during camp duties.

major_effects.label: Radio-use training
major_effects.explanation: Covered operators must ensure each counselor completes training on proper radio use and maintenance.

SB266.summary: The bill would allow municipalities with populations of 50,000 or more to transfer water or sewer system revenue to their general funds only to reimburse direct, actual costs incurred on behalf of those systems. Before granting covered water-related financial assistance, the Texas Water Development Board would have to require the municipality to certify compliance with that limit; the certification requirement would apply to applications submitted on or after September 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the authority of qualifying municipalities to transfer water or sewer system revenue and imposes a condition on their applications for financial assistance.
Changes municipal water and sewer system revenue rules and conditions for water-related financial assistance.
Makes compliance certification a prerequisite to the grant of covered state financial assistance.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply statewide to municipalities meeting the population threshold and to covered applications to the Texas Water Development Board.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities with populations of 50,000 or more
affected_groups.explanation: Their authority to transfer water or sewer system revenue is limited, and they must certify compliance when seeking covered financial assistance.

affected_groups.group: Municipally owned water and sewer utilities
affected_groups.explanation: Their owners may transfer system revenue to the municipal general fund only for reimbursement of direct, actual costs incurred on the system's behalf; covered utility applicants are also subject to the certification condition.

major_effects.label: Limits transfers of water and sewer revenue
major_effects.explanation: A municipality with a population of at least 50,000 may transfer that revenue to its general fund only to reimburse direct, actual costs incurred on behalf of the system.

major_effects.label: Requires compliance certification for covered assistance
major_effects.explanation: The Board must require a municipality to certify compliance with the municipal revenue-transfer provision before granting covered financial assistance; this applies to applications submitted on or after September 1, 2028.

major_effects.label: Directs implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: The Board's executive administrator must adopt or amend rules as necessary to implement the certification requirement.

agencies.name: Texas Water Development Board
agencies.explanation: The Board must require compliance certification before granting covered financial assistance; its executive administrator must adopt or amend rules to implement the requirement.

SB267.summary: The bill would require a person to hold a separate license for each youth camp the person owns, operates, controls, or supervises. The requirement would apply even when camps are located wholly or partly on the same premises.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the licensing requirement for people who own, operate, control, or supervise youth camps.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The licensing change applies to youth camps regulated under the Texas chapter, without a narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: People who own, operate, control, or supervise youth camps
affected_groups.explanation: These people would need a separate license for each youth camp they manage.

major_effects.label: Separate license for each youth camp
major_effects.explanation: Requires a separate license for every youth camp, including camps located wholly or partly on the same premises.

agencies.name: department
agencies.explanation: The separate-license requirement would affect administration of licenses under the chapter, but the bill refers only to a generic department and does not identify its canonical agency identity.

SB268.summary: The bill would let juvenile boards in adjacent or nearby counties agree in writing to operate jointly in specified matters, appoint a shared fiscal officer, and require them to send the agreement to the Texas Juvenile Justice Department. It would replace the daily and annual operating schedule for juvenile justice alternative education programs with a requirement to provide at least 43,200 instructional minutes per year, while allowing waivers subject to a limit tied to instructional minutes waived for school districts served by the program. The bill also repeals Human Resources Code §152.0036, but the supplied text does not show what that provision contains.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the annual instructional-time requirement and waiver limit for juvenile justice alternative education programs.
Changes operations of juvenile boards and a juvenile justice education program.
Authorizes county juvenile boards to arrange joint operations and share a fiscal officer.
Creates a framework for juvenile boards to jointly conduct specified matters.

locations.name: Counties adjacent to or in close proximity to one another
locations.explanation: Juvenile boards in these counties may arrange joint operations.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The revised instructional-time rule applies generally to juvenile justice alternative education programs, without a geographic limitation in the bill.

affected_groups.group: County juvenile boards
affected_groups.explanation: Boards in nearby counties may jointly operate in specified matters and share a fiscal officer.

affected_groups.group: Juvenile justice alternative education programs
affected_groups.explanation: Programs must meet the revised annual instructional-time requirement and may seek a waiver subject to a new limit.

affected_groups.group: Students served by juvenile justice alternative education programs
affected_groups.explanation: The annual minimum instructional time for their programs would be measured in minutes rather than by the former daily and yearly schedule.

major_effects.label: Joint juvenile-board operations
major_effects.explanation: Nearby county juvenile boards may agree in writing to operate jointly in specified matters and may appoint one fiscal officer for both boards.

major_effects.label: Submission of joint-operation agreements
major_effects.explanation: Boards that agree to operate jointly must provide a copy of their written agreement to the Texas Juvenile Justice Department.

major_effects.label: Juvenile-program instructional time and waivers
major_effects.explanation: Sets a 43,200-minute annual minimum in place of the former daily and 180-day schedule. A program may still seek a waiver, but the waiver cannot exceed the highest number of instructional minutes waived by the commissioner for any school district served by the program during the same school year.

major_effects.label: Repeal of Human Resources Code §152.0036
major_effects.explanation: Repeals the section, but the supplied bill text does not identify the provision being removed.

agencies.name: Texas Juvenile Justice Department
agencies.explanation: Must receive copies of joint-operation agreements and may grant instructional-time waivers subject to the bill's revised limit.

SB269.summary: For a party-filed motion under Estates Code Section 32.003 that is granted, the bill would require the assigned statutory probate court judge, to the extent possible and equitable, to order reimbursement of the county's qualifying compensation and expenses. The judge would also set the amount and manner of equitable apportionment among the estate and parties.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes how a county may recover compensation and expense payments for qualifying assigned judges.
Creates a cost-allocation duty for an assigned statutory probate court judge when a qualifying assignment motion is granted.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions apply to qualifying statutory probate court judge assignments across the state, rather than to a specified county or place.

affected_groups.group: Counties paying compensation and expenses for assigned statutory probate court judges
affected_groups.explanation: A judge must, to the extent possible and equitable, order reimbursement of qualifying amounts paid by the county.

affected_groups.group: Estates and parties in contested probate proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: The judge must prescribe how qualifying costs are equitably apportioned among the estate and parties, as applicable.

affected_groups.group: Statutory probate court judges assigned to hear contested matters
affected_groups.explanation: The assigned judge receives the new duty to order reimbursement and prescribe the cost apportionment when the motion is granted.

major_effects.label: Conditional reimbursement and cost apportionment
major_effects.explanation: For motions filed on or after the Act's effective date, if a party's assignment motion is granted, the judge must, to the extent possible and equitable, order reimbursement of qualifying county compensation and expenses and prescribe their equitable apportionment among the estate and parties, as applicable.

major_effects.label: Additional daily compensation made subject to the new provision
major_effects.explanation: The additional $25-per-day compensation for a judge assigned outside the judge's county of residence remains payable from the county general fund, but Section 25.0022(p) makes that payment subject to subsection (o-1). It is therefore included in the compensation subject to the applicable reimbursement and equitable-apportionment requirements.

SB270.summary: In counties with populations of at least 50,000 but less than 250,000, justice courts and municipal courts may appoint spoken-language interpreters who are not certified or licensed court interpreters only when conducting a proceeding other than a jury trial in a Class C misdemeanor case, subject to the bill’s specified conditions. Appointees must meet the stated expert, age, and nonparty requirements.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes appointment authority for justice and municipal courts in counties within a specified population range.
The bill changes which interpreters certain courts may appoint for proceedings.
The appointment authority is limited by specified misdemeanor and felony case exclusions.

locations.name: Counties with populations of 50,000 or more but less than 250,000
locations.explanation: The new appointment authority applies to courts in counties within this population range.

affected_groups.group: Justice courts, municipal courts, and municipal courts of record in qualifying counties
affected_groups.explanation: These courts receive the discretionary authority to appoint non-certified or non-licensed spoken-language interpreters for eligible proceedings.

affected_groups.group: People participating in proceedings who need spoken-language interpretation
affected_groups.explanation: They may be served by an interpreter appointed under the new authority, subject to the listed case exclusions.

affected_groups.group: People appointed as interpreters under the new authority
affected_groups.explanation: They must satisfy the court-qualification, age, and nonparty requirements.

major_effects.label: Appointment of non-certified interpreters
major_effects.explanation: Covered courts may appoint a spoken-language interpreter who is not certified or licensed for proceedings other than the specified Class C jury trials, Class A or B misdemeanor proceedings, and felony proceedings.

major_effects.label: Requirements for appointees
major_effects.explanation: The subsection (e) requirements are extended to appointments under the new authority: appointees must be qualified as experts, at least 18, and not parties to the proceeding.

SB271.summary: The bill would require the Health and Human Services Commission to establish a prescription drug purchasing pool through which eligible health plan issuers and employers could buy drugs for employees, dependents, and retirees at discounted rates or under terms the commission negotiates; it also provides an option to purchase negotiated stop-loss coverage. Participants would remain responsible for their claims and drug costs, and the commission must implement the bill only if the legislature specifically appropriates money for that purpose, though it may use other available money.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a prescription drug purchasing program for eligible health benefit plan issuers and employers.
Allows political subdivisions, including counties, municipalities, and public school districts, to qualify as public employers participating in the pool.
Makes implementation contingent on a specific legislative appropriation, while permitting use of other available money.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The pool is available to qualified employers and issuers connected to Texas, including private employers conducting business in the state.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plan issuers
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible issuers may enroll and purchase prescription drugs through the pool.

affected_groups.group: Public employers, including local governments and public school districts
affected_groups.explanation: Qualified public employers may participate in the purchasing pool.

affected_groups.group: Self-insured private employers conducting business in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: These employers may qualify to enroll in the pool.

affected_groups.group: Employees, their dependents, and retirees of participating issuers and employers
affected_groups.explanation: They are the people for whom participants may purchase prescription drugs through the pool.

major_effects.label: Prescription drug purchasing pool
major_effects.explanation: Directs HHSC to establish a pool for eligible issuers and employers to buy prescription drugs at discounted rates or on terms negotiated by the commission. The pool is not a risk pool, and participants remain responsible for claims and drug costs.

major_effects.label: Participation and administration procedures
major_effects.explanation: Requires the executive commissioner to establish rules and procedures for eligibility, enrollment, contributions, and ending participation.

major_effects.label: Optional stop-loss coverage and joint purchasing
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to offer participants an option to purchase stop-loss coverage at a negotiated rate and permits participants to purchase jointly through the pool.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission is defined as HHSC and is assigned responsibility for establishing the pool; the executive commissioner is directed to set administrative procedures and rules.

SB272.summary: SB 272 would require a pharmacy to disclose to a patient the pharmacy’s lowest cash price for the prescribed drug or biological product. It leaves in place the existing option to pay that lower price instead of a higher insurance copayment when that condition applies.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes price disclosure for prescribed drugs and biological products provided to patients.
The bill imposes a price-disclosure requirement on pharmacies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Texas Occupations Code applicable to pharmacies statewide.

affected_groups.group: Patients receiving prescribed drugs or biological products
affected_groups.explanation: Patients are to be told the pharmacy's lowest cash price for their prescribed product.

affected_groups.group: Pharmacies
affected_groups.explanation: Pharmacies would have to disclose their lowest cash price for a prescribed product.

major_effects.label: Pharmacy price disclosure
major_effects.explanation: Requires disclosure to the patient of the pharmacy's lowest cash price for the prescribed drug or biological product.

SB273.summary: The bill would prohibit a governmental entity from entering into a lease or other agreement for installing or constructing border security infrastructure on state park property. The prohibition applies to state and political-subdivision entities, but is limited to agreements for that infrastructure on that property.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill protects state park property from agreements for installing or constructing the specified border-security infrastructure.
The bill's definition includes political subdivisions, whose governmental entities would be subject to the agreement prohibition.
The bill restricts governmental entities' ability to enter into specified leases or agreements.

locations.name: State park property
locations.explanation: The prohibition is limited to agreements concerning infrastructure installed or constructed on state park property.

affected_groups.group: State and political-subdivision governmental entities
affected_groups.explanation: Entities covered by the bill's definition would be unable to enter the specified leases or other agreements.

major_effects.label: Restriction on specified agreements
major_effects.explanation: Governmental entities may not enter into a lease or other agreement for installing or constructing border security infrastructure on state park property; the text does not prohibit all such infrastructure activity apart from this agreement restriction.

agencies.name: Governmental entities of this state (not individually identified)
agencies.explanation: The bill directly bars entities within its broad definition from entering the specified agreements; it does not identify individual state agencies by name.

SB274.summary: The bill would expand enforcement of human-trafficking awareness and prevention requirements for commercial lodging establishments by allowing county and district attorneys to issue cure notices and bring actions for civil penalties or injunctive relief. Before suing, those attorneys would have to notify the attorney general, and civil penalties they recover would be payable to the county where the court heard the action.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands enforcement of requirements applying to commercial lodging establishments.
The bill expands enforcement of human-trafficking awareness and prevention requirements.
County and district attorneys gain enforcement authority, and recovered civil penalties are directed to a county.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The enforcement provisions apply in counties where commercial lodging establishments or violations are located, without limiting the bill to a named county.

affected_groups.group: Commercial lodging establishment operators
affected_groups.explanation: Operators may receive cure notices and face civil-penalty or injunctive actions brought by county or district attorneys.

affected_groups.group: County and district attorneys
affected_groups.explanation: They would gain authority to issue cure notices and bring enforcement actions, subject to notifying the attorney general before suit.

affected_groups.group: Counties
affected_groups.explanation: A county would receive civil penalties recovered by a county or district attorney in an action heard in a district court located there.

major_effects.label: County and district attorney enforcement authority
major_effects.explanation: County and district attorneys may bring actions to recover civil penalties or obtain injunctive relief; their actions must be brought in a county where some part of the violation or threatened violation occurs.

major_effects.label: Notice to the attorney general before suit
major_effects.explanation: A county or district attorney must notify the attorney general before bringing an action, using the form and manner the attorney general prescribes.

major_effects.label: Civil-penalty revenue to counties
major_effects.explanation: Civil penalties recovered by county or district attorneys go to the county where the district court hearing the action is located.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill requires county and district attorneys to notify the attorney general before suit and gives the attorney general authority to prescribe the notice's form and manner.

SB275.summary: The bill would raise the maximum low-income housing tax credits for an individual development from $2 million to $3 million in one application round, while retaining the $6 million applicant cap and the limits based on underwriting policy and federal law. The change would apply only to applications in cycles based on the 2028 qualified allocation plan or a later plan; earlier cycles would remain governed by the prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the allocation limit for low-income housing tax credits used for individual developments.
Raises the maximum amount of housing tax credits that may be allocated to an individual development in a round.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change concerns the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs' housing tax credit allocation process and is not limited to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for low-income housing tax credits
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants may seek a larger allocation for an individual development, subject to the existing applicant-wide cap and other limits.

affected_groups.group: Individual housing developments seeking tax-credit allocations
affected_groups.explanation: The maximum allocation for an individual development in one application round would increase.

major_effects.label: Higher per-development housing tax credit cap
major_effects.explanation: Raises the per-development limit from $2 million to $3 million per application round; it does not change the $6 million applicant cap or remove the underwriting and federal-law limits.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs
agencies.explanation: The revised allocation limit applies to applications submitted to the department, and the allocation subsection refers to the department's underwriting policy. The subsection assigns issuance of commitments to an unnamed board, so no separate identity is attributed to that board.

SB276.summary: The bill repeals the statutory designation of a portion of Loop 375 in El Paso County as the Cesar Chavez Border Highway. It does not specify a replacement designation.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the statutory designation of a state highway segment.

locations.name: Portion of Loop 375 in El Paso County
locations.explanation: This is the highway segment whose statutory designation is repealed.

major_effects.label: Repeals highway designation
major_effects.explanation: Removes the statutory designation of the specified Loop 375 segment as the Cesar Chavez Border Highway.

SB277.summary: The bill changes eligibility for juvenile drug courts when alcohol or controlled-substance use is suspected to have significantly contributed to the conduct. A juvenile may participate for conduct involving a firearm or other dangerous weapon, or serious bodily injury, only if the attorney representing the state consents; conduct involving another person's death remains disqualifying. The change applies to juveniles entering a program regardless of when the underlying conduct occurred.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the eligibility rules for juvenile drug court programs.
The eligibility change governs juvenile drug court programs established by county and municipal governing bodies.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing county and municipal drug court programs statewide.

affected_groups.group: Juveniles referred to drug court for conduct involving suspected substance use
affected_groups.explanation: Their eligibility may depend on whether the conduct involved a weapon, serious bodily injury, or death, and whether the state consents.

affected_groups.group: Attorneys representing the state
affected_groups.explanation: For the specified conduct, a juvenile is ineligible to participate unless the attorney representing the state consents; that consent is a condition of eligibility.

affected_groups.group: Counties and municipalities that establish juvenile drug court programs
affected_groups.explanation: Their programs are subject to the revised eligibility conditions.

major_effects.label: Juvenile drug-court eligibility
major_effects.explanation: For the specified conduct, a juvenile is ineligible to participate unless the attorney representing the state consents; conduct involving the death of another remains ineligible.

SB278.summary: SB 278 would expand eligibility for the existing authority of certain municipalities to use certain tax revenue for qualified projects. It would allow a municipality described by Tax Code Section 351.001(7)(E) to designate a continuous project financing zone containing the project, subject to the same maximum-area limit as the existing three-mile-radius option.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands which municipalities may use the existing project-financing-zone authority.
The bill expands eligibility for an existing authority to use certain tax revenue for qualified projects.

locations.name: Municipalities with a population of 640,000 or more that are located on an international border and have adopted a capital improvement plan for construction or expansion of a convention center
locations.explanation: The bill would extend the project-financing-zone provisions to municipalities meeting the population, location, and capital-improvement-plan criteria in Section 351.001(7)(E).

affected_groups.group: Municipalities with a population of 640,000 or more that are located on an international border and have adopted a capital improvement plan for construction or expansion of a convention center
affected_groups.explanation: The bill would make these municipalities eligible for the project-financing-zone provisions.

major_effects.label: Expands project-zone eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Adds municipalities described by Section 351.001(7)(E) to the covered categories and permits a continuous zone containing a qualified project, capped at the area allowed by the existing three-mile-radius option.

SB279.summary: The bill would establish the Cross-Agency Employment Resource Initiative to coordinate employment services for people who use workforce programs and also receive specified services from the Health and Human Services Commission or Texas Department of Criminal Justice. It would require the three agencies to make agreements for sharing relevant client data and resources, and their leaders to discuss the initiative quarterly; the agencies could accept gifts and grants and would investigate possible federal funding.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a cross-agency initiative to coordinate employment services and workforce-development goals for clients using multiple programs.
Requires specified state agencies to enter interagency agreements and agency leaders to discuss the initiative regularly.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill describes the employment services and resources being coordinated as being in this state.

affected_groups.group: People using workforce programs who also use specified HHSC or TDCJ programs
affected_groups.explanation: The initiative is intended to align services and provide program information to people served across these agencies.

affected_groups.group: State and local policymakers
affected_groups.explanation: The initiative is intended to enable policymakers to collaborate on policies and regulations related to employment and other workforce goals.

major_effects.label: Cross-agency employment initiative
major_effects.explanation: Establishes an initiative to coordinate services, information, and resources for clients using multiple programs.

major_effects.label: Interagency agreements and leadership discussions
major_effects.explanation: Requires the participating agencies to agree on processes for sharing relevant client data and resources, and their specified leaders to discuss the initiative quarterly.

major_effects.label: Potential grant and donation funding
major_effects.explanation: Allows the participating agencies to accept gifts, grants, and donations and requires them to investigate potential federal funding; it does not itself appropriate funds.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the commission as HHSC and assigns it interagency agreement, discussion, and funding-related responsibilities.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the department as TDCJ and assigns it interagency agreement, discussion, and funding-related responsibilities.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the workforce commission as TWC and assigns it interagency agreement, discussion, and funding-related responsibilities.

agencies.name: Texas Board of Criminal Justice
agencies.explanation: Its chair is expressly required to take part in the quarterly discussions and the initial discussion; the supplied registry has no matching entry.

SB280.summary: The bill would require an employer hiring for work connected to a county- or municipality-administered economic development program to contact the applicable local workforce development board and request referrals of qualified individuals served by its career development center. When filling those positions, the employer would have to give additional consideration to referred applicants who voluntarily disclose that they receive state or federal public assistance.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates workforce-referral and applicant-consideration requirements for covered hiring.
The requirements apply to employers participating in specified economic development programs.
The bill changes requirements tied to economic development programs administered by or on behalf of counties and municipalities.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The requirements apply wherever qualifying work is performed in Texas, through the applicable workforce development area.

affected_groups.group: Employers hiring for work connected to covered county- or municipality-administered economic development programs
affected_groups.explanation: These employers would have to request workforce-board referrals and give additional consideration to qualifying referred applicants.

affected_groups.group: Referred applicants who voluntarily disclose receiving state or federal public assistance
affected_groups.explanation: Employers would have to give these applicants additional consideration when filling covered positions.

affected_groups.group: Local workforce development boards
affected_groups.explanation: Boards would receive requests from covered employers for referrals of qualified individuals served by their career development centers.

major_effects.label: Workforce referral requests
major_effects.explanation: Covered employers would have to contact the applicable local workforce development board and request referrals for covered positions.

major_effects.label: Additional consideration for certain referred applicants
major_effects.explanation: When filling covered positions, employers would have to give additional consideration to referred applicants who voluntarily disclose receiving state or federal public assistance.

SB281.summary: The bill would allow a seven-member board of an independent school district eligible for the Section 48.101(b) allotment to reduce its membership to five by resolution, but only after certifying that it could not fill all trustee seats in each of the two preceding elections. The change would take effect at the next regular trustee election after adoption, would not shorten any current trustee’s term, and must provide for a transition in the number of trustees so that, when the transition is complete, trustees are elected as provided by Section 11.059.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the permitted composition and transition process for certain independent school district boards of trustees.
Changes the governance authority of eligible independent school districts, which are local governing entities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provision applies to qualifying independent school districts without limiting them to a named place or defined region.

affected_groups.group: Seven-member boards of eligible independent school districts
affected_groups.explanation: These boards could reduce their membership to five if they meet the election-related condition and adopt a resolution.

affected_groups.group: Trustees serving on eligible independent school district boards
affected_groups.explanation: Current trustees keep their terms; board membership changes at a later regular election.

major_effects.label: Option to reduce board membership
major_effects.explanation: Allows a qualifying seven-member district board to reduce to five by resolution only after it certifies that it could not fill all seats in the two preceding trustee elections; the change begins with the next regular election and preserves current terms.

agencies.name: commissioner
agencies.explanation: The board must send its certification to the commissioner; the bill does not identify the office by name or assign it a separate decision or duty.

SB282.summary: The bill clarifies that reinstating a filing entity’s certificate after forfeiture does not affect personal liability created or incurred before reinstatement, including a director’s or officer’s liability under Tax Code Section 171.255. It does not itself create that liability.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the effect of certificate reinstatement on the personal liability of persons associated with a filing entity.
Addresses whether reinstatement affects director or officer personal liability under a Tax Code provision.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The amendment concerns filing entities under Texas law and is not limited to a particular geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Filing entities' governing persons, officers, and agents
affected_groups.explanation: Their personal liability may be unaffected by reinstatement when it was created or incurred before reinstatement.

affected_groups.group: Directors and officers subject to Tax Code Section 171.255
affected_groups.explanation: The bill expressly includes their liability under that provision among liabilities unaffected by reinstatement if created or incurred before reinstatement.

major_effects.label: Effect of reinstatement on personal liability
major_effects.explanation: Clarifies that reinstatement does not affect personal liability created or incurred before reinstatement, including specified director or officer liability under the Tax Code.

SB283.summary: The bill requires the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to establish a grant program for counties to reduce illegal scrap-tire disposal, including through enforcement, public information, and removal and proper disposal of tires. It creates a dedicated account to fund grants and program administration, and requires annual recommendations to the Legislature and program-administration rules.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a program to reduce illegal scrap-tire disposal, including disposal in water and on land.
Counties may receive grants for specified remediation and enforcement activities.
Establishes a dedicated account for grant awards and administration, funded in part by legislative appropriations.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes a state program for grants to counties and specifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Texas counties
affected_groups.explanation: Counties may receive grants for enforcement, public information, and removal and proper disposal of illegally discarded tires.

affected_groups.group: People in areas affected by illegally disposed scrap tires
affected_groups.explanation: The program is intended to reduce illegal tire disposal and may support public information and cleanup.

major_effects.label: County scrap-tire remediation grants
major_effects.explanation: Requires a grant program for counties; grants may support identifying and prosecuting violators, public information, and cleanup and proper disposal.

major_effects.label: Dedicated grant account
