major_effects.explanation: Creates a dedicated general-revenue account with specified sources and limits its use to grants and program administration.

major_effects.label: Annual report to the Legislature
major_effects.explanation: Requires an annual written report with recommendations addressing illegal scrap-tire disposal.

major_effects.label: Program-administration rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to adopt rules to administer the grant program.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly requires TCEQ to establish the program; the commission also administers grants, reports to the Legislature, and adopts program rules.

SB284.summary: The bill would require directors of municipal utility districts located wholly or partly in certain counties bordering Mexico to be at least 18, Texas resident citizens, and qualified voters within the district. A nonvoter could serve only if fewer than half of the district’s retail water or sewer connections are residential and the district has not received qualified-voter candidates for every board position by the specified cutoff; the requirements apply prospectively, with current members allowed to finish their terms and seek reelection or reappointment if qualified.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes who may serve on the boards of municipal utility districts in the counties covered by the bill.
Makes district voter status a qualification for board service, subject to an exception tied to qualified-voter candidates filing for board positions.

locations.name: Counties bordering the United Mexican States that contain a municipality with a population of more than 500,000
locations.explanation: The special qualifications apply to a district wholly or partly located in a county meeting both criteria.

affected_groups.group: Prospective municipal utility district directors in covered counties
affected_groups.explanation: They would have to meet the district-voter qualification, subject to the bill’s limited nonvoter exception.

affected_groups.group: Municipal utility districts in covered counties
affected_groups.explanation: Their eligible board candidates would be limited under the new qualifications and conditional exception.

affected_groups.group: Current directors of districts covered by the bill
affected_groups.explanation: Current members may complete their terms; reelection or reappointment is permitted if they meet the new qualifications.

major_effects.label: Director qualifications in certain counties
major_effects.explanation: Requires district voter status for directors of covered districts, with a nonvoter exception only when fewer than 50 percent of retail water or sewer connections are residential and qualified-voter candidates have not applied for every board position by the specified cutoff. The rule applies to members elected or appointed on or after the effective date, while incumbents may finish their terms.

SB285.summary: The bill would require sponsors of projects financed by the Texas Water Development Board through a fund or account described by Water Code Section 15.502(b) to display a specified public sign at the project site for the duration of the project. The sign would have to meet size and design requirements, and the Board would have to adopt implementing rules.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds signage requirements for projects financed through specified Texas Water Development Board funds or accounts.

affected_groups.group: Sponsors of projects financed through funds or accounts described by Water Code Section 15.502(b)
affected_groups.explanation: They would be responsible for displaying the required sign at the project site.

affected_groups.group: Members of the public at covered project sites
affected_groups.explanation: The required sign would provide them with information about the project's financing.

major_effects.label: Required project signage
major_effects.explanation: Covered project sponsors would have to display a specified sign at the project site, meeting stated design requirements and remaining posted for the project's duration.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The Texas Water Development Board would have to adopt rules necessary to implement the signage requirement.

agencies.name: Texas Water Development Board
agencies.explanation: The bill identifies the Board and requires it to adopt rules implementing the new signage requirement.

SB286.summary: The bill would authorize the commissioners court of a county containing the intersection of U.S. Highway 287 and State Highway 70 to impose a county hotel occupancy tax. The rate could be up to 7%, but would be capped at 2% for hotels in a municipality imposing an applicable municipal hotel tax or in the extraterritorial jurisdiction of a municipality imposing an applicable tax.

policy_tags.explanation: Authorizes a county hotel occupancy tax and establishes rate limits.
Grants qualifying county commissioners courts authority to impose the tax.

locations.name: County containing the intersection of U.S. Highway 287 and State Highway 70
locations.explanation: The bill applies to a county meeting this geographic condition and does not name the county.

affected_groups.group: Commissioners courts of qualifying counties
affected_groups.explanation: These county governments would gain authority to impose the hotel occupancy tax.

affected_groups.group: Hotels and people paying for hotel rooms in a qualifying county
affected_groups.explanation: The authorized tax applies to the price paid for hotel rooms, with a lower maximum rate for hotels in specified municipal taxing areas.

major_effects.label: County hotel tax authority
major_effects.explanation: A qualifying county commissioners court could impose a county hotel occupancy tax.

major_effects.label: Hotel tax rate limits
major_effects.explanation: The county tax rate could not exceed 7%, with a 2% maximum for hotels in a municipality imposing an applicable municipal tax or its qualifying extraterritorial jurisdiction.

SB287.summary: The bill repeals specified tax preferences related to solar and wind-powered energy devices and businesses that manufacture, sell, or install them, while changing how other laws define a solar energy device. The repeal of the ad valorem preference applies to tax years beginning on or after the Act takes effect; taxable entities retain eligibility for the specified exemption or deduction for reporting periods that overlap the effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill repeals specified Tax Code tax preferences, with transition rules for tax years and reporting periods that overlap the effective date.
The repealed tax preferences concern solar and wind-powered energy devices and related businesses.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill repeals Texas Tax Code provisions and changes tax preferences with statewide application.

affected_groups.group: Taxpayers eligible for the repealed ad valorem tax preference
affected_groups.explanation: The repeal applies to ad valorem tax years beginning on or after the effective date.

affected_groups.group: Taxable entities claiming the specified exemption or deduction
affected_groups.explanation: Entities retain eligibility for the exemption or deduction for reporting periods if any part of the period occurs before the effective date.

major_effects.label: Repeals solar- and wind-related tax preferences
major_effects.explanation: Repeals the listed Tax Code provisions. The ad valorem repeal applies only to tax years beginning on or after the effective date, and the specified exemption and deduction remain available for reporting periods that overlap that date.

major_effects.label: Changes the statutory definition of solar energy device
major_effects.explanation: Defines the term directly in the Local Government Code and makes the Property Code definition refer to that definition instead of the repealed Tax Code provision.

SB288.summary: SB 288 would require the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center to evaluate statewide health, nutrition, physical activity, chronic disease, health care costs, and related economic trends. The evaluation would prioritize Texas data, use national data only when Texas data is unavailable and disclose that use; the center would report its findings by December 31, 2028, and the Act would expire January 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill mandates a statewide evaluation of health conditions, health care costs, insurance costs, and related economic effects; it does not change health care eligibility or funding.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The evaluation concerns health and related trends in this state, with Texas-specific data prioritized when possible.

locations.name: United States
locations.explanation: The evaluation includes certain national measures, including household health care spending and medical debt.

affected_groups.group: Texas residents across demographic and age groups
affected_groups.explanation: The evaluation would track chronic diseases and other health issues across demographic and age groups; it does not itself change services or eligibility.

affected_groups.group: Employers and individuals with private insurance
affected_groups.explanation: Their insurance premiums, deductibles, copays, and employer-plan costs are subjects of the evaluation, not changes made by the bill.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid and child health plan program participants
affected_groups.explanation: Enrollment and spending trends in these programs are to be evaluated; the bill does not change program eligibility or benefits.

major_effects.label: Statewide health evaluation
major_effects.explanation: Requires an evaluation using available information from the preceding 50 years on health, diet, physical activity, chronic conditions, care costs, insurance costs, and related economic effects.

major_effects.label: Evaluation report
major_effects.explanation: Requires a written report by December 31, 2028, to HHSC and the relevant standing legislative committee; the Act expires January 1, 2029.

major_effects.label: On-request agency information assistance
major_effects.explanation: Four named state agencies must provide information to assist the evaluation when requested by the health sciences center.

agencies.name: Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns this named institution the evaluation. The supplied agency registry has no matching entry, so no registry identity is assigned.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: Must provide information to assist the evaluation if the health sciences center requests it.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: Must provide information on request and receive the evaluation report.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Agriculture
agencies.explanation: Must provide information to assist the evaluation if the health sciences center requests it.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: Must provide information to assist the evaluation if the health sciences center requests it.

SB289.summary: The bill would require the department to establish a maternal health training program for health care providers serving maternal patients in Texas, with curriculum including obstetric emergency protocols, TexasAIM practices, and safety simulations. The executive commissioner and appropriate provider licensing authorities would be required to require provider participation and adopt rules, including rules for monitoring compliance.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates mandatory maternal health training for providers delivering care to maternal patients.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The training program covers providers serving maternal patients in this state.

affected_groups.group: Health care providers serving maternal patients
affected_groups.explanation: They would be required to participate in the new training program.

affected_groups.group: Maternal patients
affected_groups.explanation: The program is intended to support consistent care and reduce maternal mortality and morbidity.

major_effects.label: Maternal health training program
major_effects.explanation: Requires the department to develop and implement training for providers serving maternal patients, with a specified curriculum developed in collaboration with the review committee.

major_effects.label: Required provider participation
major_effects.explanation: Requires the executive commissioner and appropriate provider licensing authorities to require covered providers to participate.

major_effects.label: Implementation and compliance rules
major_effects.explanation: Requires rules to establish and implement the program, including monitoring provider compliance.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department responsibility for developing and implementing the program and collaborating on its curriculum; the supplied text does not establish the department's canonical identity.

agencies.name: Texas Maternal Mortality and Morbidity Review Committee
agencies.explanation: The committee is assigned a substantive role in establishing the curriculum and recommending best-practice information; no canonical registry identity is supplied.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: Its executive commissioner is expressly required to adopt the rules needed to implement the chapter.

agencies.name: each appropriate health care provider licensing authority
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns these authorities rulemaking and provider-participation duties, but does not identify which licensing authorities are covered.

SB290.summary: SB 290 would establish a fetal alcohol spectrum disorder program and advisory council, with responsibilities for statewide planning and coordination. The program would focus on awareness and prevention, screening and intervention, professional training, and information and support services for affected people and their families.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a public-health program focused on preventing fetal alcohol spectrum disorder and improving identification, intervention, and services.
Creates a state advisory council and program and assigns them planning, coordination, and implementation responsibilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The advisory council is expressly tasked with developing a statewide strategic plan.

affected_groups.group: Individuals with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder and their families
affected_groups.explanation: The program is intended to improve identification, intervention, service delivery, and access to support information for these individuals and families.

affected_groups.group: Professionals in health care, education, child welfare, and behavioral health
affected_groups.explanation: The program must provide fetal alcohol spectrum disorder training for professionals in these sectors and others it considers relevant.

affected_groups.group: People who are pregnant
affected_groups.explanation: Public-awareness initiatives must include information about risks associated with alcohol use during pregnancy.

affected_groups.group: Public and private nonprofit entities
affected_groups.explanation: These entities may receive contracts or grants to implement the program, subject to the bill's public-purpose contract condition for grants.

major_effects.label: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder program
major_effects.explanation: Creates a commission-administered program for awareness and prevention, screening and diagnosis, targeted interventions, professional training, and information about services.

major_effects.label: Advisory council and statewide planning
major_effects.explanation: Creates an advisory council to develop a statewide plan, advise on implementation, review relevant state agency programs, and promote interagency coordination when feasible.

major_effects.label: Council reports
major_effects.explanation: Requires the council to submit findings and recommendations to the governor for budget consideration and to the commission and appropriate legislative standing committees for legislative action.

major_effects.label: Rules to implement the chapter
major_effects.explanation: Requires the executive commissioner to adopt rules to implement the new chapter.

major_effects.label: Contracts, grants, and federal money
major_effects.explanation: Allows the commission to contract with or grant funds to public or private nonprofits, with grants subject to a public-purpose control contract, and to apply for, receive, and disburse federal money.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission program and advisory-council responsibilities; it also expressly assigns the Health and Human Services Commission executive commissioner rulemaking for the chapter.

agencies.name: the department
agencies.explanation: The department must designate a representative to the advisory council, but the bill does not identify which department this generic reference means.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The agency is required to designate a representative to the advisory council.

agencies.name: Department of Family and Protective Services
agencies.explanation: The department is required to designate a representative to the advisory council; no canonical registry entry is supplied.

agencies.name: Texas Juvenile Justice Department
agencies.explanation: The department is required to designate a representative to the advisory council.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission is required to designate a representative to the advisory council.

agencies.name: Texas Council for Developmental Disabilities
agencies.explanation: The council is required to designate a representative to the advisory council; no canonical registry entry is supplied.

agencies.name: Texas Judicial Branch
agencies.explanation: The Supreme Court's Permanent Judicial Commission for Children, Youth and Families is named to designate a representative to the advisory council.

SB291.summary: SB 291 would allow education savings account program money to pay for online or virtual education services from a preapproved provider or vendor only for a participating child who is homeschooled, has a disability, or has a documented medical condition preventing in-person education. The change would apply beginning with the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which education services may be paid for with education savings account program money.
Sets eligibility conditions for using education savings account program money for online or virtual education.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends a provision of the Texas Education Code governing the education savings account program.

affected_groups.group: Participating children seeking online or virtual education services
affected_groups.explanation: Program money may be used for those services only when the child meets one of the listed conditions.

affected_groups.group: Preapproved education service providers and vendors offering online or virtual services
affected_groups.explanation: Program money may pay these providers or vendors for online or virtual services only for children who meet the new conditions.

major_effects.label: Limits ESA-funded online and virtual education
major_effects.explanation: Program money may pay for online or virtual education services only for participating children who are homeschooled, have a disability, or have a documented medical condition preventing in-person education.

SB292.summary: SB 292 would make retail public utilities eligible for Department of Information Resources services if the executive director determines participation is in the state's best interest, and would allow the command to provide network security services by agreement. It would prohibit internet connections to utilities' SCADA or equivalent operational systems, require cybersecurity controls and annual employee training, allow security assessments and audits, and require notice within 48 hours for specified security incidents.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill sets cybersecurity controls, training, assessment, and incident-notification requirements for utility systems and data.
The new requirements apply to retail public utilities under the Water Code, including utilities providing water or sewer service.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The requirements apply to retail public utilities under Texas law without limiting their application to a named locality.

affected_groups.group: Retail public utilities
affected_groups.explanation: Covered utilities would face the new system, training, assessment, audit, and incident-notification requirements, while becoming eligible for specified cybersecurity services.

affected_groups.group: Utility employees and officials who use computers or access utility systems
affected_groups.explanation: Utilities must identify these employees and officials and require them to complete certified cybersecurity training annually.

major_effects.label: Access to cybersecurity services
major_effects.explanation: Retail public utilities would be added as eligible customers for Department services, subject to the executive director's best-interest determination; the command could provide network security services by agreement.

major_effects.label: Operational-system internet restriction
major_effects.explanation: Utilities may not connect SCADA or equivalent operational information technology infrastructure to the Internet; the bill allows operation by an intranet or site-to-site virtual private network.

major_effects.label: Cybersecurity controls and training
major_effects.explanation: The commission must adopt authentication requirements for employee access, and utilities must annually identify covered employees and officials and require certified cybersecurity training.

major_effects.label: Assessments, audits, and results
major_effects.explanation: Specified bodies may require a security assessment or compliance audit. If one is conducted under the section, the utility must report its results to the listed bodies, and information in the report is confidential and not subject to disclosure under Chapter 552, Government Code.

major_effects.label: Security-incident notification
major_effects.explanation: Utilities holding sensitive personal or other confidential information must notify specified bodies within 48 hours of discovery for the listed data-acquisition, ransomware, or operational-disruption incidents; a good-faith employee or agent acquisition is excluded from the data-acquisition trigger when the data is not used or disclosed improperly.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly assigns TCEQ and the Department of Information Resources responsibility to adopt implementing rules. The identity of the separately used term “commission” in the new Water Code provisions is not confirmed by the supplied text.

agencies.name: Department of Information Resources
agencies.explanation: The bill defines “Department” as the Department of Information Resources and assigns it consultation, assessment, reporting, and rule-implementation roles.

agencies.name: the commission
agencies.explanation: The new provisions assign this body rulemaking, review, assessment, and incident-notification roles, but the supplied text does not establish its canonical identity.

agencies.name: the command
agencies.explanation: The bill expands the entities to which the command may provide network security services and includes retail public utilities among entities it may contract with for cybersecurity services; the command's canonical identity is not supplied.

agencies.name: Cyber Center for Security and Analytics at The University of Texas at San Antonio
agencies.explanation: The bill defines this center and assigns it consultation, assessment-access, and incident-notification roles; its status as a state agency and canonical parent-body identity are not established by the supplied text.

SB293.summary: The bill repeals sales and use tax exemptions for qualifying data centers and large data center projects, including the related gas-and-electricity exemption and corresponding exceptions for local taxes. Existing exemptions would expire on the Act’s effective date, pending certification applications would be deemed denied, and the bill also repeals Tax Code Section 313.009, whose effect is not described in the supplied text.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill ends tax exemptions specifically available to qualifying data centers and large data center projects.
The bill repeals sales and use tax exemptions and ends exemptions already claimed by qualifying projects.
The bill removes references that preserved data-center-related exceptions in provisions applying state exemptions to municipal and other local taxes.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The changes concern statewide tax provisions, including their application to local taxes.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying data centers and large data center projects, including certification applicants
affected_groups.explanation: Existing exemptions expire on the Act’s effective date, and pending certification applications are treated as denied.

affected_groups.group: Municipal and other local taxing jurisdictions
affected_groups.explanation: Removing the data-center-related exceptions makes the general application of state exemptions to local taxes govern instead.

major_effects.label: Repeal of data-center sales and use tax exemptions
major_effects.explanation: The bill removes the exemptions for qualifying data centers and large data center projects, including the related gas-and-electricity exemption and corresponding local-tax exceptions.

major_effects.label: Existing exemptions end and pending applications are denied
major_effects.explanation: Any exemption entitlement under the repealed provisions expires on the Act’s effective date; pending certification applications are considered denied and cannot be approved.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill bars the Comptroller from approving pending applications for certification as qualifying data centers or large data center projects.

SB294.summary: SB 294 would repeal Texas Education Code Chapter 29, Subchapter J, associated with the education savings account program. The bill proposes ending that program and does not describe a replacement.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill repeals a statutory education program.
The repealed program is an education savings account program, a school-choice program.

affected_groups.group: Students and families using or seeking to use education savings accounts
affected_groups.explanation: These groups are the likely direct users or beneficiaries of the program being repealed.

major_effects.label: Repeal of education savings account program
major_effects.explanation: Repeals the Education Code subchapter associated with the program, removing its statutory basis.

SB295.summary: The bill would require an employer, except as provided by Labor Code Section 62.057, to pay each employee at least the greater of $15 an hour or the federal minimum wage. It also repeals Labor Code Section 62.151; the supplied text does not show what that section provides, so the repeal’s practical effect is unclear.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the statutory minimum hourly wage employers must pay employees.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Labor Code to establish a wage standard applicable across the state.

affected_groups.group: Employees covered by the minimum-wage requirement
affected_groups.explanation: Their statutory minimum hourly pay would be at least the greater of $15 or the federal minimum wage, subject to the stated exception.

affected_groups.group: Employers subject to the minimum-wage requirement
affected_groups.explanation: They would be required to pay the increased state minimum-wage floor, subject to the stated exception.

major_effects.label: Set a $15 minimum-wage floor
major_effects.explanation: The minimum would be the greater of $15 an hour or the federal minimum wage, except as provided by Labor Code Section 62.057.

SB296.summary: The bill would impose a two-year moratorium on permits, construction, and new or expanded electric service for covered data-center projects, with exceptions for specified emergency or maintenance work and continued operation at existing authorized levels. After the moratorium, projects would need a state impact permit, which the commission may issue only if the project’s development has been approved in a local option election, and developers would fund annual payments to eligible host-county residents. The bill would repeal specified data-center tax exemptions, end existing qualifying exemptions on the Act’s effective date, and deny pending certification applications.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a siting, permitting, operating, and community-payment framework for covered data centers.
Requires counties and municipalities to conduct elections and assigns local subdivisions roles in election costs and enforcement.
Makes local voter approval a condition for covered project permits and requires separate approvals in specified jurisdictions.
Repeals specified data-center tax provisions and ends existing qualifying exemptions when the Act takes effect.
Restricts new or expanded electric connections during the moratorium and regulates project demand, grid effects, and infrastructure costs.
Requires review and mitigation of water, drought, air-emission, noise, and cumulative environmental impacts.
Creates permit, financial-assurance, operational, and enforcement requirements for data-center developers and operators.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill establishes a statewide framework for covered data-center projects and applies restrictions to state agencies and political subdivisions.

locations.name: Host counties containing covered data centers
locations.explanation: Host counties are the counties where a covered data center is located and are central to elections, notice, and resident stipends.

affected_groups.group: Data-center developers, owners, and operators
affected_groups.explanation: Must obtain approvals and permits, meet project conditions, provide financial assurance, and make annual stipend payments.

affected_groups.group: Eligible residents of host counties
affected_groups.explanation: May receive equal per-person annual stipends if they meet the bill’s residence-duration requirement.

affected_groups.group: Registered voters in affected counties and municipalities
affected_groups.explanation: Vote on whether a covered project may proceed, with separate elections required in certain locations.

affected_groups.group: Residential electricity customers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill requires developers to bear attributable incremental infrastructure costs without shifting them to residential ratepayers and requires review of effects on residential rates.

major_effects.label: Temporary project moratorium
major_effects.explanation: For two years, covered projects generally may not receive approvals, begin or continue substantial construction, or energize new or expanded service; specified emergency and maintenance work and continued existing authorized operations are excepted.

major_effects.label: Local election and state impact-permit requirements
major_effects.explanation: Covered projects would require a state impact permit, which the commission may not issue unless voters approve the project’s development in a local option election, in addition to other legally required approvals.

major_effects.label: Project studies, monitoring, and public disclosures
major_effects.explanation: Requires studies and recurring verified reporting on project impacts and usage, with specified applications, records, and ownership information made public subject to a cybersecurity-information exception.

major_effects.label: Annual payments for host-county residents
major_effects.explanation: Requires developers and operators to fund annual payments distributed in equal per-person amounts to eligible residents, with limits on administrative expenses and use of the funds.

major_effects.label: Repeal of specified data-center tax exemptions
major_effects.explanation: Repeals the specified data-center exemption provisions, ends existing qualifying exemptions when the Act takes effect, and treats pending certification applications as denied.

major_effects.label: Civil penalties and enforcement actions
major_effects.explanation: Provides for daily civil penalties for violations and authorizes specified enforcement actions, including injunctions and cessation of unauthorized activity.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the chapter’s commission as TCEQ and assigns it permitting, review, monitoring, enforcement, and rulemaking duties.

agencies.name: Public Utility Commission of Texas
agencies.explanation: Must provide findings on electric reliability and system costs and receive project monitoring reports.

agencies.name: Texas Water Development Board
agencies.explanation: Must provide water-supply and drought-impact findings and receive project monitoring reports.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: May bring actions to enforce stipend obligations and, on request, seek injunctions and civil penalties.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill bars the Comptroller from approving pending applications for certification under the repealed data-center provisions.

agencies.name: State Office of Administrative Hearings
agencies.explanation: Must receive referred permit applications for contested case hearings when an affected person requests one; no canonical registry entry is supplied for this named office.

SB297.summary: Subject to Chapter 405A, SB 297 would create a one-time $1,500 payment for each qualified Texas household, administered by the comptroller, without creating recurring benefits. A household would qualify based on its Texas residence on January 1, 2027, and representation by an adult or emancipated minor; eligibility could not depend on income or the other listed factors. The bill would appropriate $17 billion from the economic stabilization fund for payments and administration, but that appropriation is contingent on a two-thirds vote of members present in each house.

policy_tags.explanation: Appropriates economic stabilization fund money for the payment program and its administration, subject to a specified legislative vote.
Creates a state-administered payment program and assigns the comptroller responsibilities for payments, applications, rules, and program reporting.
Limits disclosure of information collected to verify eligibility or transmit payments, with an exception for deidentified aggregate reports.

locations.name: Statewide, Texas
locations.explanation: The payment program applies to qualified households with a usual place of residence in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Qualified Texas households
affected_groups.explanation: Households meeting the residence, representation, and verification requirements could receive one payment per household, regardless of the listed income or other factors.

affected_groups.group: Households without a conventional street address, including people experiencing homelessness or residents of group quarters
affected_groups.explanation: The comptroller must adopt residence-verification rules addressing these households; payment eligibility still depends on meeting the qualified-household requirements.

major_effects.label: One-time household payments
major_effects.explanation: Creates a single $1,500 payment per qualified household; the payment is not recurring and is not increased for additional household members.

major_effects.label: Household eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Sets residence, representation, and verification criteria and bars conditioning eligibility on income, homeownership, property-tax liability, employment, public-benefit receipt, or tax-return filing.

major_effects.label: Conditional $17 billion appropriation
major_effects.explanation: Appropriates $17 billion from the economic stabilization fund for payments and administration, contingent on a two-thirds vote of members present in each house; the comptroller may not spend beyond the appropriation.

major_effects.label: Application access and information confidentiality
major_effects.explanation: Requires mail and in-person application options and procedures to correct errors and contest denials, and protects eligibility and payment information from public disclosure except in deidentified aggregate reports.

major_effects.label: Program and shortfall reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires quarterly aggregate program reports and, if the comptroller determines the appropriation will be insufficient for full payments, a prompt report of the estimated shortfall.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the comptroller as the comptroller of public accounts and assigns that office responsibility for making payments and administering the program.

SB298.summary: For residence homesteads, the bill would lower the annual increase component of the appraised-value cap from 10% to 3%, while continuing to include the market value of new improvements. It would apply only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; if they do not, the bill has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the appraised-value limit used for residence homesteads in ad valorem taxation.
Changes the limit appraisal offices apply when valuing residence homesteads.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The change applies to residence-homestead appraisals under the Texas Tax Code, with no narrower geographic limit stated.

affected_groups.group: Owners of residence homesteads
affected_groups.explanation: Their homes would be subject to the lower annual appraised-value increase cap for applicable tax years only if voters approve the constitutional amendment; otherwise, the Act has no effect.

affected_groups.group: Appraisal offices
affected_groups.explanation: They would apply the lower limit when appraising residence homesteads.

major_effects.label: Lower homestead appraisal-growth cap
major_effects.explanation: Reduces the percentage component of the annual cap from 10% to 3%; the market value of new improvements remains included in the calculation.

SB299.summary: The bill would let the department use money appropriated from general revenue, as well as accepted gifts, grants, and donations, for certain highway memorial markers honoring officers killed in the line of duty. This exception applies only to markers designating part of the highway system, including a bridge or street, for qualifying state or local officers, or federal officers performing duties in Texas; other markers remain subject to the existing grant-or-donation cost requirement.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes funding rules for memorial markers designating parts of the highway system.
It authorizes use of general revenue appropriated to the department for the specified markers.

locations.name: Part of the highway system, including a bridge or street
locations.explanation: The bill limits the covered markers to those designating part of the highway system.

affected_groups.group: State or political-subdivision law enforcement officers and peace officers killed in the line of duty
affected_groups.explanation: The bill covers memorial markers for these officers.

affected_groups.group: Federal law enforcement officers or special agents killed in the line of duty while performing duties in Texas
affected_groups.explanation: The bill also covers memorial markers for these federal officers.

major_effects.label: Funding for qualifying memorial markers
major_effects.explanation: For markers covered by the new section, the department may use general revenue appropriated for those purposes and accepted gifts, grants, and donations, rather than relying solely on a grant or donation to cover the marker's costs.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Transportation
agencies.explanation: The bill gives the department authority to use specified funds for qualifying markers, but the supplied text does not identify the department by a canonical agency name.

SB300.summary: If enacted, SB 300 would allow holders of a consumer delivery permit to deliver alcoholic beverages no more than 50 miles from the retailer’s premises, but only in an area where the sale of the beverages is legal. This would replace the current county, city, and limited area beyond a city or town boundary restrictions.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the geographic conditions under which consumer delivery permit holders may deliver alcoholic beverages.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes the statewide statutory conditions for consumer delivery permits, with delivery limited by distance from the retailer's premises and where alcohol sales are legal.

affected_groups.group: Holders of consumer delivery permits
affected_groups.explanation: Their permitted delivery area would be governed by a 50-mile limit and the legality of sales in the destination area.

affected_groups.group: Alcoholic beverage retailers
affected_groups.explanation: The delivery limit is measured from the retailer's premises.

affected_groups.group: Consumers ordering alcoholic beverages for delivery
affected_groups.explanation: Consumers may be served in areas within the new distance limit where sale of the beverages is legal.

major_effects.label: Changes the delivery-area limit
major_effects.explanation: Would replace the existing county, city or town, and limited beyond-boundary restrictions with a limit of no more than 50 miles from the retailer's premises, subject to sales being legal in the delivery area.

SB301.summary: SB 301 would authorize Texas distillers, brewers, and brewpubs to ship specified spirits or malt beverages directly to consumers, including consumers in dry areas, subject to age, delivery, and quantity limits; it would also expand consumer-delivery permit use to manufacturer sales. It would create permits or licenses for qualifying out-of-state distilleries and breweries to ship directly into Texas, require related tax payments and records and reports, and establish escalating criminal penalties for unlicensed shipments.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes licensing and operating rules for direct shipment and consumer delivery of alcoholic beverages.
New out-of-state direct shipper permits make their holders responsible for state excise and sales and use taxes on covered sales.
The bill creates offenses for unlicensed direct shipments and increases offense severity for qualifying prior convictions.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The new out-of-state shipper programs cover sales and deliveries to ultimate consumers in Texas.

locations.name: dry areas
locations.explanation: The bill permits specified direct shipments to consumers located in dry areas.

locations.name: Travis County
locations.explanation: Applicants for the new out-of-state distillery permit must submit to venue in Travis County for proceedings initiated by or against the commission.

affected_groups.group: Texas distillers, brewers, and brewpub license holders
affected_groups.explanation: They would gain specified direct-shipment authority, subject to delivery safeguards and applicable limits.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying out-of-state distilleries and breweries
affected_groups.explanation: They could apply for new Texas direct-shipper permits or licenses and would be subject to eligibility, tax, recordkeeping, and shipment requirements.

affected_groups.group: Consumers purchasing shipped alcoholic beverages
affected_groups.explanation: Consumers would have access to qualifying direct shipments, including in dry areas, but delivery requires age verification and a signed receipt.

affected_groups.group: Carriers and consumer delivery permit holders
affected_groups.explanation: Shipment and delivery of covered beverages must use a carrier or consumer delivery permit holder, with consumer delivery permits newly available for manufacturer sales.

major_effects.label: Expands direct shipment and consumer delivery
major_effects.explanation: Allows specified Texas producers to ship beverages directly to consumers, including in dry areas, with age, delivery, and quantity restrictions; also extends consumer delivery arrangements to specified manufacturer sales.

major_effects.label: Creates out-of-state direct-shipper credentials
major_effects.explanation: Creates a distillery permit and a brewery license for qualifying out-of-state producers to ship beverages they produce or bottle to Texas consumers.

major_effects.label: Sets tax treatment for out-of-state direct shipments
major_effects.explanation: Requires covered permit and license holders to pay state excise and sales and use taxes as if they were Texas producers; consumers are not charged the personal-import administrative fee for these purchases.

major_effects.label: Requires records and periodic reports
major_effects.explanation: Out-of-state direct shippers must retain sales and delivery records, make them available for inspection, and file periodic reports under commission rules.

major_effects.label: Creates penalties for unlicensed shipments
major_effects.explanation: Unlicensed direct shipment is a Class B misdemeanor, with higher classifications for qualifying prior convictions, including a state jail felony after two or more prior convictions.

agencies.name: commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directs the commission to adopt rules and forms and to require periodic reports for the new out-of-state direct-shipper programs. The supplied text does not establish the commission's canonical identity.

SB302.summary: The bill would require an owner subdividing land outside a municipality to have a plat prepared when the subdivision lays out tract features intended for private use by a purchaser or owner of a lot. The existing requirement for features dedicated for public use remains.

policy_tags.explanation: Expands the plat-preparation requirement for subdivision of land.
Changes the scope of plat-related subdivision regulation applicable to land outside municipal limits.

locations.name: Land outside the limits of a municipality
locations.explanation: The plat requirement applies to tracts in this defined area.

affected_groups.group: Owners subdividing land outside municipal limits
affected_groups.explanation: They would need to have a plat prepared when the subdivision includes tract features intended for private use by lot purchasers or owners.

affected_groups.group: Purchasers or owners of lots in subdivisions
affected_groups.explanation: The added requirement covers tract features intended for their private use.

major_effects.label: Expanded plat-preparation requirement
major_effects.explanation: Extends the requirement to have a plat prepared to subdivision layouts with tract features intended for private use by a purchaser or lot owner.

SB303.summary: SB 303 would require the executive commissioner by rule to require each inpatient mental health facility, treatment facility, or hospital providing comprehensive medical rehabilitation services to provide, as a condition of continued licensure, eight hours of initial inservice training for new employees and three hours of continuing inservice training for continuing employees annually. The amended minimums apply to training hours provided on or after the Act’s effective date by health care facilities subject to Section 161.133; earlier hours remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes required training in covered health care facilities to help identify patient abuse, neglect, and misconduct.
Revises a training requirement that facilities must meet as a condition of continued licensure.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to covered facilities across Texas, with no narrower geographic area specified.

affected_groups.group: Covered inpatient mental health facilities, treatment facilities, and hospitals providing comprehensive medical rehabilitation services
affected_groups.explanation: These facilities would have to provide the specified training to satisfy a condition of continued licensure.

affected_groups.group: New and continuing employees of covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The bill sets different minimum training hours for new employees and continuing employees.

affected_groups.group: Patients at covered facilities
affected_groups.explanation: The training is intended to help facility employees and associated health care professionals identify patient abuse or neglect and misconduct.

major_effects.label: Two-tier annual training minimum
major_effects.explanation: Covered facilities must provide eight hours of initial training for new employees and three hours of continuing training for continuing employees as a condition of continued licensure.

major_effects.label: Prospective application
major_effects.explanation: The revised minimums govern training hours provided on or after the effective date; prior training hours remain subject to prior law.

agencies.name: executive commissioner
agencies.explanation: The bill revises the training requirement the executive commissioner must require by rule; the supplied text does not identify the agency associated with this title.

SB304.summary: SB 304 changes who may serve on the Kimble County Hospital District board: the residency requirement falls from two years to one, property-tax-paying-voter status is removed, district employees are barred, and directors must take an oath and subscribe to an anti-bribery statement instead of providing a bond. It authorizes additional types of hospital-system facilities and makes adoption of district operating rules discretionary. It also revises the district’s budget, fiscal-year, and depository procedures, including annual budgeting, post-adoption budget amendments, limits on fiscal-year changes, and competitive bank bids.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes qualifications for election to the district board and eligibility to serve as a director.
It specifies additional kinds of care and facilities that may be included in the district hospital system.
The bill changes governance and fiscal administration for a local hospital district.
It revises the district board’s rulemaking and budget procedures.

locations.name: Kimble County, Texas
locations.explanation: The bill identifies Kimble County as the location of the hospital district.

locations.name: Kimble County Hospital District
locations.explanation: The bill concerns the district, whose hospital system serves residents within its boundaries.

affected_groups.group: Prospective district directors and district employees
affected_groups.explanation: Candidates face revised qualifications, and district employees are ineligible to serve as directors.

affected_groups.group: District residents and hospital-system users
affected_groups.explanation: The district’s hospital system is to provide care to district residents and may include additional kinds of facilities.

affected_groups.group: Banks eligible to serve as the district depository
affected_groups.explanation: Eligible banks may compete through the district’s required bid solicitation.

affected_groups.group: Hospital district board
affected_groups.explanation: The board’s rulemaking, budget, fiscal-year, and depository procedures are revised.

major_effects.label: Director eligibility
major_effects.explanation: The residency requirement becomes one year, the property-tax-paying-voter qualification is removed, and district employees may not serve as directors.

major_effects.label: Director oath and records
major_effects.explanation: Directors qualify by taking an official oath or affirmation and subscribing to an anti-bribery statement instead of providing a commercial bond; the oath and statement are retained indefinitely in district records.

major_effects.label: Permitted hospital-system facilities
major_effects.explanation: The district’s hospital system may include domiciliary care, outpatient clinics, pharmacies, skilled nursing facilities, community health centers, assisted living facilities, and other facilities the board considers necessary for hospital or medical care.

major_effects.label: Discretionary operating rules
major_effects.explanation: The board may adopt rules for efficient district operations rather than being required to do so.

major_effects.label: Budget process
major_effects.explanation: The district must prepare an annual budget, the board adopts it at the conclusion of the hearing, and the board may amend it after adoption.

major_effects.label: Fiscal-year flexibility with limits
major_effects.explanation: The board may establish the district’s fiscal year, but may not change it while district revenue bonds are outstanding or more than once in a 24-month period.

major_effects.label: Depository selection and deposits
major_effects.explanation: The board must solicit bids from eligible banks, consider adopted criteria, and designate a bank in Texas for a term of up to five years; district money is subject to updated investment and security provisions.

SB305.summary: The bill changes the alcohol-content threshold separating the two tax rates on vinous liquor from 14% to 16%, while retaining the existing per-gallon rates. It leaves tax liability accrued before the change takes effect unaffected.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the alcohol-content threshold that determines which per-gallon tax rate applies to vinous liquor.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing the tax on vinous liquor.

affected_groups.group: Sellers of vinous liquor
affected_groups.explanation: The tax rate applicable to vinous liquor sales depends on the liquor's alcohol content, with the dividing threshold changed by the bill.

major_effects.label: Changes the alcohol-content tax threshold
major_effects.explanation: Moves the dividing line between the 20.4-cent and 40.8-cent per-gallon rates from 14% to 16% alcohol by volume; the stated rates remain unchanged.

SB306.summary: The bill would require property owners' associations to electronically file management certificates, dedicatory instruments, and applicable enforcement policies with the Texas Real Estate Commission, which would make the information publicly accessible online. TREC would have to establish the filing system by December 1, 2027; associations that had recorded certificates by then would have until June 1, 2028, to file. During a filing failure, owners would not owe assessments, fines, or fees levied during that period, and certain attorney's fees and interest would not be recoverable; associations would generally be protected from liability for filing failures unless they were wilful or caused by gross negligence.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes filing requirements and owner protections related to property owners' associations and their management certificates.
Assigns TREC duties to establish an electronic filing system and make filed information publicly accessible.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The filing requirements apply to property owners' associations governed by the Texas Property Code provisions amended by the bill.

affected_groups.group: Property owners' associations
affected_groups.explanation: Must electronically file specified documents and policies with TREC.

affected_groups.group: Owners in property owners' associations
affected_groups.explanation: Receive specified protections from assessments, fines, fees, attorney's fees, and interest during periods when required information is not filed.

affected_groups.group: Members of the public
affected_groups.explanation: Would be able to access the filed information through an Internet website.

major_effects.label: Electronic filing of association documents
major_effects.explanation: Associations must electronically file management certificates or amended certificates, dedicatory instruments, and applicable enforcement policies with TREC after filing certificates for recording.

major_effects.label: TREC filing system and public access
major_effects.explanation: Requires TREC to establish the electronic filing system and make the collected information accessible to the public online.

major_effects.label: Owner protections during filing gaps
major_effects.explanation: Owners are not liable for assessments, fines, or fees levied during a period when required information is not filed; attorney's fees and interest are barred during the period when the management certificate itself is not electronically filed.

major_effects.label: Association liability limitation
major_effects.explanation: Generally shields associations and their officers, directors, employees, and agents from liability for delay or failure to electronically file, except when the failure is wilful or caused by gross negligence.

agencies.name: Texas Real Estate Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission a public-access function for filed information and requires it to establish the electronic filing system. The supplied canonical registry does not list the commission.

SB307.summary: The bill removes the 18-member maximum for the Central Texas Water Alliance board while retaining a minimum of five members. It also updates the cross-reference for the board’s authority to increase or decrease its size.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the governance and board-size limit of the alliance under the Special District Local Laws Code.

affected_groups.group: Central Texas Water Alliance board of directors
affected_groups.explanation: The bill removes the board’s 18-member maximum and updates the cross-reference governing changes to its size.

major_effects.label: Board-size limit
major_effects.explanation: Removes the 18-member maximum while retaining the minimum of five directors; the bill also updates the reference governing the board’s authority to change its size.

SB308.summary: The bill would create offenses involving the intentional or knowing manufacture of firearms or major components with a 3D printer and specified dealings in those items. It would also criminalize distributing or publishing digital firearm schematics when the person intends or knows they will facilitate such manufacture; the defenses specified for the firearm offenses would also apply to this offense.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates criminal restrictions on manufacturing and dealing in firearms and major components produced with a 3D printer.
Adds criminal offenses, including a Class A misdemeanor for specified digital-schematic distribution.
Creates an offense targeting digital firearm schematics shared to facilitate 3D-printed firearm or component manufacture.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and has statewide scope.

affected_groups.group: People who manufacture, possess, transport, repair, or sell covered 3D-printed firearms or major components
affected_groups.explanation: Their conduct would be subject to the new criminal offenses.

affected_groups.group: People who distribute, publish, or make digital firearm schematics available
affected_groups.explanation: They would be subject to an offense when they intend or know the schematics facilitate manufacture using a 3D printer.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying government personnel, federally licensed firearms businesses, and researchers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill provides defenses for specified official duties, compliant federal licensees, and research studies approved by the Department of Public Safety.

major_effects.label: Offenses involving 3D-printed firearms
major_effects.explanation: Adds offenses for intentional or knowing manufacture of firearms or major components with a 3D printer and for specified dealings in those items, subject to listed defenses.

major_effects.label: Digital firearm schematic offense
major_effects.explanation: Creates a Class A misdemeanor for distributing, publishing, or otherwise making a schematic available with intent or knowledge that it facilitates 3D-printed firearm or component manufacture; specified defenses also apply.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: Approval by the Department of Public Safety is a condition for the research-study defense.

SB309.summary: SB 309 would extend Insurance Code Chapter 559 to each insurer writing personal insurance and prohibit specified underwriting and rating practices based on credit information, reports, or scores. The changes would apply to policies delivered, issued for delivery, or renewed on or after January 1, 2028; applications submitted on or after that date; or policies subject to a refusal-to-underwrite, cancellation, or nonrenewal determination on or after that date. The bill also repeals specified Chapter 559 provisions and makes Section 559.055 expire September 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes statutory restrictions on insurers' underwriting, coverage decisions, premiums, rating, and payment-plan practices.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill changes Texas Insurance Code requirements for insurers writing personal insurance, with no narrower geographic area specified.

affected_groups.group: Insurers writing personal insurance
affected_groups.explanation: These insurers would be subject to the expanded chapter applicability and new credit-based practice restrictions.

affected_groups.group: Applicants and people insured under personal insurance policies
affected_groups.explanation: Their credit information could no longer be used for the specified underwriting, coverage, and rating practices.

major_effects.label: Restrictions on credit-based insurance practices
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits specified credit-based underwriting guidelines, coverage decisions, premium charges, rating practices, and payment plans; also bars treating absent or indeterminable credit information as an underwriting or rating factor.

major_effects.label: Expanded chapter applicability
major_effects.explanation: Applies Chapter 559 to each insurer writing personal insurance, without the prior limitation to insurers using credit information or reports.

major_effects.label: January 1, 2028 applicability threshold
major_effects.explanation: The changes apply to policies, applications, or specified refusal-to-underwrite, cancellation, or nonrenewal determinations meeting the bill's January 1, 2028 timing conditions.

major_effects.label: Repeals and sunset
major_effects.explanation: Repeals specified Chapter 559 provisions and subchapters and sets Section 559.055 to expire September 1, 2028; the bill text does not state the substantive content of those provisions.

SB31.summary: The bill would require the commission to provide medical assistance to applicants for whom federal matching funds are available. The provision applies to eligibility determinations or recertifications made on or after January 1, 2028, and takes effect only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment; otherwise, the Act has no effect.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility for medical assistance under Chapter 32 based on the availability of federal matching funds.
Expands access to medical assistance and requires reporting on coverage and health care costs.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The eligibility expansion concerns applicants for medical assistance in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for Medicaid medical assistance who qualify for federal matching funds
affected_groups.explanation: The bill would extend medical assistance to these applicants, subject to the bill’s effective condition and timing.

major_effects.label: Expanded medical assistance eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Requires coverage for applicants for whom federal matching funds are available; the change applies to eligibility determinations or recertifications on or after January 1, 2028, and only if voters approve the specified constitutional amendment.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: Directs the executive commissioner to adopt rules for providing medical assistance under the expansion.

major_effects.label: Annual effects report
major_effects.explanation: Requires HHSC to report on effects including coverage levels, state and local health care costs, and hospital charity and uncompensated care costs.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The Commission is assigned to provide the expanded medical assistance and submit the annual report; its executive commissioner must adopt rules and take implementation actions.

SB310.summary: The bill would replace average daily attendance with average enrollment as the principal student-count measure in the public-school finance system, changing how districts, charter schools, and education programs calculate funding and eligibility. It would raise the basic allotment from $6,160 to $7,750 and, beginning in the 2028–2029 school year, adjust it annually for increases in the Consumer Price Index. It also revises program-specific counting rules and preserves certain funding adjustments for enrollment declines, disasters, and instructional programs.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes student-counting rules, school funding formulas, and program eligibility throughout the public education system.
It increases the basic allotment and changes the enrollment basis for state education aid and other school-funding allocations.
It changes enrollment-based funding calculations for open-enrollment charter schools and education-assistance program accounts.
School districts, as local public entities, receive funding under formulas and allotments revised by the bill.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill revises statewide school-finance calculations and allocations.

affected_groups.group: Public school districts and open-enrollment charter schools
affected_groups.explanation: Their funding, student counts, and eligibility for certain allotments are recalculated using average enrollment.

affected_groups.group: Students and families using education-assistance programs
affected_groups.explanation: Program account amounts and eligibility checks are tied to enrollment-based school funding and enrollment status.

affected_groups.group: School districts and charter schools providing eligible programs, including prekindergarten and dropout recovery
affected_groups.explanation: Eligibility for partial or full average enrollment is tied to instructional-time requirements for specified programs, including prekindergarten and dropout recovery.

major_effects.label: Enrollment-based school finance
major_effects.explanation: Replaces average daily attendance with average enrollment across school-finance formulas and related allocations, subject to program-specific rules and adjustments.

major_effects.label: Higher and inflation-adjusted basic allotment
major_effects.explanation: Raises the basic allotment to $7,750 and provides for annual CPI-based increases beginning in the 2028–2029 school year.

major_effects.label: Program-specific enrollment and instructional-time rules
major_effects.explanation: Revises how enrollment counts determine funding eligibility for certain programs, including half-day prekindergarten and programs meeting specified instructional-time requirements.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the agency duties involving information for education-assistance eligibility. The source does not identify which state agency the generic term denotes.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill revises provider-approval criteria administered by the comptroller, including updated statutory cross-references.

agencies.name: Texas Juvenile Justice Department
agencies.explanation: The department's state available school fund apportionment for its educational programs is changed to an enrollment-based calculation.

SB311.summary: The bill would require each health facility licensed by the Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) to conduct employment verification for each applicant it may potentially employ before offering a position. For positions involving services to children or vulnerable adults, or handling state money, the facility must at minimum contact the previous employers listed in the application; HHSC's executive commissioner may adopt implementing rules.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a pre-offer employment verification requirement for HHSC-licensed health facilities.
Regulates employment screening of prospective hires for specified roles at health facilities.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The requirement applies to health facilities licensed by HHSC, without a narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: HHSC-licensed health facilities
affected_groups.explanation: Facilities must conduct employment verification before offering positions.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for positions serving children or vulnerable adults, or handling state money
affected_groups.explanation: Applicants for these positions are subject to minimum checks of previous employers listed in their application materials.

major_effects.label: Pre-offer employment verification
major_effects.explanation: Requires verification for each applicant a facility may potentially employ before making an offer, with previous-employer contact required at minimum for applicants in positions serving children or vulnerable adults or handling state money.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: Permits the executive commissioner to adopt rules necessary to implement the new chapter.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the Commission's executive commissioner to adopt rules to implement the chapter; the bill defines the Commission as HHSC.

SB312.summary: SB 312 would shift complaint-receipt, resolution, tracking, and related reporting responsibilities from the Department of Family and Protective Services to the Health and Human Services Commission's office of the ombudsman, while encouraging people to first submit complaints to local department personnel. The executive commissioner must adopt implementing rules by January 1, 2028, and the changes apply only to complaints filed on or after that date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which state entity handles complaints against the Department of Family and Protective Services and assigns related tracking and reporting duties.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The complaint process and tracking system are specified to operate throughout Texas.

affected_groups.group: People making complaints against the Department of Family and Protective Services, including the public, consumers, and service recipients
affected_groups.explanation: They would use the complaint process and receive information about complaint procedures and, when a complaint is pending, periodic status updates unless the information would jeopardize an undercover investigation.

affected_groups.group: Department of Family and Protective Services personnel
affected_groups.explanation: Personnel must provide information for complaint tracking, and the process is to encourage complaints to be submitted to local department personnel first so staff have an opportunity to resolve them.

major_effects.label: Complaint handling assigned to the ombudsman office
major_effects.explanation: The commission's office of the ombudsman would receive and resolve complaints against the department and maintain information files on complaints it has authority to resolve.

major_effects.label: Local-first complaint process
major_effects.explanation: The statewide process would encourage complaints to go to local department personnel before the ombudsman office, giving department staff an opportunity to resolve them; it does not require that sequence.

major_effects.label: Complaint tracking and reporting
major_effects.explanation: The ombudsman office would maintain a centralized complaint-tracking system and periodically report complaint numbers, types, and resolutions. People with pending complaints would receive status information at least quarterly unless that information would jeopardize an undercover investigation.

major_effects.label: Prospective application
major_effects.explanation: The amended complaint provisions apply only to complaints filed on or after January 1, 2028.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
agencies.explanation: The commission's office of the ombudsman receives and resolves complaints and maintains complaint records and reports; the executive commissioner adopts implementing rules.

agencies.name: Department of Family and Protective Services
agencies.explanation: The bill changes how complaints against the department are handled and requires department personnel to provide complaint information to the centralized tracking system.

SB313.summary: SB 313 would direct the Health and Human Services Commission to seek federal authorization for a program, subject to the chapter’s requirements, helping certain low-income people obtain private-market health coverage; assistance under that program would not be an entitlement. If the federal government establishes or authorizes a Medicaid block-grant system for Texas, the commission would, subject to Section 532A.0003, operate Medicaid under new managed-care, eligibility, and subsidy provisions. The bill also addresses long-term services and supports, including customized benefits, a dual-eligible demonstration, conditionally permitted parental fees and housing assistance, and required studies and an advisory task force.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates and changes programs for health coverage, Medicaid benefits, and long-term services and supports.
Reforms Medicaid eligibility and delivery, provides Medicaid-related subsidies, and changes long-term services and supports.
Requires health coverage subsidies and housing payment assistance through state-administered programs.
Requires housing payment assistance for certain Medicaid recipients receiving home and community-based services.
Sets participation and minimum-coverage requirements for health benefit plan issuers in the state Medicaid program.
Creates a temporary Medicaid Reform Task Force and assigns state agencies studies and reports.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes state Medicaid and coverage programs for residents of Texas.

affected_groups.group: Low-income people seeking health coverage
affected_groups.explanation: The private-market program targets people under 65 with income at or below 133 percent of the federal poverty level who are not otherwise eligible for Medicaid, subject to possible eligibility adjustments.

affected_groups.group: Medicaid recipients, including people needing long-term services and supports
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes Medicaid coverage and support options and directs customized benefit packages and an integrated-care demonstration for eligible people.

affected_groups.group: Parents and legal guardians of children receiving Medicaid long-term services
affected_groups.explanation: They may be required to pay a service-related fee based partly on household income, to the extent federal law allows; nonpayment cannot affect the child's Medicaid eligibility.

affected_groups.group: Health benefit plan issuers
affected_groups.explanation: Issuers authorized to write plans in Texas would be permitted to participate in the Medicaid program and could be subject to program coverage and performance provisions.

major_effects.label: Conditional Medicaid eligibility and delivery changes
major_effects.explanation: Only if the federal government establishes or authorizes a block-grant funding system, the commission must administer Medicaid under this chapter. Acute-care eligibility includes people at or below 100 percent of the federal poverty level, specified under-19 SSI or foster-care groups, and people meeting the eligibility requirements in effect on August 31, 2027; eligible benefits use a risk-based managed-care model.

major_effects.label: Private-market coverage assistance program
major_effects.explanation: Directs the commission to develop and implement a coverage-assistance program and seek federal authorization. The program is generally aimed at people under 65 with household income at or below 133 percent of the federal poverty level who are not otherwise Medicaid-eligible; the executive commissioner may modify or further define eligibility for a federal agreement, and assistance is not an entitlement.

major_effects.label: Medicaid subsidies and plan options
major_effects.explanation: Allows eligible Medicaid individuals to receive sliding-scale premium subsidies and requires additional sliding-scale help with cost-sharing. The commission must allow authorized issuers to participate and establish minimum coverage requirements subject to the requirements specified by the chapter.

major_effects.label: Long-term services and integrated-care changes
major_effects.explanation: Requires a comprehensive plan to reform long-term services delivery, customized benefit packages for people receiving home and community-based services instead of institutional services, and a dual-eligible demonstration project. Residents of nursing facilities, ICF-IIDs, and state supported living centers are exempt from the demonstration.

major_effects.label: Conditional parental fees
major_effects.explanation: To the extent federal law allows, parents or legal guardians must pay a fee for a child's institutional or home and community-based long-term services, correlated with services and household income. Failure to pay cannot affect the child's Medicaid eligibility.

major_effects.label: Conditional housing payment assistance
major_effects.explanation: Requires housing payment assistance for Medicaid recipients receiving home and community-based services, to the extent allowed by federal law.

major_effects.label: Studies, recommendations, and task-force report
major_effects.explanation: Requires studies of estate recovery and alternative long-term-care income and asset limits, with recommendations reported to state officials and legislative committees, and creates a temporary advisory task force that must report to the legislature.

agencies.name: Health and Human Services Commission
