affected_groups.explanation: The bill makes covered meeting broadcasts or recordings and notices available through public-facing websites or social media accounts.

major_effects.label: Livestreaming and archiving for qualifying executive agencies
major_effects.explanation: Governmental bodies subject to this section must livestream each open meeting, post the recording within seven days, and keep it online until the second anniversary of its first availability.

major_effects.label: Online recordings and notices for other covered agencies
major_effects.explanation: Governmental bodies subject to this section must make the required audio or audiovisual recording and meeting notice available on a website or associated social media account.

major_effects.label: Competitive-bidding consideration
major_effects.explanation: Qualifying executive agencies must consider contracting through competitive bidding with a private individual or entity to broadcast and archive an open meeting subject to this section, to minimize compliance costs; the bill does not require them to award a contract.

agencies.name: Governmental bodies subject to Section 551.024
agencies.explanation: Section 551.024 applies to governmental bodies that are executive-branch state agencies and meet its statutory criteria, including the 100-or-more full-time-equivalent criterion shown here. The bill directly requires covered bodies to broadcast open meetings online. The supplied evidence does not support including bodies subject to Section 551.025.

SB44.summary: The bill would bar videography intended for wider circulation, including livestreaming, during voir dire and certain conferences outside the jury’s hearing, and in proceedings involving specified child victims. It would also bar videography in proceedings involving adult victims of specified offenses or sufficiently embarrassing conduct unless the adult victim voluntarily authorizes it; specified court-staff uses and the admissibility of forensic or other prerecordings are preserved, and recording requires advance notice to jurors, parties, and the court’s public website. The changes would apply only to proceedings commenced on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates rules for recording court proceedings and requires courts to give notice before recording.
The restrictions apply to court proceedings involving victims of specified offenses.
Limits audiovisual recording for wider circulation in specified proceedings, including proceedings involving victims.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill adds a provision to the Texas Government Code governing covered court proceedings; no narrower geographic area is specified.

affected_groups.group: Child and adult victims in covered court proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: Videography is restricted in covered proceedings; an adult victim in the specified category may voluntarily authorize its use.

affected_groups.group: Courts and court staff
affected_groups.explanation: Courts must give recording notice, while the bill preserves specified court-staff uses of videography.

affected_groups.group: Jurors and parties to covered proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: They must be notified at least 72 hours before a proceeding is recorded.

major_effects.label: Limits on courtroom videography
major_effects.explanation: Generally bars videography in specified proceedings, including voir dire and proceedings involving covered child victims; adult victims in the specified category may voluntarily authorize it. Specified court-staff uses remain permitted.

major_effects.label: Victim choice and prerecording evidence
major_effects.explanation: Requires notice to covered adult victims of their right to authorize videography and clarifies that the restrictions do not limit admissibility of recorded forensic interviews or other prerecordings.

major_effects.label: Advance notice of recording
major_effects.explanation: Requires notice at least 72 hours before recording to jurors and parties, plus notice on the court’s public website.

agencies.name: court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly restricts the court’s use of videography and assigns the court victim-notification and recording-notice duties. The source refers generically to a court and does not identify a specific state judicial body.

SB45.summary: The bill would extend existing tuition and fee exemptions at public institutions of higher education to siblings of certain armed forces and Texas National Guard members who meet the existing death- or service-disability criteria. A sibling may qualify only if the member has no spouse or child, and must be classified as a resident when registering; the changes apply to charges beginning with the 2027 fall semester.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes eligibility for tuition and fee exemptions at public institutions of higher education.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The exemption concerns public institutions of higher education statewide, without limiting it to a named campus or locality.

affected_groups.group: Siblings of qualifying military personnel
affected_groups.explanation: Siblings are added to the existing exemption, subject to the member having no spouse or child and the sibling meeting the resident-classification requirement.

affected_groups.group: Public institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: These institutions are affected by the expansion of the tuition and fee exemption.

major_effects.label: Expanded tuition and fee exemption eligibility
major_effects.explanation: Adds eligible siblings to the existing exemption, but only if the military member has no spouse or child; the sibling must also be classified as a resident at registration. The changes apply beginning with charges for the 2027 fall semester.

SB46.summary: The bill would bar covered people from knowingly causing political advertising intended to influence an election to show an officeholder’s or candidate’s appearance, speech, or conduct that did not occur, unless the alteration is only superficial or the ad discloses that it is unreal. The commission would prescribe the disclosure’s form, and violations could result in a fine or, for a person with two or more prior convictions under the section, a Class A misdemeanor. The bill would also exclude specified service providers, broadcasters, and commercial-sign operators from liability for ads published, distributed, or broadcast by or at another person’s direction.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes requirements for political advertising intended to influence an election.
Regulates political ads containing fabricated or altered media, including media altered using generative AI.
Creates an offense with a fine and an enhanced misdemeanor classification for repeat convictions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the statewide Texas Election Code and does not limit the provisions to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Officeholders, candidates, and political committees
affected_groups.explanation: These are expressly among the people to whom the new section applies.

affected_groups.group: People who spend on or publish, distribute, or broadcast political advertising
affected_groups.explanation: The section also applies to people exceeding the specified advertising-expenditure threshold and to people publishing, distributing, or broadcasting the described ads for consideration.

affected_groups.group: Specified online, communications, broadcast, and commercial-sign service providers
affected_groups.explanation: The bill excludes listed providers and operators from liability for covered advertising carried at another person’s direction.

major_effects.label: Limits on unreal or altered political advertising
major_effects.explanation: Covered people may not knowingly cause qualifying unreal depictions to appear in election-influencing political ads unless the change is superficial or the ad carries a disclosure.

major_effects.label: Disclosure format
major_effects.explanation: The commission must prescribe the disclosure’s form, including its font, size, and color.

major_effects.label: Offense and penalties
major_effects.explanation: A violation is punishable by a fine of up to $3,000; a defendant with at least two prior convictions under the section may face a Class A misdemeanor.

major_effects.label: Specified intermediary liability exclusion
major_effects.explanation: Listed services, broadcasters, and commercial-sign operators are not liable under this section for advertising published, distributed, or broadcast by or at another person’s direction.

agencies.name: Texas Ethics Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directly assigns the commission responsibility for prescribing the disclosure form, but the supplied text does not identify the commission’s canonical name.

SB47.summary: SB 47 would create a process for petitions seeking authorization to depose a respondent who alleges the petitioner committed family violence or defined abusive conduct; a court would have to deny the petition if clear and convincing evidence shows a history or pattern involving the alleged victim and a purpose to harass, intimidate, or control. It would also let a defendant alleging victimization seek dismissal of a civil case, require dismissal on corresponding findings, and require specified disclosures of protective orders or abusive-conduct criminal complaints. These procedures would apply only to petitions or dismissal motions filed on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates procedural protections for people alleging family violence or defined abusive conduct in specified civil proceedings.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The procedures apply generally to covered civil proceedings under this Texas Act, with no narrower geographic area specified.

affected_groups.group: People alleging family violence or abusive conduct in covered civil proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: They may invoke the new dismissal process or be the alleged victims protected by the new deposition-petition standard.

affected_groups.group: Petitioners and respondents in covered proceedings
affected_groups.explanation: Depending on their role and the allegations made, they may face disclosure requirements, including disclosure whether they are or were subject to a qualifying protective order, or denial of a deposition petition or dismissal motion.

major_effects.label: Limits on covered deposition petitions and civil proceedings
major_effects.explanation: A court must deny a covered deposition petition, or grant a covered dismissal motion, when clear and convincing evidence establishes the specified history or pattern involving the alleged victim and a purpose to harass, intimidate, or control.

major_effects.label: Disclosures in covered cases
major_effects.explanation: When the specified allegations are made, parties must disclose applicable protective orders or criminal complaints arising out of abusive conduct and provide copies.

major_effects.label: Hearings and costs or attorney’s fees
major_effects.explanation: Courts may hold evidentiary hearings in the specified circumstances and may award costs and attorney’s fees under the bill’s conditions, including on request in the specified cases.

agencies.name: trial court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly requires a trial court to deny or grant specified petitions or motions and allows it to conduct hearings and award costs and fees. The bill does not identify a particular court or establish a registry identity.

SB48.summary: SB 48 would give an employee who is a victim of family violence, or whose dependent is a victim, up to 15 workdays off in a 12-month period for specified medical-recovery or legal and safety purposes; 24 hours’ written notice is generally required unless infeasible. Leave need not be paid unless the employee uses existing leave, while the employer must continue specified group health coverage during the absence. The bill would also establish confidentiality, return-to-work and anti-retaliation protections, and require employer workplace notices in a form prescribed by the Texas Workforce Commission.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a time-off entitlement and related workplace protections and employer duties for employees affected by family violence.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill adds a chapter to the Texas Labor Code; statewide geographic reach is inferred from that state-law context.

affected_groups.group: Employees who are victims of family violence or whose dependents are victims
affected_groups.explanation: These employees would qualify for the specified time off and related employment protections.

affected_groups.group: Employers
affected_groups.explanation: Employers would have duties concerning notice, leave administration, health coverage, confidentiality and protection against retaliation.

major_effects.label: Capped time off for specified purposes
major_effects.explanation: Covered employees could take up to 15 workdays in a 12-month period for medical care or recovery, or legal and safety-related activities. The employee generally must provide 24 hours’ advance written notice unless that is not feasible; the leave is unpaid unless the employee uses existing leave time.

major_effects.label: Employment, confidentiality and coverage safeguards
major_effects.explanation: The bill provides for reinstatement and protection against retaliation for qualifying leave, requires confidentiality of leave-related information subject to stated exceptions, and requires continued group health coverage during the absence. Leave itself need not be compensated unless existing leave is used.

major_effects.label: Workplace notice requirements
major_effects.explanation: Employers would have to post a conspicuous notice of employee rights, with the Texas Workforce Commission prescribing its design and content.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill directs the Commission to prescribe the design and content of the workplace sign employers must post.

SB49.summary: SB 49 would direct the Department of Public Safety to coordinate border operations and pursue border security measures, and create grant programs for border-region courts and, subject to available funds, higher-education institutions. It would make appropriated funds available to state agencies and local governments for specified border security, public-safety, criminal-justice, and transportation infrastructure, with certain federal funds also usable for dual-purpose airport projects. It would require the Department of State Health Services, consulting the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board, to prepare a plan for tuition reimbursement and student-loan repayment assistance for health professionals serving near the border; the bill requires a plan, not the immediate establishment of those assistance programs.

policy_tags.explanation: Assigns border-security duties and authorizes funding for public-safety services and border-security infrastructure.
Creates court-operation grants and authorizes funding for facilities and services connected to prosecution and adjudication.
Municipalities and counties may receive funds for the specified border-region purposes.
Creates grant programs and authorizes use of appropriated funds for border-region purposes.
Creates a grant program for higher-education institutions that run qualifying programs or research.
The higher-education grants are intended to recruit, train, retain, and increase professionals in specified fields and address workforce needs.
Requires a plan for tuition reimbursement and student-loan repayment assistance for eligible health professionals serving near the border.
Authorizes funding for construction or improvement of transportation facilities in the border region.

locations.name: Texas-Mexico border
locations.explanation: The bill directs border-security activities and inspection measures at or along this border.

locations.name: Border region as defined by Government Code Section 772.0071
locations.explanation: The bill uses this incorporated geographic definition for court, infrastructure, and education programs.

locations.name: Communities near and along the Texas-Mexico international border
locations.explanation: The health-professional assistance plan is directed to professionals serving in these communities.

affected_groups.group: Border-region courts and court personnel
affected_groups.explanation: The court grant program may reimburse operating costs, including personnel, equipment, travel, and indigent-defense expenses.

affected_groups.group: Municipalities, counties, and state agencies receiving border-related funds
affected_groups.explanation: These entities may receive funds for the purposes specified in the bill.

affected_groups.group: Higher-education institutions and professionals in qualifying fields
affected_groups.explanation: Institutions in the border region may receive grants for programs and research intended to increase the number of relevant professionals.

affected_groups.group: Health care professionals serving near the Texas-Mexico border
affected_groups.explanation: The required plan would provide for assistance programs with eligibility tied to a full-time service commitment and preference for professionals living in those communities.

major_effects.label: DPS border coordination and inspection
major_effects.explanation: Requires a DPS liaison for each specified federal border-operations sector and directs the department to pursue border-security strategies; purchasing vehicle-inspection equipment is authorized but not required.

major_effects.label: Border court grant program
major_effects.explanation: Creates a grant program funded from appropriations to support court operations in the border region; rules must include eligibility criteria limiting eligibility to applicants experiencing increased caseloads.

major_effects.label: Border protection, public-safety, and transportation infrastructure
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes appropriated funds for listed purposes for state agencies and local governments, including border security infrastructure away from ports of entry and transportation facilities. Certain federal funds may support both airport security and commercial or cargo capacity.

major_effects.label: Border institution grant program
major_effects.explanation: Subject to available funds, creates grants for border-region higher-education institutions' qualifying professional-training and research programs.

major_effects.label: Health-professional tuition and loan repayment plan
major_effects.explanation: Requires DSHS, in consultation with THECB, to prepare and submit a plan to establish new and improve existing assistance programs; the bill does not itself establish those programs.

major_effects.label: Grant and fund-use reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires annual spending reports from court and higher-education grant recipients, while other recipients of specified funds report at intervals set by the office.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Public Safety
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department border-liaison and border-security responsibilities and permits it to purchase inspection equipment.

agencies.name: Office of Court Administration of the Texas Judicial System
agencies.explanation: The office is tasked with administering the border court grant program, adopting its rules, and establishing the program.

agencies.name: Trusteed programs within the office of the governor
agencies.explanation: The bill defines this as the office responsible for making specified funds available and permits it to adopt implementing rules; the source does not establish a matching canonical registry identity.

agencies.name: Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board
agencies.explanation: Subject to the availability of funds, the board must establish a border institution grant program and award financial assistance; the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board is also consulted on the health-professional assistance plan.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The department must develop and adopt the health-professional assistance plan and submit it, with an estimated implementation cost, to the legislature.

SB50.summary: The bill would add a Texas chapter governing credit-card transactions, excluding debit-card transactions. It would restrict payment-card-network practices, require advance notice of fee-rate changes, cap interchange fees for issuers with at least $200 billion in consolidated worldwide assets, and authorize attorney-general enforcement with civil penalties and injunctions.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill imposes new restrictions and fee requirements on payment-card networks and certain credit-card issuers.
The bill assigns the comptroller a new administrative responsibility to establish and maintain an online notice mechanism.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill creates state-level restrictions and enforcement remedies for violations of the chapter.

locations.name: Travis County
locations.explanation: The bill specifies Travis County as one possible venue for state enforcement suits.

affected_groups.group: Payment-card networks
affected_groups.explanation: Networks would face restrictions on merchant discounts, disputed-transaction fees, fee schedules, and notice of rate changes.

affected_groups.group: Credit-card issuers meeting the asset threshold
affected_groups.explanation: Issuers with at least $200 billion in qualifying consolidated worldwide assets would be subject to the interchange-fee cap.

affected_groups.group: Merchants and cardholders
affected_groups.explanation: They would receive protections concerning discounts for non-credit payment and fees for disputed credit-card transactions, subject to the bill's finding and notice conditions.

major_effects.label: Restrictions on network practices
major_effects.explanation: Networks could not penalize merchants for offering discounts for cash, debit, or other legal tender; charge disputed-transaction fees unless responsibility is found and written notice is provided within 45 days; or set or recommend fee schedules they know or should know will be used to violate the issuer fee cap.

major_effects.label: Advance notice of fee-rate changes
major_effects.explanation: Networks must publish fee-rate change notices on their own website and the comptroller's website; a change cannot take effect until at least 90 days after publication. The comptroller must establish a mechanism for the notices.

major_effects.label: Interchange-fee cap for large issuers
major_effects.explanation: Issuers meeting the $200 billion consolidated worldwide asset threshold, including affiliate assets but excluding trust assets under management, could not assess or receive an interchange fee above 1.25 percent of the transaction amount.

major_effects.label: State enforcement and civil penalties
major_effects.explanation: The attorney general may investigate alleged violations and sue for civil penalties of up to $30 million or injunctive relief. The bill also states that it creates no private cause of action.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the attorney general to investigate alleged violations and bring enforcement suits, including suits for civil penalties and injunctive relief.

agencies.name: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts
agencies.explanation: The bill requires the comptroller to establish and maintain a mechanism for payment-card networks to publish fee-rate change notices on the comptroller's website.

SB51.summary: The bill would let the governing body of a public retirement system adopt a lump-sum death benefit of up to $1 million for an active peace officer who dies as the direct and proximate result of a single-event injury sustained in the performance of peace-officer duties. The benefit would go to the surviving spouse, otherwise to surviving children (equally if there is more than one), or otherwise to the estate, and could not be paid if it would threaten the system’s actuarial soundness; a system that adopts the benefit must also revise plan documents as needed to preserve qualified-plan status.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill authorizes an employment-related death benefit for active peace officers.
The bill changes the benefit authority of public retirement system governing bodies and requires plan-document revisions if a system adopts the benefit.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law governing public retirement systems; the precise systems covered depend on the referenced statutory definition.

affected_groups.group: Active peace officers who are members of a covered public retirement system
affected_groups.explanation: They may qualify for the benefit if they die under the specified work-injury circumstances and their system adopts the benefit.

affected_groups.group: Surviving spouses, surviving children, and estates of eligible peace officers
affected_groups.explanation: They are the specified recipients, in that order, of any adopted benefit.

affected_groups.group: Public retirement systems
affected_groups.explanation: Their governing bodies may adopt the benefit, subject to actuarial-soundness restrictions and qualified-plan requirements.

major_effects.label: Optional lump-sum death-benefit authority
major_effects.explanation: A public retirement system may adopt by rule a benefit of up to $1 million for a qualifying active peace officer’s death. Payment is not required, and the system may not pay it if doing so would threaten actuarial soundness.

agencies.name: governing body of a public retirement system
agencies.explanation: The bill directly authorizes this governing body to adopt the benefit by rule. The source does not identify a particular body or establish whether a given system is a state or local system.

SB52.summary: The bill would authorize specified courts to bar remote control of devices affecting protected people’s homes, vehicles, or property without effective consent in certain orders, and allow a magistrate to impose that restriction as a family-violence bond condition. It would add nonconsensual remote control to specified criminal offenses, including harassment when the required intent is present, and extend bond/order-violation coverage to unlawful tracking-device installation cases; a related presumption of no effective consent applies only in the listed protective-order or marriage-dissolution circumstances.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands specified criminal offenses to cover remote control without effective consent and adds unlawful installation of a tracking device to the cases covered by the bond/order-violation offense.
The bill adds a possible protective restriction for the safety of protected people and allows a related family-violence bond condition.
The bill addresses nonconsensual remote control of electronic devices affecting another person's residence, vehicle, or property.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill proposes changes to state law enacted by the Texas Legislature, with statewide scope.

affected_groups.group: Applicants, protected individuals, and their family or household members
affected_groups.explanation: They may receive protection through restrictions on another person's nonconsensual remote control of devices affecting their residence, vehicle, or property.

affected_groups.group: Defendants and alleged offenders in covered cases
affected_groups.explanation: They may be subject to new order or bond restrictions and expanded criminal-offense coverage.

affected_groups.group: Parties to marriage-dissolution suits
affected_groups.explanation: A court may include a restriction on nonconsensual remote control in a temporary restraining order in a dissolution suit.

major_effects.label: Order and bond restrictions
major_effects.explanation: Specified courts may include a prohibition on nonconsensual remote control in protective and temporary restraining orders, and a magistrate may impose it as a condition of release on bond in a family-violence case.

major_effects.label: Expanded criminal offense coverage
major_effects.explanation: Remote control without effective consent is added to the harassment offense when the required intent is present and to conduct covered by the bond/order-violation offense. The latter coverage is also extended to unlawful installation of tracking-device cases.

major_effects.label: Limited presumption concerning effective consent
major_effects.explanation: For the harassment provisions on tracking and remote control, lack of effective consent is presumed only in the specified protective-order or marriage-dissolution circumstances.

agencies.name: the court
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly authorizes a court to include the new restriction in specified orders, but does not identify which particular Texas court or courts; attribution to a specific state body is therefore uncertain.

agencies.name: A magistrate
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes a magistrate to impose the restriction as a bond condition in a family-violence case, but does not identify a particular magistrate or court.

SB53.summary: SB 53 changes the definition of “intervenor” for crime victims’ compensation by replacing the qualifying effort to prevent “criminally injurious conduct” with an effort to prevent “a criminal offense.” The change applies to intervenor actions taken on or after the Act’s effective date; earlier actions remain governed by prior law.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which good-faith efforts to prevent crime qualify under the intervenor definition used for crime victims’ compensation.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas law and contains no narrower geographic limitation.

affected_groups.group: Individuals killed or injured while intervening to prevent a criminal offense
affected_groups.explanation: Their qualifying efforts are described by the revised intervenor definition used for crime victims’ compensation.

major_effects.label: Revised intervenor definition
major_effects.explanation: Modifies the qualifying conduct for the intervenor definition used in crime victims’ compensation; it applies only to actions taken on or after the effective date.

SB54.summary: SB 54 would replace September 1, 2027 expiration dates for several Texas protections concerning out-of-network emergency medical services balance billing with a conditional date: the first day after the attorney general publishes a finding that a federal law prohibiting that billing has taken effect. The added Health and Safety Code provision likewise makes Section 773.061(a-1) and the new subsection expire on that trigger, so the expiration depends on the publication occurring.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the expiration trigger for statutory protections related to emergency medical services balance billing.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas Health and Safety Code and Insurance Code provisions with statewide scope.

affected_groups.group: Consumers receiving emergency medical services
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes when the cited consumer protections against certain medical and health care billing expire.

affected_groups.group: Out-of-network emergency medical services providers
affected_groups.explanation: The expiration trigger concerns federal restrictions on these providers engaging in balance billing.

major_effects.label: Conditional expiration of balance-billing protections
major_effects.explanation: Replaces specified September 1, 2027 expiration dates with the first day after the attorney general publishes a finding that a federal prohibition on the described balance billing has taken effect.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The expiration date for the affected provisions is directly keyed to the office publishing a finding in the Texas Register; the bill does not separately command the office to publish one.

SB55.summary: SB 55 sets September 1, 2029, as the expiration date for the protections in Health and Safety Code §773.061(a-1) and the related sunset subsection; that expiration does not affect DSHS authority to take licensing action for provider conduct before that date. It moves the expiration dates for seven specified Insurance Code sections from September 1, 2027, to September 1, 2029, continuing those provisions until then.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill sets or extends expiration dates for protections against certain emergency medical services billing.
The bill extends the duration of statutory protections governing certain billing by emergency medical services providers.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutes and applies statewide.

affected_groups.group: Consumers protected from certain emergency medical services billing
affected_groups.explanation: The bill sets or extends the duration of the relevant consumer protections.

affected_groups.group: Emergency medical services providers
affected_groups.explanation: The covered billing protections apply to this provider group.

major_effects.label: Set a 2029 expiration for Health and Safety Code protections
major_effects.explanation: The protections in §773.061(a-1) and the related sunset subsection expire September 1, 2029; DSHS authority for conduct before expiration is preserved.

major_effects.label: Extend expiration dates for Insurance Code provisions
major_effects.explanation: Seven specified Insurance Code sections are set to expire September 1, 2029, rather than September 1, 2027.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The sunset is expressly linked to DSHS authority: its authority to take licensing action for provider conduct before expiration remains unaffected.

SB56.summary: The bill would prohibit a defined pet store from selling or offering dogs and cats, while allowing qualifying animal-care facilities and rescue organizations to use store space for adoption showcases if the store has no ownership interest in the animals and charges no space fee. Violations could result in civil penalties and injunctions; the changes would apply only to dogs or cats obtained, sold, or offered for sale on or after September 1, 2027.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates restrictions on pet-store sales and conditions for hosting adoption showcases.
Allows county attorneys to bring enforcement actions and makes penalties collected in those actions payable to the county where the violation occurred.
Assigns the attorney general and appropriate district or county attorneys authority to seek penalties or injunctions.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The proposed restrictions apply to pet stores statewide, with penalties payable to the state or to the county where a violation occurs.

affected_groups.group: Pet stores
affected_groups.explanation: Would be barred from selling or offering dogs and cats, subject to limited adoption-showcase provisions.

affected_groups.group: Qualifying animal-care facilities and animal rescue organizations
affected_groups.explanation: May showcase animals they own for adoption in pet stores, subject to the bill's eligibility requirements and restrictions on store ownership interests and fees.

affected_groups.group: Counties
affected_groups.explanation: A county where a violation occurs may receive collected penalties, and its county attorney may bring an enforcement action.

major_effects.label: Pet-store sales restriction and adoption exception
major_effects.explanation: Prohibits pet stores from selling or offering dogs and cats, but permits qualifying animal-care facilities and rescue organizations to use store space for adoption showcases; the store may not own the animals or charge a space fee.

major_effects.label: Civil penalties and injunctions
major_effects.explanation: A violating pet store would be liable for a civil penalty of up to $500 per day for each dog or cat sold or offered for sale, and an authorized official may seek an injunction.

major_effects.label: Enforcement authority
major_effects.explanation: Authorizes the attorney general or the appropriate district or county attorney to bring an action to collect penalties or obtain an injunction.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the attorney general to bring an action to collect civil penalties or obtain an injunction.

SB57.summary: The bill would establish a Texas Seal of Biliteracy for public high school graduates who demonstrate proficiency in English and another language. The agency would set rigorous earning requirements that cannot depend on an examination created for that purpose, while districts would document the credential on qualifying students’ diplomas and transcripts; the changes would apply beginning in the 2027–2028 school year.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a biliteracy credential for public high school graduates and assigns related duties to the agency and school districts.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The duties apply to each school district, giving the credential program statewide scope.

affected_groups.group: Public high school students and graduates who meet the seal requirements
affected_groups.explanation: Qualifying students would receive the seal notation on their diploma and transcript.

affected_groups.group: School districts
affected_groups.explanation: Districts would maintain records and affix the insignia to qualifying students’ diplomas.

major_effects.label: Texas Seal of Biliteracy
major_effects.explanation: Establishes a credential recognizing high proficiency in English and another language, with requirements set by the agency in consultation with stakeholders.

major_effects.label: District credential records and documentation
major_effects.explanation: Requires districts to identify students who earn the seal and record it on their diplomas and transcripts.

major_effects.label: Administrative rules
major_effects.explanation: Directs the commissioner to adopt rules as necessary to administer the new section.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns establishment and administration duties to an entity called only “the agency.” The education context suggests an education agency, but the supplied bill text does not establish its canonical identity.

SB58.summary: The bill would let a qualified local sponsor construct or maintain certain erosion, floodwater, and sediment-control dams or reservoirs without a water permit, if normal storage does not exceed 200 acre-feet, and divert water as needed for specified repair and maintenance work. The exemption would continue after the sponsor’s agreement with the federal Natural Resources Conservation Service ends only if the sponsor continues to own or control the dam or reservoir for those purposes; the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality would adopt implementing rules.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill creates a water-permit exemption for specified dams, reservoirs, and related diversions.
Eligible districts and authorities receive authority to construct or maintain specified dams and reservoirs without a permit.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the statewide Water Code and adds a provision applicable to qualified local sponsors without limiting it to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Qualified local sponsors, including eligible districts and authorities
affected_groups.explanation: These sponsors may use the new permit exemption for qualifying dams, reservoirs, and specified related diversions.

major_effects.label: Permit exemption for qualifying dams and related work
major_effects.explanation: Qualified local sponsors may construct or maintain qualifying dams or reservoirs without a permit and divert water as needed for specified repair, maintenance, or rehabilitation. The exemption can survive termination of the federal agreement only while the sponsor continues to own or control the dam or reservoir for the stated purposes.

major_effects.label: Implementing rules
major_effects.explanation: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality must adopt rules to implement the new exemption.

agencies.name: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality
agencies.explanation: The bill expressly directs the commission to adopt rules implementing the new permit exemption.

SB59.summary: SB 59 would require the commission, its authorized agent, or a person designated under Section 366.014 to report a water well’s location to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation when an abandoned or deteriorated well is identified during an on-site sewage disposal system inspection.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill adds reporting about abandoned or deteriorated water wells identified during sewage-system inspections; it does not establish a water-use permit.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The amendment applies generally to inspections under the cited Texas statute and identifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Commission, authorized agents, and designated persons conducting on-site sewage disposal system inspections
affected_groups.explanation: These actors must report a well’s location when they identify an abandoned or deteriorated water well during an inspection.

major_effects.label: Well-location reporting
major_effects.explanation: Requires the specified inspection actors to report the location of an abandoned or deteriorated water well they identify during an inspection to TDLR.

agencies.name: commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission a reporting duty, but the supplied text does not identify which commission this means.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The department is the specified recipient of the newly required well-location reports.

SB60.summary: SB 60 would change jury instructions in capital-case sentencing: for issues under Article 37.071(b), the jury must answer no unless it unanimously answers yes; for the issue under subsection (e), it must answer yes unless it unanimously answers no. These changes apply only to criminal proceedings commencing on or after the Act's effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes jury-answer instructions in capital-case sentencing proceedings.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas criminal procedure and specifies no narrower geographic area.

affected_groups.group: Defendants in capital cases
affected_groups.explanation: The changed jury-answer instructions apply to capital-case sentencing proceedings.

affected_groups.group: Jurors serving in capital cases
affected_groups.explanation: Jurors would receive revised instructions on how to answer sentencing issues.

major_effects.label: Changes capital-sentencing jury answer defaults
major_effects.explanation: For subsection (b) issues, a unanimous yes is required for yes, and otherwise the jury must answer no. For the subsection (e) issue, a unanimous no is required for no, and otherwise the jury must answer yes.

agencies.name: the court
agencies.explanation: The bill directly changes the jury charge the court must give, but the source does not identify the court by level or institutional name.

SB61.summary: For residential property located in a colonia as defined by the bill, a Spanish copy of an executory contract would have to be provided if the purchaser or potential purchaser requests one, and the copy must be written by a translator certified in Spanish. The executed contract and other binding and controlling documents must remain in English; the change applies only to contracts entered into on or after the Act’s effective date.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes requirements for executory contracts involving residential real property in a defined area.

locations.name: Colonia as defined by the bill
locations.explanation: The covered area must be economically distressed under the referenced Water Code definition, be in a county partly within 62 miles of an international border, and contain at least 11 nearby dwellings forming a community or neighborhood.

affected_groups.group: Purchasers and potential purchasers of residential property in a colonia
affected_groups.explanation: They may request the Spanish copy of the executory contract.

affected_groups.group: Sellers of residential property in a colonia
affected_groups.explanation: They are party to the covered transactions in which a requested Spanish copy must be provided.

affected_groups.group: Translators certified in Spanish
affected_groups.explanation: The Spanish contract copy must be written by a translator meeting this qualification.

major_effects.label: Requested Spanish contract copy
major_effects.explanation: A Spanish copy of a covered executory contract must be provided on request and written by a translator certified in Spanish. The executed contract and other binding and controlling documents remain in English.

SB62.summary: The bill creates a Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation licensing framework for reroofing contractors and an advisory board, but it does not expressly bar contractors without a license from performing reroofing work. A contractor may not advertise that the company is licensed by the state or use the title “licensed reroofing contractor” unless the contractor holds a license issued under the chapter. Licensed contractors would have to disclose their license number and provide property owners a signed written contract; the department would maintain a public license list and investigate complaints. The commission must adopt rules and fees by April 1, 2028, and the department is not required to begin issuing licenses before June 1, 2028.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a licensing framework and regulates license claims, advertising, and contracts for reroofing services.
Assigns administration and enforcement duties to the department and creates a reroofing contractor advisory board.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill establishes a state licensing framework for reroofing contractors, without limiting it to a particular locality.

affected_groups.group: Reroofing contractors and businesses
affected_groups.explanation: Contractors may apply for licenses and, if licensed, must follow the bill's license-number, advertising, and contract requirements.

affected_groups.group: Property owners hiring licensed reroofing contractors
affected_groups.explanation: They must receive a signed written contract before a licensed contractor begins a reroofing project.

affected_groups.group: County and municipal building officials
affected_groups.explanation: They may request the department to verify a contractor's license status.

major_effects.label: Reroofing licensing framework and advisory board
major_effects.explanation: Creates a department-administered licensing framework and an advisory board. The text restricts claims of licensure and use of the licensed title, but does not expressly prohibit unlicensed reroofing work.

major_effects.label: License requirements and fees
major_effects.explanation: Requires the commission to set license issuance and renewal requirements by rule and establish reasonable, necessary fees capped at the state's administration costs.

major_effects.label: License-number and contract disclosures
major_effects.explanation: Requires licensed reroofing contractors to provide property owners signed written contracts that include the contractor's license number and specified contract disclosures.

major_effects.label: Public license information and verification
major_effects.explanation: Requires a searchable public list of licensed contractors in good standing and a department process to verify license status on request from county or municipal building officials.

major_effects.label: Complaint investigation and penalties
major_effects.explanation: Requires investigation of complaints and authorizes administrative penalties and sanctions, as well as civil penalties capped at $500 per violation.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the department chapter administration and enforcement, licensing, public-list, verification, and complaint-investigation duties.

agencies.name: Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: Chapter 51 defines the Commission and Department separately. This bill assigns rulemaking and fee-setting to the Commission, while the Department administers and enforces the chapter. Track the Commission distinctly from TDLR, without treating it as an independently listed agency.

agencies.name: Office of the Attorney General
agencies.explanation: The bill authorizes the attorney general, alongside the executive director, to bring an action for a civil penalty under the chapter.

SB63.summary: The bill would prohibit an individual from performing covered elevator work unless registered as an elevator mechanic, require apprentices to register, establish qualifications and continuing-education requirements, and limit apprentice work to employment by a registered contractor under a registered mechanic’s supervision, subject to Section 754.0165(g). It would also revise contractor requirements and assign registration and rulemaking responsibilities to state bodies. The mechanic and apprentice requirements would not apply until November 1, 2029; experienced individuals may use a separate registration route by applying and paying by September 1, 2029, and contractor application changes apply to applications filed on or after November 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes contractor registration requirements and restricts whom a contractor may engage to perform covered work.
The bill creates occupational registration, qualification, and continuing-education requirements for elevator mechanics and apprentices.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The registration and practice requirements apply to covered work in Texas.

affected_groups.group: Elevator mechanics and mechanic-registration applicants
affected_groups.explanation: Mechanics would need registration, meet a qualification route, and complete continuing education for renewal; experienced workers have a limited transitional application route.

affected_groups.group: Elevator apprentices
affected_groups.explanation: An individual assisting with the specified equipment work may do so only if registered as an elevator apprentice and employed by a registered contractor; the individual must be supervised by a registered elevator mechanic, subject to Section 754.0165(g).

affected_groups.group: Elevator contractors
affected_groups.explanation: Contractors would be subject to revised registration scope and could not engage unregistered mechanics or apprentices for covered work.

major_effects.label: Elevator mechanic registration
major_effects.explanation: An individual may not perform covered work unless registered as an elevator mechanic. Applicants would need an accepted training completion credential or at least five years of relevant experience, and renewals would require continuing education; the Commission must provide rules for limited registrations.

major_effects.label: Apprentice registration and supervision
major_effects.explanation: An individual may not assist with the specified equipment work unless registered as an elevator apprentice and employed by a registered contractor; supervision by a registered mechanic is required subject to Section 754.0165(g). A mechanic may supervise no more than one apprentice.

major_effects.label: Contractor registration and engagement of workers
major_effects.explanation: Contractor registration would apply to persons engaged in the business of covered work, and contractors could not employ, contract with, or obtain services from unregistered mechanics or apprentices for that work.

major_effects.label: Transitional route for experienced mechanics
major_effects.explanation: A person with at least five years of relevant in-state experience preceding the Act's effective date may obtain mechanic registration by applying and paying the required fee before September 1, 2029.

major_effects.label: Implementation rules
major_effects.explanation: The Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation must adopt rules to implement the changes, including rules for mechanic and apprentice continuing education. Except for the rules implementing Sections 754.0165(d) and 754.0166(c), the deadline is September 1, 2029; those excepted rules must be adopted as soon as practicable after the Act’s effective date.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The department administers the new mechanic and apprentice registrations and is expressly named as prescribing the application form and manner for the experienced-worker registration route.

agencies.name: Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the Commission rulemaking duties to implement the new requirements; the supplied registry does not provide a canonical entry for this named body.

SB64.summary: SB 64 would define “sanitarian in training” and create a registration certificate for employed sanitation workers who meet the applicable requirements other than the experience requirement, have less than one year of full-time sanitation experience, pay a fee, and pass the required examination. It would tie sanitarian eligibility to commission rules and require renewal of a Chapter 1953 certificate upon payment of the renewal fee and proof of applicable continuing education.

policy_tags.explanation: Amends registration and renewal requirements for the regulated sanitarian occupation, including a certificate for sanitarians in training.

locations.name: Statewide Texas
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas statutory requirements for certificates of registration under Chapter 1953.

affected_groups.group: Employed sanitation workers seeking a sanitarian-in-training certificate
affected_groups.explanation: They would need to meet the specified eligibility requirements, have less than one year of full-time sanitation experience, pay the fee, and pass the examination.

affected_groups.group: Applicants for sanitarian registration
affected_groups.explanation: Their registration eligibility would include requirements prescribed by commission rule as well as the statutory requirements.

affected_groups.group: Holders of certificates of registration under Chapter 1953
affected_groups.explanation: Renewal would be conditioned on paying the prescribed fee and providing proof of applicable continuing education.

major_effects.label: Sanitarian-in-training registration
major_effects.explanation: Creates a certificate for an employed individual who meets the applicable eligibility requirements other than experience, has less than one year of full-time sanitation experience, pays the required fee, and passes the examination.

major_effects.label: Sanitarian registration qualifications
major_effects.explanation: Makes commission-rule requirements part of the eligibility requirements for issuance of a sanitarian registration certificate.

major_effects.label: Certificate renewal conditions
major_effects.explanation: Requires renewal of a Chapter 1953 certificate when the holder pays the prescribed fee and provides proof of applicable continuing education.

agencies.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: Section 1953.001 defines the department as the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation. The bill directly amends its certificate-issuance and renewal functions.

agencies.name: Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation
agencies.explanation: Section 1953.001 defines the commission as the Texas Commission of Licensing and Regulation. The bill directly addresses the commission’s rulemaking on additional qualifications for registration.

SB65.summary: SB 65 would expand the exception to the ban on operating off-highway vehicles on state- or political-subdivision-owned or leased land that is not open to vehicular traffic, adding beaches alongside public off-highway vehicle land. Operation would still have to comply with Chapter 551A, Transportation Code, and Chapter 29, Parks and Wildlife Code. The bill also removes Section 551A.031’s safety-certificate-related provisions and repeals other Chapter 551A provisions whose subject matter is not described in the bill text.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes where off-highway vehicles may be operated.
The bill removes Section 551A.031’s safety-certificate-related language and repeals its subsections (b) and (c).

locations.name: State- or political-subdivision-owned or leased land that is not open to vehicular traffic, including public off-highway vehicle land or a beach
locations.explanation: The operating restriction and expanded exception apply to this defined category of land.

affected_groups.group: Off-highway vehicle operators
affected_groups.explanation: Operators may use a beach within the specified category of state or political-subdivision land if they comply with the applicable chapters.

major_effects.label: Expanded permitted operating locations
major_effects.explanation: Adds beaches to the qualifying land on which off-highway vehicles may be operated, subject to the stated land conditions and compliance with the cited chapters.

major_effects.label: Safety-certificate-related and other Chapter 551A provisions repealed
major_effects.explanation: Removes the safety-certificate reference from Section 551A.031’s heading and repeals subsections (b) and (c), as well as other listed Chapter 551A provisions.

SB66.summary: The bill requires the higher-education board, coordinating with the Texas Education Agency and Texas Workforce Commission, to study industry-recognized credentials and establish a pilot with at least one two-year and one four-year institution. The study must include a model framework for credential pathways, and the bill requires preliminary and final reports in 2028; this section expires September 1, 2029.

policy_tags.explanation: Creates a required study and pilot concerning credential pathways, coursework, and degree and certificate programs at public institutions of higher education.
The study examines credential pathways in relation to labor-market outcomes, employer demand, and workforce needs.

locations.name: Texas
locations.explanation: The study concerns workforce demand and credential outcomes in this state.

affected_groups.group: Public institutions of higher education
affected_groups.explanation: At least one two-year and one four-year institution must participate in the pilot, which addresses credential and degree pathways.

affected_groups.group: Students pursuing higher-education credentials
affected_groups.explanation: The model framework is intended to support students earning credentials as part of degree pathways, including pathways from high school.

major_effects.label: Credential feasibility study and model framework
major_effects.explanation: Requires assessment of credential availability, integration, transferability, and labor-market outcomes, plus a model framework for credential pathways; it does not itself require institutions to create the modeled programs.

major_effects.label: Higher-education pilot project
major_effects.explanation: Requires the board to administer a pilot using available institutional collaboration center resources, with participating two-year and four-year institutions, to reduce regulatory burdens and support partnerships.

major_effects.label: Study and pilot reports
major_effects.explanation: Requires preliminary and final reports, including findings and recommendations for legislative or other action.

agencies.name: the board
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the board responsibility for the study, pilot, and reports. Its canonical identity is not established in the supplied text.

agencies.name: Texas Education Agency
agencies.explanation: The bill defines “Agency” as the Texas Education Agency and requires it to coordinate on the study and reports.

agencies.name: Texas Workforce Commission
agencies.explanation: The bill defines “Commission” as the Texas Workforce Commission and requires it to coordinate on the study and reports.

SB67.summary: SB 67 would narrow an exemption from residential mortgage loan originator licensing under Finance Code Chapter 157. A residential real estate owner would qualify for the exemption only when making no more than three covered loans in any 12-consecutive-month period, down from five.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes who is exempt from residential mortgage loan originator licensing when an owner finances a property's purchase.

locations.name: Texas statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends the Texas Finance Code and changes a licensing exemption under that code.

affected_groups.group: Owners of residential real estate who finance purchasers
affected_groups.explanation: Their exemption from licensing would be limited to no more than three covered loans in a 12-consecutive-month period.

affected_groups.group: Purchasers whose property purchase is financed by its owner
affected_groups.explanation: The change may affect whether the owner financing their purchase qualifies for the licensing exemption.

major_effects.label: Narrower owner-financing licensing exemption
major_effects.explanation: Reduces the maximum number of covered residential mortgage loans an owner may make in a 12-consecutive-month period while using this exemption from five to three.

SB68.summary: SB 68 would expand which counties are covered by Transportation Code Chapter 258, concerning clarification of a public interest in certain roads. In addition to the existing rule for counties that initiated or completed compliance before September 1, 2011, it would cover a county adjacent to the Texas-Mexico border with fewer than 300,000 residents that contains a municipality with at least 200,000 residents.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill expands county eligibility under a chapter addressing the public interest in certain roads.
The bill expands the counties eligible to act under Chapter 258.

locations.name: Texas-Mexico border
locations.explanation: Adjacency to this area is one of the criteria for the newly eligible counties.

affected_groups.group: Counties adjacent to the Texas-Mexico border with populations under 300,000 that contain a municipality with a population of 200,000 or more
affected_groups.explanation: These counties would newly qualify for Chapter 258 to apply to them.

major_effects.label: Expands county eligibility under Chapter 258
major_effects.explanation: Chapter 258 would also apply to counties meeting the bill's border-adjacency and population criteria, extending the counties able to use the chapter's provisions concerning certain roads.

SB69.summary: SB 69 would allow commissioners courts in certain counties on the international border to abolish the appointed purchasing-agent office and employ a county purchasing agent under Section 262.0115. If the office is abolished, the incumbent’s term would end on the date set by the court’s order, and the incumbent could be employed as a county purchasing agent.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the purchasing-agent authority and staffing options available to commissioners courts in qualifying counties.

locations.name: Qualifying counties located on the international border
locations.explanation: The bill applies only to border counties with a population under 400,000 that contain at least one municipality with a population of 200,000 or more.

affected_groups.group: Commissioners courts in qualifying counties
affected_groups.explanation: They would gain discretion to abolish the appointed purchasing-agent office and employ a county purchasing agent under Section 262.0115.

affected_groups.group: Purchasing agents in qualifying counties
affected_groups.explanation: An agent whose office is abolished would have a term ending on the date set by the order and would remain eligible for employment as a county purchasing agent.

major_effects.label: County purchasing-agent options
major_effects.explanation: In qualifying counties, a commissioners court could abolish the appointed purchasing-agent office and employ a person under the alternative county purchasing-agent provision.

SB70.summary: The bill expands the definition of personal property for local-government procurement to include consultation and assistance, and work related to the property's use as well as its installation. It also allows governing bodies to contract for those materials, services, and labor when incident to installation or use.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes the personal-property definition and contracting provisions applicable to local-government agencies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The provisions concern political subdivisions under the Texas Local Government Code and are not limited to a particular place.

affected_groups.group: Political subdivisions and their governmental agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Their governing bodies may contract for the expanded categories of materials, consultation, assistance, and labor related to personal property.

major_effects.label: Expanded personal-property procurement
major_effects.explanation: Expands the covered property-related materials and work to include consultation, assistance, and labor incident to use as well as installation.

SB71.summary: The bill changes when counties may donate surplus or salvage property to a civic or charitable organization. Counties with populations under four million could donate without first determining that a sale would likely fail or cost more than it brings in, but must retain sufficient control to ensure the donation’s public purpose; counties with populations of four million or more would remain subject to the sale-related test and would not have that added control requirement.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes county commissioners courts’ authority and criteria for disposing of county property by donation.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends statewide Texas law governing county property disposal, with a separate rule for counties having a population of four million or more.

affected_groups.group: County commissioners courts and county governments
affected_groups.explanation: They receive the changed authority and must satisfy the applicable donation criteria.

affected_groups.group: Civic or charitable organizations located in a county
affected_groups.explanation: These organizations may receive county surplus or salvage property by donation if the applicable statutory conditions are met.

major_effects.label: County donation authority for surplus and salvage property
major_effects.explanation: For counties below four million population, the bill removes the requirement that a sale likely fail or cost more than it brings in, while adding a requirement to retain sufficient control to accomplish the donation’s public purpose. Counties with populations of four million or more retain the sale-related test and are exempt from the added control requirement.

SB72.summary: The bill revises the membership of the Texas Groundwater Protection Committee. It adds the executive director of the Parks and Wildlife Department and updates the health-services and Texas A&M research seats; it does not itself establish new groundwater requirements.

policy_tags.explanation: The bill changes membership of a committee concerned with groundwater protection.
The bill changes the composition of a state committee.

affected_groups.group: Texas Groundwater Protection Committee members and designated state officials
affected_groups.explanation: The bill changes which officials and organizations hold committee seats.

major_effects.label: Committee membership revised
major_effects.explanation: Adds the Parks and Wildlife Department executive director and updates the health-services and Texas A&M research seat designations.

agencies.name: Texas Groundwater Protection Committee
agencies.explanation: The bill directly revises the committee's membership.

agencies.name: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department
agencies.explanation: The department's executive director is added as a committee member.

agencies.name: Department of State Health Services
agencies.explanation: The committee seat is revised to specify the commissioner of state health services; the bill does not state the department's full name in this clause.

SB73.summary: The bill revises state agency internal-audit requirements, including the systems covered by audits and the standards governing the audit program. It also defines advisory services and requires internal auditors to communicate advisory and assurance engagement results and document deviations from the audit plan.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes internal auditing duties and standards for state agencies.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The audit-program requirements apply to state agencies as a class across Texas.

affected_groups.group: State agency internal auditors
affected_groups.explanation: Their audit planning, audit execution, and communication responsibilities are revised.

affected_groups.group: State agencies and their administrators and governing boards
affected_groups.explanation: Their internal-audit programs and the systems subject to audit are affected.

major_effects.label: Revised audit coverage
major_effects.explanation: The bill removes the word “periodic” from the requirement for audits of major systems and identifies operational or administrative and information technology systems and controls.

major_effects.label: Audit-plan execution and engagement communications
major_effects.explanation: Internal auditors must document deviations from the audit plan and communicate results of advisory and assurance engagements.

major_effects.label: Updated internal-audit standards
major_effects.explanation: The bill replaces the stated professional-practice framework with the Global Internal Audit Standards promulgated by the Institute of Internal Auditors.

agencies.name: state agency
agencies.explanation: Chapter 2102 defines “state agency” as a department, board, bureau, institution, commission, or other agency in the executive branch of state government. The bill directly imposes internal-audit requirements on that defined class.

SB74.summary: SB 74 would require the Texas Economic Development and Tourism Office to study state-agency marketing costs, results, staffing, and the feasibility and potential savings of consolidating marketing services into a proposed Department of Marketing Services. The office would report its findings and detailed cost analysis to state leaders and legislators by September 30, 2028; the bill studies the proposed department but does not create it.

policy_tags.explanation: Requires a study and report concerning state-agency marketing operations and possible consolidation of those services.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The study concerns marketing costs and results across state agencies, rather than a specified locality.

affected_groups.group: State agencies
affected_groups.explanation: Their marketing costs, staffing, grant or loan program costs, and marketing results are subjects of the required study and report.

major_effects.label: Study and report on state-agency marketing
major_effects.explanation: Requires the Office to analyze agency marketing costs, outcomes, staffing, and consolidation feasibility, then report findings and detailed cost information to state leaders and legislators. It does not establish the proposed department.

agencies.name: Texas Economic Development and Tourism Office
agencies.explanation: The bill defines the Office as the Texas Economic Development and Tourism Office and assigns it the study and reporting duties. The supplied registry does not provide a matching canonical identity.

SB75.summary: The bill sets an alternative meeting schedule for a county bail bond board in a county with fewer than 1.3 million people that contains a municipality with at least 750,000 people: six meetings each year in specified months, with additional meetings when called by the presiding officer. For renewal applications filed on or after the Act’s effective date, a license remains in effect until the board’s next meeting if the board tables the application or otherwise does not approve or deny it.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes the required meeting frequency for qualifying county bail bond boards.
Changes how a bail bond license operates when a qualifying board has not acted on a renewal application.

locations.name: Counties with fewer than 1.3 million people that contain a municipality with at least 750,000 people
locations.explanation: The alternative board meeting schedule applies to counties meeting these population criteria.

affected_groups.group: County bail bond boards in counties meeting the population criteria
affected_groups.explanation: These boards receive an alternative meeting schedule.

affected_groups.group: Bail bond license holders with pending renewal applications
affected_groups.explanation: Their current licenses continue until the board’s next meeting if the board tables the renewal or otherwise does not approve or deny it; the amended provision applies to applications filed on or after the Act’s effective date.

major_effects.label: Alternative meeting schedule for qualifying boards
major_effects.explanation: Qualifying boards meet six times each year in the specified months, with additional meetings when called by the presiding officer, instead of the general monthly schedule.

major_effects.label: Continuation of licenses pending board action
major_effects.explanation: For applications filed on or after the Act’s effective date, a current license continues until the next meeting if the board tables the renewal application or otherwise does not approve or deny it.

SB76.summary: The bill would exempt people who casually sell used automotive parts or recycle them incidentally as part of their business from Chapter 2309, and direct the commission to adopt implementing rules. It would also require used automotive parts recyclers to remove all license plates and any registration insignia immediately upon receiving a vehicle.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes which people are subject to used automotive parts recycling regulation and adds a rulemaking duty and vehicle-identification removal requirement for recyclers.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The amendments govern Chapter 2309 of the Occupations Code without limiting their application to a particular area.

affected_groups.group: People who casually sell used automotive parts or recycle them incidentally as part of a business
affected_groups.explanation: They would be excluded from Chapter 2309 under the new applicability provision.

affected_groups.group: Used automotive parts recyclers
affected_groups.explanation: They would have to remove all license plates and registration insignia immediately after receiving a vehicle.

major_effects.label: Exemption from Chapter 2309
major_effects.explanation: The chapter would not apply to casual sales of used automotive parts or recycling that is incidental to a person's business.

major_effects.label: Rules for the new exemption
major_effects.explanation: The commission would adopt rules to implement the exemption.

major_effects.label: Expanded vehicle-identification removal requirement
major_effects.explanation: Upon receiving a vehicle, recyclers would have to remove license plates without limiting the requirement to unexpired plates, and also remove registration insignia.

agencies.name: commission
agencies.explanation: The bill assigns the commission a rulemaking duty, but the supplied text does not establish the commission's canonical identity.

SB77.summary: The bill expands public information to include official-business electronic communications on any device and database field descriptions, except security-sensitive metadata. It requires governmental bodies to provide covered electronic information in searchable or sortable formats when requested, with limits tied to available software and existing confidentiality exceptions, and updates the statutory fee reference for county clerks’ nonpaper copies.

policy_tags.explanation: Changes public-information duties and the handling and production of government records.
Sets requirements for access to electronic records and database information while retaining security and confidentiality limits.
Changes the statutory fee reference governing county clerks’ nonpaper copies of records.

locations.name: Statewide
locations.explanation: The bill amends Texas public-information law and imposes duties on governmental bodies generally.

affected_groups.group: Public information requestors
affected_groups.explanation: May request electronic public information in searchable or sortable formats, or request a paper printout.

affected_groups.group: Governmental bodies that maintain electronic public information
affected_groups.explanation: Must meet the bill’s electronic-record access and production requirements, subject to its stated limits and exceptions.

affected_groups.group: County clerks
affected_groups.explanation: Must use the referenced Government Code provision when providing and charging for nonpaper copies of records they maintain.

major_effects.label: Expands electronic information covered by public-information law
major_effects.explanation: Includes official-business electronic communications on any device and database field descriptions, but excludes metadata that directly implicates database security.

major_effects.label: Requires accessible electronic copies
major_effects.explanation: Requires searchable or sortable copies in the requested format when applicable, using software the governmental body uses; existing confidentiality exceptions remain in place.

major_effects.label: Addresses contracts and third-party custody
major_effects.explanation: Requires reasonable efforts to ensure information-maintenance contracts do not impair public access and applies the section when a third party is the governmental body’s custodian.

major_effects.label: Updates county clerk copy-fee reference
major_effects.explanation: Directs county clerks to the referenced Government Code provision for nonpaper copies and repeals Section 552.231; the bill does not specify a new fee amount.

SB78.summary: A municipality that adopted a Chapter 334 sports and community venue sales tax and has or will have qualifying bond debt outstanding on September 1, 2027, may convert all or part of that tax to an economic-development sales tax with majority voter approval.
